Role Access Admin Full access: set schedules from Customer Reports or Edit Customer, and send statements manually. Manager Can set the schedule from Customers > Edit Customer. Can use Reports > Customer Reports (inline schedule, counters, manual Email) only if your account allows managers to view reports. Dispatch / Customer Service No access to Customer Reports. Can set the schedule from Edit Customer only if your account allows dispatchers to manage customers. Customer Service users have the same permissions as Dispatch. Accountant No access. Accountants can't open Customer Reports or edit customers, so they can't change statement schedules. Customer / Driver / Warehouse / Garage No access.

See User Roles for how roles and account options work.

docs.title: Schedule Options
docs.text:
The same list of options appears in the customer form and in the Customer Reports dropdown (titled Select Statement Day).

Option When the statement is sent Weekly on Sunday … Weekly on Saturday Every week on that weekday. Bi-Weekly on the 2nd and 16th Twice a month, on the 2nd and the 16th. Despite the name, this is not every two weeks. Monthly on the 1st Once a month, on the 1st. Monthly on the 15th Once a month, on the 15th. Not Scheduled No automatic statement. This removes the schedule.

Labels

On the customer form the field is called Send weekly statement on, even though it also holds the monthly and twice-a-month options. In the Customer Reports column, the twice-a-month option shows as Bi-Weekly on 2nd and 16th.

There is no "send now" or "Today" option. To send a statement right away, use the Email button (see Sending a statement manually).

docs.title: Adding a Statement Schedule to a Customer
docs.text: You can set the schedule in 2 ways. Both save the same setting.

docs.title: Edit the schedule on the Customer Reports screen
docs.text:
1. Navigate to Reports Customer Reports.
  2. Find your Customer by name. You can pick one customer in the Customer filter and click Update Report, or leave [ALL CUSTOMERS].
  3. Click the value in the Delivery Day / Next Date column for this customer.
  4. Choose an option from the dropdown.
  5. Click the check-mark button to save.
  6. Once saved, the Next Date badge shows when the statement will be delivered automatically.

docs.title: Edit the Customer to set the schedule
docs.text:
1. From the left menu, select Customers.
  2. Find your Customer by name.
  3. Click Edit Customer.
  4. In the Automatic Statement schedule for this customer section, choose an option from Send weekly statement on.
  5. Click Save Changes.

docs.title: Related customer fields
docs.text:
These fields on the customer form control who gets the statement and what it looks like:

Field Effect on automatic statements Accountant Email The To address. Required: if it is empty or invalid, the statement is not sent. Accountant Email (CC) Added to CC. Default Statement Format PDF Format or Excel (.xlsx): the attachment type. Active Only active customers receive automatic statements. Deleted customers are never sent one.

docs.title: The Next Date
docs.text:
The Next Date badge (and the job that sends statements) works out the next date like this:

  • Weekly: the next time that weekday comes around, counting today. If the statement was already sent today, it moves to the same weekday next week.
  • Monthly on the 1st / 15th: that day in the current month if it hasn't passed yet; otherwise that day next month. If the statement was already sent on that date, it moves to next month.
  • Bi-Weekly on the 2nd and 16th: whichever of the next 2nd or the next 16th comes first, using the monthly rule above for each.

The badge reads Today, Tomorrow, or In followed by the time left (for example In 3 days or In about 1 month).

Setting today's day

If you pick today's weekday (or today's date for a monthly option), the Next Date shows Today and the customer is picked up by the next run of the job that day, unless a statement was already sent to them today. If the job does not run again before the end of the day, nothing is sent and the Next Date moves to the following scheduled date.

docs.title: How the job runs
docs.text:
• Statements are sent by a background job that runs on a schedule managed by UTX. The time of day it runs isn't set in UTX Freight, so don't count on a specific hour.
  • On each run, the job looks at active (not deleted) customers that have a schedule, whose Next Date is today, and whose Sent date is not today.
  • Customers are processed in alphabetical order by name.
  • Each run handles about 20 customers, with a short pause after each one.
  • Customers that a run doesn't reach are handled by a later run, but only while their scheduled date is still today. There is no catch-up: once the date passes, the Next Date moves to the next scheduled date and nothing is sent for the missed one.

Spread your schedules

Because each run processes only about 20 customers, putting many customers on the same day increases the chance that some are not reached on their scheduled date. Since customers are processed alphabetically, those later in the alphabet are reached last. Spread customers across different weekdays and monthly options, and check the day counters (below) to keep each day light.

Update before the scheduled day

The statement reflects invoices and payments at the moment it is sent. Post payments and fix invoices the day before a customer's scheduled date so they receive an accurate statement.

docs.title: Who gets an email
docs.text:
• Single office: every due customer is processed. If the customer's unpaid balance (the total of their invoices not marked Paid, minus payments applied to those invoices) is greater than $0, the statement is emailed. If it is $0, no email is sent, but the Sent date is still set to today with the message Statement Not Sent (0.0$).
  • Multi-office: see Multi-Office Accounts below.

Zero balance applies to the automatic run only

The "no email at $0" rule only applies to the automatic job. A manual send with the Email button always sends the statement, even when the balance is zero.

docs.title: Recipients and Email Content
docs.text:
Part Value From Your company name with the Accountant Email from your application settings (described there as the default From address for invoices). Depending on how email is set up for your account, the visible sender may be a UTX sending address, with Reply-To set to that Accountant Email. See Application Settings. To The customer's Accountant Email. CC The customer's Accountant Email (CC) plus the Invoice Default CC Address from your application settings. Subject <Your company name> Statement of Account as of <date> (the company name UTX set up for your account). On multi-office accounts, - <Office name> is added at the end. Attachment Statement of account as of <date>.pdf or .xlsx, depending on the customer's Default Statement Format. Body A Statement of Account for <date> heading and a short message saying the statement of account is attached as a PDF or XLSX.

Before sending, the automatic run checks the addresses: the To address (the customer's Accountant Email) must be present and valid, the CC addresses must be valid, and the Invoice 'From' Address Override in your application settings (or the default UTX set for your account when it is empty) must be a valid address. If any check fails, the customer is skipped (see below).

The attachment is the same one a manual Email send produces. See Customer Statements for what the statement contains and Application Settings for the email settings.

docs.title: Sent Date and Delivery Status
docs.text:
Two columns on Customer Reports show the result of the last statement:

  • Sent date: the date of the last statement attempt that was recorded, or - if none.
  • Email: a label, green OK or red Failed!. Hover over the label to see the message.
What happened Sent date Email label Hover message Automatic run, balance > $0, email sent Today OK Statement Delivered Automatic run, balance $0 (single office) Today OK Statement Not Sent (0.0$) Automatic run, error while sending Today Failed! The error message Automatic run, invalid email setup (missing or invalid To, invalid CC, or invalid Invoice 'From' Address Override) Not changed Not changed Not changed Manual Email, sent successfully Today OK Statement Delivered Manual Email, error while sending Not changed Failed! The error message

A failed automatic send is not retried

When the automatic run hits an error, the Sent date is still set to today, so the customer is not retried that day. The next attempt is on the next scheduled date. Fix the problem and use Email to send the statement manually.

Check email addresses

A statement can only be sent automatically when the customer has a valid Accountant Email and the CC and Invoice 'From' Address Override addresses are valid. Check that every scheduled customer has a valid Accountant Email.

docs.title: Sending a statement manually
docs.text:
1. On Reports > Customer Reports, click the blue Email button on the customer's row.
  2. In Send statement to customer, check To (pre-filled with the customer's Accountant Email) and Cc (pre-filled with the customer's Accountant Email (CC)). Add a Bcc if needed.
  3. Click Send.

A successful manual send sets Sent date to today. If today is also the customer's scheduled date, the automatic run skips them, so they don't get two statements the same day.

docs.title: Scheduler Information (Day Counters)
docs.text:
At the top right of Customer Reports, a row of counters shows how many customers are scheduled for each option: Sun to Sat (weekend days in red, weekdays in blue), then 1st, 15th and 2nd & 16th (green).

What the counters count

The counters count customers with a schedule, not emails delivered, so the number can be higher than the number of statements actually sent. Set inactive customers to Not Scheduled to keep the counts meaningful.

docs.title: Multi-Office Accounts
docs.text:
On accounts with more than one office:

  • Statements are per office. Each email covers only that office's invoices, and the subject ends with - <Office name>.
  • The job goes office by office. A customer is emailed for an office only if they have an unpaid balance in that office. Offices where the balance is $0 are skipped, and nothing is recorded for them (no Sent date, no Statement Not Sent (0.0$) message).
  • The 20-customer limit applies to the whole run, across all offices.
  • A manual Email send uses the office you are currently working in. See Multi-Office.

docs.title: Activity Log
docs.text: UTX keeps a record of each automatic attempt (sent, not sent at $0, failed, or skipped because of an invalid email setup). This history isn't shown on a screen in the app; the Sent date and Email columns on Customer Reports are what you see. Contact UTX support if you need the history of attempts for a customer.

docs.title: The customer is scheduled but didn't receive a statement
docs.text:
Solution

Check, in order:

  1. Is the customer Active? Inactive customers are never emailed.
  2. Does the customer have an Accountant Email? Without a valid one, the statement can't be sent.
  3. Was the balance $0? Hover over the Email label. Statement Not Sent (0.0$) means there was nothing to collect.
  4. Is the label Failed!? Hover to read the error, fix it, and send manually with Email.
  5. Were many customers due that day? Each run processes about 20 customers, in alphabetical order. If the customer wasn't reached on their date, they wait for the next scheduled date. Send manually if needed and spread out the schedules.

docs.title: I changed the schedule to today but nothing was sent yet
docs.text:
Solution

The statement goes out on the next run of the job, not the moment you save. The job runs on a schedule managed by UTX. If you need it now, click Email on Customer Reports.

docs.title: Why is "Bi-Weekly" sending twice a month instead of every two weeks?
docs.text:
Solution

Bi-Weekly on the 2nd and 16th sends on two fixed dates each month, the 2nd and the 16th. There is no every-other-week option.

docs.title: I can't see the Delivery Day / Next Date column
docs.text:
Solution

Either automatic statements aren't enabled for your account (contact UTX support), or your role can't open Customer Reports. See Access & Permissions above.

docs.title: The day counter says 40 but far fewer statements went out
docs.text:
Solution

The counters count customers with a schedule, not deliveries. Inactive customers are not emailed, and customers with a $0 balance aren't emailed either.

docs.title: Do Garage customers use this schedule?
docs.text:
Solution

No. Garage customers have their own statement schedule and job. See Garage Reports.

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
Best Practices

  • Fill in Accountant Email for every customer before scheduling them.
  • Spread customers across weekdays and monthly options so each day's counter stays low.
  • Post payments the day before a customer's scheduled date.
  • Check the Email column after each scheduled day for Failed! labels.
  • Set customers you deactivate to Not Scheduled so the counters stay accurate.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text:
All notable changes to UTX Freight are documented here. Releases are listed newest first. Each release starts with its main features, followed by the smaller patch releases that shipped after it.

Current version: 3.12.19 (released 2026-09-17)

The version number has three parts: major.minor.patch. A new minor release (for example 3.12.0) brings new features. Patch releases (3.12.1, 3.12.2, ...) bring fixes and smaller improvements. Some patch releases contain only internal maintenance and have no visible change; they are grouped as Maintenance below. Release numbers and dates are those recorded in the application when each change shipped; releases 3.0 to 3.10 were re-checked against them, and entries that were filed under the wrong release or described features that do not exist are marked Corrected entry.

docs.title: Invoices
docs.text:
• Exports now match your filters — the Export button downloads exactly the invoices currently listed. Previously the export ignored the status tab and search on screen and only used a year drop-down, so, for example, exporting while on Paid still returned every invoice of that year
  • See what you are exporting before you click — the EXPORT panel states the count and the active filter, for example "Exports the 1,002 invoices currently listed (All unpaid) — not the whole database."
  • Two export layouts — choose QuickBooks columns for accounting import, or the new AR aging detail layout for collections and month-end review. Both download as Excel or CSV
  • Invoice date range — the INVOICE DATE card filters the list to a from/to range, with one-click presets: This Month, Last Month, This Year, the previous calendar year (labelled with the year number, for example 2025), and Last 12 Months
  • AR AGING card — the AR AGING (DAYS PAST DUE) card filters by how late an invoice is, using open-ended rollups (Past due, 30+ days, 60+ days) or exact bands (Not Due, 0-30, 31-60, 61-90, 91+). The bands split the unpaid ledger the same way the Aged Receivables report does. Invoices marked Paid carry no aging
  • Past-due tabs replaced — the old Past Due, Past Due (30+ days) and Past Due (60+ days) status tabs are gone. The status tabs are now only All, All Unpaid, New, Invoiced, Paid and Partially Paid; everything about how old an invoice is lives in the AR AGING card
  • Days past due and Balance in the list — the Due date column now shows a colour-coded aging badge (Not Due, 0-30, 31-60, 61-90, 91+) under the due date, and a new Balance column shows the outstanding amount with the total paid below it, so you no longer have to open the invoice
  • Filters combine instead of replacing each other — status, search, invoice date, and aging all narrow the same list. Each active filter appears as a removable chip in the search bar, with Clear All to reset
  • A cleaner invoice table — folded from 15 columns to 8 by pairing each value with its closely related detail (invoice with its date, balance with total paid, status with sent date). Nothing was removed
  • Consistent sorting — past-due views now sort newest-first like every other tab, instead of oldest-first
  • Large export guard — an export of more than 20,000 invoices is refused with a message asking you to narrow it with the invoice date range, rather than timing out
  • Fixed an error when exporting an invoice that had no company assigned, and a company drill-down that led to an empty list

See Invoices for how to use the filters and export.

Your saved links still work

Bookmarked links to the old Past Due, Past Due (30+ days) and Past Due (60+ days) tabs continue to work — they now open the matching AR AGING rollup (Past due, 30+ days, 60+ days) and return the same invoices they always did.

docs.title: 3.12.x patch releases
docs.text: Version Date Change 3.12.1 2026-08-21 Consignee order visibility (Customer Portal). A shipper/receiver record can be linked to a customer account so that account's users get read-only visibility of orders delivered to that location, including orders placed by a different customer (for example another freight forwarder). Link it from Shipper / Receiver  edit form  Portal Access — Consignee Link Linked Customer Account. Only users with the Customer role on the linked account get this access; they can view the orders and open their documents, but not edit them. Consignee users see a Consignee view: banner on the Orders page, which also states that pricing details are not shown. The Shipper / Receiver list gains a Linked filter and a Linked Account column. See Shippers & Receivers and Customer Portal. 3.12.1 2026-08-21 Orders header total. The Total figure in the Orders header now sums only the three badges beside it (New Orders, App. Made, Dispatched). It previously also counted Completed orders. 3.12.2 2026-08-23 Garage: edit work orders until the invoice leaves the shop. Work orders can now be edited at every stage, including In Progress and Completed (you no longer need Reopen Work Order just to fix a line). A work order attached to a Draft invoice can still be edited; the Draft invoice is recalculated after you save and the new total is shown. Editing locks only once the invoice is no longer a Draft (for example Sent or Paid); a Sent invoice with no payments can be returned to Draft with Reopen to Edit. The customer of an invoiced work order cannot be changed. Removing a part from a work order on a Draft invoice returns it to stock. See Garage Work Orders. 3.12.3 2026-09-04 Garage: better work order search. The work order search now also matches the attached equipment (unit / chassis number, VIN, plate, make, model, type) and the customer's company name. When nothing matches, the page says which term found nothing and offers Clear search. 3.12.4 2026-09-11 Customer page shows the country. Opening a customer (company) page directly no longer shows an error; the page shows the company's country. 3.12.5 2026-09-11 Maintenance. 3.12.6 2026-09-11 Statement send and refresh fixed. Sending a statement or refreshing a customer row from the customer list no longer shows an error; the row repaints with the correct invoice counts. 3.12.7 2026-09-11 Container tracking run no longer aborts on concurrent edits. If a dispatcher saves an order while the Port of Montreal (Termont) tracking update is filling in that order's fields, the update now retries that order instead of skipping every remaining container in the run. Values the dispatcher just saved are kept. 3.12.8 2026-09-11 Tracking popup direct links. Opening the container tracking popup's address directly (new tab, pasted link, bookmark) now sends you back with the message "Container status opens in a popup. Click the container number in the list to see it." instead of an error page. 3.12.9 2026-09-11 Mobile password reset. Resetting a password on a phone now shows the reset form (with any error message) instead of an error page. 3.12.10 2026-09-12 Stability fixes. Fixed several pages that showed an error page to signed-out visitors. 3.12.11 – 3.12.13 2026-09-12 to 2026-09-15 Maintenance. 3.12.14 2026-09-15 Broken icons fixed. The inline-edit loading spinner, the icons in the container number search, and the admin header background image now load correctly. 3.12.15 2026-09-15 Zone rates fixed. Editing a zone rate and enabling or disabling a zone on the Zones page work again (they showed an error). See Zones & Cities. 3.12.16 2026-09-15 Maintenance. 3.12.17 2026-09-16 Getting Started checklist. Admins and Managers get a setup checklist that checks the system and shows, step by step, what is still missing before you can raise a correct first invoice (zone prices, cities in zones, terminal fees, tax numbers, fuel surcharge, and so on). Exactly one step is marked Do this next. For Admins and Managers the side menu shows a Getting started item (Setup check on an account that already invoices, Setup complete when every step is done). Also in this release: users allowed to change rates can edit a terminal's default rate in place on the Terminals list, and the Cities list has a Shipping filter for cities where at least one order has been delivered. See Setup Checklist. 3.12.18 2026-09-16 Maintenance. 3.12.19 2026-09-17 Current version. Maintenance.

docs.text:
Freight

Version Date Change 3.11.1 – 3.11.5 2026-04-12 to 2026-04-13 Search fixes. Removing a filter chip while a search is active now does what you expect (the × no longer appears to do nothing, and removing a status chip no longer jumps back to the in-progress list). 3.11.6 2026-04-15 Search links and sorting. Links that open a search on the Orders page (after duplicating or creating an order, and from container tracking and alert pages) open the matching search result again instead of the default list. Freshly duplicated orders appear at the top. 3.11.8 2026-05-08 Dispatch shows all container status buttons' orders. The Dispatch page now includes New orders that have any of the container statuses on its filter buttons (Pre-Pull, Dropped / Empty / Full at customer, Empty / Full at yard, Empty / Full at Eco, Inbound), even when they have no dates yet. Previously only Pre-Pull, Empty at yard and Full at yard were included. See Dispatch. 3.11.9 2026-05-08 Cleaner order history. The order History no longer shows internal system entries. 3.11.10 2026-05-12 Changes to website pages and document types now show immediately, instead of only after the next update of the app. 3.11.17 2026-05-21 List page sizes. Lists whose page size is set above 30 rows now actually use it; for example Shipper / Receiver now shows 50 rows per page instead of 30. Orders and Customers stay at 30 per page. 3.11.18 2026-05-21 Copy container number. A copy icon () beside the container number on the Dispatch and Orders rows copies the plain number to the clipboard, so it pastes as text (not as a link) into chat apps and email. 3.11.19 2026-05-26 Invoice search fixed. Searching invoices (by container number or company name) no longer shows an error. 3.11.20 2026-06-16 Equipment notes and new statuses. Equipment has a new Notes field, shown as a column on the Equipment list, editable inline and on the edit form, and included in the CSV export. Two new equipment statuses: Parked at SAAQ and Expired; both count as out of service. The note of a chassis is shown in the Assign Equipment window so dispatchers see it when picking a chassis. See Equipment. 3.11.21 – 3.11.22 2026-06-19 Standard Aged Receivables fixes. The Standard Aged Receivables report (Reports Aged Receivables (AR)) now correctly reconstructs what was outstanding on a past as-of date (it previously showed nothing for invoices that were open then but have since been paid), and loads quickly for offices with very large invoice histories. See Aged Receivables. 3.11.27 2026-08-04 Select All in the invoice order picker. On the new and edit invoice forms, a Select All / Deselect All button above the order list selects the orders the current filter shows, with a counter of how many are selected. On the edit form, Deselect All asks for confirmation before clearing orders already on the invoice. See Creating Invoices. 3.11.28 2026-08-17 Invoice save no longer fails silently. Saving an invoice that includes an order with incomplete data (for example a blank container number) used to do nothing, with no error. The invoice now saves. Select All is now disabled, with an explanation, until a company is chosen, so it can no longer put several companies' orders on one invoice. 3.11.29 2026-08-18 Invoice counters restored. The invoice list again shows each invoice's total and order count, and moving an order off an invoice correctly lowers that invoice's total. 3.11.30 2026-08-18 Order row actions report rejected saves. Reset, go back one step, remove signature and change equipment on the Orders and Dispatch rows now show a red Order not updated! message with the reason when the order cannot be saved, and the row keeps its real status. Previously they showed success while nothing was saved.

Garage add-on

Version Date Change 3.11.7 2026-04-30 Customer-aware equipment selector and quick create. On the work order form, the equipment search lists the selected customer's equipment as soon as you click in it, and each result shows its owner. The + button opens Quick Create Equipment so you can add a vehicle without leaving the form; it is linked to the work order's customer. The chosen equipment shows as a chip with a Change button. 3.11.11 2026-05-16 One invoice for several work orders. Use Bundle with Other Work Orders (or Bundle with others in the row menu) to put several work orders of the same customer on one invoice; each work order's completion date appears on the invoice. Also: an optional Accountant Email on garage customers, CC'd on invoice and work summary emails, and a grouped row-actions menu (View, Move to, Actions) on the Work Orders list. See Garage Invoices. 3.11.12 2026-05-16 Garage invoice and work summary emails are sent from your company's accountant email address, which fixes delivery failures on some mail servers. 3.11.13 – 3.11.14 2026-05-16 to 2026-05-18 Email confirmations list all recipients. The confirmation before sending an invoice or work summary, and the message after sending, list every recipient, including the accountant CC. 3.11.23 2026-06-20 Customer statement of account. Reports Customer Statement shows a customer's unpaid invoices split into Overdue and Not Yet Due, with Print / PDF, an Email to button, Send Test Email, and Automatic Statement Emails (weekly or monthly). The confirmation dialogs on statement and work summary emails now appear before sending, and a failed send is reported. See Garage Reports. 3.11.24 2026-07-24 Pre-tax discount and Reopen. An invoice can carry one Discount, a percentage or a dollar amount, applied before taxes. A Sent invoice with no payments can be returned to Draft with Reopen to Edit, so you no longer have to void it to fix it. 3.11.25 2026-07-24 P/O number on work orders. Work orders have a P/O Number field. It shows on the work order, the estimate print, and in each work order's header on the invoice (page, print and email).

Not listed

Patch releases not listed above (3.11.15, 3.11.16, 3.11.26 and 3.11.31) contain internal or maintenance changes only.

docs.title: Charge Types, Expense Types & Taxes
docs.text: Set up the lists that price your orders, record your costs and tax your invoices: Charge Types, Expense Types and Manage Taxes.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
These three lists are master data. You set them up once, then pick from them every day on orders and invoices.

  • Charge Types (page title Order Charges) are the extra charges you bill, such as chassis or waiting time, plus the costs you track as Expense charge types. Income charge types are added to an order's total, so they end up on the invoice.
  • One charge type can be marked as the Terminal Fee. The app uses it to add the terminal's rate to Import and Export orders automatically.
  • With the Fuel Surcharge add-on, the monthly fuel rates are also charge types, but they are managed on the Fuel Schedule page and hidden from the Charge Types list.
  • Expense Types (page title Expense Categories) are the "who did we pay" entries for costs that are not a driver or a broker. They appear in the Other Expense group of an order's expense rows.
  • Manage Taxes holds your GST and QST percentages. You choose a tax on each invoice, and the app adds GST and QST to the invoice subtotal.
  • Taxes are shared with Garage. Garage > Taxes edits the same tax records.
  • Every change to a charge type, expense type or tax is recorded and can be viewed with View History.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
1. Click your name in the top menu Charge Types.
  2. Click Edit in the Actions menu of each charge type you bill for and enter your own Default Rate. Uncheck Active on the ones you never use.
  3. Make sure one charge type has Use as default for set to Terminal Fee if you charge terminal fees.
  4. Click your name Expense Types and add the non-driver costs you pay (for example tolls or repairs).
  5. Click your name Manage Taxes and check that the GST and QST percentages are right.

Setup checklist

The setup checklist has a Check your charge types step that sends you to this page. See Check your charge types.

docs.title: Access & Permissions
docs.text:
Role Charge Types Expense Types Manage Taxes Admin Full access Full access Full access Manager Full access Full access Full access Accountant Full access Full access Full access Warehouse Full access No access No access Dispatch Only with Can manage rates? Only with Can manage rates? No access All other roles (Customer, Driver, Garage and others) No access No access No access

Can manage rates? is a checkbox on the dispatcher's profile. See People & Invitations.

How to get there:

  • Click your name at the top of the screen to open the user menu. Charge Types, Expense Types and Manage Taxes are grouped together near the bottom, after the Manage … items. Each item only appears if your role allows it.
  • With the Warehouse add-on, Warehouse > Charges in the left menu opens the Charge Types page already filtered to Warehouse.
  • With the Fuel Surcharge add-on, the Charge Types page has a Back to Fuel Schedule button.

Garage users and taxes

Garage users do not see Manage Taxes, but anyone who can open Garage (Admin, Manager and Garage users, when the Garage add-on is on) can edit taxes from Garage > Taxes. See Taxes are shared with Garage.

docs.title: Charge Types
docs.text: The page opens with the title Order Charges and the subtitle Management of Order Charges.

docs.title: Filters
docs.text:
The buttons at the top of the list filter what you see. The page opens on All Active.

Button Shows All Active Active charge types only. Disabled Charge types whose Active box is unchecked. Warehouse Warehouse charge types, active and disabled. Only shown with the Warehouse add-on. Intermodal Intermodal charge types, active and disabled. Only shown with the Warehouse add-on.

The list is sorted by name and shows 50 charge types per page.

Fuel surcharge rows are hidden when the add-on is on

With the Fuel Surcharge add-on, the monthly fuel rates (charge types used as Fuel Surcharge) are left out of this list. Manage them on the Fuel Schedule page instead. See Fuel Surcharge. Without the add-on, any existing fuel surcharge rows are listed here like any other charge type.

docs.title: Columns
docs.text: Column What It Shows ID The charge type's number. (icon) A ship icon for Intermodal charge types, a warehouse icon for the others. Name Green when the charge type is active, red when it is disabled. Service The service the charge type belongs to, for example Intermodal or Warehouse. Type Income or Expense. Default Rate The default amount, shown in dollars. Rate Type The Value Type: Fixed or Monthly. Use For Terminal Fee or Fuel Surcharge in green, or not set. Effective Period The month the charge applies to (for example Mar 2026), when one is set, or not set. Fuel surcharge rows show the date as Week of date. Active Whether the charge type is active. (Actions) Edit and View History.

docs.title: Adding or editing a charge type
docs.text:
1. Open Charge Types from the user menu.
  2. Click Add a new Order Charge at the top right, or open the Actions menu on a row and click Edit.
  3. Fill in the Order Charge Information form (see the table below).
  4. Click Save. Cancel returns to the list without saving.
Field What It Does Name The name shown in the order dropdowns and on the invoice breakdown. Required. Charge Type Income: billed to the customer, listed under Additional Charges on the order. Expense: a cost to you, listed in the expense type dropdown of Order Expenses. Default Rate The amount copied onto the order when the charge type is picked. Required and must be a number. You can still change the amount on each order. Value Type Fixed or Monthly. Used by warehouse orders: a Fixed charge is added once, a Monthly charge is multiplied, for each product line, by the square footage of its unit of measure, its quantity and the number of calendar months in storage (the storage month and the closing month both count). Service Intermodal charge types are offered on freight orders. Warehouse charge types are offered on warehouse orders (Warehouse add-on only). Office The office the charge type belongs to. Lists the offices you have access to. The Charge Types page only lists the charge types of the office you are working in. Use as default for Leave blank for a normal charge. Choose Terminal Fee to use this charge type for the automatic terminal fee. With the Fuel Surcharge add-on, Fuel Surcharge is also listed. Applicable on (Month) Only shown with the Fuel Surcharge add-on. The month a fuel surcharge rate applies to. Use the Fuel Schedule page to set fuel rates rather than this field. Active Uncheck to disable the charge type.

Charge types cannot be deleted

There is no Delete option for charge types. To stop using one, edit it and uncheck Active. Existing orders that used it keep their charges.

docs.title: How charge types feed orders and invoices
docs.text:
• Additional Charges. On the order form, Order Charges for Invoice Breakdown > Additional Charges lists your Income charge types for the Intermodal service, written as Name (rate$). Picking one copies its Default Rate into the amount. See Order Charges & Expenses.
  • Order total. The order total is the base rate plus all its order charges. The invoice subtotal is the sum of its orders' totals, so every income charge ends up on the invoice. See Invoices.
  • Order Expenses. The second dropdown of each expense row lists your Expense charge types. Picking one copies its default rate into Rate. Expenses never change the order total or the invoice.
  • Warehouse orders. The warehouse order charges list your Income charge types for the Warehouse service. When the customer has its own rate for a charge type (Custom rates for this customer on the customer, Warehouse group), the dropdown shows that rate. See Warehouse Orders.

Disabling a charge type

Unchecking Active moves the charge type to the Disabled filter, takes it out of the setup checklist count and removes it from the Warehouse group of a customer's custom rates.

docs.title: The Terminal Fee default
docs.text:
Set Use as default for to Terminal Fee on the charge type you bill terminal fees with. When an Import or Export order that is not Completed and not invoiced is created, and each time it is saved from the order form, the app:

  1. Finds the charge type marked Terminal Fee.
  2. Takes the rate of the order's terminal (the pick up terminal for Import, the return terminal for Export), or the customer's custom rate for that terminal if one exists.
  3. If that rate is $1 or more, replaces any existing Terminal Fee charge on the order with one charge at that rate, with the note Computed Terminal Fee. Rates below $1 are ignored.

The Default Rate of the Terminal Fee charge type itself is not used for this. The amount always comes from the terminal or the customer's custom terminal rate. See Managing Terminals.

Keep exactly one Terminal Fee charge type

If no charge type is marked Terminal Fee, no terminal fee is ever added. If several are marked, only one of them is used. Keep a single one.

docs.title: The Fuel Surcharge default
docs.text:
Charge types with Use as default for set to Fuel Surcharge are the monthly fuel rates. Their rate is a percentage of the order's base rate, not a dollar amount, and must be greater than 0 and at most 100. When the rate changes, the name is updated automatically to Fuel Surcharge N%.

With the Fuel Surcharge add-on, these records are created and edited from the Fuel Schedule page and do not appear in the Charge Types list. See Fuel Surcharge.

docs.title: Expense Types
docs.text:
The page opens with the title Expense Categories and the subtitle Management of Expense Categories.

Expense types are the payees for order costs that are not a driver or a broker, such as tolls, repairs or a subcontractor.

docs.title: Columns
docs.text:
Column What It Shows Name The expense type's name. Charges Count How many expense lines use this expense type. Active Whether the expense type is active. (Actions) Edit, View History and, when Charges Count is 0, Delete.

There are no filter buttons on this page.

docs.title: Adding or editing an expense type
docs.text:
1. Open Expense Types from the user menu.
  2. Click Add a new Expense Category, or open the Actions menu on a row and click Edit.
  3. Fill in the Expense Category Information form.
  4. Click Save.
Field What It Does Name The name shown in the payee dropdown. Required. Office The office the expense type belongs to. Hint: Office for which this expense applies. Active Hint: Only active expenses will be visible for new orders.

docs.title: Deleting an expense type
docs.text: Delete only appears in the Actions menu when Charges Count is 0. Click it and confirm Are you sure?. An expense type that has been used on an order cannot be deleted.

docs.title: Where expense types appear
docs.text:
• Order Expenses. The first dropdown (the payee) of each expense row is grouped into Driver, Broker and Other Expense. Your expense types are the Other Expense group. See Order Charges & Expenses.
  • Expenses page. The Select a filter dropdown lets you filter expense lines by one expense type. See Expenses & Checks.

Expense Types vs Expense charge types

An expense type says who you paid (the payee). An Expense charge type (Charge Types page, Charge Type = Expense) says what the cost was and can pre-fill its amount. An expense row can use both.

docs.title: Manage Taxes
docs.text: The page opens with the title Taxes. Each tax holds a GST percentage and a QST percentage.

docs.title: Columns
docs.text: Column What It Shows Name The tax name, shown in the invoice's tax dropdown. Gst The GST (federal) percentage. Qst The QST (provincial) percentage. Invoices How many freight invoices use this tax. Active Whether the tax is active. (Actions) Edit, View History and, when Invoices is 0, Delete.

docs.title: Adding or editing a tax
docs.text:
1. Open Manage Taxes from the user menu.
  2. Click Add a new Tax, or open the Actions menu on a row and click Edit.
  3. Fill in the Tax Information form.
  4. Click Save.
Field What It Does Name The name shown in the invoice's tax dropdown. Office The office the tax belongs to. GST The federal tax percentage. Enter 5 for 5%. QST The provincial tax percentage. Enter 9.975 for 9.975%. Enter 0 if you do not charge a provincial tax. Active Used by Garage (see below).

docs.title: How taxes are applied to freight invoices
docs.text:
1. On the invoice form, choose the tax in the Tax dropdown. It lists your office's taxes.
  2. The app calculates GST as the invoice subtotal × the GST % and QST as the subtotal × the QST %, each rounded to the cent (QST is only rounded on invoices dated December 1, 2022 or later).
  3. The invoice total is the subtotal plus GST plus QST. With no tax selected, no tax is added.

The printed invoice shows the lines GST (rate%) and QST (rate%), using the percentages of the chosen tax. See Creating Invoices.

Changing a percentage changes existing invoices

Freight invoices store which tax they use, not the amount. If you edit the GST or QST % of a tax that is already on invoices, those invoices are recalculated with the new percentage. When a rate changes, create a new tax with the new percentages and use it on new invoices, and leave the old one as it is.

GST/QST numbers are elsewhere

Your GST and QST registration numbers printed on invoices are set in Settings, not here. See Application Settings.

docs.title: Deleting a tax
docs.text:
• Delete only appears in the Actions menu when the Invoices column is 0 (no freight invoice uses the tax).
  • If the Garage add-on is on and a garage invoice uses the tax, deleting is refused with the message Cannot delete — used by N garage invoices. (garage invoice when N is 1).

docs.title: Taxes are shared with Garage
docs.text:
Manage Taxes and Garage > Taxes (page title Tax Rates) show and edit the same tax records. A change made on one page applies to both freight and garage invoices. Manage Taxes lists only the taxes of the office you are working in, while Garage > Taxes lists the taxes of every office.

Manage Taxes (freight) Garage > Taxes Who can open it Admin, Manager, Accountant Anyone with Garage access (Admin, Manager, Garage) Invoices column counts Freight invoices Garage invoices Delete is allowed when No freight invoice uses it (and no garage invoice, with the Garage add-on) No garage invoice and no freight invoice uses it Active No effect on the freight Tax dropdown Only active taxes are offered on garage invoices, and work orders use the office's first active tax

See Garage Settings & Taxes.

docs.title: The Check your charge types setup step
docs.text:
The setup checklist's Check your charge types step (stage What appears on your invoice) exists because new systems come with pre-filled charge types, such as waiting time, chassis detention and storage, at guessed prices.

  • The Open Charge Types button opens this page.
  • The step is done when at least one active charge type has been edited since setup (saved more than a minute after it was created), or someone clicked Looks right to me.
  • It counts active charge types only and never counts fuel surcharge rows, so editing a fuel rate does not complete it.
  • What we found reads, for example, 12 charges, 2 changed since setup, 12 charges, none changed since setup or 12 charges, confirmed as they are.

See Setup Checklist.

docs.title: I can't see Charge Types, Expense Types or Manage Taxes in my menu
docs.text:
Solution

These items are in the user menu (click your name), not in the left menu or Settings. Dispatchers need Can manage rates? on their profile for Charge Types and Expense Types, and cannot open Manage Taxes. Warehouse users only see Charge Types. See the Access & Permissions table.

docs.title: My fuel surcharge charge types are missing from the list
docs.text:
Solution

With the Fuel Surcharge add-on, fuel rates are hidden from the Charge Types page. Click Back to Fuel Schedule and manage them there. See Fuel Surcharge.

docs.title: There is no Delete option for a charge type
docs.text:
Solution

Charge types cannot be deleted. Edit the charge type and uncheck Active instead.

docs.title: I can't delete an expense type or a tax
docs.text:
Solution

An expense type can only be deleted when its Charges Count is 0. A tax can only be deleted when no invoice uses it. Uncheck Active instead, or leave it as it is.

docs.title: No terminal fee is added to my orders
docs.text:
Solution

One charge type must have Use as default for = Terminal Fee, and the order's terminal (or the customer's custom terminal rate) must have a rate of at least $1. The fee is only added to Import and Export orders that are not Completed or invoiced, when the order is created or saved from the order form. See Managing Terminals.

docs.title: Old invoices show a different tax amount after I edited a tax
docs.text:
Solution

Freight invoices recalculate GST and QST from the tax they point to. Put the old percentages back on that tax, then create a new tax for the new rate and use it on new invoices.

Best Practices

  • Review every pre-filled charge type and put your own price on the ones you bill for.
  • Keep exactly one charge type marked Terminal Fee.
  • Use clear names: the charge type name is what your customer sees on the invoice breakdown.
  • Create a new tax when a rate changes instead of editing the one already used on invoices.
  • Add an expense type for each regular non-driver cost and record those costs as expense rows on the order, so the Order Sales / Profit report (which subtracts every expense row from the order total) shows real margins.

docs.title: Container Alerts & Integration Health
docs.text: One page that lists what changed at the terminals for your tracked containers, which Last Free Days are coming up, and whether each terminal feed is working.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The Container Alerts page (header: Container Alerts — Container Tracking & Status Alerts) is part of the Container Tracking add-on. Every 10 minutes the system pulls data from CN Rail, Termont and MGT (Racine/Cast). When a container's status changes, it creates an alert. You do not need to refresh anything or check each terminal yourself.

  • Integration Health — one card for each terminal source you have. The card shows whether the last data pull worked.
  • Six summary cards — Unread, LFD Approaching, Ready for Pickup, Customs Released, Departed and All. Click a card to filter the alert list.
  • Upcoming Last Free Days (Next 7 Days) — every tracked container whose LFD is between today and 7 days from now.
  • Alerts list — alerts from the last 90 days, newest first, with a NEW badge on unread ones.
  • Daily digest email — the users you choose get an email listing the new alerts.

There are four alert types:

Alert type Badge in the list What it means Pickup Ready Green Pickup Ready The container is off the train (CN) or available for pickup at the terminal (Termont / MGT). You can dispatch a driver. Customs Released Blue Customs Released Customs has released the container. LFD Approaching Orange LFD Approaching The Last Free Day is today, tomorrow or the day after. Schedule the pickup to avoid demurrage. Departed Gray Departed The container has left the terminal. No further action needed.

See Container Tracking for the tracking add-on itself and the tracking modal.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
1. Go to Dispatch and click the Alerts button in the header. The red badge on it is the number of unread alerts.
  2. Check the Integration Health cards. Green means the data is fresh.
  3. Look at Upcoming Last Free Days (Next 7 Days). Red and yellow rows need a pickup soon.
  4. Click a summary card (for example Ready for Pickup) to filter the alert list.
  5. Click a container number to open its tracking details, or click the order number to find the order.
  6. If you are an Admin, click Mark All Read when you have gone through the list.

docs.title: Access & Permissions
docs.text:
The page only exists when at least one Container Tracking add-on (CN, Port of Montreal / Termont, or MGT Racine/Cast) is enabled. Without one, opening the page sends you back to the home page with the message Container tracking is not enabled.

Role Access Admin Views the page. Can use Mark All Read and the per-alert read / unread toggle. Manages Alert Email Subscriptions in Settings. Manager, Dispatch, Customer Service Views the page (reached from the Dispatch header). Cannot mark alerts read or unread. Other signed-in users Can open the page from a link (for example the digest email). Cannot mark alerts read or unread.

How to get there:

  • From Dispatch: click Dispatch in the left menu, then the Alerts button in the header (shown when any tracking add-on is enabled). See Dispatch.
  • From the digest email: click View Alerts Dashboard at the bottom of the email.

No Container Tracking menu

There is no Container Tracking or Alerts item in the left menu. Use the Alerts button on the Dispatch page or the link in the digest email.

To go back, click Back to Dispatch in the top right of the page.

docs.title: Integration Health
docs.text: At the top of the page, under Integration Health, there is one card for each tracking source enabled on your account: CN Rail, Termont and/or MGT (Racine/Cast). Each card has a colored left border.

docs.title: Card color
docs.text: Color Meaning Green Healthy. The last pull ran less than 30 minutes ago and the terminal returned at least one container. Orange The last pull ran less than 30 minutes ago and asked about containers, but the terminal returned none. Usually a problem on the terminal side. Red The last pull failed (ERROR label), has not run for more than 1 hour, or has never run. Gray None of the above. For example, the last pull was between 30 and 60 minutes ago, or it had no containers to ask about.

docs.title: Card details
docs.text:
When the source has run at least once, the card shows two bars and the time of the last pull:

Line What it shows Discovery found / submitted (percent) — of the containers the system asked the terminal about, how many the terminal returned. Synced updated / found (percent) — of the containers the terminal returned, how many were saved in UTX Freight. Last pull: … ago How long ago the last pull ran.

Labels that can appear on a card:

  • Never run (red text) — the source has never been pulled.
  • ERROR (red label) — the last pull failed.
  • No API results (orange label) — the last pull asked about containers and got nothing back.

Red or orange card = data may be out of date

While a card is red or orange, statuses, LFDs and alerts for that source may be old. Alerts for that source will not appear until pulls work again. Contact UTX support if a card stays red.

The Integration Health cards do not update on their own. Reload the page to see the latest values.

docs.title: Summary Cards
docs.text:
Below Integration Health there are six cards. Click a card to filter the alert list below it.

Card Color What the number counts Filter when clicked Unread Red All unread alerts, from any date, including alerts whose order is no longer in progress Unread alerts LFD Approaching Orange Containers in the Upcoming Last Free Days table (LFD between today and 7 days from now). This is a count of containers, not alerts. LFD Approaching alerts Ready for Pickup Green Pickup Ready alerts created in the last 7 days Pickup Ready alerts Customs Released Blue Customs Released alerts created in the last 7 days Customs Released alerts Departed Gray Departed alerts created in the last 7 days Departed alerts All Default (no color) The total of the five cards above All alerts (no filter)

The card number and the list can differ

The cards use different rules from the list. For example, Ready for Pickup counts the last 7 days, but its filtered list shows the last 90 days. LFD Approaching counts containers, but its list shows LFD alerts. The cards also count alerts whose order is no longer in progress (for example Completed), which the list hides.

With multiple offices, the alert cards count alerts for orders in your current office plus alerts with no order. The LFD Approaching card and the Upcoming LFD table are not limited to an office.

docs.title: Upcoming Last Free Days
docs.text:
The table Upcoming Last Free Days (Next 7 Days) lists every tracked container (CN Rail, Termont, MGT) whose Last Free Day is from today up to 7 days from now, sorted by LFD. The table is hidden when there are none.

Past LFDs are never listed

A container drops out of this table the day after its LFD. The table does not show containers whose LFD has already passed.

Column What it shows Source CN Rail, Termont or MGT (Racine/Cast) Container The container number. If an in-progress order (New, App. Taken or Dispatched) has this container, the number is a link () that opens the container's tracking details. Shipping Line The shipping line from the terminal. Empty for CN Rail containers, because CN does not send it. Terminal The terminal section Last Free Day The date, for example Oct 14, 2026 Days Left A badge (see below) Status Green Ready when the terminal says the container is available for pickup. Otherwise the terminal's visit state, or Unknown.

Days Left badges and row colors:

Days left Badge Row color LFD is today Red EXPIRED Red LFD is tomorrow Yellow TOMORROW Yellow LFD is in 2 days Gray 2 days Yellow LFD is in 3 to 7 days Gray N days (for example 5 days) No color

EXPIRED means today

Because past LFDs are not listed, an EXPIRED badge always means the LFD is today. Pick the container up today to avoid demurrage.

Check the Status column

The table lists containers by Last Free Day, including containers that have already left the terminal. Check the Status column before dispatching a driver.

docs.title: The Alerts List
docs.text: The list title is All Alerts. When you click a summary card, the title changes to show which filter is on (for example Unread Alerts). Click All to clear the filter.

docs.title: Which alerts are listed
docs.text:
• Last 90 days by default. Click Show all time (top right of the list) to see older alerts. Click Last 90 days to go back.
  • In-progress orders only. An alert linked to an order is listed only while that order is New, App. Taken or Dispatched. When the order moves to any other status (for example Completed), its alerts disappear from the list. Alerts not linked to any order are always listed.
  • Current office. With multiple offices, you see alerts for orders in the office you are working in, plus alerts with no order.
  • Newest first, 25 per page. Use the page links under the list to see more.

If nothing matches, the list shows No alerts found.

docs.title: Columns
docs.text: Column What it shows (icon) An icon for the alert type Source CN Rail, Termont or MGT (Racine/Cast) Container The container number. A red NEW badge means the alert is unread. When the alert has an order, the number is a link () that opens the container's tracking details on this page. Type Pickup Ready, Customs Released, LFD Approaching or Departed Message The alert message (see Alert Rules and Messages) Order The order's reference number, or N/A when no order is linked. The link opens the Orders page in a new tab, searched on that reference number. When The date and time the alert was created (eye) The read / unread toggle (Admin only, see below)

docs.title: How an alert is linked to an order
docs.text: When the alert is created, the system looks for an in-progress order (New, App. Taken or Dispatched) with the same container number. If it finds one, the alert is linked to that order. If not, the alert has no order (N/A). For Pickup Ready, Customs Released and Departed alerts, the order must also have been created on or after the Order Archive Cutoff Date in Application Settings (when that date is set). The link is set once, when the alert is created. Adding the container to an order later does not link existing alerts.

docs.title: Auto-refresh
docs.text: While the page is open, the summary cards and the alerts list refresh every 60 seconds without reloading the page. The refresh pauses while the browser tab is hidden. The Integration Health cards and the Upcoming LFD table only update when you reload the page.

docs.title: Read and Unread
docs.text:
Unread alerts are shown in bold with a red NEW badge.

Action Who What it does Mark All Read (top right) Admin only Marks every unread alert as read, for all sources, all offices and all dates, not only what is on screen. Shows All alerts marked as read. / eye icon (last column) Admin only Switches one alert between read and unread. The green eye means Mark as read. The gray crossed eye means Mark as unread. The Unread card updates right away. Opening Port Tracking on Dispatch Anyone who opens it The Port Tracking window shows up to the 10 newest unread Termont and MGT alerts in an alerts panel, and marks those alerts as read. CN alerts are not affected.

Read status is shared by everyone

An alert is read or unread for the whole company, not per user and not per office. When one person marks alerts read (or opens Port Tracking), they are read for every user in every office. The Alerts badge on Dispatch also counts unread alerts for all offices.

Marking read does not delete

Read alerts stay in the list. Only the bold text and the NEW badge go away.

Only Admins can change read status. Other users see the alerts but cannot mark them read or unread.

docs.title: Alert Rules and Messages
docs.text: Alerts are created by the tracking pull that runs every 10 minutes. An alert is created only when a value changes to the new state since the last pull (or the first time the system sees the container already in that state). The same alert is not created again on later pulls while the value stays the same.

docs.title: CN Rail
docs.text:
Alert Created when Message Pickup Ready The CN status shows the container as De-ramped Container <number> has been de-ramped and is available for pickup at CN Customs Released The terminal reports the container as released by customs Customs released for container <number> Departed The visit state becomes Completed Container <number> has departed CN terminal

After a CN container's visit state is Departed or Completed, no more status alerts are created for it.

docs.title: Termont and MGT (Racine/Cast)
docs.text:
Alert Created when Message Pickup Ready The terminal shows the container as available for pickup Container <number> is now available for pickup Customs Released The terminal reports the container as released by customs Customs released for container <number> Departed The visit state becomes Departed Container <number> has departed the terminal

After the terminal reports the container as out of the terminal, no more status alerts are created for it.

docs.title: LFD Approaching (all sources)
docs.text:
After each pull, the system checks every tracked container (CN Rail, Termont and MGT) whose Last Free Day is today, tomorrow or the day after.

  • It creates an LFD Approaching alert if that container has not had one in the last 24 hours.
  • So the alert repeats about once a day: up to 3 times (2 days before, 1 day before, and on the LFD itself).
  • It never fires after the LFD. Once the date has passed, no more LFD alerts are created for that container.
  • The 24-hour check is by container number, across all sources.

Message: Last Free Day for <number> is in <N> days (<Mon DD, YYYY>). It says 1 day when the LFD is tomorrow and 0 days when it is today. Example: Last Free Day for ABCU1234567 is in 2 days (Oct 14, 2026).

Alerts are created for every tracked container

Alerts are created even when no in-progress order has the container. Those alerts show N/A in the Order column.

docs.title: Alert Email Subscriptions and the Daily Digest
Choosing who gets the email
docs.text:
Only Admins can do this, and only when a Container Tracking add-on is enabled.

  1. Open Your Name Settings.
  2. Find the Alert Email Subscriptions box, section Container Tracking Alerts.
  3. Pick a person in — Select a user —. The list shows active users of your own company (the company that owns the UTX Freight account) who are not subscribed yet. Customers' users are not listed.
  4. Click Add Subscriber.

The subscriber table shows Name, Email and Role. With no subscribers, the box says No subscribers yet. Add users from the dropdown above. To stop the email for someone, click Remove on their row and confirm Remove from alerts?.

When the add-on is enabled, the people list of a company also has an Alerts column that shows who is subscribed.

docs.title: The digest email
docs.text:
Once a day, the system sends one email to each subscriber.

  • Subject: Container Tracking — N alerts (1 alert when there is one).
  • From: your company name and the Admin Email address from Application Settings.
  • Title: Container Tracking Alerts, then Summary for — N alerts.
  • ⚠ Action Required (N) — the Pickup Ready alerts (shown as Ready for Pickup) and LFD Approaching alerts, with container, source and order number. This box only appears when there is at least one.
  • One section per alert type, titled Pickup Available, Customs Released, Departed or LFD Approaching with the count in brackets. Each has a table: Container, Source, Message, Order, Time. The Order column shows the order's reference number, or — when no order is linked.
  • With multiple offices, the email is split by office, each with its own Action Required box and type sections. Alerts with no order are under Unassigned.
  • View Alerts Dashboard button — opens the Container Alerts page.
  • Footer: This notification is sent automatically by your company name.

What goes in the email:

  • Every alert that has not been emailed yet, from all sources and all offices. Each subscriber gets the same full list.
  • Each alert is emailed only once. After a digest is sent, its alerts are not included again.
  • If there are no new alerts, no email is sent.
  • If the email fails for every subscriber, the alerts are kept and sent with the next digest. If it reaches at least one subscriber, the alerts count as sent.
  • Read status does not matter. An alert already marked read in the app is still included if it was not emailed yet.

First digest after adding subscribers can be long

Alerts are only marked as emailed when a digest is actually sent. If nobody was subscribed for a while, the first digest includes all the alerts created since then.

docs.title: Other Things on the Page
docs.text:
• Help box — click How do container alerts work? at the top to expand a short guide to alert types, terminal sources, the dashboard and the colors.
  • All clear — when every card is 0, there are no upcoming LFDs and every Integration Health card is green, the page shows All clear! No container alerts right now. A source that has never run (Never run) is ignored in this check.
  • Office name — with multiple offices, the current office name is shown next to the page subtitle.

docs.title: I can't find Container Alerts in the menu
docs.text:
Solution

There is no menu item. Go to Dispatch and click the Alerts button in the header. If the button is missing, no Container Tracking add-on is enabled on your account. Contact UTX support.

docs.title: I can't mark alerts as read
docs.text:
Solution

Only Admins can use Mark All Read and the eye icon. Ask an Admin to mark the alerts as read.

docs.title: Alerts disappeared from the list
docs.text:
Solution

The list hides alerts older than 90 days (click Show all time) and alerts whose order is no longer New, App. Taken or Dispatched. With multiple offices, check that you are in the right office.

docs.title: A container with an expired LFD is not in the Upcoming LFD table
docs.text:
Solution

The table only shows LFDs from today to 7 days ahead. Once the LFD has passed, the container leaves the table. Check the order or its tracking details instead.

docs.title: I get the same LFD alert several days in a row
docs.text:
Solution

That is expected. The LFD Approaching alert repeats about once a day while the LFD is 2 days away, 1 day away and today. It stops after the LFD.

docs.title: No alerts are coming in
docs.text:
Solution

Check the Integration Health cards. Red means the pull failed, is more than 1 hour late, or never ran. Orange means the terminal returned no data. Gray can mean the last pull is 30–60 minutes old. Contact UTX support if a card stays red or orange.

docs.title: Someone is not receiving the digest
docs.text:
Solution

An Admin should check Settings Alert Email Subscriptions. Only users of your own company can be added. No email is sent on days with no new alerts.

docs.title: "User is already subscribed to this alert type" when adding a subscriber
docs.text:
Solution

A Subscription Error popup with this message means the user is already on the list. Check the subscriber table in Alert Email Subscriptions.

Best Practices

  • Open the Alerts page from Dispatch at the start of each shift and work through Upcoming Last Free Days first.
  • Have an Admin click Mark All Read once the team has reviewed the list, so the Alerts badge on Dispatch only counts new items. Remember this is shared by everyone.
  • Subscribe at least one dispatcher to the digest so pickups and LFDs are not missed when nobody is logged in.
  • If an Integration Health card is not green, do not rely on that source's alerts until it is fixed.

docs.title: Container Statuses
docs.text: Manage the list of container statuses (such as Arrived - Awaiting delivery, Full at yard or Returned to terminal) that you set on intermodal orders to track where each container is.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
A container status is a short label that says where the container on an order is right now. It is separate from the order status (New, App. Made, Dispatched, Completed).

  • The Container Statuses page (Manage and reference all container statuses.) lists every status available in your account.
  • Built-in statuses come with UTX Freight. They cannot be edited or deleted.
  • Custom statuses are the ones your company adds. You choose the name, the colour and which order types they apply to. You can edit or delete them at any time.
  • Each status has a colour. Orders and Dispatch show the status (and the chassis number) in that colour, so you can scan the list at a glance.
  • Job Type Configuration records which order types (Import, Export, Transfer and so on) a status is meant for, with a short description for each.
  • Some statuses are set automatically by the driver app and the yard app, for example Dropped at customer when a driver captures a delivery signature on an import.
  • Every change to a custom status is recorded and can be viewed with View History.

Intermodal only

Container statuses are part of the intermodal (container) workflow. The Manage Container Statuses menu item, the C.Status column and the yard counters only appear when your account runs in intermodal mode.

Statuses are shared by all offices

The list of container statuses is the same for the whole account. With the Multi-Office add-on, a status created in one office is available in every office.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
1. Click your name in the top menu Manage Container Statuses.
  2. Click New Status at the top right.
  3. Enter the Status Name.
  4. Pick a Color with the colour picker, type a hex code (for example #28a745), or click one of the Quick Color Selection swatches.
  5. Under Job Type Configuration, tick the order types the status applies to and optionally write a description for each.
  6. Click Save.

The status is added to the Custom section of the list. Reload the Orders or Dispatch page and it appears in the container status dropdowns.

docs.title: Access & Permissions
docs.text:
Role Access Level Admin Full access: view, create, edit and delete custom statuses, view history Manager Full access: view, create, edit and delete custom statuses, view history Dispatch View only. Sees the list, colours and job type configuration. There is no New Status button and no Actions column Customer Service View only (same access as Dispatch) Accountant No access to the page All other roles (Customer, Driver, Yard Worker, Warehouse, Garage) No access to the page

Managing statuses vs. setting a status on an order

The permissions above are for managing the list of statuses. Setting the container status on an order is done from the order itself (the C.Status column or the order form) and follows the order permissions. See Where Container Statuses Appear.

How to get there:

  • Click your name at the top of the screen to open the user menu, then click Manage Container Statuses.

Manage Container Statuses is in the user menu with the other Manage … items. It is not inside the Settings page. See Navigation & Account.

docs.title: The Container Statuses List
docs.text: The list shows custom statuses first, sorted by name, then a dashed separator line, then the built-in statuses, also sorted by name.

docs.title: Columns
docs.text:
Column What it shows Status Name The status name in bold. This is the exact text saved on orders. Type A Custom badge (green) or a Built-in badge (blue). Color A small square in the status colour. One column per order type One column for each order type enabled in your account, for example Import, Export, Transfer, Dry van, International export and Warehouse. A green with the description underneath means the status is enabled for that order type. A grey with N/A means it is not. Actions Admin and Manager only. Custom statuses have an Actions dropdown. Built-in statuses have no actions.

Only the order types turned on for your account get a column. If your account does not use Warehouse orders, for example, there is no Warehouse column.

The footer shows the totals: Total: N statuses (X built-in, Y custom).

docs.title: Row Actions
docs.text:
On a custom status, open the Actions dropdown:

Action What it does Edit Opens the Edit Container Status window. See Editing a Custom Status. Delete Asks Are you sure?, then deletes the status. See Deleting a Custom Status. View History Shows the change history of the status: who created or changed it and what changed.

docs.title: Panels below the list
docs.text:
Two information panels sit under the list:

  • Color Legend: a suggested meaning for each common colour (see Color Guide).
  • Automatic Status Changes: the statuses the system can set on its own (see Automatic Status Changes).

docs.title: Built-in Statuses
docs.text:
Built-in statuses are created with your account. They cannot be edited, renamed, recoloured or deleted. Several of them drive app behaviour (driver app steps, yard counters, Dispatch tabs), which is why they are locked.

The table shows each built-in status with its default colour and the order types it is enabled for out of the box.

Status Colour Enabled for Arrived - Awaiting delivery Green #28a745 Import Arrived - Missing customs Red #dc3545 Import Arrived - On hold Red #dc3545 Import At customer Muted grey #6c757d None Driver at terminal Light green #90ee90 Import, Export, Transfer Dropped at customer Red #dc3545 Import, Export, Transfer, Dry Van Empty at customer Yellow #ffc107 Import, Export, Dry Van, International Export Empty at yard Blue #007bff Import, Export, Transfer, Dry Van Export Orange #fd7e14 Export, International Export Full at customer Orange #fd7e14 Export, Dry Van, International Export Full at yard Purple #6f42c1 Import, Export, Transfer, Dry Van Live load Red #dc3545 Import, Export, Dry Van On rail Pink #e91e63 Import, Export, Transfer, International Export On route to customer Yellow #ffc107 Import, Transfer, Dry Van On route to terminal Yellow #ffc107 Import, Export, Transfer, Dry Van, International Export On route to yard Yellow #ffc107 None On vessel Dark blue #003366 Import, Export, International Export Ready for 2nd stop Muted grey #6c757d None Returned to terminal Green #28a745 Import, Export, Transfer, International Export Reused for export Orange #fd7e14 Export

The descriptions for each order type (for example Container has arrived at terminal and is ready for pickup for Arrived - Awaiting delivery on Import) are shown in the list on the page.

Your list may also contain custom statuses set up by UTX

Some accounts already had their own statuses before the status manager existed, for example Pre-Pull, Empty at Eco, Full at Eco or Inbound. These were carried over as Custom statuses (grey, no order types ticked). You can edit them like any other custom status. Be careful renaming them: some names switch on extra Dispatch tabs and counters (see Dispatch tabs).

docs.title: Creating a Custom Status
docs.text:
1. Open Manage Container Statuses.
  2. Click New Status. The New Container Status window opens.
  3. Fill in the fields (see below).
  4. Click Save.

The window closes and Container status 'name' was created successfully. is shown. Click Cancel to close without saving.

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
Field Required Description Status Name Yes The name shown everywhere in the app and saved on the order. It must be unique. Color Yes The colour used to display the status. Use the colour picker on the left, or type a hex code in the format #RRGGBB (a # followed by six characters 0-9 / A-F, for example #17a2b8). The two stay in sync. A new status starts with light grey #cccccc. Quick Color Selection — One-click colour swatches. Hover a swatch to see its name: Green, Light Green, Blue, Yellow/Warning, Red/Danger, Purple, Dark Blue, Orange, Pink, Muted Grey, Dark Grey, Light Grey, Teal/Info, Cyan/Success. Clicking a swatch fills in Color. Job Type Configuration No One checkbox per order type enabled in your account: Import (CI), Export (CX), Transfer (TF), Dry Van (DV), International Export (IX), Warehouse (WH). Tick each order type the status applies to and, optionally, type a description in the box below it (for example Container waiting at the rail yard).

Names must be clearly different

Two names that only differ by case, spaces or punctuation, such as Pre-Pull and pre pull, are treated as the same status, so the second one cannot be saved. Choose a name that is clearly different from every existing status.

What Job Type Configuration does

The ticks and descriptions are shown in the order type columns of the Container Statuses list, so your team knows which statuses to use for which kind of order. They do not hide a status from any dropdown: every status, built-in and custom, is offered on every order that has a container status field.

docs.title: Editing a Custom Status
docs.text:
1. On the custom status, open Actions Edit.
  2. The Edit Container Status window opens with the same fields as when creating.
  3. Change the name, colour or job types.
  4. Click Update.

Container status 'name' was updated successfully. is shown.

  • Unticking an order type under Job Type Configuration clears its description.
  • A colour change shows up on the Orders and Dispatch pages the next time they are loaded, on every order that has the status.

Renaming does not update existing orders

The status name is saved as text on each order. If you rename a status, orders that already had the old name keep the old text. To move them to the new name, change the container status on those orders. Search the Orders page with the CONTAINER STATUS filter set to the old name to find them before you rename.

docs.title: Deleting a Custom Status
docs.text:
1. On the custom status, open Actions Delete.
  2. Confirm Are you sure?.

The page reloads and the status is gone from the list.

Deleting does not clear the status on orders

Orders that already have the deleted status keep its name as text. The status is no longer offered in the dropdowns or in the CONTAINER STATUS filter, and its custom colour is no longer applied. Change those orders to another status first.

Built-in statuses cannot be deleted.

docs.title: Automatic Status Changes
docs.text:
Most status changes are made by your office team. The following changes are made automatically by the mobile apps.

Trigger Order type Container status becomes The driver captures the delivery signature (Sign DELIVERY) Container Import Dropped at customer The driver captures the signature when dropping the empty (Sign DROP, step Export: Drop Empty) Container Export (not International Export) Dropped at customer The driver taps Drop Completed (step Import: Return empty) Container Import Returned to terminal The driver taps Transfer Completed Transfer Returned to terminal The yard worker taps Full at yard in the yard app Any Full at yard The yard worker taps Empty at yard in the yard app Any Empty at yard

See Driver Workflow and Yard Management for the mobile side.

Returned to terminal removes the order from the driver app

Drivers never see orders whose container status is Returned to terminal. Setting it by hand from the office has the same effect: the order leaves the driver's list. Some other statuses also close individual driver steps, for example Dropped at customer on an import closes Import: Deliver to client. See When an Order Leaves Your List.

docs.title: On the Orders and Dispatch lists
docs.text:
Where What you see C.Status column The order's container status in its colour, or a grey N/A when none is set. On the Orders page you can sort by this column. Click the status to pick a new one from a dropdown (Enter new container status) that lists every status, plus an empty choice that clears the status. The new status is saved at once and the row refreshes. Chassis # column The chassis / equipment number is shown in the colour of the order's container status. Container number Shown in red when the container status is Arrived - Missing customs or Arrived - On hold, so held containers stand out.

Admins, Managers, Dispatch and Customer Service users can click the C.Status value to change it, on both pages. On the Orders page, Accountants can also change it if UTX has turned on order management for accountants on your account (ask UTX support). See Orders and Dispatch.

docs.title: On the order form
docs.text: The Container status dropdown on the order form lists every status, sorted by name. It appears on Import, Export, Transfer and International Export orders. See Order Form.

docs.title: Orders page filter
docs.text: In the Orders page filters, the CONTAINER STATUS card has a dropdown with All Statuses, N/A (not set) and every status in the list. Use N/A (not set) to find orders that have no container status yet.

docs.title: Yard counters
docs.text:
At the top of the Orders page, next to the order status counters, intermodal accounts see:

  • Empty at Yard: number of orders with the status Empty at yard.
  • Full at Yard: number of orders with the status Full at yard.
  • Pre-Pull: only when your account has a status named exactly Pre-Pull.

Completed orders are not counted.

docs.title: Dispatch tabs
docs.text:
The Dispatch page has a row of container status tabs that filter the board:

Tab Status filtered Shown Pre-Pull Pre-Pull Only when a custom status named exactly Pre-Pull exists Dropped @ Customer Dropped at customer Always Empty @ Customer Empty at customer Always Full @ Customer Full at customer Always Empty @ Yard Empty at yard Always Full @ Yard Full at yard Always Empty @ Eco Empty at Eco Only when a custom status named exactly Empty at Eco exists Full @ Eco Full at Eco Only when a custom status named exactly Full at Eco exists Inbound Inbound Only when a custom status named exactly Inbound exists

Clicking a container status tab clears the other Dispatch filters and shows only orders with that status. Click it again to turn it off.

Turning on the optional tabs

To get the Pre-Pull, Empty @ Eco, Full @ Eco or Inbound tab, create a custom status with that exact name (same spelling and capitals). Renaming or deleting it removes the tab.

New orders on the Dispatch board

The Dispatch board normally shows dispatched orders and orders with recent dates.
