A New order also appears there when its container status is Pre-Pull, Dropped at customer, Empty at customer, Full at customer, Empty at yard, Full at yard, Empty at Eco, Full at Eco or Inbound. Completed orders never appear.

docs.title: Mobile apps
docs.text:
• Driver app: each order shows a CONTAINER STATUS line when a status is set. Orders with Returned to terminal are hidden. See Driver Workflow.
  • Yard app: each search result shows CONTAINER STATUS, with Full at yard / Empty at yard buttons. See Yard Management.

docs.title: Customer names in the status
docs.text: In the Orders column of the Equipment page and in the orders CSV export, the statuses Dropped at customer, Empty at customer and Full at customer are shown with the delivery customer's name instead of the word customer, for example Dropped at Customer name. See Equipment and Data Exports.

docs.title: Color Guide
docs.text:
You can give a custom status any colour. The Color Legend panel on the page suggests these meanings, which the built-in statuses follow:

Colour Suggested meaning Green (Success) Container ready for delivery Light Green Driver at terminal Red (Danger) Critical status requiring attention Orange (Warning) Status in progress, monitoring needed Blue (Primary) Standard operational status Purple Yard storage status Dark Blue Vessel/ocean transport Orange (Export) Export operations Pink Rail transport

Orders with no container status show N/A in grey.

docs.title: There is no Manage Container Statuses item in my menu
docs.text:
Solution

The item only appears for Admin, Manager, Dispatch and Customer Service users, and only on intermodal accounts. Accountants and other roles do not see it. Ask an Admin or Manager.

docs.title: I can't edit or delete a status
docs.text:
Solution

Built-in statuses (blue Built-in badge) are locked and have no Actions menu. Only custom statuses can be edited or deleted, and only by Admins and Managers. Dispatch and Customer Service users have view-only access. If you need a variation of a built-in status, create a new custom status with a different name.

docs.title: My new status doesn't show in the dropdown on the Orders page
docs.text:
Solution

The list of statuses is loaded when the page opens. Reload the Orders or Dispatch page after creating the status.

docs.title: I ticked only "Import" but the status still shows on Export orders
docs.text:
Solution

This is expected. Job Type Configuration documents which order types a status is meant for; it does not filter the dropdowns. Every status is offered on every order with a container status field.

docs.title: The status won't save
docs.text:
Solution

Check that:

  • Status Name is filled in and not already used by another status (including names that only differ by case, spaces or punctuation).
  • Color is a full hex code: # followed by six characters, for example #1a2b3c. Short codes like #abc and colour names like red are not accepted.
  • You are an Admin or Manager.

docs.title: I renamed a status and some orders still show the old name
docs.text:
Solution

Renaming only changes the status list. Orders store the status name as text, so existing orders keep the old name. After the rename, the old name is no longer in the CONTAINER STATUS filter, so find those orders by searching or sorting the Orders page on the C.Status column, then set the new status on each one. Next time, filter by the old name before renaming.

docs.title: An order disappeared from the driver's phone
docs.text:
Solution

Check the container status. Orders with Returned to terminal are hidden from drivers. This is set automatically when the driver taps Drop Completed or Transfer Completed, and also when someone in the office sets it by hand. Change the status back if the move is not finished.

docs.title: Why is the container number red?
docs.text:
Solution

The container status is Arrived - Missing customs or Arrived - On hold. Once the hold or customs issue is cleared, change the status (for example to Arrived - Awaiting delivery) and the number returns to normal.

docs.title: There is no Warehouse (or Dry Van) column in the list
docs.text:
Solution

The list and the Job Type Configuration section only show the order types turned on for your account. Contact UTX support if you need another order type enabled.

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
Keep the list short and consistent

  • Reuse built-in statuses where you can. They drive driver steps, Dispatch tabs and yard counters. Custom statuses only display, except the names Pre-Pull, Empty at Eco, Full at Eco and Inbound, which switch on Dispatch tabs (and, for Pre-Pull, an Orders counter).
  • Pick colours with meaning. Follow the Color Guide so red always means "needs attention" and your team can read the board at a glance.
  • Fill in Job Type Configuration with a short description for each order type, so new dispatchers know when to use each status.
  • Check for orders before renaming or deleting a custom status: filter the Orders page by that status first.
  • Use Arrived - Missing customs / Arrived - On hold for held containers, so the container number turns red on every list.

docs.title: Container Tracking
docs.text: See the latest terminal status of a container (CN Rail, Termont / Port of Montreal, or MGT Racine/Cast) from the order list, without logging in to the terminal websites.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Container Tracking (also called Track & Trace) checks your containers at the terminal on a schedule, stores the latest status, and shows it in a popup when you click the tracking icon on an order.

  • Three separate add-ons -- one per tracking source. Each source is shown and checked only when its own add-on is on for your account (see Add-ons and Options).
  • CN Rail -- containers at a pickup terminal named CN.
  • Termont (Port of Montreal) -- containers at a pickup terminal whose name contains TERMONT or VIAU.
  • MGT (Racine/Cast) -- containers at a pickup terminal whose name contains RACINE or CAST.
  • Automatic checks -- the system checks in-progress orders at those terminals on a schedule. You never trigger a check yourself.
  • Change history -- every change to the key tracking fields is recorded and shown at the bottom of the popup.
  • Auto-fill -- for Termont and MGT, blank order fields (seal, weight, steamship line, size, customs released) are filled in when new terminal data arrives.
  • Alerts and bulk updates -- status-change alerts are covered in Container Alerts; updating ETA and Last Free Day on many orders at once is covered in Tracking Bulk Update.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
1. Go to Orders (or Dispatch).
  2. Find the order. In the Container# column, click the tracking icon ( red train for CN, blue ship for Termont, orange ship for MGT). Its tooltip reads Check container status.
  3. The tracking popup opens. A green header means the container is available (CN: de-ramped; Termont / MGT: ready for pickup). Check the Customs line before you dispatch.
  4. Click Close when done.

Tip

The icon depends on the order's pickup terminal, not on the container number. If there is no icon, check the pickup terminal first. See No tracking icon on an order.

docs.title: Access & Permissions
docs.text:
Each part of the feature has its own rule:

  • Tracking icon on Orders -- needs permission to change container status on orders (the same permission as the inline container status edit).
  • Tracking icon on Dispatch -- shown to everyone who can open Dispatch.
  • Tracking popup -- needs full permission to manage the order (view-only access to an order is not enough).
Role Access Admin Icon on Orders and Dispatch, popup Manager Icon on Orders and Dispatch, popup (own offices) Dispatch / Customer Service Icon on Orders and Dispatch, popup (own offices) Accountant Icon on Orders and popup (own offices) only when your account lets accountants manage orders. This is on by default and set by UTX. No access to Dispatch Customer No tracking icon, no popup Driver / Broker / Yard Worker No tracking icon, no popup Warehouse / Garage No access -- these roles have no access to orders

How to get there:

  • Orders or Dispatch -- tracking icon in the Container# column.
  • Dispatch -- the Alerts button opens the Container Alerts page, where each container number also opens the tracking popup. See Container Alerts.

Don't see any tracking icons?

Your account may not have the tracking add-on for that terminal. Each source (CN, Termont, MGT) is a separate add-on. Contact UTX support to enable it.

docs.title: Which Containers Are Checked
docs.text:
The system checks an order's container only when all of these are true:

  • The add-on for that source is on.
  • The order is in progress: status New, App. Taken (shown as App. Made on the Orders tabs), or Dispatched.
  • The order was created on or after the Order Archive Cutoff Date in Settings (see Application Settings).
  • The order's pickup terminal is one of the terminals set up for that source.
  • The container number is not blank and is not N/A.
  • The container has not already left the terminal:
    • CN: skipped once its waybill status is Departed or Completed.
    • Termont / MGT: skipped once its transit state is Out.

Orders are processed in groups: 200 orders at a time for CN, 50 for MGT, and 10 for Termont (with a 2-second pause between Termont groups). Within a group, a container number that is on several orders is checked once.

How often? The checks run automatically on a schedule set by UTX. Use the Updated ... ago line at the bottom of the popup to see when that container was last refreshed.

Completed orders

The icon can still appear on a Completed order, and the popup still shows the last data stored for that container. It is no longer refreshed, because only in-progress orders are checked.

docs.title: The Tracking Icon
docs.text:
The icon sits in the Container# column, before the container number and the HAZMAT / scale / damaged labels.

Icon Source Shown when Red train CN Rail CN tracking add-on is on and the pickup terminal is a CN terminal Orange ship MGT (Racine/Cast) MGT tracking add-on is on and the pickup terminal is a Racine or Cast terminal Blue ship Termont Port of Montreal tracking add-on is on and the pickup terminal is a Termont / Viau terminal

Rules on the Orders page:

  • You need permission to change container status on orders (see Access & Permissions). Without it, you see the container number with its status label but no icon.
  • If the container number is longer than 20 characters (for example several numbers separated by /), there is no tracking icon. Each / becomes a line break so the numbers are shown on separate lines.
  • The icon is shown even before a container number is entered. In that case the popup says the container was not found.

On the Dispatch page the same icon appears in the container column for every order at a tracking terminal, for everyone who can open Dispatch, whatever the length of the container number.

docs.title: The Tracking Popup
docs.text:
Click the icon to open the popup. Its layout depends on the source. Fields with no data show a dash (—). Both layouts have a Container Tracking tab, the Updated ... ago line, the change history table, and a Close button.

How the source is chosen

The popup picks the source from the start of the order's pickup terminal name:

  • CN CN Rail
  • TERMONT or VIAU Termont
  • RACINE or CAST MGT (Racine/Cast)

It then looks up the stored tracking data for that source and the order's container number. If nothing is stored, the not-found popup opens instead.

docs.title: CN Rail popup
docs.text:
Header: train icon and container number, with CN Rail, the size, and Empty/Full underneath. The badge on the right shows the status.

Header color Badge Meaning Green DE-RAMPED / AVAILABLE The CLM status contains "De-ramped": the container is off the train Blue The current CLM status (or TRACKING if there is none) Anything else: in transit, at the yard, not yet de-ramped

Orange bar (CN): appears when CN reports a customs status and the customs description does not contain "release". It reads Customs Hold: followed by the customs status, with the hold description underneath.

Sections:

Section Fields Status & Location CLM Status, Event Location, Last Event (date and time, when known), Destination, Lot Location (when known), Customs Container Details Equipment Type, Size, Empty/Full (blue Full or gray Empty label), Gross Weight (KG), Net Weight, Waybill Status -- each shown only when CN sends it, except Empty/Full GPS Location Position, Location, GPS Time -- only when CN sends a GPS position Bill of Lading BOL Number, Shipper, Consignee, Commodity -- only when CN sends a BOL number Key Dates Destination ETA, Last Free Day (see Last Free Day colors) Technical Details (click to expand) EDI 214, EDI 322, CLM Code

The Customs field shows No customs info (gray) when there is nothing, a green check and the description when the description contains "release", or an orange warning triangle and the description (or hold status) otherwise.

What does De-ramped mean?

De-ramped means the container is off the train at the CN yard. A green header with DE-RAMPED / AVAILABLE is the signal to plan the pickup -- after checking the Customs line for a hold.

docs.title: Termont / MGT popup
docs.text:
Termont and MGT (Racine/Cast) use the same layout.

Header: cube icon and container number, with the source (Termont or MGT (Racine/Cast)), the shipping line, and size and type underneath.

Header color Badge Meaning Green READY FOR PICKUP The terminal reports the container as available for pickup Red NOT AVAILABLE FOR PICKUP Any other answer, including no answer

Orange bar (Termont / MGT): shows the terminal's hold message (for example "On Hold - Not available for pick up") whenever the terminal reports one. It is a terminal hold, which may or may not be customs-related -- check the Customs line for the customs status.

Sections:

Section Fields Status & Availability Terminal (the terminal section), Customs, Customs Date (when known), Hold/Perm (when known) Container & Vessel Shipping Line, Vessel, Voyage, Origin, Size / Type (when known), Empty/Full Carrier Timeline IN -- ship icon, vessel name, arrival date and time. OUT -- carrier type icon (vessel, truck, or rail), carrier name, date and time. A row with no carrier and no date reads Not yet departed (this can also appear on IN when no arrival data is known) Key Dates Destination ETA, Last Free Day (see Last Free Day colors) Technical Details (click to expand) Visit State (Active, Departed, or Unknown when not reported), Transit State (In, Out, or Unknown), Seal Number, Gross Weight (KG), Booking/BL

The Customs field works the same way as on the CN popup: No customs info, a green check when the description contains "release", or an orange warning triangle.

docs.title: Last Free Day colors
docs.text:
The Last Free Day in the Key Dates box is colored by how many days are left:

Color Days left Green 3 or more days Orange 1 or 2 days Red, light red background, EXPIRED The Last Free Day is today or earlier

EXPIRED shows on the Last Free Day itself

The popup marks the date EXPIRED from the Last Free Day onward, including the day itself. Treat it as "pick up today at the latest".

Storage and demurrage after the Last Free Day

Once the Last Free Day has passed, the terminal or steamship line may start charging storage or demurrage. The exact charges and when they start depend on the terminal and the line, not on UTX Freight. Plan pickups before the date shown.

docs.title: Change History
docs.text:
At the bottom of the CN and Termont / MGT popups, a table lists changes the system recorded for that container, newest first.

Column What it shows Tracker The tracking source, for example CN or POM (Port of Montreal / Termont) Changes Each changed field with its old and new value When Date and time of the change

Only these fields are tracked:

Label in the table Meaning Status CN CLM status Destination ETA ETA reported by the terminal Last free day Last Free Day reported by the terminal Pickup availability Termont / MGT available for pickup (Yes / No) Visit state Termont / MGT visit state; CN waybill status Transit state Termont / MGT transit state (In / Out) Customs status Customs hold status Customs description Customs description (for example a release or hold reason)

Changes to other data (vessel, seal, weight, location and so on) update the popup but do not appear in the history.

The first 5 rows are shown. If there are more, click Show all to see the rest.

docs.title: Auto-Filled Order Fields
docs.text:
When new Termont or MGT data arrives for a container, the system fills in blank fields on every in-progress order with that container number.

When it runs:

  • Only for Termont and MGT (Racine/Cast). CN data never fills order fields.
  • Only when the terminal data for that container changed (or is new) since the last check.
  • Only on in-progress orders (New, App. Taken, Dispatched) created on or after the archive cutoff that have the same container number.
  • Only fields that are blank on the order. Existing values are never overwritten.
Order field What is filled Seal Number The seal number from the terminal Weight The terminal's gross weight followed by KG (for example 24000 KG) Steamship Line The steamship line whose name matches the terminal's shipping line (not case-sensitive). If there is no exact match, a line whose name starts with the terminal's value. Nothing if there is no match Container Size The container size whose name equals the terminal's size, written either as 40 or 40'. Nothing if there is no match Customs released Set to Yes when the terminal's customs description contains "release"

ETA and Last Free Day are never auto-filled

Tracking does not copy the ETA or Last Free Day to the order. Use the bulk update tools (CN Tracking and Port Tracking on Dispatch) to apply them. See Tracking Bulk Update.

docs.title: Alerts and Bulk Updates
docs.text:
• Container Alerts -- open from the Alerts button on Dispatch. Lists pickup-ready, customs-released, LFD-approaching and departed alerts, upcoming Last Free Days, and the health of each tracking source. Click a container number there to open the same tracking popup. See Container Alerts.
  • Bulk update -- the CN Tracking and Port Tracking buttons on Dispatch. See Tracking Bulk Update.

docs.title: Container not found
docs.text:
Solution

The popup titled Container Information says This container number was not found. and There is no information available at this time. It means no tracking data is stored for that source and container number. Common causes:

  • The container has not been checked yet (new order, or the terminal does not know it yet).
  • The container number on the order is blank, N/A, or has a typo.
  • The order is not in progress, or was created before the Order Archive Cutoff Date, so it was never checked.
  • The container number on the order has extra characters (for example several numbers in one field), so it does not match the stored container number.
  • The tracking add-on for that source was off when the container was at the terminal.
  • The pickup terminal name does not start with CN, TERMONT, VIAU, RACINE or CAST. See Managing Terminals.

docs.title: No tracking icon on an order
docs.text:
Solution

Check, in order:

  1. Pickup terminal -- it must be a tracking terminal: its name must start with CN, TERMONT, VIAU, RACINE or CAST. See Managing Terminals.
  2. Add-on -- the add-on for that source must be on.
  3. Permission -- on Orders you need permission to change container status. Customers, drivers, and accountants without order management do not see the icon.
  4. Container number length -- on Orders, numbers longer than 20 characters have no icon.

If you just created or renamed a terminal and the icon still does not appear, contact UTX support.

docs.title: "Container status opens in a popup"
docs.text:
Solution

The tracking popup only works from a click inside the app. If you open its address directly (for example from a bookmark), you are sent back to the previous page, or to Container Alerts, with the message Container status opens in a popup. Click the container number in the list to see it. Click the tracking icon or the container number instead.

docs.title: Data seems out of date
docs.text:
Solution

Look at Updated ... ago at the bottom of the popup. It changes each time the terminal returns data for that container, even if nothing changed. If it is old:

  • The order may no longer be in progress, or the container is marked departed (CN Departed / Completed, Termont/MGT transit Out) and is no longer checked.
  • The terminal may not be returning data. Check the source's health card on Container Alerts.

docs.title: Customs hold still showing after release
docs.text:
Solution

Customs information comes from the terminal and updates only on the next successful check. If it stays on hold after several checks, confirm with the terminal or your customs broker.

docs.title: Best practices
docs.text:
Best Practices

Name terminals carefully. Start each tracking terminal's name with CN, TERMONT, VIAU, RACINE or CAST.

Enter one container number per order. Long multi-number entries (over 20 characters) lose the tracking icon on Orders, and tracking sends the whole field to the terminal as one container number, so it is unlikely to be found.

Green header = check customs, then dispatch. On CN, de-ramped does not mean customs is released -- read the Customs line.

Use bulk update for dates. ETA and Last Free Day are not copied to orders automatically.

docs.title: Creating & Editing Invoices
docs.text: Build an invoice from a customer's completed orders, set its terms, status and tax, then print it, export it as EDI 210, edit it or delete it.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
An invoice in UTX Freight is a header (customer, terms, date, status, tax) plus the completed orders you tick in the Invoice Orders list. The money on the invoice always comes from those orders.

  • One customer per invoice -- pick the Company first, then tick its orders
  • Completed orders only -- an order can be invoiced once it is Completed, is not already on an invoice, and its delivery date is on or after the Order Start Date in Settings
  • Due date is automatic -- calculated from the Invoice date and the Terms every time you save
  • Totals are automatic -- the sum of the order totals, plus GST and QST from the selected Tax
  • Print opens a printable invoice; EDI 210 downloads a CSV (if your account has EDI invoicing turned on -- ask UTX support)
  • Delete releases the orders so they can be invoiced again

Related pages

This page covers building and maintaining an invoice. For the Invoices list, filters and exports see Invoices. For emailing invoices and recording payments see Invoice Email & Payments. For how an order's total is built see Order Rates, Charges & Expenses.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
1. Go to Invoices in the left menu.
  2. Click Add a new Invoice (top right).
  3. Choose the Company. Its name goes into the Filter orders box, so the order list below narrows to that company.
  4. Check the Terms, Invoice date, Invoice Status and Tax.
  5. In Invoice Orders, tick the orders to bill (or click Select All).
  6. Click Save Invoice. You return to the Invoices list with the message Invoice was successfully created.

docs.title: Access & Permissions
docs.text:
Role Access Admin Full access -- create, edit, print, EDI 210, delete Manager Full access, for invoices of the offices they belong to Accountant Full access, for invoices of the offices they belong to Dispatch / Customer Service No access -- the Invoices menu is not shown Customers, drivers, warehouse and garage users No access

How to get there:

  • Invoices (left menu) > Add a new Invoice -- create an invoice (page title New Invoice)
  • Invoices > Actions menu on a row > Edit -- edit an invoice (page title Edit Invoice)

Multi-office

An invoice belongs to the office you are working in, and the Invoice Orders list only shows that office's orders. Customers are shared between offices when the multi-office add-on is on, so the Company list shows every customer; without it, only the current office's customers are listed. Switch office first if you need to invoice another office's orders. See Multi-Office.

docs.title: The Invoice Form
docs.text: The New and Edit pages use the same form, in three parts: Invoice Information, Payment Information and Invoice Orders.

docs.title: Invoice Information
docs.text:
Field Required Default (new invoice) Description Company Yes Blank The customer being billed. A new invoice lists active customers only; the Edit page also lists inactive (but not deleted) customers so older invoices still show theirs. Choosing a company also filters the order list to it (see below) Terms -- Default Terms from Settings (Invoice group); on the Edit page, the invoice's saved terms Payment terms, in two groups. Most Common: Due on Receipt, 30 Days, 10 Days, 45 Days. Other: 15 Days, 21 Days, 60 Days, 90 Days Invoice date Yes Today The date printed on the invoice. Pick it from the date picker Invoice Status -- new One of new, Invoiced, Paid, Partially Paid. If you save an invoice as Paid with no payment recorded, today's date is stored as its paid date Tax No Blank One of the taxes set up in UTX Freight (the same list in every office). Leave blank for no tax. See Charge Types & Taxes

Next to the date, an info note reads: INFO: The due date is automatically calculated based on the invoice date and the terms.

Status changes on its own when you email

You rarely set Invoiced by hand: emailing an invoice whose status is new switches it to Invoiced automatically. See Invoice Email & Payments.

docs.title: Payment Information
docs.text: Below the header fields, Payment Information lists the payments recorded on the invoice. Click (+) Add payment to add a line with Paid date, Check number and Amount (required), or (-) Remove payment to drop one. The same payments can be recorded from the Record a payment action on the Invoices list, which opens a smaller Edit Invoice window (status and payments only, plus a Balance Paid In Full button when the invoice is not already Paid) and does not change the invoice's orders. Payments are covered in Invoice Email & Payments.

docs.title: Saving
docs.text:
• Click Save Invoice. The button reads Please wait... while the invoice saves.
  • A new invoice returns you to the Invoices list with Invoice was successfully created.
  • An edited invoice returns you to the list with Invoice 00123 was successfully updated. (with your invoice number).
  • Cancel returns to the Invoices list without saving.

If Company or Invoice date is missing, the form stays open with the error, and the orders you had ticked stay ticked.

An incomplete order never blocks the invoice

Orders are attached to the invoice without re-checking their own required fields. An order with, for example, a blank container number can still be invoiced.

docs.title: Picking Orders (Invoice Orders)
docs.text: The Invoice Orders section lists every order you can put on this invoice, one checkbox per order, sorted by customer name, then delivery date, then order date.

docs.title: Which orders are listed
docs.text:
An order appears in the list when all of these are true:

  • its status is Completed,
  • it is not already on another invoice,
  • its delivery date is on or after the Order Start Date in Settings (Invoice group),
  • it belongs to the office you are working in.

On the Edit page, the orders already on this invoice are listed too.

Orders with no delivery date

An order with no delivery date is never listed, because it cannot be compared with the Order Start Date. Add the delivery date on the order, then come back to the invoice.

Find what still needs billing

On the Orders page, Admin and Manager users have two extra tabs. Not Invoiced lists Completed orders with no invoice and a delivery date on or after the Order Start Date -- the same rules as this list, except that orders created before the Order Archive Cutoff Date in Settings are also left out. Late Invoicing narrows that to orders delivered before the end of the week two weeks ago. See Orders.

docs.title: How each order reads
docs.text:
Each checkbox label shows, separated by dashes:

Order # - Customer - Container # - Reference # - Delivery date - Receiver - Status

For a transfer, the Receiver part shows the customer's name.

If the order has no scanned signed POD and no driver signature (delivery or pickup), the label ends with - MISSING PDF. This is a warning only -- you can still invoice the order -- but there is no signed POD on file to send with the invoice. See Order Documents & POD.

docs.title: Filtering the list
docs.text:
Control What it does All Clears the filter and shows every listed order Selected Orders Shows only the ticked orders. The Edit page opens with this filter on, so you first see what is on the invoice Selected Company Puts the name of the customer chosen in Company into the Filter orders box, so the list shows orders whose label contains that name Filter orders box Type any text from the order label -- order number, customer, container number, reference, date, receiver -- to narrow the list

The active button is highlighted. Choosing a Company puts its name into the Filter orders box automatically.

Under the box: You can filter by entering any text included in the order name including the dates and container number. Regardless of your filter, the selected orders will always show up.

Ticked orders never hide

Whatever you type, ticked orders always stay visible. What goes on the invoice is every ticked order, not only the ones matching your filter.

docs.title: Select All and the selection counter
docs.text:
Select All ticks every order currently shown by the filter. Hidden orders are not touched.

  • It is greyed out until you choose a Company, so you cannot select every customer's orders by accident.
  • When every shown order is already ticked, the button changes to Deselect All and unticks them.
  • On the Edit page, Deselect All asks first: Deselect all N shown orders? -- They will be removed from this invoice when you click Save Invoice. You can click Select All to re-select them. Click Yes, deselect all or Cancel.

The text next to the button tells you where you stand:

Counter text Meaning Choose a company first to select its orders No Company chosen yet; Select All is disabled No orders to select The filter shows no orders 3 of 5 shown orders selected Ticked vs shown, for the current filter 3 of 5 shown orders selected — 7 selected in total, including hidden orders Other ticked orders are hidden by the filter. All 7 go on the invoice

Review the selection before saving

An invoice is for one Company. The company filter matches text in the order label, so it can also show an order whose receiver or reference contains the same name. Click Selected Orders to review exactly what is ticked before you click Save Invoice.

docs.title: Due Date
docs.text:
The due date is recalculated from the Invoice date and Terms every time the invoice is saved:

Terms Due date Due on Receipt (or no terms on an older invoice) Same as the invoice date 10 Days, 15 Days, 21 Days, 30 Days, 45 Days, 60 Days, 90 Days Invoice date plus that many days

There is no separate due-date field. To change the due date, change the Invoice date or the Terms and save. The due date drives the aging shown on the Invoices list and the Aged Receivables reports.

docs.title: Invoice Numbers
docs.text:
Invoice numbers are assigned automatically when you save a new invoice. They are sequential and cannot be edited. Depending on how your account is configured, the number is shown in one of two formats:

Format Example How it is built Plain 00123 The invoice number padded to 5 digits Decorated A26 - 00123 First letter of the customer's name, the last two digits of the invoice date's year, then the 5-digit number

Decorated numbers follow the invoice

In the decorated format, the letter and year are read from the current Company and Invoice date. If you change either on an existing invoice, the prefix changes too; the 5-digit part stays the same.

Searching by number

On the Invoices list, search with the digits only (for example 123), not the decorated prefix.

docs.title: Totals and Taxes
docs.text:
The invoice has no line items of its own. Its amounts are calculated from the attached orders:

Amount Calculation Subtotal Sum of the attached orders' totals (each order's Base rate plus its charges) GST Subtotal × the selected Tax's GST %, rounded to the cent QST Subtotal × the selected Tax's QST %, rounded to the cent Total Subtotal + GST + QST. With no Tax selected, the total is the subtotal
  • An invoice with no orders shows a blank Total and Balance on the Invoices list, and — instead of an order count.
  • There is no "regenerate" button. The invoice total always follows its orders: when an attached order's total changes (for example you edit its base rate or add a charge), the invoice total changes with it.
  • Automatic charges are not recalculated on orders that are Completed or invoiced. A change to a terminal's default rate or to the fuel schedule does not reach orders that are already completed. To change their amounts, edit the order's charges by hand. See Order Rates, Charges & Expenses and Fuel Surcharge.

docs.title: Editing an Invoice
docs.text:
1. Go to Invoices and find the invoice.
  2. Click the Actions menu on its row > Edit.
  3. The Invoice Orders list opens on Selected Orders. Click All or Selected Company to see orders you can add.
  4. Change any field, tick orders to add them, untick orders to remove them.
  5. Click Save Invoice.

What happens on save:

  • Ticked orders not yet on the invoice are attached.
  • Unticked orders are removed from the invoice and become available to invoice again.
  • The due date, totals and taxes are recalculated.

Already-sent invoices

Editing does not re-send the invoice. If the customer already has it, email it again -- later sends are marked REVISED. See Invoice Email & Payments.

docs.title: Printing an Invoice
docs.text:
On the Invoices list, open the Actions menu > Print. The printable invoice opens in a new browser tab; use your browser's print or save-as-PDF.

Most accounts use this layout:

Area Contents Header Your logo, Invoice Number, Invoice Date, Payment Due (the due date) FROM Your company name, address and Tel BILL TO The customer's name and address, followed by the Message from Settings (Invoice group) Order sections Orders grouped by order type, one section each: CONTAINER IMPORTS, CONTAINER EXPORTS, CONTAINER TRANSFERS, DRY VAN MOVES. Within a section, orders are sorted by delivery date, then order date Taxes When a Tax is selected: GST (x%) and QST (x%) lines, next to your GST Number and QST Number from Settings (Invoice group) Totals The N.I.R number (NIR Number from Settings, POD group) and TOTAL. If the invoice is not Paid but has payments: Invoice Total, Paid to Date and Amount Due Footer THANK YOU FOR YOUR SUPPORT

Each order row shows the order number (with PO: underneath when the order has a delivery PO number), the container or trailer number (with From: / To: terminal for imports and exports), reference (plus booking and seal numbers for exports and transfers), the receiver (or the two terminals for transfers), the date (the delivery date; for dry van moves, the closing date), then one line for Base rate and one per charge, with their Price, and the order Total. Amounts are shown in the customer's default currency.

Section Columns CONTAINER IMPORTS POD · Cont.# · Reference# · Client · Delivery · Charge · Price · Total CONTAINER EXPORTS POD · Cont.# · Ref#/ Booking#/ Seal# · Client · Pickup · Charge · Price · Total CONTAINER TRANSFERS POD · Cont.# · Ref#/ Booking#/ Seal# · Terminals · Pickup · Charge · Price · Total DRY VAN MOVES POD · Trailer# · Reference# · Client · Pickup · Charge · Price · Total

Layout can differ by account

The invoice layout is set per account by UTX. Some accounts use an older layout with the same orders, charges, taxes and totals, arranged differently: the header shows Invoice #, Date and Client ID (no Payment Due), the customer's TERMS appear in a box next to the Message, each section has an extra date column (Return or Delivery), amounts are shown with a $ sign instead of the currency code, and the remaining amount is labelled BALANCE. A few accounts use a customised layout.

docs.title: EDI 210 Export
docs.text:
When EDI invoicing is enabled for your account, the Actions menu on each invoice has EDI 210. If you don't see it, EDI invoicing is not turned on for your account -- ask UTX support.

Clicking it downloads a CSV named EDI210_<invoice number>_<YYYYMMDD>.csv (the date is the download date). The file has a header row and one row per order on the invoice. Dates use the dd/mm/yyyy format and amounts have no thousands separator or currency sign.

Column Value DOC TYPE Always INV INVOICE-NUMBER Invoice number, as displayed ITEM NUMBER 1, 2, 3... one per order MSC PO The order's delivery PO number TERMS Terms in days (0 for Due on Receipt) INVOICE-DATE / INVOICE-DUE DATE Invoice date and due date CURRENCY The customer's default currency BASE RATE The order's base rate PRE-PULL, STORAGE, FUEL Always 0.00 OTHER Sum of all the order's charges (including terminal fee and fuel surcharge) INVOICE TOTAL The whole invoice total with taxes (repeated on every row) WAYBILL-NUMBER The order's reference number WAYBILL-DATE The order's waybill date VESSEL / VOYAGE NUMBER From the order UNIQUE-SHIPMENT-ID Container number EQUIP-INITIAL First four characters of the container number DESTINATION - UNLOC The receiver's UN/LOCODE, when set NOTES Always *

These columns are present but always empty: BOND CHARGES, CHASSIS DETENTION, DROP CHARGES, GENSET COST, OVERWEIGHT, SPECIAL PERMIT, WAITING TIME COST, DEAD RUN, OVERDIMENTION, SCALING, HAZMAT, RESERVATION FEE, EQUIP-NUMBER, ORIGIN-UNLOC, ORIGIN-PROV, DESTINATION-PROV, WEIGHT, UOM, EQUIP-SIZE, EQUIP-TYPE.

Charges are reported together

All of an order's charges are reported in OTHER, including the fuel surcharge. FUEL, STORAGE and PRE-PULL are always 0.00.

docs.title: Deleting an Invoice
docs.text:
1. On the Invoices list, open the Actions menu > Delete.
  2. Confirm Are you sure?.

The invoice disappears from the list. Its orders are released: they are no longer invoiced, appear again in Not Invoiced on the Orders page, and can be put on a new invoice.

Deleted invoices cannot be restored from the app

There is no undo button. If you deleted an invoice by mistake, contact UTX support. UTX support can restore a recently deleted invoice (within the last 12 months), provided its customer and office still exist. The invoice comes back with its original number, date, terms, status and tax, and its orders are re-attached if they have not been put on another invoice since. Check the restored invoice's orders afterwards.

docs.title: What Invoicing Does to Orders
docs.text:
Once an order is on an invoice:

Effect Details Cannot be deleted Delete Order is greyed out. Remove the order from the invoice first (Edit the invoice and untick it) Cannot be transferred In multi-office accounts, Transfer to Office is greyed out as Transfer (Invoiced) No automatic charge updates Terminal fee and fuel surcharge are no longer recalculated (this already applies once the order is Completed) Total still flows to the invoice Editing the order's base rate or charges by hand updates the invoice total Invoice icon on Orders Admin, Manager and Accountant see a Get order invoice button in the order's invoice column. It opens the Invoices list searched to that invoice. Customer Service sees the order total but not the button Status unchanged The order stays Completed -- being invoiced is not an order status

Removing an order from an invoice (untick and save, or delete the invoice) undoes all of this.

docs.title: Can't create an invoice -- the order isn't in the list
docs.text:
Solution

The order must be Completed, not already on an invoice, and have a delivery date on or after the Order Start Date in Settings (Invoice group). It is the delivery date that counts, not the date the order was completed. Also check that you are in the right office, and that the filter (Filter orders box, Selected Orders, Selected Company) is not hiding it -- click All.

docs.title: Select All is greyed out
docs.text:
Solution

Choose a Company first. Select All is also disabled when the current filter shows no orders (No orders to select).

docs.title: An order shows MISSING PDF
docs.text:
Solution

The order has no scanned signed POD and no driver signature. You can still invoice it, but there is no signed POD on file for it. Upload the signed POD on the order first if the customer needs it. See Order Documents & POD.

docs.title: Invoice shows wrong amounts
docs.text:
Solution

Invoice amounts come from the orders. Edit the order's Base rate or charges; the invoice total updates by itself. Completed and invoiced orders do not recalculate the Terminal Fee or fuel surcharge automatically, so adjust those charges by hand. If taxes are wrong, edit the invoice and check the Tax selected.

docs.title: The invoice total is blank in the list
docs.text:
Solution

The invoice has no orders. Edit it and tick its orders, or delete it.

docs.title: The due date is wrong
docs.text:
Solution

The due date is calculated from the Invoice date and Terms. Edit the invoice, correct either one, and click Save Invoice.

docs.title: I can't delete an order
docs.text:
Solution

The order is on an invoice. Use Get order invoice on the order row to find the invoice, edit it, untick the order and save. Then delete the order.

docs.title: I deleted an invoice by mistake
docs.text:
Solution

Contact UTX support with the invoice number and customer. UTX support can restore invoices deleted within the last 12 months, with the same number and, where they can still be found, its orders. Check the orders on the restored invoice afterwards.

docs.title: There is no EDI 210 option
docs.text:
Solution

EDI invoicing is an account option that UTX turns on. Ask UTX support if you need it.

Best Practices

  • Set the Order Start Date in Settings to the day you started invoicing in UTX Freight, so older work doesn't clutter the order list.
  • Always pick the Company first, then use Select All -- it only works on the shown orders of that company.
  • Watch the counter: if it says including hidden orders, click Selected Orders to see everything that will be billed.
  • Resolve MISSING PDF orders before invoicing, so a signed POD is on file for every order you bill.
  • Check rates on the order before invoicing -- completed orders do not recalculate automatic charges.

docs.title: Customer & Consignee Portal
docs.text: What your customers see and can do when they sign in to UTX Freight: their company's orders, optional order creation and editing, PODs, and the read-only consignee view for linked shippers/receivers.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Every person you add under a customer company can sign in to UTX Freight with the Customer role. Customers get a short version of the app built around one page: Orders.

  • Company-wide visibility: a customer user sees every order placed for anyone in their company, not only their own, in the office they are working in.
  • View only by default: customers can search, filter and open order details. They cannot change statuses, edit fields inline, or see drivers and pricing.
  • Optional order management: if your account has customer order entry turned on (ask UTX support), customers can also create orders and edit orders that are still New. It is off by default.
  • PODs: customers can open the scanned POD and the signed POD of their orders.
  • Emails: the person on the order gets an email when it is dispatched and when it is completed (if their Email Notifications setting is on). Invoices, statements and PODs are emailed by your staff.
  • Consignee view: when a customer company is linked to a Shipper / Receiver record, its users also see, read-only, every order delivered to that location, from any freight forwarder, with no pricing.
  • No back office: customers cannot open Dispatch, Invoices, Reports or any other menu.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
For your staff (giving a customer access):

  1. Go to Customers, find the company, and click Add Person.
  2. Enter the person's details and click Add this person. They get an invitation email right away and choose their own password. See People & Invitations.
  3. Optional: to give the company the consignee view, go to Shipper / Receiver, edit the delivery location, pick the company in Linked Customer Account, and click Save Changes.

For the customer:

  1. Accept the invitation and sign in. The Orders page opens.
  2. Type a container #, order # or P/O in the Container #, Order # and more box and click Search, or use the status tabs (All, In Progress, New, App. Made, Dispatched, Completed).
  3. Open an order with the caret next to the grey Actions button View Details.
  4. Click the PDF or signature icon in the POD column to open the order's POD.

docs.title: Access & Permissions
docs.text:
What a Customer user can do, compared with your staff:

Action Customer Customer (consignee orders) See orders on the Orders page All orders of their company, in their office(s) Orders delivered to the linked shipper/receiver View Details Open the scanned or signed POD (POD column) Create a new order Only when customer order entry is turned on — Edit Order Only when customer order entry is turned on, and only while the order is New Never Change status (Make App., Dispatch, Complete), Reset, Go Back 1 Step Inline editing on the list (dates, numbers, container status) Duplicate, Delete Order, Transfer to Office, View History See rates, totals, invoice links See drivers and the Special Note Send POD to client (Email POD column) Dispatch, Invoices, Customers, Shipper / Receiver, Equipments, Reports menus Edit Profile (own details and Email Notifications)
  • The sidebar shows only Orders. The user menu shows Edit Profile and Logout. See Navigation & Account.
  • If a customer opens a page they are not allowed to see (for example by typing its address), UTX Freight sends them back to Orders.
  • The top bar also shows Feedback and Online Documentation, and the office switcher on Multi-Office accounts when the customer belongs to more than one office.
  • Customer order entry is an account-wide option that only UTX can switch on. It applies to all customers at once; it can't be turned on for a single customer. Contact UTX support to change it.

Who sets things up:

Task Who can do it Add customer people (invitations) Admin, Manager. Dispatch too, if your account lets dispatchers manage customers (ask UTX support). See Customers Link a shipper/receiver to a customer account (consignee) Admin, Manager, Dispatch (anyone who can edit Shipper / Receiver). See Shippers & Receivers

docs.title: What Customers See on the Orders Page
docs.text: Customers use the same Orders page as your staff (see Orders), with fewer columns, filters and actions.

docs.title: Which orders are listed
docs.text:
A customer sees an order when both are true:

  • the order was placed for any person of the customer's company (the Place the order on behalf of person), and
  • the order belongs to one of the customer's offices.

The list shows the orders of the office the customer is currently working in. On Multi-Office accounts, a customer who belongs to more than one office can change office with the office switcher in the top bar.

Company-wide, not per person

Every user of a customer company sees the same orders: all orders placed for anyone in that company. There is no setting to limit a customer user to only their own orders. If two groups in one company must not see each other's orders, set them up as two separate customers.

docs.title: Header and filters
docs.text:
• Counters: New Orders, App. Made, Dispatched, Total, and on intermodal accounts the yard counters (Empty at Yard, Full at Yard, and Pre-Pull when that container status exists). They count only the orders the customer can see.
  • Create a new order button: only when customer order entry is turned on.
  • Search box (Container #, Order # and more) and Clear All.
  • Status tabs: All, In Progress, New, App. Made, Dispatched, Completed. On intermodal accounts with order tagging, tag buttons also appear.

Customers do not see the Not Invoiced and Late Invoicing tabs, the ORDER TYPE, CONTAINER STATUS and TERMINAL filter cards, or the ACTION & ORDERS card (Equipment, Legend, Export).

docs.title: Columns
docs.text:
Customers see the order's status, order #, P/O#, Deliver To and Bill To (the company that placed the order), the delivery/pickup date and appointment time, container or trailer details (size, steamship line, weight, container #, booking and seal #, Last Free Day), the vessel, the pickup terminal and pickup #, the chassis or equipment, C.Status, Return To / Return Date, and the POD and DOC columns. Columns depend on your account type (intermodal or ground), as described in Orders. All values are read-only.

Customers do not see:

  • the ETA, Storage (STO), Demurrage (DEM), ERD and Cutoff Date values (these cells stay empty for customers),
  • the Driver columns,
  • the Invoiced / Rate column (invoice link, total and zone),
  • the Email POD column,
  • the Special Note (the red comment your staff can add under the status).

The Special Note is internal

The Special Note ("Comment which appears under the status for each order and on the drivers phone") is shown to your staff and to drivers. It is hidden from customers on the Orders list and is not shown on View Details. Use it for internal instructions. Don't rely on it to tell the customer anything.

docs.title: Row actions
docs.text:
The status button is always the grey Actions button for customers: they can't move an order to the next status. The caret next to it opens the menu:

Menu item When a customer sees it View Details Always Edit Order Only when customer order entry is turned on and the order is a New order of their own company. Consignee orders can't be edited

Customers never see Duplicate, Reset Order to New, Go Back 1 Step, Transfer to Office, View History, Remove Signature, Delete Order, View POD / View eBoL, View Internal POD or View Carrier Confirmation.

docs.title: View Details
docs.text:
View Details opens the page Order #<number> with the ordering company and the name and email of the person the order is placed for, Order Information, Client Information (delivery company, address, contact, instructions, P.O. #), Return Address, Container Information (including the zone name) and Goods Information.

The Administrative Information section (rates, total, appointment date and time, delivery date, comments) is shown to Admin, Manager and Dispatch only. Customers don't see it.

docs.title: Creating and Editing Orders (Optional)
docs.text: These features are available only when your account has customer order entry turned on. It is off by default and only UTX can turn it on, so ask UTX support. When it is off, customers have no Create a new order button and no Edit Order item.

docs.title: Creating an order
docs.text:
1. On Orders, click Create a new order.
  2. The New order form opens. The Customer Information box shows the customer's own company and name. A customer always places orders for themselves: there is no Place the order on behalf of field.
  3. Fill in the order. See Order Form for the fields.
  4. Click Create Job (or Cancel).

The order is created with the status New in the office the customer is working in. The customer returns to Orders, searched for the new order, with the message Order #<number> was successfully created.

Creating an order sends the New Order email (subject New Order #<number> from <company>) to your Admins who have Email Notifications on, with the office Managers who have Email Notifications on in CC. See Notifications & Emails.

Staff-only sections of the form are not shown to customers: Change Customer, Administrative information (including Special Note and the signed POD upload), Appointment Information, rates, Order Expenses, Order Legs and Comments.

docs.title: Editing an order
docs.text:
1. On Orders, click the caret next to Actions Edit Order.
  2. Change the fields and click Update Job (or Cancel).

The customer sees Order #<number> was successfully updated. The person on the order can't be changed by a customer.

Customers can edit any New order of their company, including orders a colleague placed or your staff entered for them.

Only while the order is New

As soon as your staff take an appointment (App. Made), the order becomes read-only for the customer and Edit Order disappears. If the customer needs a change after that, they must contact you.

Someone else changed the order

If your staff saved the order while the customer was editing it, the customer's changes are not saved and they see: This order was modified by another user while you were editing. Your changes were NOT saved. Please try again.

docs.title: Deleting an order
docs.text: The Delete Order item in the actions menu is shown to staff only. A customer who wants a New order cancelled should ask you to delete it. See Order Workflow.

docs.title: Documents and PODs
docs.text:
The POD column shows icons once a POD exists. Customers (and consignees) can open them:

Icon What it opens Red PDF The scanned signed POD uploaded by your staff Green signature (Open signed POD) The signed POD captured on the driver's phone

Documents attached to an order are managed by your staff. Customers can't upload documents or the signed POD; your staff do that. To send documents to a customer, include them in the invoice email or use Send POD to client. See Order Documents & POD.

docs.title: Emails Customers Receive
docs.text:
Email Subject Sent to When Dispatched Order #<number> is now dispatched The person the order is placed for When your staff dispatch the order with the Dispatch window. Includes the new status, appointment date and time, order #, client name, reference #, and the container # and pickup terminal (or pickup and delivery addresses) Completed Order Completed for order #<number> The person the order is placed for When your staff complete the order with the Complete window. Includes the empty container return date when set Invoice Set by your staff when sending The addresses entered when sending (by default the customer's Accountant Email) When your staff email an invoice. The invoice PDF is attached with the POD of each order, and optionally the order documents. See Invoice Email & Payments Statement of account <Your company> Statement of Account as of <date> (followed by the office name on multi-office accounts) The customer's Accountant Email (pre-filled, and editable, when your staff send it by hand) When your staff send a statement, or on the customer's automatic schedule. PDF or Excel, per the customer's Default Statement Format. See Customer Statements and Automatic Statements POD <Your company> Order #<number> Delivered The addresses entered in Send POD to client (pre-filled with the delivery Email of the order) When your staff click the envelope in the Email POD column. The signed or scanned POD is attached
  • The Dispatched and Completed emails go only to the person on the order, and only when that person has Email Notifications ticked (customers can change this under Edit Profile). Other users of the same company don't get them.
  • Taking an appointment (Make App.) never emails the customer. See Order Workflow.
  • Invoice, statement and POD emails go to addresses, not to user accounts. The customer doesn't need a login to receive them.

docs.title: Consignee View
docs.text: A consignee is a customer user whose company is linked to one or more Shipper / Receiver records. Typically this is the receiver of the goods (for example, a warehouse or importer) that wants to follow every container delivered to its door, whichever freight forwarder ordered the move.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Linked users see, read-only, every order whose delivery location (Deliver To) is one of the linked shipper/receiver records, from any customer (freight forwarder). They also keep seeing their own company's orders as usual.
  • Only the delivery location counts. Orders where the linked location is the pickup location are not added.
  • Pricing is never shown, the same as for every customer.
  • Consignee orders can't be edited, even when customer order entry is turned on. Consignees can use View Details and open the POD.
  • The Bill To line shows the company that placed the order (the forwarder).
  • As for other customers, the list shows the orders of the office the user is currently working in.

A blue banner appears above the Orders list for consignee users:

Consignee view: you are seeing all delivery orders addressed to <linked shipper/receiver names> — from all freight forwarders. Pricing details are not shown.

docs.title: Linking a shipper/receiver to a customer account
docs.text:
1. Go to Shipper / Receiver and edit the delivery location.
  2. In the Portal Access — Consignee Link section, choose the customer company in Linked Customer Account. The list shows all active companies.
  3. Click Save Changes.

All users of that customer company become consignees for that location right away. To remove access, set Linked Customer Account back to — No linked account — and save.

A linked shipper/receiver shows the company name with a badge in the Linked Account column of the Shipper / Receiver list. Use the Linked filter to see all linked records. See Shippers & Receivers.

Consignees see other forwarders' orders

Linking gives the customer visibility of orders placed by your other customers for that delivery location: order numbers, container details, dates, the forwarder's name in Bill To, the forwarder contact's name and email on View Details, and PODs. Only link a location to the company that actually operates it.

One link per location

Each shipper/receiver record can be linked to one customer company. A customer company can be linked to several shipper/receiver records; the banner lists them all.

docs.title: The customer has no "Create a new order" button
docs.text:
Solution

Customer order entry is an account option that is off by default. Contact UTX support to turn it on. It applies to all customers. Also check that your account isn't suspended: during a suspension nobody can create orders.

docs.title: The customer can't edit an order
docs.text:
Solution

Customers can only edit orders that are still New, and only when customer order entry is turned on. Once an appointment is made the order is read-only for them. Orders seen through the consignee view are never editable. Make the change for them, or use Reset Order to New if the order must go back to the customer.

docs.title: A customer user can't see an order
docs.text:
Solution

Check that the order is placed for a person of their company (the Bill To line) and that it belongs to the office they are working in. If the customer belongs to several offices (multi-office accounts), they need to switch office with the office switcher. For a consignee, check that the order's Deliver To is the shipper/receiver record that is linked to their company (a duplicate record with the same name is not linked). Also try the All tab: the list opens on In Progress.

docs.title: A customer user sees orders placed by colleagues
docs.text:
Solution

This is expected. Customer users see all orders of their company. To separate two groups, create them as two customers.

docs.title: The customer didn't get the dispatched or completed email
docs.text:
Solution

These emails go only to the person the order is placed for, and only if their Email Notifications setting is ticked. Check it on the person's Edit Person page (or ask the customer to check Edit Profile). Make App. never sends an email.

docs.title: The customer asks for prices or invoices in the portal
docs.text:
Solution

Customers never see rates, totals or invoices in UTX Freight, and they can't open Invoices. Email the invoice from Invoices, or send a statement. Make sure the customer's Accountant Email is filled in.

docs.title: The customer didn't see our Special Note
docs.text:
Solution

The Special Note is internal: staff and drivers see it, customers don't. Send the information to the customer by email or phone instead.

docs.title: The POD column is empty
docs.text:
Solution

The icons appear only once the driver has signed on the phone or your staff have uploaded the scanned signed POD. Customers can't upload it themselves.

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
Tips for the customer portal

  • Invite every customer contact who needs to follow orders. They all see the company's orders, so you don't need to forward updates by hand.
  • Make sure the main contact on each customer has Email Notifications on, so they get the dispatched and completed emails.
  • Keep the Special Note for internal and driver instructions. Customers never see it.
  • Link a shipper/receiver to a customer account only after confirming the customer operates that location. Consignees see orders from all your other customers delivered there.
  • Keep one shipper/receiver record per location. Orders delivered to a duplicate record that isn't linked won't show in the consignee view.

docs.title: Customer Statements
docs.text: Email, print or download a Statement of Account that lists a customer's unpaid invoices, split into past due and not yet due, from the Customer Reports page.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
• One row per customer: Reports > Customer Reports lists every customer that has at least one invoice whose status is not Paid, with their balances and the result of the last statement email.
  • Email: the blue Email button on a row opens the Send statement to customer window. The statement is attached as a PDF or an Excel file, depending on the customer's Default Statement Format.
  • Print: opens the statement in a new browser tab, ready to print or save as PDF from your browser.
  • Excel: the green Excel button downloads the statement as an .xlsx file.
  • Delivery tracking: after each send, the row shows the Sent date and an OK or Failed! label in the Email column.
  • Balances only count unpaid invoices: every invoice whose status is not Paid is included. Amounts are the invoice total with taxes minus the payments recorded on it.

Manual vs automatic statements

This page covers statements you send yourself. To have statements emailed on a fixed weekday, see Automatic Statements. A manual send always goes out when you click Send, even if the customer's balance is zero. The automatic schedule only sends when the balance is greater than zero.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
To email a statement:

  1. Go to Reports > Customer Reports.
  2. Find the customer and click the blue Email button on their row.
  3. Check the To and Cc addresses, and add a Bcc if needed.
  4. Check the format line at the bottom of the window (PDF or Excel icon).
  5. Click Send. A notification confirms the result, and the row updates with today's Sent date and OK (or Failed!).

To print or download a statement:

  1. Go to Reports > Customer Reports.
  2. Click Print to open the statement in a new tab, or click the green Excel button to download the .xlsx file.

docs.title: Access & Permissions
docs.text:
Role Access Admin Full access: view Customer Reports, email, print and download statements Manager Same as Admin, but only when reports are enabled for managers on your account. Otherwise the Reports menu is not shown Accountant No access to the Reports menu, so cannot open Customer Reports Dispatch No access to the Reports menu Customer, Warehouse, Garage, drivers No access

Two permissions are involved:

  • Opening Customer Reports requires access to Reports (the same access that shows the Reports menu in the left navigation).
  • Sending a statement also requires permission to manage customers. Admins and Managers have it.

How to get there:

  • Left menu Reports > Customer Reports

Manager can't see Reports?

Whether Managers can see the Reports menu is an account-level option. Contact UTX support if your managers need it.

docs.title: Choosing customers
docs.text:
At the top of the page, the Customer dropdown lets you pick one customer. Click Update Report to apply.

  • [ALL CUSTOMERS] (the default) shows every customer that has at least one invoice whose status is not Paid. Customers whose invoices are all Paid do not appear.
  • Picking a single customer shows only that customer, even if all their invoices are paid.
  • The list shows 30 customers per page. Active customers come first, then inactive ones, each sorted by name. Use the page links at the bottom to see more.

docs.title: Columns
docs.text:
Column What it shows Status A red label if the customer has at least one past due invoice, a green label if not Name Customer name. Inactive customers are shown in red Orders Number of orders for this customer Invoices Number of invoices for this customer, all statuses Income Total of all the customer's orders Past Due Unpaid balance of invoices whose due date is before today Not Yet Due Unpaid balance of invoices due today or later Unpaid Invoices Number of past due invoices (shown in a red label when above zero) Sent date Date of the last statement send, or - if none was recorded. A manual send only updates it when the email goes out. An automatic statement run also updates it, including a run that skipped a zero balance or failed Email Result of the last statement send: OK (green) or Failed! (red), empty if no statement was ever sent. Hover the label to see the message: Statement Delivered, Statement Not Sent (0.0$) (an automatic run skipped a zero balance, still shown as OK), or the error Delivery Day / Next Date Only when automatic statements are enabled. See Automatic Statements (buttons) Email, Print and the green Excel button

Unpaid means not Paid

An invoice counts as unpaid as long as its status is not Paid, whatever payments are recorded on it. Its amount is the invoice total with taxes minus the payments recorded. To remove an invoice from statements, set its status to Paid (see Sending Invoices & Recording Payments).

docs.title: The Send statement to customer window
docs.text:
Click the blue Email button on a customer's row. The Send statement to customer window opens. Starred (*) fields are required.

Field Prefilled with Notes To * The customer's Accountant Email Required. You can enter several addresses separated by commas Cc The customer's Accountant Email (CC) Optional. Several addresses allowed, separated by commas Bcc Empty Optional. Several addresses allowed, separated by commas

Both prefilled addresses come from the customer's record. To change them for future sends, edit the customer (see Managing Customers).

Below the fields, the window reads The customer will receive the statement in [icon] format:

  • a red PDF icon means the statement is attached as a PDF
  • a green Excel icon means the statement is attached as an Excel (.xlsx) file

The format follows the customer's Default Statement Format. You cannot change it in this window.

Click Send to send, or Close to cancel. While the email is being sent, the row shows a wait indicator in place of the Email button. When it finishes, the row refreshes.

docs.title: Notifications
docs.text:
Result Notification Row after send Sent Statement Sent! — The statement was sent successfully. Sent date set to today, Email shows OK (hover: Statement Delivered) Sending error Sending Statement Failed! — The statement was not sent due to [error]. Please try again or contact the administrator. Sent date unchanged, Email shows Failed! (hover shows the error)

Zero balance statements are still sent

A manual send does not check the balance. If the customer owes nothing, they still receive a statement showing zero amounts. Check the Past Due and Not Yet Due columns before you click Send.

docs.title: The email the customer receives
docs.text:
Part Content Subject <Your company> Statement of Account as of <YYYY-MM-DD> Subject (multi-office) <Your company> Statement of Account as of <YYYY-MM-DD> - <Office name>, where the office is the one you are currently working in Attachment (PDF) Statement of account as of <YYYY-MM-DD>.pdf Attachment (Excel) Statement of account as of <YYYY-MM-DD>.xlsx Body A Statement of Account for heading, a note that the attachment contains the current statement of the account as a PDF (or XLSX), Thank you!, and your company name

The date is the day the statement is sent. The email is sent through your invoice email settings.

Multi-office

When your account uses multiple offices, the emailed statement only includes the customer's invoices from the office you are currently working in, and the office name is added to the subject. Switch office before sending if you need another office's statement.

docs.title: PDF vs Excel Format
docs.text:
Each customer has a Default Statement Format on their customer record (in the Rate to apply for new orders section of the customer form):

Option What the customer receives PDF Format (default) The statement as a PDF attachment Excel (.xlsx) The statement as an Excel attachment
  1. Go to Customers, find the customer and edit them.
  2. Choose Default Statement Format.
  3. Save the customer.

This setting only controls the emailed attachment. The Print and Excel buttons on Customer Reports are available for every customer.

docs.title: PDF and Print version
docs.text:
The Print page and the PDF attachment use the same layout.

Left side:

  1. Customer Statement heading and the customer name.

  2. A summary box Customer Statement as of :

    Line Amount Past Due Unpaid balance of invoices whose due date is before today Not Yet Due Unpaid balance of invoices due today or later Total Billed Unpaid balance of all invoices that are not Paid

  3. A Detailed Summary with two tables, Past Due and Not Yet Due. Each lists Invoice (invoice number), Issue Date, Due Date and Amount (the remaining balance of that invoice).

  4. A Total Billed line at the bottom.

All amounts are followed by the customer's Default Currency (CAD or USD).

Right side (your company block): your logo, address, city and province/state, postal code, Tel:, Fax:, website, and the line THANK YOU FOR YOUR BUSINESS!

Per-order detail

On accounts where detailed statements are enabled, each invoice in the detailed tables is followed by one line per order on it, showing the container number, the order reference number and the order total. This is an account-level option. Contact UTX support to turn it on or off.

docs.title: Excel version
docs.text:
The Excel file has one sheet named Statement. The download from the green button is named <Customer name> Statement of Account as of <YYYY-MM-DD>.xlsx. The emailed attachment uses the name shown in the email table above.

Rows Content 1–2 Invoice Statement, then the customer name 4 Invoice Statement as of 5 Past Due Invoices and the past due balance (column D), currency (column E) 6 Due Invoices and the not yet due balance 7 Total Billed and the total unpaid balance 9 Detailed Summary 10 onward Past Due Invoices table with Invoice, Issue Date, Due Date, Amount columns Next Due Invoices table with the same columns Last Total Billed

Your company block (company name in capitals, address, city and province/state, postal code, Tel:, Fax:, website and THANK YOU FOR YOUR BUSINESS!) is in column H, rows 4 to 11. When detailed statements are enabled, per-order lines (container number, reference number, order total) appear under each invoice, as in the PDF.

Section names in the Excel file

In the Excel file, the Due Invoices section holds the invoices due today or later, the same invoices as the Not Yet Due section of the PDF. Past due invoices are under Past Due Invoices.

Print and Excel buttons are not filtered by office

The Print and Excel buttons, and the balance columns on the Customer Reports page, include all of the customer's unpaid invoices from every office. Only the emailed statement is limited to the current office on multi-office accounts.

docs.title: A customer is missing from Customer Reports
docs.text:
Solution

With [ALL CUSTOMERS] selected, only customers with at least one invoice that is not Paid are listed. If all of a customer's invoices are Paid, select the customer by name in the Customer dropdown and click Update Report. Also check the other pages of the list (30 customers per page).

docs.title: The Email column shows Failed!
docs.text:
Solution

Hover the Failed! label to read the error. Check the addresses in To, Cc and Bcc, then send again. If the error is about the mail server or authentication, ask your administrator to check the invoice email settings in Application Settings.

docs.title: The To field is empty when I open the window
docs.text:
Solution

To is prefilled from the customer's Accountant Email. If the customer has none, type the address in the window, or edit the customer and fill in Accountant Email (and Accountant Email (CC)) so it is prefilled next time.

docs.title: The customer received Excel but wanted a PDF (or the reverse)
docs.text:
Solution

Edit the customer and change Default Statement Format to PDF Format or Excel (.xlsx), save, then send the statement again.

docs.title: A paid invoice still appears on the statement
docs.text:
Solution

Statements include every invoice whose status is not Paid, even if payments cover the full amount. Set the invoice status to Paid (see Sending Invoices & Recording Payments).

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
Tips

  • Fill in Accountant Email, Accountant Email (CC) and Default Statement Format on each customer so statements go to the right people in the right format without retyping.
  • Mark invoices Paid as soon as payment is complete so statements only show what is really owed.
  • Check the Past Due and Not Yet Due columns before sending: a manual send goes out even when the balance is zero.
  • Use Print to preview the statement layout before emailing it (on multi-office accounts, remember the email only includes the current office's invoices).
  • For regular statements, set up Automatic Statements instead of sending each one by hand.

docs.title: Data Exports
docs.text: Every file you can download from UTX Freight in one place: where the button is, who can use it, which filters it follows, what columns it contains and what the file is called.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
UTX Freight has three kinds of downloads:

  • List exports (CSV): Customers, Shipper / Receiver, Equipments and open Orders. These are Admin only and ignore the filters and search on the page. Each one exports a fixed set of records.
  • Accounting exports: the Invoices export (QuickBooks columns or AR aging detail, Excel or CSV), the per-invoice EDI 210 file, the Income by Customer CSV, customer statements (Excel download, PDF or Excel by email), the Standard Aged Receivables Excel and the saved AR Export Excel files. The Invoices export follows every active filter and is capped at 20,000 invoices.
  • Garage: the Parts Inventory CSV.

What this page does not cover

Order documents and POD files are covered in Order Documents & POD. There is no data export for people (contacts), drivers, users, checks, expenses or warehouse records.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
To export a list (Admin):

  1. Open Customers, Shipper / Receiver, Equipments or Orders from the left menu.
  2. Click the green Export button. On Orders it is in the ACTION & ORDERS panel.
  3. The CSV downloads. It is the same file whatever filter or search is on screen.

To export invoices:

  1. Go to Invoices and filter the list (status tab, search, INVOICE DATE range, AR AGING option).
  2. Read the caption under EXPORT, for example Exports the 1,002 invoices currently listed (All unpaid) — not the whole database.
  3. Pick QuickBooks columns or AR aging detail, then Excel or CSV, and click Export.

docs.title: All Exports at a Glance
docs.text:
File Where Who can download Follows on-screen filters? Format File name Customers Customers > Export Admin No CSV <account>-companies-YYYY-MM-DD.csv Shippers / Receivers Shipper / Receiver > Export Admin No CSV <account>-shippers-receivers-YYYY-MM-DD.csv Equipment Equipments > Export Admin No CSV <account>-equipments-YYYY-MM-DD.csv Open orders Orders > ACTION & ORDERS > Export Admin No CSV <account>-orders-open-YYYY-MM-DD.csv Invoices Invoices > EXPORT panel Admin, Manager, Accountant Yes (status, search, date range, aging) Excel or CSV <account>-invoices-<status>[-<from>-to-<to>]-on-DDMMYY.xlsx / .csv EDI 210 Invoices > row menu > EDI 210 Admin, Manager, Accountant (only when EDI invoicing is enabled) One invoice CSV EDI210_<invoice number>_YYYYMMDD.csv Income by Customer Reports > Income by Customer > Export Report Users with the Reports menu Yes (customer, start and end date) CSV <account>-income_by_customer-<start>-<end>.csv Statement (Excel) Reports > Customer Reports > green Excel button Users with the Reports menu One customer Excel <Customer name> Statement of Account as of YYYY-MM-DD.xlsx Statement (email) Reports > Customer Reports > Email Users with the Reports menu One customer PDF or Excel attachment Statement of account as of YYYY-MM-DD.pdf / .xlsx Standard AR Excel Reports > Aged Receivables (AR) > Download Excel Users with the Reports menu Yes (As of Date:) Excel Standard_Aged_Receivables_YYYY-MM-DD.xlsx AR Export Excel Reports > AR Export > Generated Reports > Download Users with the Reports menu Yes (Report Period) Excel Starts with ar-report-, includes year and month Garage parts Garage > Parts > Export Admin, Manager, Garage (Garage add-on on) No CSV parts_catalog_YYYYMMDD.csv

<account> is the short account name UTX set up for your company. It is the same at the start of every list export file name. In invoice export file names it is written in lower case with hyphens.

docs.title: Access & Permissions
docs.text:
Role List CSVs (Customers, Shipper / Receiver, Equipments, Orders) Invoices export and EDI 210 Reports downloads (Income by Customer, statements, Standard AR, AR Export) Garage parts CSV Admin Yes Yes Yes Yes, when the Garage add-on is on Manager No Yes, for the offices they belong to Only if UTX has turned on report access for managers on your account (ask UTX support) Yes, when the Garage add-on is on Accountant No Yes, for the offices they belong to No (no Reports menu) No Dispatch No No (no Invoices menu) No No Garage No No No Yes, when the Garage add-on is on Customer, Warehouse, drivers No No No No

List exports are Admin only

The Export button on Customers, Shipper / Receiver, Equipments and Orders is only shown to Admins. If another role opens an export link directly (for example from a link an Admin shared), the download is refused and they are sent back to the dashboard with an access denied message. Ask an Admin to export the file.

See User Roles for the full permission list.

docs.title: List Exports (CSV)
docs.text:
All four list exports work the same way:
