  3. Pick a unit in the Equipment list. Each option shows Name - Type name with an icon:
    • green — available
    • orange — usable, with a warning (inspection due this month)
    • red — not available (inspection past due, mechanical issue, or already on another order in progress)
  4. Read the message and the status report below the list (see the tables below).
  5. Click Update Order. To remove the equipment from the order, pick -- No Equipment -- and click Update Order. Cancel closes without changes.

The list only contains enabled Chassis and Trailer units of your current office. Available units are listed first, then units with a warning, then unavailable ones; within each group, by type name and then by the number at the start of the unit name (names that do not start with a number come first).

Warnings never block

The red and orange messages are there to help you choose. UTX Freight still saves the assignment when you click Update Order, even for a unit that is past due, has a mechanical issue or is on another order.

docs.title: Message at the top
docs.text: Message Colour When Select an equipment for this order Blue No unit selected Click on UPDATE ORDER to assign this equipment Green The unit passes every check Please review the warnings below before assigning the equipment Orange Inspection is due this month; everything else is fine Please review the errors below before assigning the equipment Red At least one check is red

docs.title: Status report
docs.text: Under the list, a box shows one line per check: Active or Disabled, the inspection status, the mechanical status, and the assignment status (see Availability Rules). If the unit has notes, they appear last in red with a icon.

docs.title: Confirmation messages
docs.text:
Title Message When Order Updated The chassis for Order was updated to A unit was assigned Order Updated The chassis was released from the Order -- No Equipment -- was saved Order not updated! The order was not saved: . or The order could not be saved. Please try again or contact the administrator. The order could not be saved for another reason (for example a validation error on the order)

Who sees the button

On the Orders list, the button is only clickable for users allowed to change an order's equipment; others see the equipment name as a plain label.

Other ways equipment leaves an order

  • Tapping Ground Container in Yard Management removes the equipment from the order.
  • When you duplicate an order, the equipment is not copied to the new order.

docs.title: Available Equipments Modal
docs.text:
A quick, read-mostly view of the units you can assign, without leaving the order screens.

  • Orders: click Equipment in the ACTION & ORDERS box above the list.
  • Dispatch: click the Chassis header button.

The Available Equipments modal lists the same units as the Assign Equipment list (enabled Chassis and Trailer units of your current office, available first). It shows the Current Availability, Name/Number / Type, Next Inspection, Mechanical Status and Orders columns. You can change the Mechanical Status inline here too. Click Close to return.

Available to Admin, Manager, Dispatch and Customer Service.

docs.title: Borrowed Equipment
docs.text:
When you use a chassis that you do not own (for example one borrowed from another carrier), you can record its number on the order without creating a unit for it.

  1. Create one unit named exactly Borrowed (capital B) with a Chassis or Trailer type, and keep it enabled.
  2. Assign Borrowed to the order in the Assign Equipment modal.
  3. On the Orders list and the Dispatch board, an editable chassis number now appears under the button. Click it, type the number in Enter chassis number, and confirm. If you leave it empty it shows N/A.

Borrowed shows as already assigned

Borrowed is a single unit, so once it is on one order in progress the Assign Equipment modal flags it Already assigned to another order on the next one. This is expected. The warning does not block the assignment.

docs.title: Export
docs.text:
The green Export button at the top of the Equipments page downloads a CSV file. It is Admin only.

  • The export ignores the filters and the search box. It contains your equipment, enabled and disabled, sorted by name.
  • The file name ends with -equipments-YYYY-MM-DD.csv.
CSV column Content Id Record ID number Name Name/Number Equipment type display name Sub Category: Type name, for example Chassis: 40' - 2 AXLES Inspection date Next Inspection Date Serial number Serial Number Model Model Year Year Plate number Plate number Lessor Lessor or Morgagee Status Mechanical status Notes Notes Weight Tare weight Weight unit Lbs or Kgs Active true (enabled) or false (disabled)

See Data Exports for the other exports.

docs.title: Garage equipment is separate
docs.text: If you use the Garage add-on, the Equipment page in the Garage sidebar is a different list. Garage equipment is the trucks, trailers and chassis you service for garage customers, and it is used on garage work orders. It does not appear on the Equipments page, cannot be assigned to freight orders, and freight equipment does not appear in the Garage. See Garage Customers & Equipment.

docs.title: A unit doesn't appear in the Assign Equipment list
docs.text:
Solution

Only enabled units whose type is in the Chassis or Trailer sub category, in your current office, are listed. Check that the unit is enabled and that its type's Sub Category is not Truck (Manage Equipment Types Edit).

docs.title: I assigned a unit with a red warning and it saved
docs.text:
Solution

That is how it works. The availability checks are advisory and never block the assignment. Review the red lines in the status report before clicking Update Order.

docs.title: A unit shows Past Due although the inspection was only yesterday
docs.text:
Solution

Inspection is compared by month. A date in any earlier month is Past Due, and any date in the current month is Due. Update the Next Inspection Date after each inspection.

docs.title: A unit without an inspection date shows green
docs.text:
Solution

When no Next Inspection Date is set, the inspection status is In Compliance. Set a date to get due and past-due warnings and to make the unit appear under the Inspection Due and Inspection Past Due filters.

docs.title: I disabled a unit but it is still on orders
docs.text:
Solution

Disabling only stops the unit from being offered for new assignments. Open each order's Assign Equipment modal and pick another unit or -- No Equipment -- to release it.

docs.title: Who can re-enable a disabled unit?
docs.text:
Solution

Any Admin, Manager, Dispatch or Customer Service user can use Actions Enable. There is no restriction to the person who disabled it.

docs.title: How do I delete a unit?
docs.text:
Solution

You can't. The Actions menu has no Delete option for equipment. Disable the unit instead. An unused equipment type can be deleted from the Equipment Types page.

docs.title: A unit is FREE but the order still shows it
docs.text:
Solution

Only orders that are New, App. Made or Dispatched count as in progress. A Completed order keeps its equipment for the record, but the unit is free for new work.

docs.title: Saving fails with "has already been taken" on Name/Number
docs.text:
Solution

Equipment names must be unique across the whole installation, including other offices. Search with All selected to find the existing unit, which may be disabled.

docs.title: I don't see the Export button
docs.text:
Solution

Only Admins can export equipment.

Best practices

  • Set a Next Inspection Date on every unit, and check Inspection Due at the start of each month.
  • Change the Mechanical Status as soon as a unit goes to the garage, and back to Available when it returns.
  • Use Notes for anything a dispatcher should know before taking the unit — they show in red when it is picked.
  • Give each type the correct Sub Category so filters and assignment work as expected.
  • Disable units you sell or return instead of renaming them.

docs.title: Expenses & Checks
docs.text: Review what you owe drivers, brokers and other payees, and record the checks you write to pay them.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Expenses and checks are the "money out" side of UTX Freight. Each one has its own page in the left sidebar:

  • Expenses -- a list of every expense line entered in the Order Expenses panel of your orders (driver pay, broker fees, other costs). You can filter by payee, order status and payment status, and see which check paid each line.
  • Checks -- a list of the checks you issued. Each check records a vendor invoice (amount, number, date) and the payee's name and address.
  • Linking -- when your account has check expenses turned on (ask UTX support), you tick expense lines on a check. Saving the check marks those lines as Paid on the Expenses page.
  • Printing -- each check has a Print button that opens a printable check layout in a new tab.
  • Vendors -- every time you save a check, the payee's name and address are saved as a vendor, so you can pick them again on the next check. There is no separate vendor page.

Expenses are entered on the orders themselves, not on these pages. See Order Rates, Charges & Expenses.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
Already familiar with the feature? Here is the fastest path to pay a driver or broker:

  1. Add the expense on the order, in Order Expenses, and complete the order.
  2. Click Expenses in the left sidebar. Unpaid lines are shown by default.
  3. Pick the payee in Select a filter and click Search to see what you owe them.
  4. Click Checks in the left sidebar, then Add a new Check.
  5. Fill in Issue date, Check Number, the Vendor Invoice Information and the payee under Vendor Information (type a few letters in Search for a vendor to reuse a saved one).
  6. Under Check Expenses, tick the expense lines this check pays.
  7. Click Save Changes, then click Print on the check's row.

docs.title: Access & Permissions
docs.text:
Role Expenses page Checks Admin Yes Yes (view, add, edit, delete, print, history) Manager No sidebar link Yes, when your edition allows managers to manage checks Accountant No sidebar link Yes, when your edition allows accountants to manage checks All other roles No sidebar link No
  • The Expenses link appears in the left sidebar for Admin users only.
  • The Checks link appears for anyone who can manage checks. For Managers and Accountants this depends on your UTX Freight edition: check management for each of these roles is an option only UTX can turn on. If you are a Manager or Accountant and you do not see Checks, contact UTX support to ask whether it can be enabled for your edition.
  • Managers and Accountants only see and manage checks belonging to the offices they are assigned to.
  • Expense lines are added on orders by users who can manage rates (Admin, Manager, and Dispatch or Customer Service users with Can manage rates? checked). See Order Rates, Charges & Expenses and User Roles.

docs.title: Offices
docs.text:
Page Office behaviour Expenses Not limited to the current office. It lists expense lines from orders in all offices. Checks list Shows only the checks of the office you are currently working in. Check Expenses on the check form Offers only expense lines from orders in the current office.

If you work with several offices, switch to the right office before creating a check. See Multi-Office.

docs.title: The Expenses Page
docs.text: Click Expenses in the left sidebar. The page title is Expenses (subtitle Tracking of expenses for brokers). There is no "add" button here: expenses are created from the order forms.

docs.title: Filters
docs.text:
The Filters box at the top has three dropdowns and a Search button. The list refreshes in place when you click Search.

Filter Options Default Select a filter No Filter, or one payee. The list contains all your brokers, drivers and expense types, grouped by kind of payee. No Filter Order status All statuses, or one order status (for example Completed). Only statuses that exist on your orders are listed. All statuses Expense payment status Paid and Unpaid, Paid Only, Unpaid Only Unpaid Only
  • Paid Only shows lines that are linked to a check. Unpaid Only shows lines that are not linked to any check.
  • When you first open the page, it shows Unpaid Only for all payees and all order statuses.

docs.title: Columns
docs.text:
The list is sorted by order, newest first, and is split into pages.

Column What It Shows Type Driver, Broker or Expense (one of your Expense Types) Name The payee's name Category The charge type picked on the expense line, if any (one of your Charge Types whose Charge Type is Expense, see Charge Types & Taxes) Order The order reference Order Status The order's status, shown as an icon. Hover over it to see the status (for example Order Completed). Delivery Date The order's delivery date Paid green check when the line is linked to a check; red cross when it is not Check Info For paid lines, the check's payee name and number (for example Company XYZ #1042). Click it to open the check. Amount The expense amount (the Rate entered on the order) (button) View Check on paid lines -- opens the check's edit form

docs.title: TOTAL row
docs.text:
The last row of the table shows TOTAL, the sum of the Amount column. It adds up the lines shown on the current page of results only, not every page.

Find what you owe one payee

Pick the payee in Select a filter, set Order status to Completed and keep Unpaid Only. The TOTAL row then shows what you still owe them for completed orders (on the current page of results).

docs.title: The Checks List
docs.text: Click Checks in the left sidebar. The page title is Checks (subtitle Management of Checks). Checks are listed newest first, 50 per page.

docs.title: Columns
docs.text: Column What It Shows Check # The check number Vendor Invoice Date Date of the vendor's invoice Vendor Invoice Number The vendor's invoice number Vendor Invoice Amount The invoice amount, shown as currency Vendor The payee name Issue Date The date the check was issued Print Opens the printable check in a new tab. See Printing a Check. Actions View History, Edit, Delete

docs.title: Search
docs.text: Use the search box at the top right (placeholder Check #, Vendor or Invoice Number) and click Search. It matches any part of the check number, the vendor name or the vendor invoice number, ignoring upper/lower case.

docs.title: Actions menu
docs.text: Action What It Does View History Opens a History window listing each change to the check: the User who made it, the Changes (field and old/new values) and When. If there is nothing to show, it reads No history found for this item. Edit Opens the Edit Check form. Delete Deletes the check after an Are you sure? confirmation.

docs.title: Creating or Editing a Check
docs.text: Click Add a new Check at the top right of the Checks list (or Edit in a check's Actions menu). The form opens in a box titled Check Information.

docs.title: Check fields
docs.text: Field Required Notes Issue date Yes Date picker. Printed as the check date. Check Number No Free text. Shown in the list and in Check Info on the Expenses page. It is not printed on the check.

docs.title: Vendor Invoice Information
docs.text:
Field Required Notes Vendor invoice amount Yes The amount of the check. This is the amount printed on the check, in figures and in words. Vendor invoice number No Printed on the check stubs. Vendor invoice date No Date picker. Printed on the check stubs.

The check amount is not calculated from expenses

Ticking expense lines under Check Expenses does not fill or change Vendor invoice amount. Enter the amount yourself. Use the Expenses page and its TOTAL row to work out what you owe.

docs.title: Vendor Information
docs.text:
Field Required Notes Search for a vendor No Type at least 2 letters of a saved vendor's name and pick it from the suggestions. The fields below fill in automatically. See Vendors. Name Yes The payee, printed on the check. Address 1 No Street address. City No State No State or province. ZIP/Postal Code No Country No Canada or United States.

You can change any of the filled-in fields after picking a vendor.

Fill in the full address before printing

The printed check shows the payee's name, address, city, state, ZIP/postal code and country. Complete these fields before you click Print.

docs.title: Check Expenses
docs.text:
This section appears only when your account has check expenses turned on (ask UTX support). It lists expense lines as checkboxes, each showing the kind of payee (driver, broker or expense type), the payee name, the order reference and the amount.

Form Expense lines offered New Check Unpaid lines (not on any check) from Completed orders in the current office. Edit Check The same, plus the lines already linked to this check (ticked).
  • Tick a line and save: the line is linked to this check. On the Expenses page it shows the green Paid icon, the check in Check Info and a View Check button.
  • Untick a line on an existing check and save: the line is released and shows as unpaid again.
  • Expenses on orders that are not Completed are not offered. Complete the order first. See Order Workflow.

docs.title: Saving
docs.text: Click Save Changes. You return to the Checks list with the message Check was successfully created. (or Check was successfully updated.). Click Cancel to leave without saving.

docs.title: Step-by-step: Pay a driver by check
docs.text:
1. Click Expenses in the left sidebar.
  2. In Select a filter, pick the driver. Set Order status to Completed, keep Unpaid Only, and click Search.
  3. Note the TOTAL (or add up the lines you are paying).
  4. Click Checks in the left sidebar, then Add a new Check.
  5. Enter the Issue date and Check Number.
  6. Enter the amount in Vendor invoice amount (and the vendor invoice number and date, if any).
  7. In Search for a vendor, type the driver's name and pick it, or fill in Name and the address by hand.
  8. Under Check Expenses, tick the driver's lines.
  9. Click Save Changes.
  10. Click Print on the check's row and print it from your browser.

docs.title: Printing a Check
docs.text:
Click Print on a check's row in the Checks list. The check opens in a new browser tab, laid out for printing on check stock. Use your browser's print command to print it.

The printed check shows:

Part Content Check face DATE followed by the issue date (MM DD YYYY), the amount in words (written as ... dollars & ... cents), the amount in figures preceded by $, the payee's name, address, city, state and ZIP/postal code in capital letters, and the country Two stubs The issue date, the payee name, the vendor invoice date, the word Invoice, the vendor invoice number and the amount
  • The amount always comes from Vendor invoice amount.
  • The check number is not printed. Your company name and logo are not printed either.
  • Anyone who can see the check in the Checks list can print it.

Test your alignment

Print one check on plain paper first and hold it against your check stock to confirm the fields line up with your printer.

docs.title: Vendors
docs.text:
UTX Freight keeps a vendor directory automatically. There is no page to add, edit or delete vendors.

  • Saved on every check save. Each time a check is created or updated with a Name, its name and address (Name, Address 1, City, State, ZIP/Postal Code, Country) are added to the vendor directory, linked to the check's office.
  • Search for a vendor suggests saved vendors whose name contains what you typed (at least 2 letters, upper/lower case ignored). Suggestions come from the vendors of all offices. Entries with exactly the same name and address are shown only once. Picking one fills Name, Address 1, City, State, ZIP/Postal Code and Country.
  • Address changes create a new entry. If you change a vendor's address on a check, the new address is saved as well. The old one stays, so the same name can appear more than once in the suggestions, once per address.

Drivers and brokers are not vendors automatically

Drivers and brokers you pick as payees in Order Expenses are not added to the vendor directory. A payee becomes a vendor the first time you save a check with their name.

docs.title: I don't see Expenses or Checks in the sidebar
docs.text:
Solution

Expenses is shown to Admin users only. Checks is shown to Admins, and to Managers and Accountants only when your edition allows them to manage checks. Ask your administrator, or contact UTX support about your edition's options. See User Roles.

docs.title: An expense is missing from Check Expenses
docs.text:
Solution

The check form only offers expense lines that are (1) on a Completed order, (2) in the office you are currently working in, and (3) not already linked to another check. Complete the order, switch to the right office, or check on the Expenses page whether the line is already Paid (its Check Info shows which check).

docs.title: There is no Check Expenses section on the check form
docs.text:
Solution

Linking expenses to checks is an option that only UTX can turn on for your account. When it is off, checks record the vendor invoice and payee only, and the Expenses page keeps showing every line as unpaid. Contact UTX support if you need it enabled.

docs.title: The check amount doesn't match the expenses I ticked
docs.text:
Solution

The amount on the check is whatever you typed in Vendor invoice amount. It is never calculated from the ticked expenses. Edit the check and correct the amount.

docs.title: I linked the wrong expense to a check
docs.text:
Solution

Open the check (Actions > Edit, or View Check on the Expenses page), untick the line under Check Expenses, and click Save Changes. The line returns to unpaid.

docs.title: The Expenses page shows lines from another office
docs.text:
Solution

By design. The Expenses page is not limited to the current office; it lists expense lines from all offices. Use Select a filter and Order status to narrow it down. The Checks list, by contrast, shows only the current office's checks.

docs.title: A vendor shows up twice in the search
docs.text:
Solution

The search shows one entry per distinct name and address, from all offices. If a vendor's address was typed differently on different checks, each version appears. There is no vendor page to merge or remove entries. Pick the suggestion with the right address, or correct the fields after picking.

Best Practices

  • Record driver, broker and other costs in Order Expenses on every order, so the Expenses page is your complete payables list.
  • Complete orders promptly -- their expenses can only be linked to a check once the order is Completed.
  • Filter the Expenses page by payee with Unpaid Only before writing a check, and tick exactly those lines on the check.
  • Use Search for a vendor instead of retyping addresses, to keep the vendor directory clean.
  • Keep the Check Number filled in so you can find checks with Search and see them in Check Info.
  • Use View History to see who changed a check and when.

docs.title: Fuel Surcharge
docs.text: Set monthly fuel surcharge rates, per-customer overrides and exemptions on the Fuel Schedule page. UTX Freight applies the right rate to qualifying orders automatically.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The fuel surcharge is a percentage of an order's base rate. UTX Freight adds it automatically to Import, Export and Transfer orders that have Auto compute fuel surcharges for this order set to Yes. You set the rate once per month, and the system does the rest.

Here is how it works at a glance:

  • Add-on feature -- the Fuel Schedule exists only when your system has the fuel surcharge add-on.
  • Rates are monthly -- each rate covers one full calendar month. There are no weekly rates.
  • The order's delivery date decides which month's rate applies.
  • Customer overrides let you set a different rate for a specific customer in a given month.
  • Exempt customers get no fuel surcharge at all.
  • Recalculate updates every open order in a month in one step, after a preview.
  • Completed or invoiced orders are never changed.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
Already familiar with fuel surcharges? Here is the fastest path to setting a rate:

  1. Click Fuel Schedule in the left menu.
  2. In Quick Set Fuel Rate, enter the Rate (%) and pick the Month.
  3. Leave Customer (optional) on All customers (general).
  4. Click Save Rate.

The rate is now live for that month. Orders delivered in that month pick it up the next time they are created or saved.

Tip

Changed a rate after orders were already created? Click Recalculate on that month's row to update all open orders at once.

docs.title: Access & Permissions
docs.text:
The Fuel Schedule page requires the fuel surcharge add-on and one of these roles:

Role Access Level Admin Full access Manager Full access Accountant Full access Warehouse Full access Dispatch Only with Can manage rates? checked on their profile Garage, customers, drivers No access

Can manage rates? is a checkbox on the dispatcher's profile. See People & Invitations and User Roles.

How to get there:

  • Click Fuel Schedule ( icon) in the left menu. It is its own top-level item, just below Invoices. It is not under Charges or the Charge Types page.

Can't find Fuel Schedule?

  • If your system does not have the fuel surcharge add-on, the menu item is hidden. Opening the page directly sends you to the Charge Types list with the message Fuel surcharge addon is not enabled. See Add-ons & Options.
  • If you are a dispatcher, ask an administrator to check Can manage rates? on your profile.

docs.title: Page header and help panel
docs.text:
The page is titled Fuel Surcharge Schedule with the subtitle Monthly fuel surcharge rate management. On the right of the header is the Exempt Customers button (see Viewing all exempt customers).

Below the header, a blue panel titled How does the fuel surcharge work? is collapsed by default. Click it to open a short built-in guide covering when the surcharge is applied, how rates are matched, overrides and exemptions, the calculation, missing rates, recalculating and reading the table.

docs.title: Setting a Fuel Rate
docs.text: Use the Quick Set Fuel Rate form near the top of the page to create or update a rate.

docs.title: Quick Set Fuel Rate fields
docs.text: Field What It Does Rate (%) Required. The surcharge percentage. Enter 15 for 15%. Must be above 0 and at most 100. Decimals such as 15.5 are allowed. Month Required. A date picker, pre-filled with the 1st of the current month. Whatever day you pick is snapped to the 1st of that month (help text: The rate will apply starting the 1st of the selected month.). Service Type Defaults to intermodal. It is stored with the rate but has no effect on which orders get the rate. Saving a rate for a month that already has one overwrites it, whatever service you pick. Customer (optional) Leave on All customers (general) for the general rate (help text: Leave blank for general rate.). Pick an active customer to save a customer override instead. Copy Fwd Number of extra months (mo) to copy the same rate into, from 0 to 12. Defaults to 0. A value of N saves N + 1 months: the selected month plus the next N.

docs.title: Step-by-step: Create or update a monthly rate
docs.text:
1. Click Fuel Schedule in the left menu.
  2. Enter the Rate (%) -- for example, 15.
  3. Pick any day in the Month you want.
  4. Leave Customer (optional) on All customers (general) for a general rate.
  5. Optionally enter a number in Copy Fwd to repeat the rate for following months.
  6. Click Save Rate (it shows Saving... while working).

You see a message such as Saved general rate for 4 month(s). or, for an override, Saved Customer Name override for 1 month(s).

If a rate already exists for that month (and the same customer, or general), it is updated, not duplicated. Copy Fwd overwrites existing rates in the following months too.

Time Saver

If your rate stays the same for the next few months, set Copy Fwd to 3 and four months are saved in one click.

docs.title: Rate names
docs.text: Each rate is named automatically Fuel Surcharge N%, where N is the rate with the decimals cut off (not rounded). A 15.5% rate is named Fuel Surcharge 15%, but the Rate column shows 15.5% and the full 15.5% is used in the calculation. The name updates itself whenever the rate changes.

docs.title: Messages you may see
docs.text:
Message Meaning Saved general rate for N month(s). General rate saved for N months. Saved Customer override for N month(s). Customer override saved for N months. Invalid company selected. The selected customer does not belong to your office. Nothing was saved. Invalid date provided. The Month value could not be read as a date. Nothing was saved.

A rate of 0, a negative rate, or a rate above 100 is rejected and not saved.

docs.title: Understanding the Schedule Table
docs.text:
The table shows a fixed 9-month window: the 2 previous months, the current month, and the next 6 months. Months are listed oldest first.

Column What It Shows Month The month name, with General Rate in green underneath. The current month has an arrow and a Current label. Name The rate's name, such as Fuel Surcharge 15%, or — when there is no general rate. Rate The general rate in green, always shown with decimals (for example 15.0%). Click it to edit for current and future months. When there is no general rate: No rate in red with Orders this month won't have fuel surcharge applied. Orders Affected A badge with the number of open, non-exempt orders delivered that month. Shown only when the month has a general rate. May also show a red exempt note (see below). Actions Edit and Recalculate buttons (see below).

Customer override rows appear indented under their month's general rate, sorted by customer name.

docs.title: Green -- General Rate
docs.text: The General Rate is the default rate for all customers that month. Customers without an override use it.

docs.title: Blue -- Customer Override
docs.text: A blue customer name on a grey indented row is a custom rate for that customer in that month. It takes priority over the general rate.

docs.title: Red -- Attention Needed
docs.text:
• No rate -- no general rate is defined for that month.
  • (N exempt — charges pending removal) -- N open orders of exempt customers still carry fuel charges. Recalculate the month to clear them.

docs.title: Other visual indicators
docs.text:
• Current -- a blue label, bold text and a highlighted row mark the current month.
  • Faded rows -- past months are faded and their rates cannot be edited inline.
  • Double borders -- a double line separates each month.

docs.title: Orders Affected and the exempt note
docs.text:
• The badge counts open orders (see Which orders count as open) delivered in that month for customers who are not exempt. It includes customers who have an override. Override rows themselves show —.
  • The badge appears only when the month has a general rate and at least one such order.
  • The red (N exempt — charges pending removal) note counts open orders for exempt customers that still have a fuel charge. It can appear even in a month with No rate.

docs.title: Action buttons
docs.text:
Month General rate exists Buttons shown Current or future Yes Edit, Recalculate Current or future No, but exempt charges are pending Recalculate only Current or future No, and nothing pending None Past Yes Edit only Past No None

Customer override rows show a red Remove button for current and future months only.

docs.title: Inline edit (current and future months)
docs.text:
1. Click the rate value (the green general rate or a blue override rate).
  2. In the Enter new rate (%) pop-up, type the new rate.
  3. Confirm. The page reloads with the new rate and name.

The same rule applies: above 0, at most 100.

docs.title: The Edit button
docs.text:
Edit on a general rate row opens the full charge type form (Order Charge Information). It is available for past months too, even though past rates cannot be edited inline. Rates in the Historical Rates table also have an Edit button. Override rows have no Edit button; change their rate inline.

After you click Save in that form, you land on the Charge Types list (where fuel rates are hidden). Click Back to Fuel Schedule to return.

Applicable on (Month)

A rate is matched to orders by month, so Applicable on (Month) should always be the 1st of a month. If you change it, pick the 1st.

Changing a rate does not change orders by itself

Saving a new rate, by any method, does not touch existing orders. They pick up the new rate the next time they are saved, or all at once when you click Recalculate (current and future months only).

docs.title: Customer Overrides (Custom Rates)
docs.text: Need a different rate for one customer? Create an override for that month.

docs.title: Step-by-step: Set a custom rate for a customer
docs.text:
1. Click Fuel Schedule in the left menu.
  2. In Quick Set Fuel Rate, pick the customer in Customer (optional).
  3. Enter the Rate (%).
  4. Pick the Month, and optionally set Copy Fwd.
  5. Click Save Rate.

The override appears indented under that month's general rate. For orders of that customer delivered in that month, the override is used instead of the general rate. The order's fuel charge note then reads Computed Fuel Surcharge N% (custom rate for Customer).

Overrides are month by month

An override covers only the months you saved it for. Use Copy Fwd to cover several months. A month with an override but no general rate still appears in the Missing Rates banner, because the banner checks general rates only.

docs.title: Removing an override
docs.text:
1. Click the red Remove button on the override row (current and future months only).
  2. Confirm Remove fuel surcharge override for Customer?

What happens next:

  • If orders already have fuel charges linked to the override, those charges are moved to that month's general rate. Their amounts do not change until the orders are recalculated or saved.
  • If there are linked charges and no general rate for that month, nothing is removed and you see Cannot delete override: it has linked charges and no general rate exists for this month. Set a general rate first.
  • On success you see Removed fuel surcharge override for Customer. If that customer has open orders in the month, the message adds N open order(s) for this customer may need recalculation — use the Recalculate button for Month Year.

Recalculate after removing an override

Click Recalculate on that month so the customer's open orders move to the general rate amount.

docs.title: Exempting a Customer
docs.text: Some customers have agreements with no fuel surcharge. Mark them as exempt.

docs.title: Step-by-step: Exempt a customer
docs.text:
1. Open the customer list and click Edit on the customer. See Managing Customers.
  2. Find the Fuel Surcharge section (shown only with the add-on).
  3. Check Exempt from Fuel Surcharge. Its hint reads: When checked, fuel surcharge will NOT be applied to this customer's orders. Use this for customers who have negotiated no fuel surcharge.
  4. Click Save Changes.

You return to the customer list with Customer was successfully updated. If you just turned the exemption on and the customer has open (not completed, not invoiced) orders that already carry fuel charges, a yellow warning also appears:

Customer has N open order(s) with fuel surcharges that need recalculation. Visit the Fuel Schedule to recalculate.

Exempting does not clean up existing orders by itself

Existing fuel charges stay on the customer's open orders until each order is saved again or you click Recalculate for the affected month(s). On the next save of an open Import, Export or Transfer order with auto-compute on, the exempt customer's fuel charge is removed.

To remove an exemption, uncheck the box and click Save Changes. Open orders get a fuel charge again the next time they are saved or recalculated.

docs.title: Viewing all exempt customers
docs.text:
Click Exempt Customers in the top-right of the Fuel Schedule page. The badge on the button shows how many active customers are exempt.

The Exempt Customers window lists them (Customer Name, with an Edit button for each) under the line These customers will not have fuel surcharge applied to their orders. If none are exempt, it says No customers are currently exempt from fuel surcharge.

docs.title: Stale Charges on Exempt Customers
docs.text:
When a customer is exempt but their open orders still carry fuel charges, those charges are stale. The schedule flags them in red on the month's row:

Example

(3 exempt — charges pending removal)

How to fix it: click Recalculate on that month's row (the button appears for current and future months even when the month has no general rate). The preview lists those orders under Exempt Customers, and confirming removes their fuel charges.

docs.title: Recalculating Fuel Charges
docs.text: Recalculate re-runs the charge calculation on every open order delivered in a month, so they all use the current rate.

docs.title: Step-by-step: Recalculate a month
docs.text:
1. On the Fuel Schedule page, find the current or future month.
  2. Click Recalculate on that month's row.
  3. Review the Recalculate Fuel Surcharges preview (subtitle Month of Month Year).
  4. Click Yes, Update These Orders, or Cancel to close without changes.

You return to the Fuel Schedule with Recalculated charges for N open order(s) in Month Year.

docs.title: What the preview shows
docs.text:
At the top: N order(s) will be recalculated. (non-exempt orders only), then General fuel surcharge rate: N% (or No general fuel surcharge rate is defined for this month. in red), and, when relevant, N order(s) use a custom company rate.

The main table (under Preview: Review the changes below before confirming.) lists non-exempt open orders, sorted by customer and delivery date:

Column What It Shows Customer The order's customer. Order # The order number. The link opens the Orders list searched for that number in a new tab -- not the order itself. Type Import, Export or Transfer. Delivery Delivery date (e.g. Oct 14). Base Rate The order's base rate. Rate The fuel % that will apply: green for the general rate, blue with a Custom label for an override. Shown as a whole number. Current Fuel The fuel amount on the order now. New Fuel The fuel amount after recalculation. Difference Orange with + for an increase, green for a decrease, grey for no change. New Total The expected order total after recalculation.

If exempt customers have fuel charges in that month, a second section appears: Exempt Customers — fuel surcharge will be removed from these orders. Its columns are Customer (with a red Exempt label), Order #, Current Fuel and New Fuel (always $0.00).

The footer reads This will update fuel surcharges on all listed orders. next to the Yes, Update These Orders button.

If there is nothing to do, the preview says No open orders found for this month. There is nothing to recalculate. and Only import, export, and transfer orders that are not completed or invoiced are included. The confirm button is not shown.

docs.title: What recalculation actually does
docs.text:
• Each open order in the month (exempt or not) is saved again with a full charge refresh. This also refreshes the automatic Terminal Fee (Import and Export orders) and the order total, not just fuel.
  • Orders with Auto compute fuel surcharges for this order set to No are skipped for fuel. Their fuel charge does not change -- including exempt customers' orders.
  • Completed and invoiced orders are never changed.
  • If the month has no rate at all (no general rate and no override for the customer), existing fuel charges on non-exempt orders are kept as they are.

Past months cannot be recalculated

Past months have no Recalculate button. To fix a past month, open and save the orders one by one (if they are still open), or adjust their charges individually. See Order Charges & Expenses.

docs.title: How the Fuel Amount Is Calculated
docs.text:
Formula

Base Rate x Fuel Rate % = Fuel Surcharge Amount, rounded to the nearest cent.

Example: base rate $1,000, fuel rate 15% → $150.00 fuel surcharge.

The charge is added to the order's charges with the note Computed Fuel Surcharge 15% (or Computed Fuel Surcharge 15% (custom rate for Customer) for an override). The % in the note is a whole number, but the exact rate is used for the amount.

docs.title: Calculation rules
docs.text:
Rule Detail When fuel is computed When an order is created, each time it is saved from the order or dispatch forms, when its return terminal is changed inline, when an order is duplicated, and when you click Recalculate. Order types Import, Export and Transfer only. Auto-compute Auto compute fuel surcharges for this order must be Yes (the default for new orders). Open orders only Not Completed and not invoiced. After that the fuel charge is final. Which month The month of the order's delivery date. An order with no delivery date gets no new fuel charge, and any existing one is left as it is. Which rate The customer's override for that month if there is one, otherwise the general rate. Replacement The previous fuel charge is removed and replaced on every computation. Manual edits to it are overwritten. Exempt customers Any fuel charge is removed and none is added. No rate for the month Nothing is changed: no fuel charge is added, and an existing one is left as it is.

Delivery date decides the month

If you move an order's delivery date into another month, the next save uses the new month's rate.

docs.title: Which orders count as open
docs.text:
For Orders Affected, the exempt note and Recalculate, an order counts as open when it is:

  • in the office you are working in,
  • not invoiced,
  • not Completed,
  • an Import, Export or Transfer order,
  • delivered (by delivery date) within that calendar month.

docs.title: Missing Rates Warning
docs.text:
If the current month or any of the next 5 months has no general rate, an amber banner appears near the top of the page: Missing Rates: followed by a red label for each month, and These months have no fuel surcharge rate defined. Orders delivered in these months will not have fuel surcharges applied.

Customer overrides do not count -- a month is listed until it has a general rate.

Stay Ahead

Set rates a few months in advance with Copy Fwd so the banner stays empty.

docs.title: Historical Rates (before March 2026)
docs.text:
The monthly Fuel Schedule replaced the old setup in March 2026. Weekly fuel rates no longer exist: all older weekly rates were converted to monthly rates, keeping one rate per month (per customer and office). If that month already had a monthly rate, it was kept; otherwise the earliest week's rate was kept. Existing order charges were moved to the kept rate, and their amounts were not changed.

If your account has general rates dated before March 2026, a Historical Rates (before March 2026) panel appears at the bottom of the page. It shows the 6 most recent of them, with the columns ID, Name, Month, Rate, Service and Actions (Edit).

These rates only matter for orders delivered in those months. Set all new rates with Quick Set Fuel Rate.

docs.title: Related Features
docs.text:
• Setup checklist -- with the add-on, the onboarding checklist has the step Set this month's fuel surcharge (button Open Fuel Schedule). It is done only when the current month has a general rate, so it reopens at the start of every month: last month's rate does not carry forward. See Setup Checklist.
  • Charge Types -- monthly fuel rates are stored as charge types but are hidden from the Charge Types list when the add-on is on. That page shows a Back to Fuel Schedule button. See Charge Types, Expense Types & Taxes.
  • Order charges -- how the fuel charge appears on an order and the Auto compute fuel surcharges for this order setting. See Order Charges & Expenses.

docs.title: Customer was exempted but still has fuel charges
docs.text:
Solution

Exempting does not remove existing charges by itself. On the Fuel Schedule, find the month(s) with the red charges pending removal note and click Recalculate. The orders appear under Exempt Customers in the preview with New Fuel at $0.00. If an order still keeps its charge, check that Auto compute fuel surcharges for this order is Yes -- orders with auto-compute off are skipped.

docs.title: No Recalculate button for a past month
docs.text:
Solution

By design, Recalculate only appears on the current and future months. Past months only have Edit. Fix past-month orders individually.

docs.title: Rate was changed but orders still show the old amount
docs.text:
Solution

Changing a rate does not update existing orders. Click Recalculate on that month, review the preview, then click Yes, Update These Orders.

docs.title: Customer has a custom rate but orders use the general rate
docs.text:
Solution

Check that the override is saved for the month of the order's delivery date (overrides are per month). If the override was added after the orders were saved, click Recalculate. The Service Type does not matter.

docs.title: An order has no fuel surcharge
docs.text:
Solution

Check that: the month of the delivery date has a rate; the order is Import, Export or Transfer; Auto compute fuel surcharges for this order is Yes; the customer is not exempt; the order is not completed or invoiced. Then save the order or recalculate the month.

docs.title: An order still has a fuel charge in a month with "No rate"
docs.text:
Solution

When a month has no rate, existing fuel charges are left untouched (they are not set to zero). Set a rate for the month and recalculate, or remove the charge from the order manually.

docs.title: I picked a different Service Type and my old rate was replaced
docs.text:
Solution

Expected. There is one general rate per month (and one override per customer per month). Service Type does not create a separate rate.

docs.title: "Cannot delete override" when removing a custom rate
docs.text:
Solution

The override is already used by order charges and the month has no general rate to move them to. Set a general rate for that month with Quick Set Fuel Rate, then click Remove again.

docs.title: Clicking an order number in the preview opens a search
docs.text:
Solution

By design, the link opens the Orders list searched for that order number in a new tab. Open the order from there.

docs.title: Tips for managing fuel surcharges
docs.text:
Best Practices

Set rates early. Use Copy Fwd so the Missing Rates banner stays empty.

Watch for red. No rate and charges pending removal always need attention.

Recalculate after changes. After changing a rate, exempting a customer or removing an override, recalculate the affected current and future months.

Read the preview. Check the Difference column before clicking Yes, Update These Orders.

docs.title: Garage Customers & Equipment
docs.text: Keep the list of people and companies your garage works for, and the trucks, trailers and chassis you service for them, with a full service history per unit.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
• Customers (Garage sidebar) lists your garage customers: a person (first and last name) with an optional company name, email, phone and Accountant Email.
  • Equipment (Garage sidebar) lists the units you service. Each unit is a Truck, Trailer or Chassis and can have an Owner (Customer).
  • The equipment form has a Decode button that fills Year, Make and Model from the VIN using the public NHTSA VIN decoder.
  • Each unit has a Service History page with its work orders, Total Work Orders, Total Spent and Last Service.
  • The customer's Accountant Email is added in CC on garage invoice, work summary and statement emails.
  • Equipment can be disabled and enabled again. Garage customers and garage equipment are kept rather than deleted, so their history stays available.
  • Both lists show only the office you are currently working in.
  • Garage customers and garage equipment are separate from the freight Customers and Equipments pages. See How these differ from freight Customers and Equipments.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
1. Open the Garage: left menu Garage.
  2. In the Garage sidebar, click Customers New Customer. Enter the First Name and Last Name (required), plus Email, Accountant Email, Company Name if you have them, and click Create Customer.
  3. In the Garage sidebar, click Equipment New Equipment. Pick the Equipment Type, enter the Unit Number and VIN, click Decode to fill year, make and model, choose the Owner (Customer) and click Create Equipment.
  4. Back on Customers, click the button on the customer's row to start a work order for them.
  5. To see everything done on a unit, click the (Service History) button on its row in Equipment.

docs.title: Access & Permissions
docs.text:
The Garage is an add-on. When it is not turned on for your installation, the Garage menu item does not appear and the Garage pages send you back to the dashboard.

Role Garage Customers (list, add, edit) Garage Equipment (list, add, edit, disable/enable, service history) Admin Yes Yes Manager Yes Yes Garage Yes Yes Dispatch, Accountant, other roles No No

Where to find it:

  • Left menu Garage Garage sidebar Customers
  • Left menu Garage Garage sidebar Equipment
  • Back to TMS at the bottom of the Garage sidebar returns you to the freight side.

Current office

Garage customers and equipment belong to an office. The lists, the edit pages and the Service History page only show records of the office you are currently working in. With multiple offices, switch office to see another office's garage records. See User Roles for what each role can do elsewhere.

docs.title: The Customers list
docs.text:
The page header reads Customers — Manage garage customers, with a New Customer button on the right.

Tabs

Tab Shows Active Customers that are active (the default). Every customer you create is active. Disabled Customers that have been marked inactive.

Search

Type in the Search customers... box and press Enter or click . The search matches part of the first name, last name or company name (not email or phone) and is not case sensitive. It searches within the tab you are on.

Columns

The list is sorted by last name, then first name, 25 customers per page.

Column Shows Name First and last name Company Company name, or - Phone Phone, or - Email Email, or - Accountant Email Accountant email, or - Actions The three buttons below

Row actions

Button Tooltip What it does New work order for (name) Opens a new work order with this customer already selected. See Garage Work Orders. Work summary for (name) Opens the customer's work summary report. See Garage Reports. Edit (name) Opens the customer form.

When there are no customers in the tab, the list shows No customers yet — Add your first customer to start creating work orders. with a New Customer button.

docs.title: Creating or editing a customer
docs.text:
1. Click New Customer (or the button on a row to edit).
  2. Fill in the fields below.
  3. Click Create Customer (new) or Update Customer (edit). Click Cancel to go back to the list without saving.

The list shows Customer created successfully. or Customer updated successfully. If something is wrong, the form stays open with the errors in a red box at the top.

Field Required Notes First Name * Yes Last Name * Yes Email No Must be a valid email address if filled. Garage invoices, work summaries and statements are sent to this address. Phone No Free text Accountant Email No Must be a valid email address if filled. Hint under the field: CC'd automatically on invoice and work summary emails. Company Name No Shown in brackets after the name wherever a customer is picked (see below) Notes No Free text

The edit page title is Edit Customer: (name), and the form card heading reads Edit: (name).

Accountant Email

Use Accountant Email when invoices should also reach the customer's bookkeeper. It is added in CC on garage invoice emails and work summary emails, as the hint says, and also on garage statement of account emails (but not on a statement test send). The main Email stays in the To field.

docs.title: How a customer's name is displayed
docs.text:
Outside the Name column of the Customers list (for example in the work order Customer search, the Owner (Customer) dropdown and the Owner column on Equipment), a customer appears as:

  • First Last (Company Name) when a company name is filled in, for example Jane Smith (Smith Hauling)
  • First Last when it is not

Fill in Company Name so customers with similar names are easy to tell apart.

docs.title: Adding a customer from a work order
docs.text: You don't have to leave the work order form to add a customer. On the work order form, the green button next to the Customer * field (tooltip Quick create customer) opens Quick Create Customer, which asks for First Name *, Last Name *, Phone and Company. Click Create & Select. If first or last name is empty you see First name and last name are required. The new customer is created in your current office, selected on the work order, and a Customer created message appears. The button is hidden while the work order is on a draft invoice, because the customer can't be changed then. Add the email and accountant email later from Customers.

docs.title: Customers you no longer serve
docs.text: Garage customers are kept with their work order history. To flag a customer you no longer serve for your team, add a note in Notes.

docs.title: The Equipment list
docs.text:
The page header reads Equipment — Track trucks, trailers, and chassis, with a New Equipment button on the right.

Tabs

Tab Shows Active Enabled units (the default) Disabled Units you have disabled

Type chips

Next to the tabs are three chips: Truck, Trailer, Chassis. Click one to show only that type within the current tab. The selected chip is highlighted. There is no "All" chip: to remove the type filter, click the Active or Disabled tab again.

Search

Type in the Search equipment... box and press Enter or click . The search matches part of the unit number, make, model, VIN or license plate and is not case sensitive. It searches within the tab you are on.

Columns

The list is sorted by type (alphabetically: Chassis, Trailer, Truck), then unit number, 25 units per page.

Column Shows Type A coloured badge: Truck (blue), Trailer (green), Chassis (orange) Unit # Unit number, or - Year / Make / Model For example 2019 Freightliner Cascadia, or - VIN VIN, or - Plate License plate, or - Owner The owner's display name (see How a customer's name is displayed), or - Actions The buttons below

Row actions

Button What it does (tooltip Service History) Opens the unit's Service History page Opens the equipment form (red, Active tab) Disables the unit after you confirm Disable this equipment? in the Are you sure? dialog (green, Disabled tab) Enables the unit again, no confirmation

When there is nothing to show, the list reads No equipment yet — Track trucks, trailers, and chassis serviced in your garage. with a New Equipment button.

docs.title: Creating or editing equipment
docs.text:
1. Click New Equipment (or the button on a row, or Edit on the Service History page).
  2. Fill in the fields below. Use Decode to fill year, make and model from the VIN.
  3. Click Create Equipment (new) or Update Equipment (edit). Click Cancel to go back to the list.

The list shows Equipment created successfully. or Equipment updated successfully. Errors appear in a red box at the top of the form.

Field Required Notes Equipment Type * Yes Truck, Trailer or Chassis. Starts on Select type... Unit Number No Your or the customer's unit number Year No A number; the field accepts 1970 to 2030 Make No Placeholder e.g. Freightliner, Volvo Model No VIN No Placeholder Enter 17-character VIN, with the Decode button next to it License Plate No Odometer No A whole number, 0 or more. Also raised automatically from a work order's Odometer In (see below) Owner (Customer) No The garage customer who owns the unit. Starts on No owner Notes No Free text

The edit page title is Edit Equipment: (unit name), and the form card heading reads Edit: (unit name).

Odometer updates from work orders

When you save a work order for this unit with an Odometer In value higher than the unit's current Odometer, the unit's Odometer is updated to that value automatically. A lower value never replaces it.

docs.title: How a unit's name is displayed
docs.text: Outside the list, a unit is shown as Type - Unit Number - Year Make Model, skipping the parts that are empty. For example Truck - 104 - 2019 Freightliner Cascadia, or just Trailer when only the type is set. The year is only shown when a make or model is filled in. On a work order, the selected unit also shows its owner after a dash: Truck - 104 - 2019 Freightliner Cascadia — Jane Smith (Smith Hauling).

docs.title: VIN Decode
docs.text:
The purple Decode button (tooltip Decode VIN via NHTSA) looks the VIN up in the free public VIN decoder of the U.S. National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA), directly from your browser.

  1. Type or paste the VIN in the VIN field.
  2. Click Decode. The button shows Decoding... while it waits (up to 10 seconds).
  3. If the decoder returns any of make, model or model year, the Year, Make and Model fields are filled in and a VIN Decoded message shows the result for 2 seconds.
  4. Check the values and click Create Equipment or Update Equipment. Decoding alone does not save anything.
Message Meaning Please enter a valid VIN (at least 11 characters). The VIN field is empty or shorter than 11 characters. Nothing is sent. VIN Decoded — (year make model) The fields were filled in. VIN was found but no make/model/year data returned. Please enter manually. The decoder answered but had no make, model or year for this VIN. Unexpected response from NHTSA. Please enter vehicle details manually. The decoder's answer could not be read. Could not reach NHTSA VIN decoder. Please enter vehicle details manually. The decoder could not be reached (no internet, blocked, or no answer within 10 seconds).

Decoder coverage

NHTSA mainly covers vehicles sold in the U.S. A Canadian-market or older unit may decode only partly or not at all. You can always type the values yourself. The VIN itself is not checked for length or format when you save.

docs.title: The Owner (Customer) dropdown
docs.text: The Owner (Customer) dropdown lists active garage customers sorted by last name, shown with their display name. Adding a Company Name to your customers makes them easy to tell apart.

docs.title: Adding equipment from a work order
docs.text: On the work order form, the green button next to the Equipment field (tooltip Quick create equipment) opens Quick Create Equipment: Equipment Type * (if empty you see Equipment type is required.), Unit Number, Year, Make, Model and License Plate. Click Create & Select: the unit is created in your current office, selected on the work order, and an Equipment created message appears. When a customer is already selected on the work order, the new unit is linked to that customer as its owner. VIN, odometer and notes can be added later from Equipment. See Garage Work Orders.

docs.title: Disabling and enabling equipment
docs.text:
1. On the Active tab, click the red button on the unit's row.
  2. In the Are you sure? dialog (Disable this equipment?), click Yes, proceed.
  3. The list shows (unit name) disabled. and the unit moves to the Disabled tab.

To bring it back, open the Disabled tab and click the green button. The list shows (unit name) enabled.

A disabled unit:

  • no longer appears in the work order Equipment search, so it can't be picked for new work orders,
  • keeps its service history and stays on any existing work orders,
  • can still be opened and edited from the Disabled tab.

There is no delete for garage equipment.

docs.title: Service History
docs.text:
Click on a unit's row to open its page. The title is the unit's display name, with a type badge, the unit number and the VIN under it, and an Edit button on the right.

Detail cards

Card Shows Year / Make / Model For example 2019 Freightliner Cascadia, or - Odometer The unit's current Odometer (from the equipment form, or raised by a work order's Odometer In), with thousands separators, or - License Plate Plate, or - Owner Owner's display name, or -

Stats

Stat How it is calculated Total Work Orders Every work order for this unit, in any status, including estimates Total Spent For all those work orders (including estimates and work orders not yet invoiced): parts (quantity × charge price) plus labour (hours × rate). It does not include the shop supplies fee, taxes or payments Last Service The most recent Date In of a work order that is not an estimate, for example Mar 04, 2026. Shows None when the unit only has estimates or no work orders

Total Spent is not an invoiced total

Total Spent is the sum of parts and labour lines on the unit's work orders, not what was billed or paid. To see billed and paid amounts, use Garage Invoices or Garage Reports.

Service History table

Lists every work order for the unit, newest Date In first, 20 per page.

Column Shows WO # The work order number (for example #123), as a link to the work order Date Date In, or - Description The work order description, cut to 50 characters Status Estimate (yellow), Approved (blue), In progress (purple), Completed (green), Invoiced (grey) Total Parts + labour + Shop Supplies Fee of that work order, before taxes

With no work orders, the table shows No service history for this equipment yet. Click Back to Equipment at the bottom to return to the list.

docs.title: How these differ from freight Customers and Equipments
docs.text:
The Garage keeps its own customers and equipment. Nothing is shared or synced with the freight side.

Garage Freight Customers page Garage sidebar Customers Left menu Customers (Customers) A customer is A person (first and last name) with an optional company name A company, with people (users) invited under it Disable / delete customer Customers are kept with their history Available (see Customers) Equipment page Garage sidebar Equipment Left menu Equipments (Equipment) Equipment type Fixed: Truck, Trailer, Chassis Types you create under the Chassis, Truck or Trailer sub categories Equipment is used on Garage work orders Freight orders (chassis and trailers only) Tracks VIN, plate, odometer, owner, service history Inspection date, mechanical status, availability Who can manage customers Admin, Manager, Garage Admin, Manager (Dispatch too when UTX support has turned this on for your account, see Customers) Who can manage equipment Admin, Manager, Garage Admin, Manager, Dispatch, Customer Service

Same truck in both places

If you service your own fleet in the Garage, enter the unit again under Garage Equipment (for example with your company as a garage customer and owner). Work orders, inspection dates and mechanical status are not copied between the two lists.

docs.title: How do I mark a garage customer we no longer serve?
docs.text:
Solution

Garage customers are kept with their work order history. Add a note in Notes so your team knows the customer is no longer active.

docs.title: A unit doesn't show up when I search for it on a work order
docs.text:
Solution

The work order Equipment search only shows active units of your current office, and once a Customer is selected on the work order it only shows that customer's units (the Owner (Customer) must match). Check the Disabled tab on Equipment and enable the unit with the green button, set the unit's Owner (Customer) to the work order's customer, or switch to the office the unit was created in.

docs.title: Decode says it could not reach NHTSA
docs.text:
Solution

The lookup runs from your browser to the public NHTSA service. Check your internet connection, and that your network or browser extensions don't block it, then try again. If it still fails, type Year, Make and Model yourself and save.

docs.title: The accountant didn't get the invoice email
docs.text:
Solution

Open the customer from Customers and check the Accountant Email is filled and spelled correctly. It is added in CC only when the email is sent after it was saved.

docs.title: Total Spent doesn't match the customer's invoices
docs.text:
Solution

Total Spent adds parts and labour of every work order on the unit, including estimates and work orders not yet invoiced, and leaves out the shop supplies fee and taxes. Invoices only cover invoiced work orders (an invoice can group several, possibly for other units) and can add taxes and discounts. See Service History.

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
Best Practices

  • Fill in Company Name for every customer that is a business. It shows next to the name everywhere you pick a customer.
  • Add an Accountant Email for customers whose bookkeeper should get invoices, so you don't have to forward them.
  • Always enter the VIN and use Decode, then check the result. The VIN is also searchable on the Equipment list.
  • Set the Owner (Customer) on every unit. On a work order, once a customer is selected, the Equipment search lists only that customer's units, so a unit without an owner won't show up there.
  • Disable units that are sold or scrapped instead of leaving them active. Their service history is kept.
  • Enter Odometer In on each work order. It keeps the unit's Odometer current automatically, so the Service History page shows the latest reading.

docs.title: Garage Invoices & Payments
docs.text: Bill your garage customers for completed work orders, email the invoice as a PDF, and record the payments you receive.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Garage invoices live in the Garage area under Invoices (subtitle Manage garage invoices and payments). They are kept completely separate from freight invoices: they have their own list, their own numbering and their own payments, and they never appear on the freight Invoices page.

  • Built from work orders: an invoice bills one or more Completed work orders for a single customer. See Garage Work Orders.
  • Single or bundled: Generate Single Invoice bills one work order in one click. Bundle with Other Work Orders (or New Invoice) lets you pick several work orders for the same customer.
  • Numbering: every invoice gets a number like GRG-00001 from the Invoice Prefix in Garage Settings. Numbers are never reused.
  • Totals: subtotal of parts and labour, an optional discount (applied before taxes), shop supplies, GST and QST.
  • Lifecycle: Draft > Sent > Partially paid > Paid, or Void at any point.
  • Email: Email Invoice sends the invoice PDF to the customer, with the customer's accountant in CC.
  • Payments: record payments on the invoice page. The status moves to Partially paid or Paid automatically.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
To invoice one completed work order:

  1. Open the work order (its status must be Completed).
  2. Click Generate Single Invoice and confirm. A Draft invoice opens.
  3. Check the totals, then click Email Invoice (which also marks it Sent) or Mark Sent if you deliver it another way.

To bundle several work orders on one invoice:

  1. Go to Invoices and click New Invoice.
  2. Pick the Customer and click Continue.
  3. Tick the work orders to include, adjust the invoice fields, and click Create Invoice.

To record a payment:

  1. Open a Sent or Partially paid invoice.
  2. In Record Payment, check the Amount (it defaults to the balance due), pick a Method, and click Record Payment.

docs.title: Access & Permissions
docs.text:
Garage invoices are available only when the Garage add-on is enabled for your company (see Add-ons & Options).

Role Access Admin Full access to garage invoices and payments Manager Full access to garage invoices and payments for the offices they belong to Garage Full access to garage invoices and payments for the offices they belong to Accountant, Dispatch, Warehouse, Customer, drivers No access to the Garage area

Invoices belong to an office. The list, the counts on the tabs and the customers and work orders you can pick from only cover the office you are currently working in (see Multi-Office).

How to get there:

  • Main menu Garage > Invoices in the Garage sidebar
  • A completed work order > Generate Single Invoice or Bundle with Other Work Orders
  • The Work Orders list > row actions menu > Generate invoice or Bundle with others

docs.title: The Invoices List
docs.text: The list shows the newest invoices first, 20 per page.

docs.title: Tabs
docs.text:
Each tab shows a count of matching invoices.

Tab Shows All Every invoice, including void ones Draft Invoices with status Draft Sent Invoices with status Sent (no payment yet) Unpaid Invoices with status Sent or Partially paid Paid Invoices with status Paid Void Invoices with status Void

There is no Partially paid tab

Partially paid invoices appear under Unpaid (and All). Drafts are not counted as unpaid because they have not been sent to the customer yet.

docs.title: Columns
docs.text:
Column What it shows Invoice # The invoice number. Click it to open the invoice Customer The customer name, with the company name in brackets when there is one WOs The number of work orders on the invoice. Hover over it to see their numbers (for example Work orders: #12, #15), or No work orders linked Status Draft, Sent, Partially paid, Paid or Void Date The invoice date Due The due date. Shown in red once it has passed and the invoice is not Paid Total The invoice total, taxes included Balance Total minus payments. Red while something is owed, green when nothing is Actions The eye button opens the invoice

When there are no invoices you see No invoices yet and Create one from the New Invoice button, or generate from a completed work order.

docs.title: Status colours
docs.text: Status Badge colour Meaning Draft Grey Created but not sent. Can be edited or deleted Sent Blue Sent to the customer, no payment recorded Partially paid Yellow At least one payment recorded, balance still owing Paid Green Payments cover the full total Void Red Cancelled. Excluded from all financial reports

docs.title: Creating an Invoice
docs.text: Only work orders that are Completed and not already on an invoice can be invoiced. One invoice always belongs to one customer, so you cannot bundle work orders of different customers.

docs.title: Generate Single Invoice
docs.text:
Use this when a work order is billed on its own.

  1. Open a work order with status Completed.
  2. Click Generate Single Invoice (on the Work Orders list, open the row actions menu and click Generate invoice).
  3. Confirm Generate a single-WO invoice for this work order only? You can still edit the work order while the invoice stays in Draft.

The invoice is created as a Draft with these values, and the invoice page opens with Invoice generated successfully.

Field Value Customer The work order's customer Tax Rate The first active tax of your office Invoice Date Today Terms Default Payment Terms from Garage Settings Due Date Invoice date plus the terms (see Terms and due date) Shop Supplies Fee The work order's Shop Supplies Fee Discount None

The work order's status changes to Invoiced. If the work order is already on an invoice, you are taken to that invoice instead (Invoice already exists.). If the work order is not Completed, you see Work order must be completed before invoicing.

docs.title: Bundle work orders (New Invoice)
docs.text:
Use this to put several work orders for the same customer on one invoice. Clicking Bundle with Other Work Orders on a work order (or Bundle with others in the row actions menu) skips step 1 below and pre-ticks that work order.

Step 1: pick the customer

  1. Go to Invoices and click New Invoice.
  2. Choose the Customer * (only active customers are listed). The form reminds you: An invoice can only bundle work orders for a single customer.
  3. Click Continue.

Step 2: pick the work orders and fill in the invoice

The customer is now locked. Click Change customer to go back to step 1.

Field Default Notes Tax Rate The first active tax of your office Choose another rate, or No tax Terms Default Payment Terms from Garage Settings (Net 30 if none) Due on Receipt, Net 15, Net 30, Net 45 or Net 60 Invoice Date Today Shop Supplies Fee Empty (Auto from WOs) Leave empty to use the sum of the selected work orders' shop supplies fees. Type an amount to override it Discount No discount Percent (%) or Fixed amount ($) Discount Value Empty For example 10 for 10% or 50 for $50. Applied before taxes. One discount per invoice. Notes Empty Printed at the bottom of the invoice

Under Work Orders to Include * the table lists only completed, uninvoiced work orders for this customer, oldest first, with WO #, Date, Equipment, Description and Subtotal (parts plus labour). Tick the ones to bill and click Create Invoice.

If the customer has nothing to bill, you see This customer has no completed work orders ready to invoice.

The invoice is created as a Draft, the page shows Invoice created., and every selected work order moves to Invoiced.

Someone else may have invoiced it first

If a selected work order was invoiced or reopened by someone else in the meantime, the invoice is not created and the form shows an error such as Work orders #15 is not available for invoicing. Untick it and try again. No invoice number is used up when this happens.

docs.title: Terms and due date
docs.text:
The new invoice form has no due date field. The due date is the invoice date plus the terms:

Terms Due date Due on Receipt Same day as the invoice date Net 15 Invoice date + 15 days Net 30 Invoice date + 30 days Net 45 Invoice date + 45 days Net 60 Invoice date + 60 days

When you edit a draft, the Edit Invoice page has a Due Date field:

  • Changing Terms or Invoice Date on the page fills in the Due Date from the table above. You can then type a different date.
  • When you save, if the Terms changed, the due date is always recalculated from the invoice date and the terms, so a date you typed by hand in the same save is replaced.
  • If the Terms did not change, the Due Date shown in the field is saved as is.

docs.title: Invoice Numbering
docs.text:
The number is assigned the moment the invoice is created, including drafts. It is built from two Garage Settings:

  • Invoice Prefix (for example GRG)
  • the next sequence number, padded to five digits

So the first invoice with prefix GRG is GRG-00001, the next GRG-00002, and so on. The prefix is GRG until you change it. The Invoice Prefix field in Garage Settings shows the number the next invoice will get (Next invoice: GRG-00042). See Garage Settings & Taxes.

Garage Settings are kept per office, so each office has its own prefix and its own sequence. Give each office its own prefix so invoice numbers stay unique across your company.

Numbers are never reused

The sequence only moves forward. Deleting a draft or voiding an invoice does not give its number back, so you will see a gap in the sequence. Changing the prefix affects new invoices only.

docs.title: How Totals Are Calculated
docs.text:
Totals are recalculated whenever the invoice is created, saved from Edit Invoice, or one of its work orders is edited while the invoice is a Draft.

Line How it is calculated Subtotal Parts plus labour of all work orders on the invoice (quantity x charge price, hours x rate) Discount Percent (%): that percentage of the subtotal. Fixed amount ($): the amount, capped at the subtotal. Shown as Discount (10%) or Discount Shop Supplies The work orders' shop supplies fees added together, unless you typed an amount on the invoice GST GST rate of the selected Tax Rate x taxable amount QST QST rate of the selected Tax Rate x taxable amount Total Subtotal - Discount + Shop Supplies + GST + QST Paid Sum of recorded payments Balance Due Total - Paid

Taxable amount = taxable parts + taxable labour + shop supplies - discount (never below zero). Parts and labour lines whose Tax box is unticked on the work order are left out of the taxable amount. Shop supplies are always taxed. With No tax selected, GST and QST are zero.

Discount is applied before taxes

The discount reduces the amount taxes are calculated on. Example: subtotal $1,000, 10% discount, all lines taxable, no shop supplies, GST 5% and QST 9.975%. Discount = $100, taxable amount = $900, GST = $45.00, QST = $89.78, total = $1,034.78.

Percent discount limit

A Percent (%) discount cannot be more than 100. A Fixed amount ($) discount larger than the subtotal is reduced to the subtotal, so the invoice never goes negative.

Lines with a zero amount (discount, shop supplies, GST, QST) are hidden on the invoice page, the printout and the email.

docs.title: Editing a Draft
docs.text:
Only Draft invoices can be edited. Open the invoice and click Edit.

The Edit Invoice page shows the customer (it cannot be changed) and these fields: Tax Rate, Terms, Invoice Date, Due Date, Shop Supplies Fee, Discount, Discount Value and Notes.

Work Orders on this Invoice lists the work orders already on the invoice (ticked) plus the customer's other completed, uninvoiced work orders (unticked):

  • Untick a work order to remove it. It returns to Completed.
  • Tick a work order to add it. It moves to Invoiced.

Click Update Invoice to save. The totals are recalculated and you see Invoice updated successfully.

Shop Supplies Fee on edit

The Shop Supplies Fee field shows the invoice's current fee. If you add or remove work orders and want the fee recalculated from the work orders, clear the field before saving. If you leave a number in it, that number is kept.

An invoice should always keep at least one work order. To drop a draft you no longer need, use Delete.

docs.title: Fixing a work order on a draft invoice
docs.text:
A work order on a Draft invoice can still be edited. On the invoice page, each work order section has an Edit work order link. Saving the work order updates the draft invoice's totals automatically, so there is no need to void the invoice. When you started from the invoice page you are taken back to it, with a message such as Work order updated. Draft invoice GRG-00001 was recalculated to $1,034.78. The work order page also reminds you with a banner (...which is still a draft — you can still edit it...) and an Open draft invoice link.

  • If you change the work order's Shop Supplies Fee, the invoice's fee goes up or down by the same difference, so an amount you typed on the invoice is adjusted rather than replaced.
  • The work order's customer cannot be changed while it is on an invoice. Remove it from the invoice first.

Once the invoice is Sent, Partially paid or Paid, its work orders are locked. To change them, reopen the invoice (see below) or void it.

docs.title: Invoice Lifecycle and Actions
docs.text:
The buttons at the top of the invoice page depend on its status.

Button Shown when What it does Confirmation Edit Draft Opens Edit Invoice None Mark Sent Draft Changes the status to Sent without emailing anything Mark this invoice as sent? Reopen to Edit Sent with no payments Returns the invoice to Draft so you can edit it Reopen this invoice for editing? It will go back to Draft status — remember to mark it as sent again afterwards.
