Print Any status except Void Opens the printable invoice in a new tab None Email Invoice Any status except Void Emails the PDF (see Emailing an Invoice) Send invoice to: followed by the customer and the addresses Delete Draft Deletes the invoice. Its work orders return to Completed Delete invoice GRG-00001? The work order will return to Completed status. This cannot be undone. Void Any status except Void Voids the invoice. Its work orders return to Completed Void invoice GRG-00001? The work order will return to Completed status and you can generate a new invoice. The voided invoice will be excluded from reports.

After Mark Sent you see Invoice marked as sent. After Delete you are returned to the list with Invoice GRG-00001 deleted.

When Edit is not available, a greyed-out Edit button with a lock is shown instead. Hover over it to see why:

Situation Tooltip Paid Paid invoices cannot be edited. Use Void if this invoice is wrong. Payments recorded (Partially paid) Remove the recorded payments below first, then you can reopen this invoice.

docs.title: Reopen to Edit
docs.text:
Use this when a sent invoice needs a correction (for example a forgotten discount) and you do not want to void it and lose the number.

  1. Open the Sent invoice and click Reopen to Edit, then confirm.
  2. The invoice is back in Draft (Invoice reopened for editing. Mark it as sent again when you are done.).
  3. Edit the invoice or its work orders.
  4. Click Mark Sent or Email Invoice again.

Reopen is blocked as soon as a payment is recorded (Remove the recorded payments before reopening this invoice.). Remove the payments first, then reopen.

docs.title: Void
docs.text:
Void cancels an invoice that should not be collected, at any status including Paid.

  • The status changes to Void and a red banner says This invoice has been voided and is excluded from all financial reports.
  • All work orders are detached from the invoice and return to Completed, so you can invoice them again (Generate Single Invoice reappears on the work order). The confirmation tells you how many: Invoice GRG-00001 voided. 2 work order(s) reverted to completed.
  • The voided invoice keeps its number and stays in the list under Void. Its page shows No work orders are linked to this invoice (it may have been voided).
  • Payments already recorded stay listed on the voided invoice.
  • No action buttons are shown on a void invoice. Voiding cannot be undone from the screen.

Delete vs Void

Delete is only for drafts and removes the invoice completely. For anything that has been sent or paid, use Void: the record stays for your audit trail. Trying to delete a non-draft invoice shows Only draft invoices can be deleted. Use void for sent or paid invoices.

docs.title: Print
docs.text:
Print opens the invoice in a new browser tab, ready to print or save as PDF. It is the same layout as the emailed PDF:

  • Your logo, company name, Garage Services, and the Company Address and Phone from Garage Settings
  • INVOICE, the invoice number and the number of work orders
  • Bill To: customer name, phone and email
  • Invoice Date, Due Date and Terms
  • One section per work order: Work Order #, equipment and plate, P/O number, Completed date, then each part and labour line (Description, Qty/Hours, Rate, Amount) and a Work Order Subtotal
  • Subtotal, discount, Shop Supplies, GST and QST (each with your registration number from Garage Settings when set), and Total Due
  • Notes

Total Due is the invoice total

The printout and PDF show the full invoice total. Payments and the remaining balance are not printed.

docs.title: Emailing an Invoice
docs.text:
1. Open the invoice and click Email Invoice.
  2. The confirmation lists who will receive it: Send invoice to: the customer name, then each address.
  3. Click OK. The page shows Invoice emailed to customer@example.com, accounting@example.com.
Item Value To The garage customer's Email CC The garage customer's Accountant Email, when filled in From Your company name and the Accountant Email from the application settings (see Application Settings) Subject Invoice GRG-00001 from \<your company name> Body A summary of the invoice: your company name with Garage Services and your Phone, the customer name and phone, invoice date, due date and terms, the work order lines and the totals, then Thank you for your business! and your Company Address from Garage Settings Attachment \<your company name> Invoice GRG-00001.pdf

After sending:

  • A Draft invoice is marked Sent automatically. Other statuses do not change.
  • A purple Emailed badge with the date appears next to the status. It shows the most recent send.
  • You can send the same invoice again at any time (for example as a reminder), except when it is Void.

When you cannot email:

Situation What you see The customer has no Email Email Invoice is greyed out with the tooltip Customer has no email address The invoice is Void The button is not shown

Add the email on the customer record to fix the first case (see Garage Customers & Equipment).

docs.title: Payments
docs.text: The Payments section at the bottom of the invoice page lists every payment recorded (Date, Method, Reference, Amount), newest first, or No payments recorded.

docs.title: Recording a payment
docs.text:
The Record Payment form appears only when the invoice is Sent or Partially paid and has a balance due. You cannot record payments on a Draft (mark it sent first), a Paid or a Void invoice.

Field Required Default Notes Amount Yes The balance due Must be more than zero and cannot exceed the balance due Method No Select... Cash, Check, Credit card, E transfer or Debit Reference # No Empty Cheque number, transaction ID, etc. Date Yes Today The date you received the payment

Click Record Payment. The page shows Payment recorded successfully.

If the amount is too high you see Amount cannot exceed balance due of .... Overpayments cannot be recorded: the most you can enter is the balance due.

docs.title: Automatic status
docs.text:
You never set the payment status by hand. After each payment is recorded or removed:

Result New status Payments cover the total (balance zero) Paid Some payment recorded, balance still owing Partially paid All payments removed Sent

docs.title: Removing a payment
docs.text:
1. Click the on the payment row.
  2. Confirm Remove this payment?. The page shows Payment removed. and the status and balance update.

Payments cannot be removed from a Paid invoice (Cannot remove payments from a fully paid invoice.). If a paid invoice is wrong, void it and invoice the work orders again.

docs.title: My work order does not appear in the New Invoice list
docs.text:
Solution

Only work orders that are Completed, not already on an invoice, and belong to the selected customer are listed. Check the work order's status and customer. A work order still In Progress must be marked Completed first. A work order on a voided invoice is available again.

docs.title: Can I put work orders from two customers on one invoice?
docs.text:
Solution

No. An invoice can only bundle work orders for a single customer. Create one invoice per customer.

docs.title: I need to change an invoice I already sent
docs.text:
Solution

If no payment is recorded, click Reopen to Edit, make the change, then Mark Sent or Email Invoice again. The invoice keeps its number. If payments are recorded, remove them first. If the invoice is Paid, use Void and create a new invoice.

docs.title: There is a gap in my invoice numbers
docs.text:
Solution

A number is taken as soon as an invoice is created, even as a draft. Deleting a draft does not give its number back. This is expected.

docs.title: The Email Invoice button is greyed out
docs.text:
Solution

The customer has no email address. Add an Email to the garage customer and reload the invoice. Fill in Accountant Email too if their accountant should get a copy.

docs.title: The Record Payment form is missing
docs.text:
Solution

Payments can only be recorded on Sent or Partially paid invoices with a balance due. If the invoice is a Draft, click Mark Sent first.

docs.title: Taxes look lower than expected
docs.text:
Solution

Taxes are calculated after the discount and only on lines marked taxable on the work orders (plus shop supplies). Check the Tax Rate on the invoice and the taxable setting of the parts and labour lines.

docs.title: My garage invoices are not on the Invoices page
docs.text:
Solution

Garage invoices are separate from freight invoices. Open Garage in the main menu, then Invoices in the Garage sidebar.

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
Tips

  • Fix work order lines while the invoice is still a Draft. Saving the work order updates the invoice totals without voiding anything.
  • Use Reopen to Edit rather than Void for corrections on unpaid sent invoices, so the invoice keeps its number.
  • Fill in the customer's Accountant Email so their accounting team is copied on every invoice.
  • Use Email Invoice instead of Mark Sent when you can: it sends the PDF and marks the invoice sent in one step.
  • Record the Reference # (cheque number or transfer ID) with each payment to make reconciliation easier.

docs.title: Garage Module Overview
docs.text: The Garage add-on is a repair shop module inside UTX Freight: you keep garage customers and their vehicles, write work orders for repairs and service, turn finished work into invoices, and record payments, all separately from your freight orders and invoices.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
• Garage is an add-on. It only appears when it is turned on for your installation. See Add-ons & Options.
  • You open it from the Garage item in the main (left) menu of UTX Freight. It always opens on Work Orders.
  • The Garage has its own screen layout with a dark sidebar: Work Orders, Invoices, Equipment, Parts, Templates, Customers, Taxes, Settings, Reports, and Back to TMS at the bottom.
  • Garage customers, garage equipment, garage invoices and garage statements are separate from their freight counterparts. Nothing is shared between the two except the tax rates (see How Garage data differs from Freight).
  • Everything in the Garage belongs to the office you are working in. You only see the work orders, invoices, customers, equipment, parts, templates and settings of your current office.
  • The typical flow is: Customer Equipment Work Order (Estimate Approved In Progress Completed) Invoice (Draft Sent) Payment (Partially paid / Paid).
  • Admin, Manager and Garage users can use it.

What the Garage does not do

The Garage is built around work orders and invoicing. It does not schedule preventive maintenance or track service due dates, and it has no vehicle import: the only CSV import in the Garage is for Parts. Earlier versions of the release notes described these features; they are not part of the current module.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
1. In the main menu, click Garage. The Work Orders page opens.
  2. Go to Settings and fill in Garage Settings (labor rate, shop supplies, payment terms, invoice prefix, company details). See Garage Settings & Taxes.
  3. Go to Taxes and make sure an active tax rate exists for your office.
  4. Go to Customers New Customer, then Equipment New Equipment for the customer's vehicle. (You can also create both on the fly from the work order form.)
  5. Go to Work Orders New Work Order, pick the Customer and Equipment, add parts and labor, and click Create Work Order. It starts as an Estimate.
  6. Move it through Approved, In Progress and Completed with the Mark ... buttons on the work order page (Mark Approved, Mark In progress, Mark Completed) or the Move to section of the row's actions menu ().
  7. On the completed work order, click Generate Single Invoice (Generate invoice in the row's actions menu). The invoice opens as a Draft.
  8. Click Email Invoice (or Mark Sent if you deliver it another way), then use Record Payment when the customer pays.

docs.title: Access & Permissions
docs.text:
Role Garage access Admin Full access to every Garage page Manager Full access to every Garage page, for the offices they belong to Garage Full access to every Garage page, for the first office on their user account (they cannot switch office). No access to freight pages Dispatch, Customer Service, Accountant, Customer, Warehouse, drivers and yard workers No access. The Garage menu item is hidden
  • The add-on must be turned on. If it is off, the Garage menu item is hidden for everyone, and opening a Garage page sends you back to the main application.
  • The Garage role is only offered in the role list when the Garage add-on is on. See User Roles and People & Invitations.
  • Inside the Garage there are no finer permissions: anyone who can open the Garage can create, edit, invoice, void, record payments and change settings.

Where to find it:

  • Main menu Garage — opens Work Orders
  • Garage sidebar Back to TMS — returns to the main UTX Freight application

docs.title: The sidebar
docs.text:
The sidebar shows Garage with your company name at the top, then these items, in this order:

Sidebar item What it opens Details Work Orders The work order list with status tabs (All, Estimates, Approved, In Progress, Completed, Invoiced) and New Work Order Garage Work Orders Invoices The garage invoice list with tabs (All, Draft, Sent, Unpaid, Paid, Void) and New Invoice Garage Invoices Equipment Vehicles and units serviced by the shop (truck, trailer or chassis), with New Equipment and a VIN Decode button on the form Garage Customers & Equipment Parts Parts Inventory, with Import CSV, Export and New Part Garage Parts & Templates Templates Job Templates (pre-filled parts and labor you can apply to a work order), with New Template Garage Parts & Templates Customers Garage customers, with New Customer Garage Customers & Equipment Taxes Tax Rates (GST/QST), with New Tax Rate Garage Settings & Taxes Settings Garage Settings for the current office Garage Settings & Taxes Reports A Dashboard plus Profit Report, Customer Work Summary and Customer Statement Garage Reports

At the bottom of the sidebar:

  • Back to TMS — returns to the main UTX Freight application.
  • Release — the UTX Freight version number.

The current page is highlighted in blue in the sidebar.

docs.title: The top bar
docs.text: The top bar shows the page title on the left, and your name and the office you are working in on the right.

docs.title: On a phone or small screen
docs.text:
On screens narrower than 1024 pixels the sidebar is hidden:

  1. Tap the menu button at the top left to slide the sidebar in.
  2. Tap a sidebar item, or tap (or the dimmed area beside the sidebar) to close it.

When you print a Garage page, the sidebar and top bar are left out.

docs.title: Confirmation pop-ups
docs.text: Actions that change a status or remove something (for example Mark Sent, Void, Delete, Reopen, removing a payment, or moving a work order to In Progress) ask for confirmation in an Are you sure? pop-up window. Read the message (it explains what will happen) and click Yes, proceed to continue, or Cancel to stop.

docs.title: No Feedback button
docs.text: The Feedback button you see in the main UTX Freight application is not available inside the Garage. To send feedback, click Back to TMS first (Admins and Managers), or contact your administrator.

docs.title: Office Scoping
docs.text:
Every Garage record belongs to one office: customers, equipment, parts, job templates, work orders, invoices (and their payments) and Garage settings. The Garage always works in your current office, shown in the top bar.

  • Lists, searches, reports and statements only include the current office's records.
  • New records are created in the current office.
  • Garage Settings (labor rate, payment terms, invoice prefix and numbering, company details) are kept per office, so each office has its own invoice number sequence.
  • Admins and Managers can change office from the office selector in the main application (with the Multi-Office add-on and more than one office), then click Garage again. See Multi-Office.
  • Garage users cannot switch offices. They always work in the first office on their user account. If a Garage user needs to work for another office, ask your administrator to change the offices on their account.

Tax rates are the exception

The Taxes page lists the same tax rates as the main application, from all offices. New tax rates are created in your current office, and a new invoice picks the current office's active tax rate by default. See Garage Settings & Taxes.

docs.title: Customer and equipment
docs.text:
1. Go to Customers New Customer. A garage customer needs at least a first and last name. Add an email address if you want to email invoices and statements.
  2. Go to Equipment New Equipment and link the unit to the customer. Use Decode next to the VIN to fill in vehicle details automatically.

Create them from the work order

On the work order form, the green buttons next to Customer and Equipment open Quick Create Customer and Quick Create Equipment. Fill in the short form and click Create & Select. On the customer list, the work order button on a row starts a new work order for that customer.

docs.title: Work order
docs.text:
1. Go to Work Orders New Work Order.
  2. Search and select the Customer (required) and the Equipment. Optionally use Apply Template to load parts and labor from a job template.
  3. Fill in the details (Description, P/O Number, Date In, Est. Completion, Odometer In, Assigned Technician), the parts and labor lines, Shop Supplies Fee and Internal Notes (not shown on invoice).
  4. Click Create Work Order. It starts in Estimate. You can print it with Print Estimate on the work order page (Print estimate in the row's actions menu).

Then move it forward:

Status How it gets there Notes Estimate New work order Can move to Approved or straight to In Progress Approved Customer agreed to the estimate Can move to In Progress In Progress Work has started Moving here decrements parts inventory (quantity on hand) for the work order's parts that were picked from Parts inventory. Stock never goes below zero Completed Work is finished The Date Out is set to today if it is empty. You can now invoice it, or reopen it with Reopen Work Order (Reopen in the row's actions menu), which sends it back to Approved Invoiced The work order was put on an invoice Set when the work order is added to an invoice. Still editable while the invoice is a Draft; locked once the invoice is sent

On the work order page the status buttons read Mark Approved, Mark In progress and Mark Completed, and the status badge shows the status in sentence case (for example In progress). Each move asks for confirmation first. Statuses only move forward; the only way back is Reopen Work Order (Completed to Approved) or taking the work order off its invoice (Invoiced to Completed), which happens when you remove it from a draft invoice, delete the draft invoice or void the invoice.

Billing a completed work order

To bill a completed work order, use Generate Single Invoice or Bundle with Other Work Orders. These create the invoice and set the work order to Invoiced for you.

Details: Garage Work Orders.

docs.title: Invoice
docs.text:
From a Completed work order:

  • Generate Single Invoice (Generate invoice in the row's actions menu) creates a draft invoice for this work order only.
  • Bundle with Other Work Orders (Bundle with others in the row's actions menu) opens New Invoice for the same customer so you can put several completed work orders on one invoice.

You can also start from Invoices New Invoice. Invoice numbers come from the office's Invoice Prefix and sequence in Garage Settings.

Invoice status Meaning Draft Not sent yet. You can Edit or Delete it, and still edit its work orders Sent Sent to the customer, by Email Invoice (which marks a draft as sent) or Mark Sent. While no payment is recorded, Reopen to Edit returns it to Draft Partially paid At least one payment is recorded, but a balance remains Paid Payments cover the full total Void Cancelled. Its work orders go back to Completed so you can invoice them again. Voided invoices are excluded from reports

Details: Garage Invoices.

docs.title: Payment
docs.text: On a Sent or Partially paid invoice with a balance due, fill in Record Payment (Amount, Method, Reference #, Date) and click Record Payment. The invoice status updates automatically. A payment cannot be larger than the balance due. Method is one of Cash, Check, Credit card, E transfer or Debit. Remove a payment with the on its row; this is refused once the invoice is Paid (Cannot remove payments from a fully paid invoice.).

docs.title: Follow-up
docs.text: Use Reports for the profit report, per-customer work summaries and customer statements, including scheduled emails. See Garage Reports.

docs.title: How Garage Data Differs from Freight
docs.text:
Freight (main application) Garage Customers Customer companies on the Customers page (Managing Customers) Garage customers on the Garage Customers page: a person (first and last name) with an optional company name. Not linked to freight customers Equipment Chassis, trailers and trucks you assign to orders (Equipment) Units belonging to garage customers, used on work orders. Not visible on the freight Equipments page and cannot be assigned to freight orders Work Orders (Orders) Work orders Invoices Freight invoices (Invoices) Garage invoices with their own numbering (Invoice Prefix). Never shown on the freight Invoices page or in Aged Receivables Payments Invoice Email & Payments Record Payment on the garage invoice Statements Customer Statements and Automatic Statements Customer Statement and its own schedule in Garage Reports (Garage Reports) Taxes Tax rates The same tax rates (shared)

Tax rates used by garage invoices cannot be deleted

Because tax rates are shared, a tax rate that is used by any garage invoice cannot be deleted from the main application either. You see Cannot delete — used by N garage invoices. (for example used by 1 garage invoice.). On the Garage Taxes page, the delete button only appears for rates that no garage invoice uses, and deleting is also refused if a freight invoice uses the rate. Make the rate inactive instead.

docs.title: I don't see Garage in the menu
docs.text:
Solution

The Garage add-on must be turned on for your installation, and your role must be Admin, Manager or Garage. Dispatch, Customer Service and Accountant users do not get the Garage. Ask your administrator.

docs.title: I can't find a customer, work order or invoice
docs.text:
Solution

Garage data is per office. Check the office name in the top bar. Admins and Managers can switch office in the main application and reopen the Garage. Also check that you are not looking for a freight customer: freight customers do not appear in the Garage.

docs.title: My garage invoices are not on the Invoices page or in Aged Receivables
docs.text:
Solution

That is by design. Garage invoices only appear under Garage Invoices and in Garage Reports.

docs.title: Where do I schedule preventive maintenance or import my vehicles?
docs.text:
Solution

The Garage does not have maintenance scheduling or a vehicle import. Add equipment one by one (the VIN Decode button helps), or create it from the work order with Quick Create Equipment. Parts can be imported with Import CSV on the Parts page.

docs.title: Where is the Feedback button?
docs.text:
Solution

It is not shown in the Garage. Admins and Managers can click Back to TMS and use Feedback there.

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
Getting the most out of the Garage

  • Fill in Garage Settings and an active tax rate for each office before creating the first invoice, so invoice numbers, terms and taxes are right from the start.
  • Add an email address to garage customers so you can use Email Invoice and emailed statements.
  • Move work orders to In Progress only when work actually starts, since that is when parts are taken out of inventory.
  • Use Bundle with Other Work Orders to send one invoice for several completed jobs for the same customer.
  • Fix a mistake on a sent invoice with Reopen to Edit (only when no payment is recorded) or Void, rather than creating a duplicate.

docs.title: Garage Parts Inventory & Job Templates
docs.text: Keep a catalogue of the parts your shop uses, with cost, charge price and stock levels, import or export it as CSV, and save common jobs as Job Templates that fill in parts and labor on a work order in one click.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
• Parts (Garage sidebar) opens Parts Inventory: every part of your current office with its SKU, Category, Cost, Charge, Margin and Qty, 25 per page.
  • Three tabs: Active, Low Stock and Disabled. A part is low on stock when it has a Reorder Point above 0 and its quantity on hand is at or below that reorder point.
  • There is no delete for parts. Disable a part you no longer use; you can enable it again at any time.
  • Import CSV adds parts in bulk, with a preview before anything is saved. Export downloads the active parts of your office as a CSV file.
  • Templates (Garage sidebar) opens Job Templates: named jobs (for example Oil Change) with a list of parts and labor lines. On the work order form, Apply Template adds a template's lines to the work order.
  • Stock goes down automatically when a work order with catalogue parts moves to In progress. See Parts inventory.
  • Parts and templates belong to the office you are working in. Each office has its own catalogue and its own templates.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
Add a part:

  1. In the Garage sidebar, click Parts, then New Part.
  2. Enter the Name (required), and optionally the SKU, Category and Description.
  3. Enter the Purchase Price (your cost), the Charge Price (what the customer pays), the Qty on Hand and a Reorder Point.
  4. Click Create Part.

Create a job template:

  1. In the Garage sidebar, click Templates, then New Template.
  2. Enter the Template Name (required) and a Description.
  3. Under Parts, search for a catalogue part (or type a description) and set Qty, Cost and Charge. Click Add Part for more lines.
  4. Under Labor, enter a Description, Hours and Rate. Click Add Labor for more lines.
  5. Click Create Template.
  6. On a new or existing work order, pick the template under Apply Template and click Apply.

docs.title: Access & Permissions
docs.text:
Role Parts and Templates Admin Full access: create, edit, disable/enable, import, export Manager Full access, for the offices they belong to Garage Full access, for the first office on their user account (they cannot switch office) Dispatch, Customer Service, Accountant, Customer, Warehouse, drivers and yard workers No access (the Garage menu item is hidden)
  • The Garage add-on must be turned on. See Garage Module Overview.
  • There are no finer permissions inside the Garage: anyone who can open it can manage parts and templates.

Where to find it:

  • Main menu Garage sidebar Parts — page Parts Inventory
  • Main menu Garage sidebar Templates — page Job Templates

docs.title: The Parts Inventory Page
docs.text:
The page header shows Parts Inventory (Manage parts, pricing, and stock levels) with three buttons:

Button What it does Import CSV Opens Import Parts (see Importing parts from CSV) Export Downloads the active parts as CSV (see Exporting parts) New Part Opens the New Part form

docs.title: Tabs
docs.text:
Tab Shows Active (default) All active parts Low Stock Active parts whose Reorder Point is greater than 0 and whose quantity on hand is equal to or lower than the reorder point Disabled Parts you have disabled

Parts with a Reorder Point of 0 are never low on stock

A part with Reorder Point 0 never appears on the Low Stock tab and never gets the red quantity badge, even when its quantity on hand is 0. Set a reorder point on every part you want to monitor.

docs.title: Search
docs.text: Type in Search parts... and press Enter (or click ). The search matches part of the Name or the SKU, is not case-sensitive, and stays within the tab you are on.

docs.title: Columns
docs.text:
The list is sorted by name, 25 parts per page.

Column What it shows Name Part name SKU Part number, or - if empty Category Category, or - if empty Cost Purchase Price Charge Charge Price Margin Margin as a percentage of the charge price (see below) Qty Quantity on hand. Shown in a red badge when the part is low on stock Actions edit, and disable (active parts) or enable (disabled parts)

docs.title: Margin colours
docs.text:
Margin = (Charge Price − Purchase Price) ÷ Charge Price × 100, rounded to one decimal. A part with a charge price of 0 shows 0%.

Colour Margin Green 50% or more Yellow 30% to under 50% Red Under 30% (including negative margins, when the cost is higher than the charge)

docs.title: Empty list
docs.text: When the tab has no parts, you see No parts yet — Add parts to your inventory to use them in work orders. — and a New Part button.

docs.title: Adding and Editing a Part
docs.text:
Click New Part, or the edit icon on a row (page Edit Part: ).

Field Required Notes Name Yes Shown in part searches on work orders and templates SKU No Part number. Must be unique across all offices (see below). Searchable Category No Pick from the list, or leave Select category... Description No Free text Purchase Price No (defaults to 0) Your cost. 0 or more, up to 2 decimals Charge Price No (defaults to 0) Price charged to the customer. 0 or more, up to 2 decimals Qty on Hand No (defaults to 0) Whole number, 0 or more Reorder Point No (defaults to 0) Whole number, 0 or more. Above 0, it turns on the low stock warning

Click Create Part (new) or Update Part (edit). You return to the list with Part created successfully. or Part updated successfully. Cancel returns to the list without saving. If something is wrong, the form shows the errors in a red box at the top (for example Name can't be blank).

docs.title: Categories
docs.text:
The Category list is fixed:

Brakes, Engine, Tires, Electrical, Suspension, Transmission, Cooling, HVAC, Exhaust, Filters, Fluids, Body, Lighting, Other.

You cannot add your own categories. Use Other for anything that does not fit.

SKUs are unique across all offices

When you save a part, its SKU must not be used by any other part, in any office, including disabled parts. The comparison is exact (ABC-1 and abc-1 count as different SKUs). If the SKU is taken, you see Sku has already been taken. Use a different SKU.

Changing a part's price

Work order and template lines keep the cost and charge they had when the part was added. Changing the price in the catalogue does not change existing work orders or templates.

docs.title: Disabling and enabling a part
docs.text:
• Click on an active part and confirm with Yes, proceed in the Are you sure? pop-up (Disable ?). The part moves to the Disabled tab with the message disabled.
  • On the Disabled tab, click to enable it again (no confirmation). Message: enabled.

A disabled part:

  • no longer appears in the part search on the work order form and the template form,
  • is left out of Export,
  • stays on the work orders and templates that already use it.

docs.title: Adjusting stock
docs.text:
There is no separate stock-adjustment or receiving screen. To record parts you received or to correct a count, edit the part and change Qty on Hand.

Stock is taken out automatically when a work order moves to In progress (only for lines picked from the catalogue), and put back when such a line is removed from a work order that is In progress, Completed or on a draft invoice. Details: Parts inventory.

docs.title: Importing Parts from CSV
docs.text: Use Import CSV to add many parts at once. The import only adds new parts. It never updates or disables parts that already exist.

docs.title: Step by step
docs.text:
1. On Parts Inventory, click Import CSV. The Import Parts from CSV page opens.
  2. Optional: click Download Current Catalog as CSV Template to get a file with the right headers (it contains your current active parts).
  3. Prepare your CSV file (see CSV columns).
  4. Choose the file in the upload area and click Preview Import.
  5. Check the Import Preview page (see The preview page).
  6. Click Import N Parts (N is the number of rows ready to import), or Cancel to go back.
  7. You return to Parts Inventory with Import complete: X parts imported, Y skipped.

docs.title: CSV columns
docs.text:
The first row must contain these column headers:

name, sku, category, description, purchase_price, charge_price, quantity_on_hand, reorder_point
Column Required How it is imported name Yes Rows without a name are not imported sku No Rows whose SKU already exists in your office (ignoring capitals) are skipped. SKUs must be unique across all offices category No Must be exactly one of the categories, with the same spelling and capitals (for example Brakes, HVAC), or left empty description No Free text purchase_price No Plain number such as 12.50, 0 or more. Empty or not a number becomes 0. Do not use $ or thousands separators: $12.50 becomes 0 and 1,250.00 becomes 1 charge_price No Same rules as purchase_price quantity_on_hand No Whole number. Empty, not a number or negative becomes 0; decimals are dropped reorder_point No Whole number. Empty, not a number or negative becomes 0; decimals are dropped
  • Header names are not case-sensitive, and spaces are read as underscores (Purchase Price works like purchase_price). Columns can be in any order; other columns are ignored.
  • Spaces at the start and end of each value are removed.
  • Every imported part is active.

docs.title: File rules and messages
docs.text: Message Cause Please select a CSV file. You clicked Preview Import without choosing a file Please upload a CSV file (.csv). The file is not a CSV File too large. Maximum size is 1 MB. The file is larger than 1 MB Invalid CSV file: ... The file could not be read as CSV (for example a broken quote). The message gives the technical reason No CSV data found. Please upload again. The uploaded file was no longer available when you clicked Import N Parts (for example you clicked it a second time, or reloaded the page). Upload the file again

docs.title: The preview page
docs.text:
Import Preview shows three counters:

Counter Meaning Ready to import Rows that passed the preview checks Duplicate SKUs (will skip) Rows whose SKU already exists in your current office Invalid rows (will skip) Rows with a problem (see below)

Below the counters:

  • Parts to Import (N) lists the rows ready to import, with Row (the line number in your file, the header being line 1), Name, SKU, Category, Cost, Charge and Qty. Only the first 20 rows are listed, followed by ...and N more rows.
  • Skipped Rows lists the duplicate and invalid rows, with Row, Name (or (blank)), SKU and Issue.
  • If no row is ready, you see No valid rows found. Please check your CSV and try again. and a Try Again link.

Nothing is saved until you click Import N Parts.

docs.title: What the preview checks
docs.text:
Issue shown Rule SKU already exists The SKU matches a part of your current office (active or disabled), ignoring capitals Name is required The name column is empty Purchase price must be >= 0 purchase_price is negative Charge price must be >= 0 charge_price is negative

A row with a duplicate SKU is listed only as a duplicate, even if it also has other problems.

Parts without a SKU are never treated as duplicates

The duplicate check only works on SKUs. If you import the same file twice, or re-import the Download Current Catalog as CSV Template file, every row without a SKU is added again as a new part. Give your parts a SKU, or remove rows you have already imported.

docs.title: Exporting Parts
docs.text:
Click Export on Parts Inventory (or Download Current Catalog as CSV Template on the import page). The browser downloads parts_catalog_YYYYMMDD.csv (today's date, for example parts_catalog_20261010.csv).

  • It contains the active parts of your current office, sorted by name. Disabled parts are not exported.
  • It ignores the tab and search you are on: it always exports all active parts.
  • Columns: name, sku, category, description, purchase_price, charge_price, quantity_on_hand, reorder_point — the same headers the import expects.

docs.title: Job Templates
docs.text: A job template is a reusable job: a name, a description, and lists of parts and labor lines with their quantities, hours and prices. Templates are only used to fill in work orders; changing a template later does not change work orders it was applied to.

docs.title: The Job Templates page
docs.text:
Click Templates in the Garage sidebar. The page Job Templates (Pre-defined jobs to quickly populate work orders) has a New Template button and two tabs:

Tab Shows Active (default) Templates you can apply to work orders Disabled Templates you have disabled

The list is sorted by name, 20 per page, and has no search box.

Column What it shows Name Template name Description The description, shortened to 60 characters (ending with ...) when longer Parts Number of part lines Labor Number of labor lines Actions view, edit, and disable (active) or enable (disabled)

When the tab is empty, you see No templates yet — Create reusable job templates to speed up work order creation. — and a Create Your First Template button.

docs.title: Creating and editing a template
docs.text:
Click New Template, or on a row (page Edit Template).

Field Required Notes Template Name Yes For example Oil Change, Brake Service. Shown in the Apply Template list on work orders Description No Short description of the job

Parts section (one row per part, Add Part adds a row, removes one):

Column Notes Part / Description Type at least 2 characters to search active catalogue parts by name or SKU (up to 15 results, shown as Name (SKU)). Picking a part links the line to the catalogue and fills in Cost and Charge from the catalogue. You can also type a free description without picking a part Qty Whole number, at least 1. Defaults to 1 Cost Purchase price for the line. 0 or more Charge Price charged to the customer. 0 or more

When a line is newly linked to a catalogue part and you leave Cost or Charge at 0, or leave the description empty, the template takes the part's catalogue values when you save.

Labor section (one row per labor line, Add Labor adds a row, removes one):

Column Required Notes Description Yes For example Replace front pads Hours Yes 0 or more, in steps of 0.25 Rate Yes Hourly rate, greater than 0. It is not taken from Garage Settings; enter it on each line

Click Create Template or Update Template. You return to the list with Template created successfully. or Template updated successfully. Cancel returns without saving. If something is wrong, a red box lists the errors (N errors prevented this template from being saved:).

Remove empty rows you don't need

A new template starts with one empty part row and one empty labor row (a template being edited with no parts or no labor also shows one). If the template has no labor, remove the empty labor row with before saving, since every labor line needs a Description and a Rate. Likewise, remove an unused empty part row so the template only lists the parts you need.

docs.title: Viewing a template
docs.text:
Click on a row. The page shows the template name and description, an Edit button, and two tables:

  • Parts: Description, Qty, Cost, Charge (or No parts in this template).
  • Labor: Description, Hours, Rate (or No labor in this template).

Back to Templates returns to the list.

docs.title: Disabling and enabling a template
docs.text:
• Click on an active template and confirm with Yes, proceed (Disable this template?). Message: disabled.
  • On the Disabled tab, click to enable it again (no confirmation). Message: enabled.

    Only active templates are offered under Apply Template on the work order form. Work orders that a template was already applied to are not affected.

    Templates cannot be deleted

    There is no delete button for templates. Disable the ones you no longer use; they stay on the Disabled tab and can be enabled again.

docs.title: Applying a template to a work order
docs.text:
1. Open a new or existing work order (Work Orders New Work Order, or edit one).
  2. In the purple Apply Template box at the top of the form, pick a template in -- Select a template --.
  3. Click Apply. A Template Applied message confirms "" has been applied.

    What happens:

    • Empty part and labor rows on the form are removed, then the template's lines are added after the existing ones. Nothing you already entered is replaced, so applying a template twice adds its lines twice.
    • Part lines get the template's catalogue part link, description, quantity, cost and charge. Labor lines get the description, hours and rate. The prices are the ones saved in the template, not the current catalogue prices. Exception: on a template line linked to a catalogue part whose Cost or Charge is 0, the work order takes the part's current catalogue price for that value when you save it.
    • Every added line has its Tax checkbox ticked (taxable). Untick it on lines that should not be taxed.
    • You can still change or remove any line before saving the work order.
    • Catalogue parts added by a template are taken out of stock like any other catalogue line when the work order moves to In progress.

    The Apply Template box only appears when your current office has at least one active template. Details: Garage Work Orders.

docs.title: "Sku has already been taken" but I can't find the part
docs.text:
Solution

SKUs must be unique across all offices, including disabled parts. Check the Disabled tab, and ask someone in your other offices (or an Admin who can switch office) whether the SKU is used there. Otherwise use a different SKU.

docs.title: I imported the same file twice and now have duplicate parts
docs.text:
Solution

Duplicates are only detected by SKU. Parts without a SKU are added again on every import. Disable the extra copies (parts cannot be deleted), and give your parts a SKU to avoid this in the future.

docs.title: How do I update prices for many parts at once?
docs.text:
Solution

The import only adds new parts; it never updates existing ones. Change prices one by one with edit on Parts Inventory.

docs.title: A part is out of stock but not on the Low Stock tab
docs.text:
Solution

The part's Reorder Point is 0. Only parts with a reorder point above 0 can be low on stock. Edit the part and set a reorder point.

docs.title: I can't find a part when adding it to a work order or template
docs.text:
Solution

The search only lists active parts of your current office, and needs at least 2 characters of the name or SKU. Check the Disabled tab on Parts Inventory and enable the part if needed.

docs.title: My template doesn't appear under Apply Template
docs.text:
Solution

Only active templates of your current office are listed. Check the Disabled tab on Job Templates and click to enable it.

docs.title: How do I delete a template or a part?
docs.text:
Solution

Neither can be deleted from the screen. Disable them instead: they disappear from searches and from Apply Template, but stay available on the Disabled tab.

docs.title: I changed a part's price but my template still uses the old price
docs.text:
Solution

Templates keep the prices they were saved with. Edit the template and update Cost and Charge on the line (or pick the part again from the search to reload the catalogue prices), then click Update Template.

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
Keeping your catalogue and templates useful

  • Give every part a SKU and a Category. SKUs make searches faster and protect you from duplicate imports.
  • Set a Reorder Point on parts you keep in stock, and check the Low Stock tab regularly.
  • Watch the Margin colours: red means less than 30% of the charge price is profit, or you even sell at a loss.
  • Copy category names exactly from the list on this page when you prepare a CSV import.
  • Use Export as a quick backup of your active catalogue before a large import.
  • Build templates for your most common jobs (oil changes, brake jobs, inspections), and review their prices when your catalogue prices change.
  • Disable seasonal or outdated templates instead of letting the Apply Template list grow.

docs.title: Garage Reports, Work Summaries & Statements
docs.text: See how the garage is doing at a glance, check work order margins, and send customers a work summary or a statement of account, by hand or on a schedule.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Garage Reports is the last item in the Garage sidebar menu, just above Back to TMS. It opens a Dashboard with links to three reports:

  • Dashboard: four cards (WOs Opened, WOs Completed, Revenue, Outstanding) for Today, This Week or This Month, plus Overdue Invoices, Low Stock Parts, Technician Hours and Recent Work Orders panels.
  • Profit Report: revenue, parts cost and profit per work order for a date range (Work order margins by date range).
  • Customer Work Summary: the completed work orders of one customer for a week or a month, with what was invoiced and paid. Print it, email it, or schedule it (Weekly/monthly summary by customer).
  • Customer Statement: a statement of account listing the customer's unpaid invoices, split into Overdue and Not Yet Due. Print it, email it, send yourself a test, or schedule it (Due & overdue invoices by customer).
  • Automatic emails: UTX Freight sends scheduled work summaries and statements for you, and shows the result (Summary delivered, Statement delivered, a skip message or an error) on the report page.

Garage reports only use garage data (garage work orders, garage invoices, garage customers). They are separate from the freight Reports, Customer Statements and Automatic Statements.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
To email a customer their work for last week:

  1. Go to Garage > Reports and click Customer Work Summary.
  2. Pick the Customer, pick any day of last week in Date, keep Week selected and click View Report.
  3. Check the list, then click Email to customer email and confirm.

To send a statement of account:

  1. Go to Garage > Reports and click Customer Statement.
  2. Pick the Customer and click View Statement.
  3. Click Email to customer email and confirm. Use Send Test first if you want to see the email yourself.

To schedule either email:

  1. Open the customer on Customer Work Summary or Customer Statement.
  2. In Automatic Summary Emails or Automatic Statement Emails, choose a Frequency and click Save Schedule.

docs.title: Access & Permissions
docs.text:
Garage reports are available only when the Garage add-on is enabled for your company (see Add-ons & Options).

Role Access Admin Full access to all garage reports, emails and schedules, for the office they are working in Manager Full access, for the office they are working in (they can switch between the offices they belong to) Garage Full access, for the first office on their user account (they cannot switch office) Dispatch, Customer Service, Accountant, Customer, Warehouse, drivers and yard workers No access to the Garage area

There are no separate permissions for reports: anyone who can open the Garage can view every report, send emails and change schedules.

The Dashboard, the Profit Report and the customer lists only cover the office you are currently working in (see Multi-Office). The customer lists on Customer Work Summary and Customer Statement only show active customers.

How to get there:

  • Main menu Garage > Reports in the Garage sidebar (opens the Dashboard)
  • The cards at the bottom of the Dashboard: Profit Report, Customer Work Summary, Customer Statement, All Work Orders, Invoices
  • Garage Customers list > the clipboard button (Work summary for (name)) opens that customer's work summary for the current week
  • Every report has a Back to Reports link at the bottom

docs.title: The Dashboard
docs.text:
The page is titled Dashboard. Use the toggle at the top right to choose the period for the cards and the Technician Hours panel. The default is Today.

Period Covers Today Today This Week Monday of the current week up to now This Month The 1st of the current month up to now

docs.title: Cards
docs.text:
Card What it counts Uses the period? WOs Opened Work orders created in the period Yes WOs Completed Work orders whose status is now Completed or Invoiced and that were last updated in the period Yes Revenue The sum of the Total (taxes included) of all garage invoices created in the period, except Void ones. Drafts are included Yes Outstanding What is still owed on all Sent and Partially paid invoices (total minus payments). Shown in red when above zero No, always all unpaid invoices

WOs Completed uses the last update date

The card counts work orders by the date they were last updated. A work order completed last week and invoiced today counts as completed Today.

docs.title: Panels
docs.text:
Panel What it shows Overdue Invoices Up to 10 Sent or Partially paid invoices whose due date is before today, oldest due date first: invoice number, customer, Nd overdue and balance due. View all opens the Unpaid tab of Garage Invoices. When there are none: No overdue invoices Low Stock Parts Up to 10 active parts whose quantity on hand is at or below their reorder point (parts with a reorder point of 0 or none are ignored), lowest quantity first: name, SKU and quantity / reorder point. The quantity is red at zero, yellow otherwise. View all opens the Low Stock tab of Parts. When there are none: All parts above reorder point Technician Hours Labour hours per technician, highest first, for work orders last updated in the period. Hours are credited to the work order's assigned technician, not to individual labour lines. Work orders with no one assigned are left out. When there are none: No technician hours recorded Recent Work Orders The 8 most recently created work orders, whatever the period: number, customer, status and total (parts, labour and shop supplies). View all opens Work Orders. When there are none: No work orders yet

See Garage Parts & Templates for reorder points and Garage Work Orders for assigning a technician.

docs.title: Profit Report
docs.text:
The Profit Report shows the margin on each work order in a date range.

  1. On the Dashboard, click Profit Report.
  2. Set From and To. The defaults are the 1st of the current month and today.
  3. Click Filter.

Which work orders are included: work orders whose date in falls between From and To (both days included), in any status except Estimate (so Approved, In progress, Completed and Invoiced). Newest date in first.

Column What it shows WO # The work order number. Click it to open the work order Customer The customer name, followed by the company name in brackets when the customer has one Date The work order's date in Status The work order status Revenue Parts (quantity x charge price) + labour (hours x rate) + Shop Supplies Fee Parts Cost Parts at purchase price (quantity x purchase price) Profit Parts (charge price) - Parts Cost + labour. Green when zero or more, red when negative

A Totals row adds up the three amount columns.

Revenue includes shop supplies, Profit does not

The Shop Supplies Fee is part of Revenue but not of Profit, so Revenue - Parts Cost differs from Profit by the shop supplies amount. Labour is counted entirely as profit because labour lines have hours and a rate, with no cost.

Work order amounts, not invoice amounts

The report uses the work order lines. Invoice discounts, GST and QST are not included, and the report does not check whether the work was invoiced or paid. For billed and paid amounts, use the Customer Work Summary, the Customer Statement or Garage Invoices.

docs.title: Customer Work Summary
docs.text: The Customer Work Summary lists one customer's finished work for a week or a month, with what was invoiced, what was paid and the balance.

docs.title: Choosing the customer and period
docs.text:
Field What to enter Customer Choose from -- Select customer --. Only active customers are listed Date Week: any day of the week you want (defaults to today). The hint says Report snaps to Monday of selected week: the report always covers Monday to Sunday of that week. Month: a month picker (defaults to the current month); the report covers the whole month Week / Month The period type. Week is the default. Clicking Week or Month reloads the report straight away, switching the Date field between a day picker and a month picker

Click View Report.

docs.title: Which work orders are included
docs.text:
A work order is included when:

  • it belongs to the selected customer,
  • its status is Completed or Invoiced, and
  • its date out falls in the period, or, if it has no date out, it was last updated in the period.

Work orders that are still Estimate, Approved or In progress never appear. They are listed by date out, oldest first.

docs.title: What the report shows
docs.text:
Under the customer name you see the period (for example Oct 05 - Oct 11, 2026, or October 2026 for a month) and the number of work orders.

Card What it shows Work Orders How many work orders are included Total Invoiced The sum of the Total of the invoices linked to those work orders (each invoice counted once, Void invoices excluded) Total Paid Payments recorded on those invoices Balance Due Total Invoiced - Total Paid. Red when above zero Column What it shows WO # The work order number. Click it to open the work order Equipment The work order's equipment, or - Description The work order description, shortened Completed The date out, or - Invoice The invoice number (click to open it), or - if not invoiced yet Amount Parts + labour of the work order (no shop supplies, discount or taxes) Status The status of the linked invoice: Draft, Sent, Partially paid or Paid, or -

The Totals row shows Total Invoiced, not the sum of the Amount column. When nothing matches you see No completed work orders in this period.

Why Total Invoiced can differ from the Amount column

Amount is the work order's parts and labour only. Total Invoiced uses the full invoice totals, which include shop supplies, discounts and taxes. If an invoice bundles work orders from outside the period, its whole total is still counted.

docs.title: Print
docs.text: Click Print to open the summary in a new tab, ready to print or save as PDF. It shows your logo and company name, the Company Address and Phone from Garage Settings, the title WORK SUMMARY with the period, Prepared For (customer name, phone and email), the work order table, Total Invoiced, Total Paid and Balance Due, and Generated on (date). The emailed PDF uses the same layout.

docs.title: Email the summary
docs.text:
1. Click Email to customer email.
  2. Confirm Email work summary to: followed by the customer name and each address.
  3. The page shows Work summary emailed to (addresses).
Item Value To The garage customer's Email CC The garage customer's Accountant Email, when filled in From Your company name and the Accountant Email from Application Settings Subject Work Summary (period) - (your company name), for example Work Summary Oct 05 - Oct 11, 2026 - (your company name) Body Dear (customer name), Here is a summary of work completed on your vehicles during this period., a work order table (WO #, Equipment, Completed, Invoice, Amount, Status) and Total Invoiced, Total Paid and Balance Due, ending with Thank you for your business! In the email body, Amount is the total of the linked invoice (or - if not invoiced), not the work order's parts and labour Attachment (your company name) Work Summary (period).pdf

The period in the subject and file name always uses the first and last day, also for a month (for example Oct 01 - Oct 31, 2026).

If the customer has no Email, the button is replaced by a greyed-out No email on file (Add an email address to this customer first). See Garage Customers & Equipment.

Manual sends and the schedule are independent

Sending a summary by hand does not change Next send or the delivery status, and a scheduled summary due the same day is still sent.

docs.title: Automatic Summary Emails
docs.text:
The Automatic Summary Emails box (Schedule recurring summary emails to this customer) sits below the buttons.

  1. Choose a Frequency.
  2. Click Save Schedule. The page shows Automatic summary set to Weekly on Monday. (or the option you chose), or Automatic summary disabled.
Frequency Sends on Period covered Disabled Never Weekly on Sunday ... Weekly on Saturday That weekday, every week Monday of the week that contains yesterday, through yesterday Monthly on the 1st The 1st of each month The whole previous month Monthly on the 15th The 15th of each month The whole previous month

Examples of the weekly period:

Schedule Sent on Covers Weekly on Monday Monday The previous Monday to Sunday (a full week) Weekly on Saturday Saturday Monday to Friday of the same week Weekly on Sunday Sunday Monday to Saturday of the same week

Use Weekly on Monday for full weeks

Any other weekday sends a partial week (Monday up to the day before the send day).

When a schedule is active the box also shows:

  • Next send: the next date the summary is due. For a weekly schedule this is the next occurrence of that weekday (today if it is that weekday and nothing was sent today). For a monthly schedule it is the 1st or 15th of this month, or of next month once that day has passed or the summary was already sent on it.
  • The result of the last automatic send, in green or red:
Message Meaning Summary delivered The email was sent No work orders in period - skipped No completed or invoiced work orders in the period, so nothing was sent An error message (red) The email could not be sent. It is not retried that day

docs.title: Customer Statement
docs.text:
The Customer Statement (Outstanding invoices — overdue and not yet due — ready to print or email.) lists what a customer still owes.

  1. On the Dashboard, click Customer Statement.
  2. Choose the Customer (only active customers are listed) and click View Statement.

docs.title: Which invoices are included
docs.text:
Only invoices with status Sent or Partially paid. Draft, Paid and Void invoices never appear. Each invoice shows its balance due (total minus payments), not its full total.

Section Invoices Overdue Due date before today Not Yet Due Due date today or later, or no due date

Within each section, invoices are sorted by due date, earliest first (invoices with no due date last). The statement is always as of today: there is no date to choose.

docs.title: What the statement shows
docs.text:
Under the customer name: Statement of account as of (today's date) and the number of outstanding invoices.

Card What it shows Overdue Total balance due of the overdue invoices. Red when above zero Not Yet Due Total balance due of the invoices not yet due Total Outstanding Overdue + Not Yet Due Table Columns Empty message Overdue (n) Invoice, Issued, Due, Days Overdue (for example 12 days), Balance Due, and an Overdue Subtotal row No overdue invoices. Not Yet Due (n) Invoice, Issued, Due, Terms, Balance Due, and a Not Yet Due Subtotal row No upcoming invoices.

Click an invoice number to open the invoice.

docs.title: Print / PDF
docs.text: Click Print / PDF to open the statement in a new tab. It shows your logo and company name, the Company Address and Phone from Garage Settings, the title STATEMENT OF ACCOUNT As of (date), Statement For (customer name, phone and email), the Overdue, Not Yet Due and Total Outstanding amounts, both tables (with Issue Date and Due Date columns), THANK YOU FOR YOUR BUSINESS! and Generated on (date). The emailed PDF uses the same layout.

docs.title: Email the statement
docs.text:
1. Click Email to customer email.
  2. Confirm Email statement of account to: followed by the customer name and each address.
  3. The page shows Statement of account emailed to (addresses).
Item Value To The garage customer's Email CC The garage customer's Accountant Email, when filled in BCC The Admin Email from Application Settings, when filled in, so you keep a copy of every statement (manual and automatic) From Your company name and the Accountant Email from Application Settings Subject Statement of Account as of (date) - (your company name), for example Statement of Account as of Oct 10, 2026 - (your company name) Body The overdue, not yet due and total outstanding amounts. When something is overdue it adds A balance of (amount) is past due. We kindly ask that you arrange payment at your earliest convenience. It ends with Thank you for your business! Attachment (your company name) Statement of Account (date).pdf, with the date as year-month-day (for example 2026-10-10)

The email is sent immediately, so the result is known right away:

  • Success: the delivery status becomes Statement delivered and today is recorded as the statement's sent date.
  • Failure: you see Statement could not be sent: (reason) and the delivery status shows the error in red.

When you cannot email:

Situation What you see The customer has no Email A greyed-out No email on file (Add an email address to this customer first) Nothing is outstanding A greyed-out Nothing to send (This customer has no outstanding invoices to send). If you get there another way: This customer has no outstanding invoices — nothing to send.

A manual send replaces today's automatic send

Sending a statement by hand records today as the sent date. If the same customer's automatic statement is due today, it is skipped, and Next send moves to the following scheduled date. This avoids the customer getting two statements on the same day.

docs.title: Send Test Email
docs.text:
The Send Test Email box (Preview exactly what the customer receives — sent to you, not to them.) sends the same statement and PDF to an address you choose.

  1. Check Recipient. It is prefilled with your own user email.

  2. Click Send Test. The page shows Test statement sent to (address).

  3. The subject starts with [TEST] and ends with the customer name: [TEST] Statement of Account as of (date) - (your company name) (customer name).

  4. It goes only to the Recipient: no CC to the customer's accountant and no BCC to the admin.
  5. It does not change the delivery status, the sent date or Next send.
  6. It works even when the customer has no email or nothing outstanding.

If Recipient is empty you see Please enter a recipient email address. If sending fails: Could not send test email: (reason).

docs.title: Automatic Statement Emails
docs.text:
The Automatic Statement Emails box (Schedule recurring statements of account to this customer) works like the summary schedule.

  1. Choose a Frequency: Disabled, Weekly on Sunday to Weekly on Saturday, Monthly on the 1st or Monthly on the 15th.
  2. Click Save Schedule. The page shows Automatic statement set to (frequency). or Automatic statement disabled.

A statement has no period: each automatic statement lists the invoices outstanding on the day it is sent.

When a schedule is active the box shows Next send: (calculated as for the work summary) and the result of the last send:

Message Meaning Statement delivered The statement was sent (automatically or with the email button) No outstanding invoices - skipped Nothing was owed on the scheduled day, so nothing was sent An error message (red) The email could not be sent. It is not retried that day

docs.title: How Automatic Emails Are Sent
docs.text:
UTX Freight sends the scheduled emails automatically: work summaries and statements are sent separately. Sending times are managed by UTX, so don't count on a specific time of day. Nothing is sent when the Garage add-on is off.

A scheduled email is sent to a customer only when:

  • the customer is active,
  • a Frequency other than Disabled is saved,
  • Next send is today,
  • the customer has an Email (customers without one are not sent anything and no status message is shown), and
  • nothing was already sent (or attempted) for that customer today.
Work summary Statement Content Work orders completed in the period (see the periods above) Invoices outstanding today Skipped when No work orders in the period: No work orders in period - skipped Nothing outstanding: No outstanding invoices - skipped Recipients To customer Email, CC Accountant Email To customer Email, CC Accountant Email, BCC Admin Email Success message Summary delivered Statement delivered

Skips and errors also count as "done for today": the customer is not tried again until their next scheduled date.

Spread your schedules

Spread customers across different weekdays and the 1st and 15th to keep each day light.

docs.title: I picked a Wednesday but the summary starts on Monday
docs.text:
Solution

That is expected. In Week view the report always covers Monday to Sunday of the week that contains the date you picked (Report snaps to Monday of selected week). Switch to Month for a calendar month.

docs.title: A work order is missing from the work summary
docs.text:
Solution

Only Completed and Invoiced work orders appear, and only when their date out is in the period (or, with no date out, when they were last updated in the period). Check the work order's status and date out. Also check that it belongs to this customer.

docs.title: The automatic summary says "No work orders in period - skipped"
docs.text:
Solution

No completed or invoiced work orders matched the period, so no email was sent. Remember that a weekly schedule only covers Monday up to the day before the send day. Schedule Weekly on Monday to cover full weeks.

docs.title: An invoice is missing from the statement
docs.text:
Solution

Statements only list Sent and Partially paid invoices. A Draft invoice must be marked sent or emailed first (see Garage Invoices). Paid and Void invoices are never listed.

docs.title: The Email button says "Nothing to send" or "No email on file"
docs.text:
Solution

No email on file: add an Email to the garage customer. Nothing to send (statement only): the customer has no outstanding balance. You can still use Print / PDF or Send Test.

docs.title: The scheduled statement did not go out today
docs.text:
Solution

Check the message next to Next send. If someone emailed the statement by hand today, the automatic send is skipped on purpose. If the customer has no Email, nothing is sent: add one, then send the statement with the email button.

docs.title: Revenue minus Parts Cost does not equal Profit
docs.text:
Solution

Revenue includes the Shop Supplies Fee; Profit does not. The difference is the shop supplies amount.

docs.title: The Dashboard numbers do not match my invoices for the month
docs.text:
Solution

Revenue uses the date the invoice was created in UTX Freight (not its invoice date), includes drafts and taxes, and excludes void invoices. Outstanding is always the total of all unpaid invoices, whatever period is selected.

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
Tips

  • Fill in each customer's Email and Accountant Email so summaries and statements reach both the customer and their bookkeeper.
  • Use Send Test before the first statement to a new customer, so you see exactly what they will receive.
  • Schedule weekly summaries on Monday so each email covers a full week.
  • Spread automatic schedules across weekdays and the 1st and 15th to keep each day light.
  • Check the delivery message next to Next send now and then to catch failed emails.
  • Mark invoices Sent (or email them) promptly: drafts never appear on statements.

docs.title: Garage Settings & Tax Rates
docs.text: Set the defaults your garage uses for each office (labor rate, payment terms, invoice numbering and the company details printed on documents) and manage the GST/QST tax rates applied to garage invoices.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The Garage sidebar has two setup pages: Settings (page title Garage Settings) and Taxes (page title Tax Rates).

  • Garage Settings are per office. Each office has its own labor rate, payment terms, invoice prefix, invoice number sequence and company details. The page always shows the settings of the office you are currently working in (see Multi-Office).
  • Default Labor Rate ($/hour) pre-fills the Rate of each new labor line on a work order.
  • Default Payment Terms pre-fills the Terms of new garage invoices.
  • Invoice Prefix and the office's invoice sequence build garage invoice numbers such as GRG-00001. The page shows the number the next invoice will get.
  • Company Information (address, phone, GST and QST numbers) is printed on garage invoices, work order estimates, statements and summaries.
  • Tax Rates are shared with freight. Garage > Taxes shows and edits the same tax records as Manage Taxes in the main application, from all offices. See Charge Types, Expense Types & Taxes.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
To set up a new office's garage:

  1. In the Garage sidebar, click Settings.
  2. Enter the Default Labor Rate ($/hour), pick the Default Payment Terms and set the Invoice Prefix.
  3. Under Company Information (shown on invoices), fill in Company Address, Phone, GST Number and QST Number.
  4. Click Save Settings.
  5. Click Taxes in the sidebar and check that your office has an Active tax rate. If not, click New Tax Rate, enter the Name, GST (Federal Tax %) and QST (Provincial Tax %), tick Active and click Create Tax Rate.

Do this before the first invoice

Invoice numbers are assigned the moment an invoice is created, and new invoices take their terms and tax from these pages. Set them up first so your numbering, terms and taxes are right from the start.

docs.title: Access & Permissions
docs.text:
Both pages are part of the Garage area, which is only available when the Garage add-on is enabled for your company (see Add-ons & Options).

Role Garage Settings Tax Rates Admin View and edit View, create, edit and delete Manager View and edit View, create, edit and delete Garage View and edit View, create, edit and delete Accountant, Dispatch, Warehouse, Customer, drivers No access to the Garage area No access to the Garage area

Garage Taxes also apply to freight

The Garage Taxes page edits the same tax records as Manage Taxes in the main application. A change made there by anyone with Garage access also applies to freight invoices. See Tax Rates are shared with freight.

How to get there:

  • Garage sidebar Settings opens Garage Settings.
  • Garage sidebar Taxes opens Tax Rates.

See Garage Overview for how to open the Garage area.

docs.title: Garage Settings
docs.text:
The Garage Settings page is a single form for the current office. An office's settings are created automatically the first time they are needed (for example when someone opens Settings, or creates a work order or invoice in that office), with these starting values:

Setting Starting value Default Labor Rate ($/hour) 95.00 Shop Supplies (% of subtotal) 5.00 Default Payment Terms Net 30 Invoice Prefix GRG Next invoice number 1 (shown as GRG-00001) Company Information fields Empty

docs.title: Editing the settings
docs.text:
1. Make sure you are working in the right office (see Multi-Office).
  2. In the Garage sidebar, click Settings.
  3. Change the fields you need (see the table below).
  4. Click Save Settings. The page reloads with the message Settings updated successfully.

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
Field Hint shown on the page What it does Default Labor Rate ($/hour) Applied to new labor line items Pre-fills the Rate of each new labor line on a work order. You can change the rate on any line. Existing labor lines keep their rate when you change this setting. Must be 0 or more. Shop Supplies (% of subtotal) Suggested percentage for shop supplies fee Your office's suggested shop supplies percentage, for reference. The fee itself is entered as a dollar amount on the work order or invoice. See How shop supplies are charged. Must be between 0 and 100. Default Payment Terms — Pre-fills Terms on new garage invoices. Choices: Due on Receipt, Net 15, Net 30, Net 45, Net 60. Invoice Prefix Next invoice: followed by the next number, for example GRG-00042 The text placed before the number on new garage invoices. See Invoice numbering. Company Address Placeholder 123 Main St\nCity, Province Postal Code Multi-line address printed on garage documents. Press Enter to start a new line. Printed documents keep your line breaks; emails show the lines joined with \|. Phone — Phone number printed on garage documents. GST Number — Your GST registration number, printed next to the GST line on invoices and work order estimates. QST Number — Your QST registration number, printed next to the QST line on invoices and work order estimates.

Garage company details are separate from freight

Company Address, Phone, GST Number and QST Number here are used only by Garage documents. Freight invoices use the GST and QST numbers in the main application settings (see Application Settings). If you use both, fill in both places.

Allowed values

The labor rate must be 0 or more and the shop supplies percentage must be between 0 and 100. Settings outside these ranges are not saved.

docs.title: Invoice numbering
docs.text:
Every garage invoice gets its number when it is created (drafts included). The number is built as:

<Invoice Prefix>-<next number padded to 5 digits>

For example, prefix GRG and next number 42 give GRG-00042. After each new invoice, the office's next number goes up by one.

  • The Next invoice: line under Invoice Prefix shows the number the next invoice will get. It reflects the saved prefix, so it updates after you click Save Settings.
  • The next number cannot be edited on this page. It only moves forward as invoices are created. It is never reset and numbers are never reused, even if an invoice is voided.
  • Changing the Invoice Prefix only affects invoices created afterwards. Existing invoices keep their numbers, and the sequence continues from where it was (for example GRG-00042 is followed by SHOP-00043).
  • Each office has its own sequence, but invoice numbers must be unique across all offices. If you use the Garage in more than one office, give each office a different prefix so their invoice numbers never overlap.

Always set a prefix

GRG is only the starting value. Keep a prefix in the Invoice Prefix field so your invoice numbers stay easy to recognise.

See Garage Invoices & Payments for how invoices are created.

docs.title: Where the company information appears
docs.text:
Document Company Address and Phone GST Number and QST Number Printed / PDF garage invoice Printed work order (estimate) Invoice email (body) — (they are on the attached PDF invoice) Work summary email (body and attached PDF) — Customer statement (print and email) — Customer summary (print) —

Each item is only printed when it is filled in. The GST and QST numbers appear in brackets next to the GST and QST lines, and only when the document has a GST or QST amount above 0. See Garage Work Orders, Garage Invoices & Payments and Garage Reports.

docs.title: How shop supplies are charged
docs.text:
Shop supplies are charged as a dollar amount:

  • On a work order, enter the amount in Shop Supplies Fee.
  • On an invoice, the shop supplies amount is the sum of the work orders' fees, unless you enter a different amount on the invoice.

Shop supplies are taxable: GST and QST are calculated on them along with the taxable parts and labor. See Garage Work Orders and Garage Invoices & Payments.

docs.title: Tax Rates
docs.text: The Tax Rates page (subtitle Manage GST/QST rates for invoices) lists tax rates in alphabetical order by name.

docs.title: Columns
docs.text:
Column Shows Name The tax rate name. This is what appears in the Tax Rate dropdown on garage invoices. GST % The federal tax percentage. QST % The provincial tax percentage. Active An Active (green) or Inactive (grey) badge. Invoices How many garage invoices use this tax rate. Actions Edit, and Delete when no garage invoice uses the tax rate.

The list shows all offices

The page lists every tax rate in the application, from all offices, and does not show which office each one belongs to. Use names that make the office clear (for example QC GST/QST 2025) if you have several offices.

If there are no tax rates at all, the page shows No tax rates yet with a Create Tax Rate button.

docs.title: Adding a tax rate
docs.text:
1. Click New Tax Rate.
  2. Fill in the form (see below).
  3. Click Create Tax Rate. You return to the list with the message Tax rate created successfully.

The new tax rate belongs to the office you are currently working in. There is no office field on this form.

docs.title: Editing a tax rate
docs.text:
1. Click the Edit icon on the row. The page Edit Tax Rate: name opens.
  2. Change the fields.
  3. Click Update Tax Rate (or Cancel to go back). You return to the list with the message Tax rate updated successfully.

Editing does not change which office the tax rate belongs to.

docs.title: Form fields
docs.text: Field Hint shown on the page Notes Name * Placeholder e.g. GST/QST 2025 The name shown in the Tax Rate dropdown on garage invoices and wherever freight lists taxes. Active Available for use on invoices Only active tax rates of your current office are offered on garage invoices. New tax rates are active by default. GST (Federal Tax %) Federal Goods & Services Tax percentage (placeholder 5.0) Enter 5 for 5%. The browser accepts 0 to 100 in steps of 0.001. QST (Provincial Tax %) Quebec Sales Tax percentage (placeholder 9.975) Enter 9.975 for 9.975%. Enter 0 if you do not charge a provincial tax. The browser accepts 0 to 100 in steps of 0.001.

docs.title: How garage documents use tax rates
docs.text:
• New invoice: the Tax Rate dropdown lists only the active tax rates of your current office, plus No tax. The first active tax rate of the office is pre-selected.
  • Invoice from a work order (Generate Single Invoice): the office's first active tax rate is used.
  • Work order totals and printed estimate: use the office's first active tax rate. With no active tax rate, no tax is shown.
  • GST and QST are calculated on the taxable parts and labor plus shop supplies, after any discount. The amounts are saved on the garage invoice and recalculated when a draft invoice is saved again.

Keep one active tax rate per office

Work orders and one-click invoices pick "the first active tax rate" of the office. If an office has several active tax rates, you cannot be sure which one is picked. Keep only one active per office and set the others to inactive.

docs.title: Deleting a tax rate
docs.text:
1. Click the Delete icon on the row.
  2. Confirm the Delete name? prompt.
  3. The tax rate is removed and the message Tax rate deleted. appears.

A tax rate can only be deleted when no invoice uses it, garage or freight. If invoices use it, the tax rate is kept and the message below appears:

Cannot delete tax rate — N invoice(s) use it.

where N is the number of garage and freight invoices using it. Set the tax rate to inactive instead.

Deleting cannot be undone

A deleted tax rate cannot be restored. If you only want to stop offering it on new garage invoices, untick Active instead.

docs.title: Tax Rates are shared with freight
docs.text:
Garage Taxes and Manage Taxes in the main application show and edit the same tax records. A change on either page applies to both freight and garage invoices.
