Garage > Taxes Manage Taxes (freight) Who can open it Anyone with Garage access (Admin, Manager, Garage) See Charge Types, Expense Types & Taxes Which tax rates are listed All offices See Charge Types, Expense Types & Taxes New tax rates belong to Your current office The office chosen on the form Invoices column counts Garage invoices Freight invoices Delete is allowed when No garage invoice and no freight invoice uses it See Charge Types, Expense Types & Taxes

Changing a rate affects freight invoices

Freight invoices store which tax they use, not the amount. If you edit the GST % or QST % of a tax rate that freight invoices use, those freight invoices are recalculated with the new percentage. When a rate changes, create a new tax rate, make it active, set the old one to inactive and leave its percentages unchanged.

docs.title: How do I change the next invoice number?
docs.text:
Solution

You cannot. The Next invoice: line is a preview only, and the number moves forward by one each time a garage invoice is created. You can change the Invoice Prefix, which applies to invoices created afterwards.

docs.title: How do I charge shop supplies?
docs.text:
Solution

Enter the fee as an amount in Shop Supplies Fee on the work order, or enter it on the invoice. See How shop supplies are charged.

docs.title: I changed the labor rate but my work order still shows the old rate
docs.text:
Solution

Default Labor Rate ($/hour) only pre-fills new labor lines. Existing lines keep the rate they were created with. Edit the Rate on those lines if needed.

docs.title: The settings look different from what I saved
docs.text:
Solution

Garage Settings are per office. Check which office you are working in (see Multi-Office). Each office has its own labor rate, terms, prefix, invoice sequence and company details.

docs.title: My tax rate is not in the invoice's Tax Rate dropdown
docs.text:
Solution

The garage invoice dropdown only lists active tax rates of your current office. Check that the tax rate is ticked Active and that it was created in the office you are working in. The Tax Rates page lists all offices, so a tax rate can appear there but belong to another office.

docs.title: Why can't I delete a tax rate?
docs.text:
Solution

A tax rate used by any garage or freight invoice cannot be deleted. The Invoices column on this page counts garage invoices only, while the message Cannot delete tax rate — N invoice(s) use it. counts garage and freight invoices together. To stop offering the tax rate, untick Active instead.

docs.title: My address or GST number is missing from the invoice
docs.text:
Solution

Fill in Company Address, Phone, GST Number and QST Number under Company Information (shown on invoices) in Garage Settings for the office that owns the invoice. GST and QST numbers only print next to a GST or QST line above 0, and they are not shown in the invoice email body.

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
Best Practices

  • Fill in Garage Settings and create an active tax rate for each office before creating the first garage invoice.
  • Give each office a distinct Invoice Prefix so invoice numbers never collide.
  • Keep one active tax rate per office so work orders and invoices always pick the right one.
  • When tax rates change, create a new tax rate and deactivate the old one instead of editing its percentages.
  • Remember that tax rates are shared with freight: agree with your accounting team before editing or deleting one.

docs.title: Garage Work Orders
docs.text: Create, price and track repair and service jobs in the Garage add-on, from the first estimate through to the invoice.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
• The Work Orders page is the first page of the Garage. It lists every work order of your current office, newest first, 20 per page, with status tabs, a search box and an Actions menu on each row.
  • A work order has a Customer (required), optional Equipment, a description, dates, an odometer reading, an assigned technician, Parts lines, Labor lines, a Shop Supplies Fee and Internal Notes.
  • Every work order moves through five statuses: Estimate Approved In progress Completed Invoiced. An estimate can also go straight to In progress. A completed work order can be Reopened back to Approved. A completed work order becomes Invoiced when you generate an invoice for it.
  • When a work order moves to In progress, the quantities of its catalogue parts are taken out of parts inventory.
  • You can edit a work order at any status, including Invoiced while its invoice is still a draft. Saving then recalculates the draft invoice. Only a work order billed on an invoice that has left draft (sent, partially paid, paid) is locked.
  • Print Estimate opens a printable estimate for the customer. Internal notes are never printed.
  • The Odometer In you enter updates the equipment's odometer, but only when the new reading is higher.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
1. Click Garage in the left menu of UTX Freight. The Garage opens on Work Orders.
  2. Click New Work Order.
  3. Type at least two letters in Customer and pick the customer from the list (or click the green + to create one).
  4. Click in Equipment to see that customer's units and pick one (or click + to create one).
  5. Optional: pick a template under Apply Template and click Apply to fill in parts and labor.
  6. Add or adjust Parts and Labor lines, then click Create Work Order. It is saved as an Estimate.
  7. Click Print Estimate to give the customer a copy. When they agree, click Mark Approved.
  8. When work starts, click Mark In progress (parts are taken out of inventory). When it is done, click Mark Completed.
  9. Click Generate Single Invoice to bill it, or Bundle with Other Work Orders to put several completed work orders on one invoice. See Garage Invoices.

docs.title: Access & Permissions
docs.text:
The Garage is an add-on. When it is not turned on for your company, the Garage menu item does not appear and Garage pages send you back to the dashboard. See Add-ons and Options.

Role Work Orders (view, create, edit, change status, print, invoice) Admin Yes Manager Yes, for the offices they belong to Garage Yes, for the offices they belong to Dispatch, Accountant, Customer, Driver, Warehouse and other roles No — the Garage menu item is hidden

Where to find it:

  • Left menu Garage — opens the Work Orders list
  • Garage sidebar Work Orders
  • Garage sidebar Customers the work order button on a customer row — opens New Work Order with that customer already filled in

Current office

Work orders belong to an office. The list, the counts, the customer, equipment and part searches, the technician list and the tax used for totals all follow the office you are currently working in. With multiple offices, switch office to see another office's work orders. See User Roles for what each role can do elsewhere.

docs.title: Status tabs
docs.text:
Above the list is one tab per status, each with a count:

Tab Shows All Every work order (selected by default) Estimates Status Estimate Approved Status Approved In Progress Status In progress Completed Status Completed Invoiced Status Invoiced

The counts follow the search: while a search is active, each tab counts only the work orders that match it.

docs.title: Search
docs.text:
Type in the search box and click Search. One search term is matched (case-insensitive, anywhere in the text) against:

  • the customer's first name, last name and company name
  • the work order description
  • the equipment unit number, VIN, license plate, make, model and equipment type (truck, trailer, chassis)

Work orders with no equipment are still found by customer or description.

The search keeps the tab you are on. Clicking a different tab starts again without the search term.

docs.title: Columns
docs.text:
Column What it shows ID The work order number, for example #128. Click it to open the work order. Customer The customer name, with the company in brackets when there is one Equipment Type, unit number and year/make/model of the equipment, or - if none Status A coloured badge (see Status colours) Date In The Date In of the work order Technician The Assigned Technician, or - Total Parts + labor + shop supplies fee, before tax Actions The menu (see below)

Work orders are sorted by creation date, newest first, 20 per page, with page links at the bottom when there is more than one page.

docs.title: Row Actions menu
docs.text:
Click on a row. The menu has up to three sections and only shows what applies to that work order:

Section Item Shown when View View details Always Open invoice (with the invoice number) The work order is on an invoice that is not void Print estimate Always (opens in a new tab) Move to Approved, In progress, Completed The next statuses allowed from the current one (see Status workflow) Actions Edit The work order is not locked. Shows updates draft when it is on a draft invoice. Generate invoice Status is Completed and there is no active invoice Bundle with others Same as Generate invoice Reopen Status is Completed

A status change or reopen started from the list brings you back to the list, on the same tab.

docs.title: Empty states
docs.text:
• No work orders yet — shown when no search is active and the tab you are on has no work orders (for example the Invoiced tab when nothing is invoiced yet). Click Create Your First Work Order.
  • No work orders match "…" — your search found nothing. The message reminds you what the search covers. Click Clear search to go back to the tab without the search term.

docs.title: Creating and Editing a Work Order
docs.text: Click New Work Order on the list, or Edit on a work order. New work orders start with Date In set to today and one empty part row and one empty labor row.

docs.title: Apply Template
docs.text:
The purple Apply Template box appears at the top of the form only when your office has at least one active template (Garage sidebar Templates, see Garage Parts and Templates).

  1. Pick a template in -- Select a template --.
  2. Click Apply.

What happens:

  • Empty part and labor rows are removed first.
  • The template's parts and labor lines are added after the lines already on the form. Nothing you already entered is replaced, so applying a template twice adds its lines twice.
  • Part lines get the template's part (when it is a catalogue part), description, quantity, cost and charge. Labor lines get the template's description, hours and rate.
  • A Template Applied message confirms "" has been applied. Message Meaning Please select a template first. You clicked Apply without picking a template Failed to load template. The template could not be loaded. Try again.

docs.title: Customer
docs.text:
Customer * is required.

  • Type at least 2 characters. The list shows up to 15 active customers of your office whose first name, last name or company name contains what you typed. Pick one.
  • Typing a name without picking it from the list does not select a customer. If you save that way, you get Customer is required. Please search and select a customer.
  • Click the green button to open Quick Create Customer: fill in First Name *, Last Name *, and optionally Phone and Company, then click Create & Select. The new customer is created and selected. If a name is missing you see First name and last name are required.
  • While the work order is on a draft invoice, the customer box is greyed out, the green button is not shown, and the customer cannot be changed (see Editing a work order on a draft invoice).

docs.title: Equipment
docs.text:
Equipment is optional.

  • When a customer is selected, clicking in the equipment box immediately lists that customer's active equipment. Type to narrow the list.
  • With no customer selected, typing searches all active equipment of the office.
  • The search matches unit number, make, model, VIN and license plate, and shows up to 15 results.
  • After you pick a unit, it is shown as a blue chip (equipment — owner). Click Change on the chip to clear it and search again.
  • Text you type but never pick from the list is cleared when you leave the box.
  • Click the green button to open Quick Create Equipment: pick the Equipment Type * (Truck, Trailer or Chassis) and optionally fill in Unit Number, Year, Make, Model and License Plate, then click Create & Select. If a customer is already selected on the work order, the new equipment is linked to that customer. If no type is picked you see Equipment type is required.

Full equipment records (VIN, odometer, service history) are managed under Garage sidebar Equipment. See Garage Customers and Equipment.

docs.title: Job details
docs.text:
Field Notes Description The work to be done. Shown on the work order, the printed estimate, and searchable from the list. P/O Number The customer's purchase order number. Shown on the work order and the printed estimate. Date In Defaults to today on a new work order Est. Completion Expected completion date. Printed on the estimate as Estimated Completion. Odometer In Current mileage. Whole number, 0 or more. See Odometer updates. Assigned Technician Pick from the active users of your current office. The field is hidden when there are none. Shop Supplies Fee A dollar amount, 0 or more. Added to the total and always counted as taxable. Internal Notes (not shown on invoice) For your shop only. Shown on the work order page, never on the printed estimate.

There is no Date Out field on the form. Date Out is set automatically when the work order is marked Completed.

docs.title: Parts lines
docs.text:
Each part row has: Part / Description, Qty, Cost, Charge, Line Total, Tax and a red to remove the row. Click Add Part to add a row.

  • From the parts catalogue: type at least 2 characters of a part name or SKU in Part / Description. The list shows up to 15 active parts of your office as Name (SKU). Picking one links the line to the catalogue part and fills in the name, Cost (purchase price) and Charge (selling price). You can change the prices afterwards.
  • Low Stock warning: if the picked part's quantity on hand is at or below its reorder point, a Low Stock message appears for a few seconds: has only left in stock. It is a warning only; the line is still added.
  • Free-text line: type a description without picking from the list. The line is not linked to the catalogue and never affects inventory.
  • When a line is first saved with a catalogue part (or switched to a different one) and Cost or Charge is 0, or the description is empty, they are filled from the catalogue when you save.
  • Qty must be a whole number greater than 0. Cost and Charge must be 0 or more.
  • Line Total (Qty × Charge) updates as you type.

docs.title: Labor lines
docs.text:
Each labor row has: Description, Hours, Rate, Line Total, Tax and . Click Add Labor to add a row.

  • Rate is pre-filled with the Default Labor Rate ($/hour) from Garage sidebar Settings (see Garage Settings and Taxes). You can change it per line.
  • Description is required. Hours must be 0 or more (in steps of 0.25). Rate must be greater than 0.
  • Line Total (Hours × Rate) updates as you type.

docs.title: Taxable flag
docs.text: The Tax checkbox on each part and labor line is ticked by default, including on lines added by a template. Untick it for lines that should not be taxed. Only ticked lines, plus the shop supplies fee, are taxed in the totals.

docs.title: Saving
docs.text:
Click Create Work Order (new) or Update Work Order (edit). Cancel leaves without saving.

Message When Work order created successfully. A new work order was saved. It is always created as Estimate. Work order updated successfully. Changes saved Work order updated. Draft invoice was recalculated to . Changes saved on a work order that is on a draft invoice errors prevented this work order from being saved: followed by a list Something is missing or invalid (for example no customer, a part quantity of 0, a labor line with no description). Fix the listed items and save again.

Remove rows you don't use

Every part and labor row on the form is saved and checked as a line. Click on any empty part or labor row you do not need before saving.

docs.title: Status Workflow
docs.text:
From Can move to Button on the work order page Confirmation text Estimate Approved Mark Approved Mark as Approved? The customer has agreed to the estimate. Estimate In progress Mark In progress Mark as In Progress? Parts inventory will be decremented. Approved In progress Mark In progress Mark as In Progress? Parts inventory will be decremented. In progress Completed Mark Completed Mark as Completed? You can generate an invoice or reopen the work order from the completed state. Completed Invoiced Generate Single Invoice or Bundle with Other Work Orders See Garage Invoices Completed Approved (reopen) Reopen Work Order Reopen this work order? It goes back to Approved because the work is not actually finished. You do not need this just to edit it — use Edit instead.

The same moves are in the row Actions menu under Move to and Actions (the Completed confirmation there reads Mark as Completed? You can generate an invoice or reopen the work order., and Reopen asks Reopen this work order? It will return to Approved.).

After a move you see Work order #: status changed to . Reopening shows Work order #: reopened to Approved.

What each move does:

  • To In progress: catalogue parts on the work order are taken out of inventory (see Parts inventory).
  • To Completed: Date Out is set to today, unless it already has a date. Date Out is not shown on the work order page or the printed estimate; it appears as Completed: on the invoice and in the customer summary report.
  • To Invoiced: happens when the work order is put on an invoice (Generate Single Invoice, Bundle with Other Work Orders, or adding it to an invoice).
  • Reopen: only from Completed. The work order goes back to Approved. Date Out is not cleared.

You cannot move a work order backwards (other than Reopen), and there are no moves out of Invoiced. To take a work order off an invoice, delete or void the invoice, or remove the work order from it, on the invoice side. See Garage Invoices.

Message Meaning Cannot transition to . That move is not allowed from the current status Cannot modify an invoiced work order. The work order is on an invoice that has left draft Only completed work orders can be reopened. Reopen was used on a work order that is not Completed Work order must be completed before invoicing. An invoice was requested for a work order that is not Completed

Editing does not need Reopen

You can edit a completed work order directly with Edit. Use Reopen only when the work is actually not finished.

docs.title: Status colours
docs.text: Badge Status  Yellow Estimate  Blue Approved  Purple In progress  Green Completed  Grey Invoiced

docs.title: Deleting a work order
docs.text: Work orders are not deleted from the Work Orders list or the work order page. Leave unused estimates in the Estimates tab.

docs.title: Parts Inventory
docs.text:
Inventory is the quantity on hand of each part in Garage sidebar Parts (see Garage Parts and Templates). Only lines linked to a catalogue part count; free-text lines never touch inventory.

Event Effect on quantity on hand Work order moves to In progress Each catalogue part line's Qty is subtracted. Stock never goes below 0. A catalogue part line is removed while the work order is In progress, Completed or Invoiced (draft invoice) The line's Qty is added back A catalogue part line is removed while the work order is Estimate or Approved Nothing (stock was never taken out)

Add parts before In progress

Stock is taken out when the work order moves to In progress. Put all catalogue parts on the work order before that step. To correct a part's stock at any time, adjust its quantity on hand under Garage Parts.

docs.title: Editing a Work Order on a Draft Invoice
docs.text:
A work order that is Invoiced on an invoice still in draft stays editable, so you can fix a line without voiding the invoice.

  • The work order page shows an amber banner: This work order is on which is still a draft — you can still edit it. Saving a change updates the draft invoice totals automatically. No need to void the invoice. with an Open draft invoice link.
  • The edit form shows: This work order is on draft invoice . Your changes will be saved and the draft invoice total will be updated automatically. You do not need to void the invoice. The customer cannot be changed here — remove the work order from the invoice first.
  • The Customer box is read-only. To bill a different customer, remove the work order from the invoice first.
  • When you save, the draft invoice totals are recalculated. A change to the work order's Shop Supplies Fee moves the invoice's shop supplies fee by the same amount, so an amount typed directly on the invoice is kept.
  • If you started the edit from the draft invoice page, saving takes you back to the invoice. Otherwise you return to the work order.

docs.title: When the work order is locked
docs.text:
Once the invoice is marked sent (or has payments), the work order is locked. Edit is greyed out with a and the tooltip This work order is billed on a sent invoice. Reopen that invoice to Draft to edit it again. Trying to edit shows one of these messages:

Invoice status Message Way out Sent Cannot edit this work order — it is billed on invoice . Use 'Reopen to Edit' on that invoice first. Use Reopen to Edit on the invoice, then edit the work order Partially paid Cannot edit this work order — it is billed on invoice , which has payments recorded. Remove the payments, then use 'Reopen to Edit' on it. Remove the payments on the invoice, then Reopen to Edit Paid Same message as partially paid See the warning below

If the invoice was marked sent between opening the form and saving, the save is refused with the same message and nothing is changed.

Work orders on paid invoices

Payments cannot be removed from a fully paid invoice (Cannot remove payments from a fully paid invoice.), and only sent invoices without payments can be reopened. So a work order on a paid invoice cannot be edited. Voiding the invoice takes its work orders off it and returns them to Completed, but it also voids a paid invoice — check with your accountant first. See Garage Invoices.

docs.title: The Work Order Page
docs.text: Click the work order ID or View details.

docs.title: Header
docs.text:
• Work Order #, the total including tax, the status badge, Date In, the technician and the P/O number.
  • Buttons, depending on status: Edit, Print Estimate, Mark Approved / Mark In progress / Mark Completed, and for Completed work orders Generate Single Invoice, Bundle with Other Work Orders and Reopen Work Order. View Invoice appears when the work order is on an invoice that is not void.

docs.title: Status hint
docs.text:
A blue bar under the header tells you the next step:

Status Hint Estimate This is an estimate. When the customer approves, click 'Mark Approved' to proceed. Approved Customer approved. Click 'Mark In Progress' when work begins. In progress Work is being performed. Click 'Mark Completed' when the job is done. Completed Work is finished. Click 'Generate Invoice' to bill the customer. Invoiced This work order has been invoiced. with a View Invoice link

On a draft invoice, the amber draft banner replaces this bar.

docs.title: Cards and tables
docs.text:
Section Contents Customer Name (with company), phone and email Equipment Equipment name, VIN, Odometer (the equipment's current reading), Odometer In (this work order's reading) and a View Service History link to the equipment page. Shows No equipment assigned when there is none. Description Shown when filled in Parts Description, Qty, Unit Price (the charge price), Total, Tax ( taxable, not taxable), and Parts Subtotal. No parts added when empty. Cost prices are not shown here. Labor Description, Hours, Rate, Total, Tax, and Labor Subtotal. No labor added when empty. Totals Parts, Labor, Shop Supplies (when above 0), then, when a tax is set up, Subtotal, GST (x%), QST (x%), and Total Internal Notes Yellow box, shown when filled in

Back to Work Orders returns to the list.

docs.title: How tax is calculated
docs.text:
• The tax rates come from the first active tax set up for your current office (Garage sidebar Taxes, see Garage Settings and Taxes). If there is no active tax, no tax lines are shown and the total has no tax.
  • Taxable amount = ticked part lines + ticked labor lines + the Shop Supplies Fee.
  • GST and QST are each that taxable amount × their rate, rounded to the cent.
  • Total = parts + labor + shop supplies + GST + QST.

List total vs. page total

The Total column on the list is before tax. The total in the work order header and at the bottom of the page includes tax. The final invoice amount can differ again if the invoice has a discount or a different tax. See Garage Invoices.

docs.title: Print Estimate
docs.text:
Click Print Estimate on the work order page, or Print estimate in the row Actions menu. The estimate opens in a new browser tab; use your browser's print command to print it or save it as PDF.

The estimate shows:

  • A faint ESTIMATE watermark, your logo (when one is set up for your installation), company name, Garage Services, and the Company Address and Phone from Garage Settings (Company Information), when filled in.
  • ESTIMATE and WO # at the top right.
  • Prepared For: customer name, phone and email.
  • Vehicle / Equipment (when equipment is set): equipment name, VIN and Plate.
  • P/O Number (when set), Date In, Estimated Completion (when set) and Status.
  • Description (when set).
  • One table with all part lines, then all labor lines: Description, Qty/Hours, Rate, Amount, Tax ( for taxable lines).
  • Totals: Subtotal (parts + labor), Shop Supplies (when above 0), GST and QST (only when above 0, with your GST/QST numbers from Garage Settings when set), and Estimated Total.

Not printed: internal notes, the assigned technician, odometer readings and part cost prices.

The estimate can be printed at any status; the Status line shows where the work order is.

docs.title: Odometer Updates
docs.text:
When you save a work order with an Odometer In value and equipment selected:

  • If the reading is higher than the equipment's current odometer (or the equipment has none), the equipment's odometer is set to it.
  • If it is the same or lower, the equipment's odometer is left unchanged. The work order still keeps its own Odometer In.

This happens when you first enter Odometer In, change it, or change the equipment on the work order. The equipment odometer never goes down from a work order.

docs.title: "Customer is required" but I typed the customer name
docs.text:
Solution

Typing is not enough: you must pick the customer from the drop-down list that appears after 2 characters. If the customer does not exist, click the green + next to Customer and use Quick Create Customer.

docs.title: The equipment list is empty when I click in Equipment
docs.text:
Solution

With a customer selected, the list, and anything you type, only covers that customer's active equipment. A unit linked to no customer or to another customer does not appear. Check under Garage Equipment that the unit is active and linked to the right customer, or create it with the + button (it is linked to the selected customer). Equipment that is not linked to any customer can only be found when no customer is selected yet.

docs.title: Inventory did not go down for a part I added
docs.text:
Solution

Stock is taken out when the work order moves to In progress, and only for lines linked to a catalogue part (picked from the list). Free-text lines never change inventory. To correct stock, adjust the part's quantity on hand under Garage Parts.

docs.title: I can't edit an invoiced work order
docs.text:
Solution

If the invoice is a draft, Edit works and the invoice total is recalculated. If the invoice was sent, open it and use Reopen to Edit. If it has payments, remove them first. A fully paid invoice cannot be reopened (see When the work order is locked).

docs.title: How do I delete a work order?
docs.text:
Solution

Work orders are not deleted from the Garage screens. Leave unused estimates in the Estimates tab.

docs.title: The total on the list is different from the total on the work order
docs.text:
Solution

The list total is before tax. The work order page total includes GST and QST from your office's active tax.

docs.title: I don't see Apply Template
docs.text:
Solution

The box only appears when your current office has at least one active template. Create or enable one under Garage Templates.

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
Tips

  • Pick parts from the catalogue instead of typing them, so inventory and costs stay accurate.
  • Get all parts on the work order before marking it In progress, since that is when stock is taken out.
  • Use Edit, not Reopen, to fix lines on a completed work order.
  • Bill completed work orders with Generate Single Invoice or Bundle with Other Work Orders.
  • Fix mistakes while the invoice is still a draft. Once it is sent, you have to reopen the invoice; once it is paid, you cannot edit the work order.
  • Enter Odometer In on every visit to keep the equipment's mileage and service history up to date.
  • Use Internal Notes for shop-only information; it never appears on the printed estimate.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: Set up a new UTX Freight account by hand and take your first order from creation to invoice.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
A new account needs a few things in place before the first order can be priced, dispatched and invoiced. This page walks through them in order:

  • Prices: zone prices, delivery cities assigned to zones, terminal default rates and, if you have the fuel surcharge add-on, this month's fuel surcharge. Without them an order prices at $0.00.
  • A customer: the company you haul for.
  • A contact at that customer. Every order is placed on behalf of a person, not just a company.
  • Your yard: at least one chassis and one driver, so the order can be dispatched.
  • Your tax numbers: GST, QST and NIR, printed on invoices and proofs of delivery.
  • The first order: create it, dispatch it, invoice it.

Use the in-app checklist

Admins and Managers see a setup checklist entry at the top of the left menu. On a new account it reads Getting started. Once the account has issued at least one invoice it reads Setup check, and when every required step is done it reads Setup complete with a green check. The checklist checks your data, shows which steps are still missing, and has a button for each step that opens the right screen. See Setup Checklist.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
1. Set your prices. Open your name at the top of the screen, then use Manage Zones, Manage Cities (assign a zone to each city you deliver to), Manage Terminals (default rate) and Charge Types (set one charge type's Use as default for to Terminal Fee). If the fuel surcharge add-on is on, set this month's rate in Fuel Schedule in the left menu.
  2. Go to Customers and click Add a new Customer. Enter the Name and click Save Changes.
  3. On the Customers list, find the company and click Add Person. Enter First Name, Last Name and Email, then click Add this person.
  4. Add one chassis in Equipments and one driver in Mobile Users > Drivers, Brokers & Yard.
  5. Admins only: open your name > Settings > Edit settings and fill in GST Number, QST Number and NIR Number.
  6. Go to Orders, click Create a new order, pick the contact in Place the order on behalf of, choose the Job type, fill in the order and click Create Job.
  7. Dispatch the order to your driver from Dispatch, then create the invoice from Invoices.

docs.title: Access & Permissions
docs.text:
Step Who can do it Set zone, city, terminal and charge type prices Admin, Manager Create a customer and add people Admin, Manager. Dispatch only if your account has dispatcher customer management turned on (off by default; ask UTX support). Set a person's role (staff logins) Admin only Add equipment and drivers Admin, Manager, Dispatch Enter GST, QST and NIR numbers (Settings) Admin only Create an order Admin, Manager, Dispatch. Accountant if your account allows accountants to manage orders (on by default). Customer only if your account has customer order entry turned on (off by default; ask UTX support). Choose who the order is for (Place the order on behalf of) Admin, Manager and Dispatch. Anyone else creates the order for themselves. See the setup checklist Admin and Manager

The Customer Service role has the same access as Dispatch everywhere in this table. Options such as dispatcher customer management and customer order entry are turned on for your account by UTX support. See Add-ons and Options and User Roles.

docs.title: Step 1: Set Your Prices
docs.text:
UTX Freight prices an order by looking up the delivery city, reading which zone it is in, and taking that zone's price. Do this before the first order: an order whose delivery city has no zone price is priced at $0.00.

The screens below are in the menu under your name at the top of the screen (Manage Zones, Manage Cities, Manage Terminals, Charge Types).

  1. Zone prices: open Manage Zones and enter the price you charge for a delivery into each zone you use. Zones start at $0.00. Disable the zones you do not use.
  2. Cities in zones: open Manage Cities, click the Shipping filter (cities where at least one order has been delivered), and set the zone on each city you deliver to. A city with no zone prices at $0.00.
  3. Terminal fees: open Charge Types, edit the charge you bill for terminals and set Use as default for to Terminal Fee. Then open Manage Terminals and enter a Default Rate on the terminals you pull from. That rate is added as a charge to every order using the terminal. Without both, terminal fees never appear on an invoice.
  4. Fuel surcharge (only if the fuel surcharge add-on is on): open Fuel Schedule in the left menu and enter the percentage for the current month. With no rate for the month, orders are built without a fuel charge. The rate does not carry forward, so set it again each month.

Details: Zones and Cities, Managing Terminals, Charge Types and Taxes, Fuel Surcharge.

Negotiated prices

A price agreed with one customer is set later on that customer's record and overrides the zone price for that customer only. It shows in blue so nobody mistakes it for the standard rate. See Managing Customers.

docs.title: Step 2: Create Your First Customer
docs.text:
All orders in UTX Freight are placed on behalf of a contact Person from a Customers company, so the first step is to create the customer company.

  1. From the left menu, select Customers.
  2. Click Add a new Customer at the top right.
  3. Enter the Name. It is the only required field.
  4. If your account has the warehouse or garage add-on, the Service field offers more than one choice. Keep Intermodal (or Intermodal & Warehouse) for a company you haul for. Only people at companies with the Intermodal service can be picked on a new order.
  5. Click Save Changes.

docs.title: Finding a customer on the list
docs.text:
The Customers page opens on your own company. Use the search box labelled Filter companies and users: type at least two characters of a company name, or of a person's first name, last name or email, to narrow the list. The filter tabs on the left change which companies are listed:

Tab Shows Your company name Your own company (where your office staff logins live) All Active Active customer companies Disabled Disabled customer companies Brokers Companies marked as brokers

If the warehouse add-on is on, Warehouse and Intermodal tabs are also shown.

docs.title: Step 3: Add a Contact Person
docs.text:
Once the customer exists, add a contact Person for it. Orders are attached to people, and a customer with no contact cannot be ordered for.

  1. From the left menu, select Customers.
  2. In Filter companies and users, type the company name.
  3. On the company row, click Add Person.

  1. Fill in First Name, Last Name and Email. Title, Office #, Office Ext. #, Mobile # and Fax # are optional.
  2. Click Add this person.

An invitation email is sent immediately

Clicking Add this person emails an Invitation instructions message to the address you entered. To set someone up quietly, use a placeholder address such as customername+1@yourdomain.com and change it later.

docs.title: What the invited person sees
docs.text:
1. They receive the Invitation instructions email with an Accept invitation link.
  2. The link opens a page where they confirm their first and last name, choose a password, confirm it, and click Create your account.
  3. They are signed in. You can attach orders to them before they accept.

docs.title: Roles: everyone starts as a Customer
docs.text:
Every person added with Add Person is created with the Customer role, including people you add to your own company. To give office staff a staff role (Dispatch, Accountant, Manager, and so on):

  1. Add them with Add Person under your own company on the Customers list.
  2. An Admin opens their Edit Person page, picks the Role, and clicks Save Changes.

The Role field is only shown to Admins, and only for people in your own company. See People and Invitations and User Roles.

Customer logins and orders

A Customer-role person can log in and see their company's orders. They can only create orders themselves if your account has customer order entry turned on (ask UTX support). See Customer Portal.

docs.title: Notification emails
docs.text: When an order is dispatched or completed, the person it was placed for gets an email, but only while Email Notifications is ticked on their Edit Person page. The box is ticked by default for new people. Untick it for anyone who should not receive these emails. See Notifications and Emails.

docs.title: Step 4: Set Up Your Yard
docs.text:
An order is dispatched onto a piece of equipment and to a driver. Before you dispatch, add at least:

  • One chassis: open Equipments and add one unit with its Name/Number, Type and plate number. See Equipment.
  • One driver: open Mobile Users > Drivers, Brokers & Yard, click Add a new mobile user, set the Role to Driver and click Save. Note the Access Code: that is what the driver enters in the phone app, and only active drivers can use it. See Mobile Users.

docs.title: Step 5: Add Your Tax Numbers
docs.text:
Your registration numbers are printed on every invoice and proof of delivery, and they start blank. Only an Admin can change them.

  1. Open your name at the top of the screen, then Settings.
  2. Click Edit settings.
  3. Under Invoice Settings, enter your GST Number and QST Number.
  4. Under POD Settings, enter your NIR Number.
  5. Click Save Changes.

These are your own registration numbers, not tax rates. See Application Settings.

docs.title: Step 6: Create Your First Order
docs.text:
1. From the left menu, select Orders.
  2. Click Create a new order.
  1. Under Change Customer, pick the contact in Place the order on behalf of. The list shows people, written as PERSON NAME [ Company ], not companies. Only active people at active Intermodal companies are listed. The order is created for whoever is selected here, so check it before you submit. This field is shown to Admin, Manager and Dispatch only; other users create the order for themselves.
  2. Under Order Information, choose the order type in Job type. Start with Container Import. The rest of the form appears only after you choose a type.
  3. For an Import or Export, choose the Terminal Name in the pick-up terminal section. For an Import it is titled Full container pick up terminal; for an Export, Empty container pick up terminal.
  4. Fill in the delivery address (titled Container delivery address for an Import). Choosing the delivery City is what looks up the zone and the price.
  5. Enter the Container number under Information.
  6. Click Create Job at the bottom of the form.

docs.title: Required fields
docs.text:
Field Required when Container number (shown as Trailer number for a Dry Van Move) Always Job type Always Terminal Name (pick-up terminal) Import and Export orders

Everything else is optional for saving the order, but the delivery city is what prices it. If the price shows $0.00, go back to Step 1 above. Full field reference: Order Form.

docs.title: Order types
docs.text:
The types offered in Job type depend on your account. By default only Container Import and Container Export are enabled. Other accounts may also have Container Transfer, Dry Van Move or International Export. Ask UTX to enable a type you need.

Suspended accounts cannot create orders

If your account is suspended, the Create a new order button turns red and opens a notice instead of the order form, and new orders are blocked. See Add-ons and Options.

docs.title: Step 7: Dispatch and Invoice
docs.text:
1. Dispatch: open Dispatch and assign the order to your driver and the chassis you added. Have the driver open the phone app and confirm they see the load. When the order is dispatched, the contact gets an Order #... is now dispatched email if Email Notifications is ticked. See Dispatch and Driver Workflow.
  2. Invoice: open Invoices and create an invoice for the order. Check the amount against what you expected, and email it to yourself first to see what your customer will receive. See Creating Invoices.

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
• Order Workflow: the order statuses from new to completed
  • Dispatch: assigning drivers and equipment
  • Driver Workflow: pickup, delivery and signature on the phone app
  • Container Tracking: tracing the shipment
  • Creating Invoices: invoicing and getting paid

docs.title: My new order shows $0.00
docs.text:
Solution

The delivery city has no zone, or the zone has no price. Open Manage Cities (Shipping filter) and set the zone, then open Manage Zones and set its price. If a shipper / receiver was used, make sure it has a city set. See Zones and Cities.

docs.title: The customer is not in "Place the order on behalf of"
docs.text:
Solution

The list shows people, not companies. Add a contact to the company with Add Person. If the person exists, check that they are active (Active for orders on Edit Person), that the company is active, and that the company's Service includes Intermodal.

docs.title: No terminal fee on the invoice
docs.text:
Solution

One charge type must have Use as default for set to Terminal Fee in Charge Types, and the terminal needs a Default Rate in Manage Terminals. See Managing Terminals.

docs.title: My contact gets no emails
docs.text:
Solution

Make sure Email Notifications is ticked on the person's Edit Person page, and that the order was placed on behalf of that person. Dispatched and completed emails go only to the person the order is for.

docs.title: I added a dispatcher but they log in as a customer
docs.text:
Solution

Everyone added with Add Person starts as a Customer. Make sure they were added under your own company, then have an Admin set their Role on Edit Person.

docs.title: I cannot open Settings to add my tax numbers
docs.text:
Solution

Only an Admin can change Settings. Ask an Admin to enter the GST Number, QST Number and NIR Number.

Best Practices

  • Work through the in-app setup checklist; it checks your data and tells you exactly what is missing.
  • Use a placeholder email for test contacts so no one receives an invitation by accident.
  • Send your first invoice to yourself before sending one to a customer.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text: An A–Z list of the terms, screen labels, abbreviations and status names used in UTX Freight, each with a short definition and a link to the page that explains it in full.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
UTX Freight uses trucking, port and rail vocabulary, and some things have more than one name: one name in exports and order history, another on a filter tab, and a third in a tooltip. This page puts all of those names side by side.

  • Labels are written exactly as the screen shows them, in bold. Status names keep their capitals and punctuation (for example App. Taken, Arrived - Awaiting delivery).
  • Synonyms are grouped. When two names mean the same thing, both are listed and point to the same definition. See Synonyms & Alternate Names.
  • Every entry links to its page. The glossary only gives the short version; the linked page has the details, steps and permissions.
  • Some terms only exist on some accounts. Add-ons (for example Garage, Warehouse, Fuel Surcharge, container tracking) and the shipment mode (intermodal or ground) decide which screens you see. Entries say so when it matters. See Add-ons & Options.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
1. Use your browser's search (Ctrl+F, or Cmd+F on a Mac) and type the word, label or abbreviation you are looking for.
  2. If the word is a nickname or an older name (for example Canned Jobs or App. Made), start with the Synonyms & Alternate Names table.
  3. For a short code on the Orders page (CI, LFD, B# …), see Order Type Codes and Abbreviations.
  4. Click the link in the See column to open the full page.

docs.title: Access & Permissions
docs.text:
The glossary is a reference page. Everyone can read it. The terms it defines are used by the roles below; each user has exactly one role.

Sees rates only with Can manage rates? See User Roles & Permissions for the full permission matrix.

docs.title: Order Type Codes
docs.text:
Each order row on the Orders page starts with a short code badge. The Orders Page Legend lists the same codes.

Code Full name (Legend) Job type on the form Filter card name CI Container Import Container Import Import CX Container Export Container Export Export TF Container Transfer Container Transfer Transfer DV Dry Van Move Dry Van Move Dry Van IX International Export International Export International Export WH Warehouse Warehouse orders (separate list) Listed in the Legend only when warehouse orders are enabled

Order types are switched on per account by UTX. By default only Import and Export are enabled. See Orders.

docs.title: Order Status Names
docs.text:
Exports / history Tooltip / Legend Filter tab Icon and colour Next button new New Order New red Make App. App. Taken Appointment Made App. Made orange Dispatch Dispatched Order Dispatched (Legend: Dispatched) Dispatched green Complete Completed Order Completed (Legend: Completed) Completed grey Actions

Other tabs on the Orders page group statuses:

  • In Progress (the default tab): New + App. Taken + Dispatched.
  • Not Invoiced: Completed orders not on an invoice, delivered on or after the Order Start Date (Admin / Manager).
  • Late Invoicing: like Not Invoiced, but only orders delivered before the end of the week two weeks ago (Admin / Manager).

Invoiced is not an order status

Putting an order on an invoice does not change its status. It stays Completed. Invoices have their own statuses (new, Invoiced, Paid, Partially Paid). See Creating Invoices.

See Order Status Workflow.

docs.title: Container Status Names
docs.text:
A container status says where the container is. It is separate from the order status. These are the built-in statuses that come with UTX Freight. Your company can add custom statuses with its own names and colours; those are not listed here. Statuses can be shown in any colour you configure; the colours below are the defaults.

Container status Default colour Short meaning Arrived - Awaiting delivery Green Import: the container has arrived at the terminal and is ready for pickup Arrived - Missing customs Red Import: arrived, but customs clearance is missing Arrived - On hold Red Import: arrived, but on hold At customer Grey The container is at the customer (no default job type description) Driver at terminal Light green The driver is at the terminal for the pickup Dropped at customer Red Delivered to the customer. Set automatically on an import's delivery signature and an export's drop signature Empty at customer Yellow An empty container is at the customer (waiting for pickup, or for loading) Empty at yard Blue An empty container is stored at your yard. Set by the yard worker's Empty at yard button Export Orange The container is processed for export Full at customer Orange Loaded at the customer and ready for pickup Full at yard Purple A full container is stored at your yard. Set by the yard worker's Full at yard button Live load Red The container is being loaded or unloaded live On rail Pink The container is on rail transport On route to customer Yellow Being moved to the customer On route to terminal Yellow Being moved to the terminal (empty return on imports, loaded on exports) On route to yard Yellow Being moved to the yard (no default job type description) On vessel Dark blue The container is on the vessel Ready for 2nd stop Grey Ready for a second stop (no default job type description) Returned to terminal Green Returned to the terminal; the order leaves the driver app. Set automatically by Drop Completed (import) and Transfer Completed Reused for export Orange Export: the container is reused for another export shipment

When an order has no container status, N/A is shown in grey. See Container Statuses.

docs.title: Are App. Taken and App. Made different statuses?
docs.text:
Solution

No. It is one status. App. Taken is the name in exports and order history, App. Made is the filter tab, and Appointment Made is the tooltip. See Order Status Workflow.

docs.title: Is a Client the same as a Customer?
docs.text:
Solution

No. A Customer is the company you bill. A Client is a Shipper / Receiver: a pickup or delivery location. Manage Clients opens the Shipper / Receiver list. A customer only sees a Shipper / Receiver's deliveries when it is linked to it as a consignee. See Shippers & Receivers.

docs.title: Someone mentioned a "broker". Which one?
docs.text:
Solution

Check where they saw it. On a Dry Van order's Broker field or in Order Expenses, it is a name from Manage Brokers. In Transport Company ( broker ) or on the Customers list, it is a customer flagged Broker. On a phone, it is a mobile user with the Broker role. See Lookup Lists.

docs.title: What is MGT?
docs.text:
Solution

MGT is Montreal Gateway Terminals, the container tracking source for the Racine and Cast terminals. On screens it is shown as MGT (Racine/Cast). See Container Tracking.

docs.title: A term in this glossary does not appear in my account
docs.text:
Solution

Many terms belong to an add-on (Garage, Warehouse, Fuel Surcharge, Multi-Office, container tracking, Driver Login Links, tags) or to one shipment mode (intermodal or ground). If the add-on is off, its screens are hidden. Contact UTX support to ask about turning it on. See Add-ons & Options.

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
Speaking the same language

  • When you report a problem to UTX support, use the label exactly as the screen shows it (for example App. Made tab, C.Status column), and the order number.
  • Use Special Note for instructions drivers must see, and Comments for internal notes.
  • Name custom container statuses clearly so they do not look like built-in ones.
  • Open the Legend on the Orders page when you see a code or icon you do not recognise.

docs.title: Integrations
docs.text: Every outside service UTX Freight connects to, what data goes back and forth, which add-on turns it on, and where you see it in the app.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
UTX Freight connects to a small number of outside services. All of them are set up and run by UTX: you never enter API keys or terminal passwords yourself, and most integrations only need an add-on turned on for your account.

Integration What it does for you Add-on / option Where you see it CN Rail Container status, ETA, Last Free Day, customs, GPS and bill of lading from CN CN tracking Tracking icon on Orders / Dispatch, CN Tracking and Alerts on Dispatch Port of Montreal (Termont) Container availability, holds, customs, vessel and carrier data from Termont / Viau Port of Montreal tracking Tracking icon on Orders / Dispatch, Port Tracking and Alerts on Dispatch MGT (Racine/Cast) Container availability, holds, customs, vessel and carrier data from MGT MGT tracking Tracking icon on Orders / Dispatch, Port Tracking and Alerts on Dispatch AWS Textract Reads uploaded delivery orders and pre-fills a new order Auto Orders (beta) Upload button and AUTO ORDERS card on Orders Postmark Sends all outgoing emails through a UTX-managed email service Email Delivery Method = Postmark in Settings Settings page, the From line of every email EDI 210 invoice CSV Downloads one invoice as an EDI 210 CSV file EDI invoicing (account option set by UTX) Invoices > Actions > EDI 210 QuickBooks-ready export Exports the listed invoices in a QuickBooks import layout None (standard) Invoices > Export panel NHTSA VIN decoder Fills Year, Make and Model from a VIN Garage Garage Equipment form > Decode
  • Add-ons are turned on per account by UTX. If a button or icon described here is missing, the add-on is probably off. See Add-ons and Options.
  • Automatic vs. on demand -- container tracking and Auto Orders run in the background on a schedule. EDI, QuickBooks export and VIN decoding happen only when you click the button.
  • Credentials -- the CN, MGT, AWS and Postmark accounts belong to UTX and are stored on the server. They are never shown in the app.
  • No public API -- UTX Freight does not offer an API for customers. See Is there an API?.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
• Track containers: ask UTX to turn on the tracking add-on for your terminal (CN, Port of Montreal, MGT). Make sure your pickup terminals are named as in Which terminal triggers which source. Then click the tracking icon in the Container# column on Orders or Dispatch.
  • Create orders from documents: with the Auto Orders add-on, click Upload on Orders, wait for the document to reach Need Review, then click Review.
  • Send an invoice as EDI 210: on Invoices, open the Actions menu of the invoice and click EDI 210.
  • Export invoices for QuickBooks: on Invoices, filter the list, choose Layout QuickBooks columns in the Export panel and click Export.
  • Decode a VIN: in the Garage, on the equipment form, type the VIN and click Decode.

docs.title: Access & Permissions
docs.text:
Each integration follows the permissions of the feature it lives in.

Integration Who can use it Container tracking popup (CN, Termont, MGT) Admin, Manager, Dispatch, Customer Service. Accountant on Orders only when your account lets accountants manage orders (an option set by UTX -- ask UTX support). Customers, drivers, warehouse and garage users don't see it. See Container Tracking Container Alerts page Opened with the Alerts button on Dispatch, so Admin, Manager, Dispatch and Customer Service. Only Admins can mark alerts read or unread. See Container Alerts Auto Orders Admin, Manager, Dispatch and Customer Service can upload and review. See Auto Orders Email Delivery Method (Postmark) Admin only (Settings). See Application Settings EDI 210 and QuickBooks export Admin, Manager and Accountant (the roles that can open Invoices). Dispatch and Customer Service have no access VIN Decode Admin, Manager and Garage users (the roles that can edit Garage equipment)

docs.title: Container Tracking (CN, Termont, MGT)
docs.text: The three tracking integrations work the same way from your point of view: the system checks containers in the background, stores the latest terminal data, and shows it in a popup. The full guide is Container Tracking.

docs.title: Which terminal triggers which source
docs.text:
The source is chosen from the order's pickup terminal name (upper or lower case does not matter), not from the container number.

Source Pickup terminal name Icon in Container# CN Rail Exactly CN (nothing else in the name) Red train Termont (Port of Montreal) Contains TERMONT or VIAU Blue ship MGT (Racine/Cast) Contains RACINE or CAST Orange ship

Start the terminal name with the keyword

The tracking popup picks its source from the first word of the terminal name (CN, TERMONT, VIAU, RACINE or CAST). Name tracked terminals so the keyword comes first, for example CAST Montreal rather than Montreal CAST.

New or renamed terminals

If tracking does not start for a terminal you have just added or renamed, contact UTX support.

See Managing Terminals to set up your terminals.

docs.title: What each source sends
docs.text:
Source How UTX gets the data Data you see CN Rail CN's intermodal tracking service, using UTX's CN account. Each check combines five CN data sets: shipment tracking, ETA, bill of lading, GPS position and shipment status CLM status (for example De-ramped), event location, destination, lot location, customs status, equipment type, size, empty/full, weights, waybill status, GPS position, BOL number, shipper, consignee, commodity, Destination ETA, Last Free Day Termont The terminal operator's public container lookup web page (no login needed) Terminal section, hold message, available for pickup (yes/no), visit and transit state, customs status, shipping line, vessel, voyage, origin, size/type, seal, gross weight, carrier IN / OUT timeline, ETA, Last Free Day MGT (Racine/Cast) MGT's container inquiry web page, signed in with UTX's MGT account. Containers no longer in the yard are looked up in MGT's history Same layout as Termont

If one of CN's supplementary data sets (ETA, BOL, GPS or status) fails, the rest of the check still goes through: you simply see fewer sections in the popup.

docs.title: Refresh behaviour
docs.text:
• Stored data is refreshed automatically. A scheduled job run by UTX checks the containers and stores the result. You cannot trigger that check from the app. The refresh interval is set by UTX. The Updated ... ago line in the popup tells you when that container was last refreshed.
  • One live lookup: the CN Tracking button on Dispatch asks CN live (basic tracking data only) each time you open it. It does not refresh the stored data that the popup, alerts and Port Tracking use. Port Tracking shows stored data only. See Tracking Bulk Update.
  • Only in-progress orders (status New, App. Taken or Dispatched) created after the Order Archive Cutoff Date are checked. A container stops being checked once it has left the terminal (CN: Departed or Completed; Termont / MGT: transit state Out).
  • Batches: orders are processed in groups of 200 for CN, 50 for MGT and 10 for Termont. Within a group, a container number that appears on several orders is checked once. Blank container numbers and N/A are skipped.
  • What changes on your orders: for Termont and MGT only, when a container's terminal data changes, blank fields on the in-progress orders with that container number (Seal Number, Weight in KG, Steamship Line and Container Size when a matching list entry exists, and Customs released set to yes when the customs description contains "release") are filled in. Existing values are never overwritten. CN data never changes order fields. ETA and Last Free Day are never copied automatically -- use the CN Tracking and Port Tracking buttons on Dispatch (Tracking Bulk Update).
  • Alerts: status changes (pickup ready, customs released, departed) and approaching Last Free Days create alerts on the Container Alerts page and in the daily digest email. See Container Alerts.
  • Health: the Integration Health cards at the top of Container Alerts show, per source, whether the last pull worked and returned containers. See Container Alerts.

Terminal websites can change

Termont and MGT data is read from the terminals' own web lookups. When a terminal changes its website or is down, tracking for that source can stop until UTX adapts. Check Integration Health on Container Alerts, and contact UTX support if a source stays stale.

docs.title: Auto Orders (AWS Textract)
docs.text:
Add-on: Auto Orders (beta). Where: Orders > Upload button and the AUTO ORDERS card (Processing, Need Review, Completed).

Data flow:

  1. You upload a document in Upload a Document.
  2. UTX Freight sends the file to Amazon Web Services (AWS) Textract, a text-recognition service, through UTX's AWS account. The document shows in Processing.
  3. A scheduled background check collects the recognised text, extracts the order details (container number, reference, seal, terminal, size, weight and so on, depending on the document layout) and moves the document to Need Review.
  4. You check the values in the review window and save. Nothing becomes an order until a person saves it.

Refresh: the move from Processing to Need Review waits for the next scheduled check, so there is a delay. Reload the Need Review tab after a while.

Full guide, including recognised document layouts and error messages: Auto Orders.

docs.title: Postmark Email
docs.text:
Option: Settings > Edit settings > Email Delivery Method > Postmark — Use the Postmark email API. The other choice is SMTP — Use your own SMTP server credentials (the default).

What happens when Postmark is selected:

  • UTX Freight's outgoing emails (for example invoices, PODs, notifications and alert digests) go through Postmark, an email delivery service managed by UTX, instead of your SMTP server. The SMTP sections of the settings are not used.
  • The From address is replaced by a UTX sending address. The sender name is kept.
  • The Reply-To is set to your original From address (unless the email already has its own Reply-To), so replies from customers still reach your mailbox.
  • The Postmark access token is managed by UTX. When Postmark is selected, the Settings page shows API Token as Configured or Not configured, and the Message Stream used for your system.

Check with UTX before switching

If the Postmark token is not configured, emails cannot be sent. Switch to Postmark only when UTX support confirms it is ready, then use Test Email Configuration > Send Test on the Settings page. See Application Settings.

docs.title: EDI 210 Invoice CSV
docs.text:
Option: EDI invoicing, an account option turned on by UTX. Where: Invoices > Actions menu on a row > EDI 210.

Data flow: one way, on demand. Clicking EDI 210 downloads a CSV file named EDI210_<invoice number>_<YYYYMMDD>.csv (the date is the download date). UTX Freight does not send the file anywhere: you upload or email it to your customer's EDI system yourself.

What is in the file:

  • One header row, then one row per order on the invoice.
  • Dates in dd/mm/yyyy, amounts without thousands separator or currency sign.
  • Invoice number, item number (1, 2, 3... per order), the order's delivery PO number (MSC PO), terms in days (0 for Due on Receipt), invoice and due dates, currency (the customer's default currency), the order's base rate, the order's reference number as WAYBILL-NUMBER, waybill date, vessel, voyage, container number, the first four characters of the container number, the receiver's UN code and the invoice total (with taxes when the invoice is taxed), repeated on every row.
  • Many other columns (bond, chassis detention, hazmat, weight, size and so on) are always empty.

FUEL is always 0 -- fuel goes under OTHER

The FUEL, PRE-PULL and STORAGE columns are always 0.00. All of an order's charges, including the fuel surcharge, are added together in the OTHER column. Charges are not split by type.

Fill in UN codes

The DESTINATION - UNLOC column is the UN Code of the receiver's city. Set it in the Un Location Information (EDI Compatible) form for each city (see Zones & Cities) so the column is not empty.

Full column list: Creating Invoices.

docs.title: QuickBooks-Ready Invoice Export
docs.text:
Add-on: none. Where: Invoices > Export panel in the filter bar.

Data flow: one way, on demand. UTX Freight does not connect to QuickBooks. It builds a file that you import into QuickBooks yourself.

  1. Filter the Invoices list (status tab, search, invoice date range).
  2. In the EXPORT panel, choose QuickBooks columns in the first drop-down (the other choice, AR aging detail, is not a QuickBooks layout) and Excel (.xlsx) or CSV (.csv) in the second.
  3. Click Export. The panel tells you how many invoices are currently listed; only those are exported.

The file has one row per listed invoice, sorted by invoice date, with the columns Invoice, Invoice Date (YYYY-MM-DD), Customer, Details (<type> - <container> per order, separated by commas; the type is CI import, EX export, DV dry van, TF transfer or IX international export), Amount before sales taxes, GST Charged, QST Charged (both 0.00 when the invoice is not taxed) and Amount after sales taxes. An export is limited to 20,000 invoices; above that you see a message and nothing is downloaded.

Full guide: Invoices.

docs.title: NHTSA VIN Decoder (Garage)
docs.text:
Add-on: Garage. Where: Garage > Equipment > new or edit form > Decode button next to VIN.

Data flow: when you click Decode, your browser sends the VIN directly to the free public VIN decoder of the U.S. National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA). Nothing goes through UTX's servers and nothing is saved until you save the equipment form.

  • The VIN must be at least 11 characters, otherwise you see Please enter a valid VIN (at least 11 characters).
  • If NHTSA returns at least one of make, model or model year, Year, Make and Model are all replaced with what NHTSA returned (a value NHTSA did not return is cleared), and a short VIN Decoded message shows the result.
  • If NHTSA knows the VIN but returns no make, model or year: VIN was found but no make/model/year data returned. Please enter manually.
  • If NHTSA does not answer within 10 seconds or cannot be reached: Could not reach NHTSA VIN decoder. Please enter vehicle details manually.

Full guide: Garage Customers & Equipment.

docs.title: Is There an API?
docs.text:
No. UTX Freight has no public API for customers. You cannot connect your own software to read or create orders, invoices or tracking data.

UTX Freight has a few internal endpoints that UTX uses to monitor and support your system. They are protected, not documented, and not available to customers.

To get data out of UTX Freight, use the built-in exports (for example the invoice Export panel and EDI 210). See Data Exports.

docs.title: I don't see a tracking icon, Upload button or EDI 210 option
docs.text:
Solution

Each of these needs its own add-on or account option. Check Add-ons and Options and contact UTX support to turn it on. For tracking, also check that the order's pickup terminal is named as in Which terminal triggers which source.

docs.title: Can I force a container to refresh now?
docs.text:
Solution

No. The stored tracking data is refreshed on UTX's schedule. For CN, the CN Tracking button on Dispatch shows a live answer from CN, but it does not update the popup. Look at Updated ... ago in the popup and the Integration Health cards on Container Alerts. If a source has not updated for a long time, contact UTX support.

docs.title: The EDI file shows FUEL 0.00 but the order has a fuel surcharge
docs.text:
Solution

This is expected. The fuel surcharge is included in the OTHER column together with all other charges. FUEL is always 0.00.

docs.title: Does UTX Freight sync with QuickBooks automatically?
docs.text:
Solution

No. The QuickBooks columns export is a file you import into QuickBooks yourself. Nothing is sent to QuickBooks.

docs.title: Customers say our emails come from a different address
docs.text:
Solution

With Postmark selected, the From address is a UTX sending address, while the sender name stays yours and Reply-To points to your original address. Replies still reach you. If you need your own From address, switch Email Delivery Method back to SMTP.

docs.title: Can I get an API token?
docs.text:
Solution

No. There is no customer API. Use the exports described in Data Exports.

Best Practices

  • Name the CN pickup terminal exactly CN, and start other tracked terminal names with TERMONT, VIAU, RACINE or CAST, so tracking and the popup pick the right source.
  • Check Integration Health on Container Alerts before trusting a status that hasn't changed in a while.
  • Always review Auto Orders values before saving -- text recognition can misread characters.
  • Set the UN Code on your receivers' cities before sending EDI 210 files.
  • Send a test email from Settings after any change to Email Delivery Method.

docs.title: Sending Invoices & Recording Payments
docs.text: Email an invoice to your customer with its proof of delivery attached, then record the payments you receive against it.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Both tasks start from a row on the Invoices list (see Invoices):

  • Sending: the envelope button on a row opens the Send invoice to customer window. The email carries the invoice PDF, the POD of each order that has one, and optionally the order documents.
  • Status on send: a successful send of a new invoice changes its status to Invoiced. Any other status is left as it is.
  • Delivery label: every send attempt leaves an OK or Failed! label next to the status.
  • REVISED: once an invoice has been sent successfully, the next send is marked REVISED in the subject and the PDF file name.
  • Payments: Record a payment in the cog menu opens the invoice in a pop-up where you add payment lines (date, check number, amount) or click Balance Paid In Full.
  • Status is yours to set: adding payments never changes the status by itself. An invoice is treated as settled only when its status is Paid.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
To email an invoice:

  1. Go to Invoices and find the invoice.
  2. Click the envelope button on its row.
  3. Check To, Cc and Subject, and tick or untick Include documents.
  4. Click Send. A notification confirms the result, and the row shows OK or Failed!.

To record a payment:

  1. On the invoice row, open the cog menu and click Record a payment.
  2. Click Balance Paid In Full, or click (+) Add payment and fill in the payment line.
  3. Set Invoice Status if needed (for example Partially Paid).
  4. Click Update Invoice.

docs.title: Access & Permissions
docs.text:
Role Access Admin Can send invoices, record payments and change status. Also has access to Settings, including Test Email Configuration Manager Can send invoices, record payments and change status for invoices of the offices they belong to Accountant Can send invoices, record payments and change status for invoices of the offices they belong to Dispatch, Customer Service No access to invoices Customer, Warehouse, Garage, drivers No access

How to get there:

  • Invoices > envelope button on a row (send)
  • Invoices > cog menu on a row > Record a payment (payments)
  • Invoices > click the status text on a row (change status inline)

docs.title: The envelope button
docs.text:
Each invoice row has an envelope button in the Actions column:

Button Tooltip Meaning Blue envelope Email Invoice The invoice has never been sent successfully Grey envelope Resend Invoice The invoice was sent successfully before

Click it to open the Send invoice to customer window.

docs.title: Fields in the Send invoice to customer window
docs.text:
The window reminds you that Starred (*) fields are required. Several fields are filled in for you when it opens. You can change any of them before sending.

Field Required Pre-filled with To Yes The customer's Accountant Email (from the customer record) Cc No The Invoice Default CC Address from Settings, followed by the customer's Accountant Email (CC), separated by a comma. Either part is left out if it is empty Bcc No Empty Subject Yes Built from your company name and the invoice number (see below) Include documents No Ticked

To, Cc and Bcc accept several addresses separated by commas (,) or semicolons (;). Each address must be a valid email address, or the invoice is not sent.

Fix the source, not just the email

If To or Cc is wrong every time, correct the Accountant Email or Accountant Email (CC) on the customer. See Managing Customers. The company-wide CC is the Invoice Default CC Address in Application Settings.

docs.title: Subject line
docs.text:
The subject is pre-filled in this format:

<Your company name>[ REVISED] Invoice #<invoice number>[ - PO#<PO or reference>]

Part When it appears REVISED Only if the invoice has already been sent successfully (its row shows the green OK label). See The REVISED rule - PO#… Only if the invoice has exactly one order. It shows that order's delivery PO number, or its reference number if there is no PO number

Examples:

  • Acme Transport Invoice #01234 - PO#45-7781 (first send, one order)
  • Acme Transport REVISED Invoice #01234 (resend, several orders)

docs.title: Warnings in the window
docs.text:
Two notices can appear under the fields. Neither one stops you from sending.

Notice When it appears WARNING: This order is missing (N) PODs in PDF format (yellow) One or more orders on the invoice have no signed POD and no scanned signed POD. N is the number of those orders. They are sent without a POD N additional documents will be attached if Include Documents is selected! (blue) The invoice has one order and that order has documents uploaded. N is the number of documents

Document count notice

The blue document count only appears on invoices with one order. On invoices with several orders it does not appear, even when the orders have documents. The documents are still attached if Include documents is ticked.

docs.title: Sending
docs.text:
1. Review the fields.
  2. Click Send (or Close to cancel).
  3. The window closes and a spinner replaces the envelope on the row while the email is built and sent.
  4. When it finishes, the row refreshes and a notification appears at the top of the page:
Result Notification Sent Invoice Sent! The invoice was sent successfully. Sending failed Sending Invoice Failed! The invoice was not sent due to …error…. Please try again or contact the administrator. An address was rejected Sending Invoice Failed! The invoice was not sent. Please correct the email address and try again.

docs.title: Email body
docs.text:
The email is headed New invoice from your company name. It says the invoice is attached as a PDF and that the attachments include the invoice and the proof of delivery (if available) for each order on the invoice. It ends with Thank you for your business. and your company name.

If your account is set up to link emails back to the app, the email also contains a View your orders link.

docs.title: Attachments
docs.text:
Attachment File name When Invoice PDF <Your company name> Invoice <invoice number>.pdf, or <Your company name> Invoice REVISED <invoice number>.pdf on a revised send Always Signed POD (one per order) <Your company name> POD Signed #<order ID>.pdf. International export orders use eBoL instead of POD When the order has a signature captured on the delivery or pickup Scanned signed POD (one per order) The scanned file's own name When the order has no captured signature but has a scanned signed POD uploaded Order documents Each document's own file name Only when Include documents is ticked. Every document of every order on the invoice is attached

For each order, a captured signature takes priority: if the order has one, the signed POD PDF is generated and the scanned POD is not attached. Orders with neither get no POD attachment (this is what the yellow warning counts).

For how PODs and documents get onto an order, see Order Documents & POD.

One failed attachment fails the whole email

The PODs and documents are downloaded from file storage while the email is built. If the download of any of them fails with an error, nothing is sent and the row shows Failed!. Hover over the label to read the error.

docs.title: On success
docs.text:
• Sent date is set to today. The row shows sent date under the status.
  • The delivery label shows a green OK. Hovering over it shows Email Delivered.
  • Status changes to Invoiced, but only if it was new. An invoice that is already Invoiced, Partially Paid or Paid keeps its status.
  • The envelope turns grey (Resend Invoice).

docs.title: On failure
docs.text:
• The delivery label shows a red Failed!. Hover over it to see the error message.
  • Status is not changed.
  • Sent date is not changed: the row keeps showing the date of the last successful send, or not sent.

If the invoice was rejected because an address was invalid, the invoice is not touched at all: the label and status stay as they were.

docs.title: The REVISED rule
docs.text:
REVISED is added to the subject and to the invoice PDF file name once the invoice has been sent successfully, meaning the row shows the green OK label.

  • First send of an invoice: no REVISED.
  • Any send after a successful one: REVISED.

Resending after a correction

After you change an invoice that was already sent (orders, charges, terms), resend it from the envelope button. The REVISED marking tells the customer this copy replaces the previous one.

docs.title: Opening the payment window
docs.text:
On the invoice row, open the cog menu and click Record a payment. A pop-up titled Edit Invoice invoice number - customer name opens.

The top of the window summarizes the invoice (read-only):

Item Shows Invoice Total Total of the orders including taxes Invoice Date Date on the invoice Invoiced Orders Reference numbers of the orders on the invoice Invoice Due Date Due date

Below that:

  • Invoice Status: a drop-down with new, Invoiced, Paid, Partially Paid.
  • Balance Paid In Full: a button, shown only when the status is not Paid.
  • Payment Information: the invoice's payment lines, with (+) Add payment to add another.

docs.title: Balance Paid In Full
docs.text:
Click Balance Paid In Full when the customer has paid everything that is left. It:

  1. Sets Invoice Status to Paid.
  2. Adds a payment line with Paid date set to today and Amount set to the remaining balance.
  3. Hides itself.

Fill in the Check number if you have one, then click Update Invoice.

docs.title: Payment lines
docs.text:
Click (+) Add payment to add a line. Each line has:

Field Required Description Paid date No Date of the payment (placeholder Payment date). Pick it from the calendar Check number No Cheque or reference number (placeholder Check Number) Amount Yes Amount received (placeholder Amount). The window will not save while a line has no amount Action — (-) Remove payment deletes the line when you click Update Invoice

An invoice can have as many payment lines as you need. On the list, the number of lines shows as N checks under Last payment, and their sum shows as paid $ … under Balance.

docs.title: Saving
docs.text:
Click Update Invoice. The window closes and the invoice row refreshes with the new balance, payments and status. Click Close to leave without saving.

Partial payments do not change the status

Adding payment lines never changes Invoice Status on its own. A part payment leaves the invoice as new or Invoiced until you pick Partially Paid. A payment that covers the whole total leaves it unpaid until you pick Paid. Set the status in the same window before clicking Update Invoice.

You can also manage payment lines and status from the full invoice form (cog menu > Edit). The Balance Paid In Full button is only in the Record a payment window. See Creating Invoices.

docs.title: Changing the Status Inline
docs.text:
You can change an invoice's status straight from the list without opening anything:

  1. Click the status text on the row (for example Invoiced).
