  2. A small editor titled Enter new invoice status opens.
  3. Pick new, Invoiced, Paid or Partially Paid and confirm.

The change is saved immediately. This does not add or remove payment lines.

docs.title: Statuses
docs.text: Status Meaning Set by new Created, not sent yet Automatically when the invoice is created Invoiced Sent to the customer, waiting for payment Automatically on the first successful send of a new invoice, or by you Partially Paid Some money received You only Paid Fully settled You only (directly, or with Balance Paid In Full)

docs.title: How Paid Affects Balances
docs.text:
Paid is the status that settles an invoice. Whatever the payment lines say, an invoice with status Paid:

  • Shows a Balance of $ 0.00, and paid $ … equal to the full invoice total.
  • Has no aging badge and is left out of every AR Aging filter and the All Unpaid tab.
  • Gets a paid date of today if it has no payment line with a date and no paid date yet. This date appears under Last payment when there are no payment lines.

Any other status (new, Invoiced, Partially Paid) is treated as unpaid. Its Balance is the invoice total minus the sum of its payment lines, and it stays on All Unpaid and in aging, even when the payments cover the total.

Find mismatches

Because Paid overrides the payment lines, a Paid invoice can have payment lines that don't add up to its total. Audit Payments on the Invoices page lists those. See Invoices.

docs.title: The row shows Failed! after sending
docs.text:
Solution

Hover over Failed! to read the error. Common causes:

  • The email settings for invoices are wrong or the mail server refused the message. An admin can check with Settings > Test Email Configuration: enter an address in the Enter recipient email box and click Send Test. It sends one test email with the Notification settings and one with the Invoice settings. On success it reports Test emails sent successfully to …; otherwise it reports Email test failed. followed by which one failed (for example Invoicing Failed: …).
  • A POD or document could not be fetched. Check the order's documents, then send again.

The status was not changed, so you can simply click the envelope and send again once the cause is fixed.

docs.title: "Please correct the email address and try again"
docs.text:
Solution

One of the addresses in To, Cc or Bcc is not a valid email address. Separate several addresses with commas or semicolons, and check for typos. If the addresses look right, ask an admin to check that the Invoice 'From' Address Override in Settings is either empty or a valid email address. When it is left empty, your account's default sender address is used.

docs.title: The customer didn't get a POD for one of the orders
docs.text:
Solution

That order had no captured signature and no scanned signed POD when you sent. The yellow WARNING in the send window shows how many orders are missing one. Upload the POD to the order (see Order Documents & POD) and resend the invoice.

docs.title: Why does the subject say REVISED?
docs.text:
Solution

The invoice was already sent successfully once, so the new copy is marked as revised. Delete the word from Subject if you don't want it. The invoice PDF's file name will still include REVISED.

docs.title: I recorded the full payment but the invoice is still on All Unpaid
docs.text:
Solution

Payments don't change the status. Set the status to Paid: click the status text on the row, or open Record a payment and change Invoice Status.

docs.title: I sent an invoice and its status didn't change to Invoiced
docs.text:
Solution

The automatic change only happens when the status was new. An invoice already Invoiced, Partially Paid or Paid keeps its status when sent. If the row shows Failed!, the email was not sent.

docs.title: I can't find Balance Paid In Full
docs.text:
Solution

The button is hidden when the invoice is already Paid, and it disappears after you click it once. It is only in the Record a payment window, not on the full Edit page.

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
Tips

  • Keep every customer's Accountant Email and Accountant Email (CC) up to date so the send window fills itself correctly.
  • Look at the yellow POD warning before sending. Upload missing PODs first so the customer gets everything in one email.
  • Untick Include documents when the orders carry large or internal files the customer doesn't need.
  • Record every payment as its own line with the check number. It keeps Audit Payments and your reconciliation clean.
  • Set the status as you record money: Partially Paid for part payments, Paid once settled.

docs.title: Invoices
docs.text: Find, filter, follow up on and export your freight invoices from one list.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The Invoices page (subtitle Management of Invoices) is the working list for accounts receivable. From here you can see what each customer owes and how late it is, open the tools for emailing and payments, and export what you filtered for your accounting system.

  • Status tabs: All, All Unpaid (the default), New, Invoiced, Paid, Partially Paid
  • Search by invoice ID, container number or company name
  • Invoice Date range with quick presets
  • AR Aging (Days Past Due) rollups and exact bands, plus an aging badge on every unpaid row
  • Export the invoices currently listed as QuickBooks columns or AR aging detail, in Excel or CSV
  • Audit Payments lists Paid invoices whose payment lines do not add up to the invoice total

This page covers the list. These topics have their own pages:

  • Creating and editing an invoice: Creating Invoices
  • Emailing an invoice and recording payments: Invoice Email & Payments
  • Customer statements: Customer Statements and Automatic Statements
  • Totals per customer by age: Aged Receivables

Garage invoices are separate

If you use the Garage add-on, garage invoices are kept apart from freight invoices and never appear on this page. See Garage Invoices.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
1. Click Invoices in the left menu. The list opens on All Unpaid, newest invoices first.
  2. Narrow it with a status tab, the search box, an Invoice Date range or an AR Aging option.
  3. Click the envelope on a row to email that invoice, or open the cog menu to Print, Record a payment, Edit or Delete.
  4. To get the list into a file, pick a layout and a format in the Export panel and click Export.

To create an invoice, click Add a new Invoice at the top right. See Creating Invoices.

docs.title: Access & Permissions
docs.text:
Role Access Admin Full access: view, create, edit, email, record payments, delete, export, Audit Payments Manager Full access to invoices of the offices they belong to Accountant Full access to invoices of the offices they belong to Dispatch No access. The Invoices menu item is not shown Customer, Warehouse, Garage, drivers No access

How to get there:

  • From the left menu, click Invoices

One office at a time

The list, the totals, the search and the export only cover the office you are currently working in. If your company runs several offices, switch office to see that office's invoices. See Multi-Office. (Audit Payments is the exception. See Audit Payments below.)

docs.title: Adding an Invoice
docs.text:
Click Add a new Invoice at the top right of the page. This opens the invoice form, where you pick the customer, terms, tax and the orders to bill.

Invoices are created from this form only

There is no "create invoice" action on an order. To bill orders, start from Invoices > Add a new Invoice. The full walkthrough is in Creating Invoices.

docs.title: Invoice Filters
docs.text:
The filter bar sits at the top of the Invoices page. Every control narrows the same list, and they combine. Pick a status, add a date range, add an aging option, and you get the invoices matching all three.

Your filters follow you into the export

The Export panel tells you exactly what you are about to download, for example "Exports the 1,250 invoices currently listed (All unpaid) — not the whole database." The file always matches the list on screen.

docs.title: Search
docs.text:
The search box (placeholder Invoice #, Container # or company name) matches any of these:

You type Matches Digits only, e.g. 1234 The invoice whose ID is that number. Leading zeros don't matter, so 01234 works too The start of a container number, e.g. MSCU12 Invoices with an order whose container number starts with that text Part of a company name, e.g. logist Invoices for any customer whose name contains that text

The three checks run together, so a digits-only search also returns invoices whose container number starts with those digits or whose company name contains them. Search is not case-sensitive. Type your text and click Search (or press Enter).

Search by the invoice digits

Invoice search matches the invoice's number. If your invoice numbers are shown with a prefix (for example A26 - 01234), type only the digits: 1234.

Searching narrows what you are already looking at. It keeps your status tab, date range and aging option. On the default All Unpaid tab, a search will not find a paid invoice. Click All first if you are looking for an invoice that may be paid.

docs.title: Filter chips and Clear All
docs.text:
Active filters show as small chips inside the search box. Click a chip (it ends in ✕) to drop that one filter and keep the rest.

Chip Appears when Removing it Status tab name, e.g. Paid ✕ Any tab other than the default All Unpaid is selected Goes back to All Unpaid Date range, e.g. Jan 1, 2026 – Mar 31, 2026 ✕, From Jan 1, 2026 ✕, Up to Mar 31, 2026 ✕ An invoice date range is set Clears both dates Aging, e.g. Past due ✕, 30+ days ✕, Aged 31-60 ✕ An AR aging option is selected Clears the aging option

The search text itself is not a chip. It stays in the box. Clear All (to the right of Search) resets the page to its default view: All Unpaid, no search, no dates, no aging.

docs.title: Status tabs
docs.text:
The status tabs filter on the invoice's Status value. The selected tab is highlighted in green.

Tab Shows All Every invoice, whatever its status All Unpaid Invoices with status new, Invoiced or Partially Paid. This is the default tab New Status new. A new invoice starts here and normally stays here until it is emailed Invoiced Status Invoiced. A successful email moves a new invoice here Paid Status Paid Partially Paid Status Partially Paid

Tabs follow the Status value, not the balance

A tab picks invoices by what is in the Status column. An invoice whose payments cover the total stays on All Unpaid until its status is changed to Paid.

docs.title: Invoice Date
docs.text:
Filter by the date on the invoice (both ends included). Pick a from and/or to date and click Apply, or click a preset:

This Month · Last Month · This Year · last year (shown as the year itself, e.g. 2025) · Last 12 Months

You can set only one end: a from date alone shows everything from that day on, and a to date alone shows everything up to that day. The active preset is highlighted in green. Click Clear dates to drop the range and keep your other filters.

docs.title: AR Aging (Days Past Due)
docs.text:
Aging answers "how late is this?" It is measured in days past the invoice's due date, as of today.

There are two ways to ask, side by side:

Type Options Meaning Rollups (open-ended) Past due · 30+ days · 60+ days "This old and worse." 30+ days covers 31-60, 61-90 and 91+ together Bands (exact) Not Due · 0-30 · 31-60 · 61-90 · 91+ Splits the unpaid ledger into exact buckets, the same way the Aged Receivables report does

Only one aging option can be active at a time. Click the active option again to turn it off.

Details worth knowing

  • Past due means at least one day late. An invoice falling due today sits in the 0-30 band without being past due.
  • Invoices with status Paid carry no aging, so no aging option returns them. Picking an aging option while on the Paid tab switches you to All Unpaid. Clicking Paid clears the aging option.
  • New, Invoiced and Partially Paid combine with aging. For example, Invoiced + 60+ days lists invoices sent and more than 60 days late.
  • An old invoice with no due date on record is aged from its invoice date.

docs.title: Invoice List Columns
docs.text:
The list shows eight columns. Most pair a main value with a smaller related value underneath. Invoices are sorted newest first (by invoice ID) on every tab, 50 per page.

Column Main value Underneath Invoice Invoice number Invoice date Company Customer name (a link, see below), or Unknown if none Number of orders: 1 order, N orders, or — Due date Due date, with the aging badge beside it — Total Invoice total including taxes — Balance Amount still owed. Shown in bold red when above zero, $ 0.00 otherwise paid $ …: total paid so far Last payment Date of a payment line (see below), or — Number of payment lines, e.g. 2 checks Status Status value, with a delivery label sent date or not sent Actions Envelope button and cog menu —

docs.title: Company link
docs.text:
Click a company name to see all unpaid invoices for that company. The list switches to All Unpaid with the company name in the search box. Your date range and aging option are dropped. Add them back from the filter bar if you need them.

This is an ordinary search, so it also lists invoices of any other customer whose name contains the same text (for example, clicking ABC Logistics also shows ABC Logistics East).

docs.title: Aging badge
docs.text:
Each unpaid invoice shows a small coloured badge next to its due date, naming its aging bucket:

Badge Colour Meaning Not Due Grey Due date is still ahead 0-30 Blue 0 to 30 days past due 31-60 Orange 31 to 60 days past due 61-90 Red 61 to 90 days past due 91+ Darker red More than 90 days past due — Muted The invoice is Paid and has no aging

Hover over a badge to see the exact count, for example "12 days past due" or "Due in 5 days".

docs.title: Last payment
docs.text:
Last payment shows a payment date from the invoice's payment lines. If the invoice has no payment lines, the invoice's own paid date is shown, or —. The count underneath (1 check, 3 checks, 0 checks) is the number of payment lines.

For a Paid invoice, paid $ … under the Balance shows the full invoice total.

docs.title: Status
docs.text:
The Status column shows the value stored on the invoice, exactly as saved. A brand-new invoice reads new in lowercase. The others read Invoiced, Paid and Partially Paid.

Changing the status inline: click the status text to open a small editor titled Enter new invoice status. Pick new, Invoiced, Paid or Partially Paid and confirm. The change saves immediately.

Changing the status here does not add or remove payment lines. If you set an invoice to Paid and it has no payment lines and no paid date yet, today's date is recorded as its paid date.

Next to the status, a small label shows how the last email went:

Label Meaning OK (green) The last invoice email was handed off successfully Failed! (red) The last attempt failed. Hover over the label to see the error message (none) The invoice has never been emailed

Underneath, sent date shows the date of the last successful email, or not sent.

docs.title: Totals footer
docs.text:
The Total of invoices row at the bottom adds up the Total and Balance columns for the current page only (up to 50 invoices), not for everything matching your filters. The line under the table says so, for example:

"Totals above cover the 50 invoices on this page of 1,250 matching the current filters."

For a total across all matching invoices, use the Export (the AR aging detail layout ends with a TOTALS row) or the Aged Receivables report.

docs.title: Row Actions
docs.text: Each row has two controls in the Actions column.

docs.title: Envelope button: Email Invoice / Resend Invoice
docs.text:
There is no separate Send button. Click the envelope to open the email window for that invoice:

  • Blue envelope (tooltip Email Invoice): the invoice has not been sent yet.
  • Grey envelope (tooltip Resend Invoice): it was sent before.

A successful email of a new invoice changes its status to Invoiced. For recipients, attachments and the REVISED marking, see Invoice Email & Payments.

docs.title: Cog menu
docs.text:
Item What it does Print Opens the printable invoice in a new browser tab EDI 210 Downloads the invoice as an EDI 210 file named EDI210_<invoice number>_<YYYYMMDD>.csv. Only shown if your account has EDI invoicing turned on (ask UTX support) Record a payment Opens the invoice in a pop-up window so you can add payment lines. See Invoice Email & Payments Edit Opens the full invoice form. See Creating Invoices Delete Deletes the invoice after an Are you sure? confirmation

Deleting an invoice

Delete removes the invoice itself and cannot be undone from this page. Its orders are not deleted: they are only detached from the invoice.

docs.title: Exporting Invoices
docs.text:
The Export panel is part of the filter bar. It exports the invoices currently listed, across all pages: whatever your status tab, search, invoice date range and aging option have narrowed the list to.

The line under the button always states what you are about to get, for example "Exports the 1,250 invoices currently listed (All unpaid, past due) — not the whole database."

To export:

  1. Filter the list until it shows what you want.
  2. In Export, pick a layout (QuickBooks columns or AR aging detail) and a format (Excel or CSV).
  3. Click Export. The file downloads.
Setting Options Description Layout QuickBooks columns One row per invoice with amounts before and after tax, for importing into QuickBooks AR aging detail One row per invoice with balance and aging detail, for collections and month-end Format Excel (.xlsx) Default CSV (.csv) Comma-separated values

docs.title: QuickBooks columns layout
docs.text:
Rows are sorted by invoice date (oldest first), then invoice ID.

Column Contents Invoice Invoice number Invoice Date YYYY-MM-DD Customer Company name, or Unknown Details One entry per order, <type> - <container>, separated by commas. Types: CI import, EX export, DV dry van, TF transfer, IX international export Amount before sales taxes Subtotal of the orders GST Charged GST (0.00 if the invoice has no tax) QST Charged QST (0.00 if the invoice has no tax) Amount after sales taxes Invoice total

docs.title: AR aging detail layout
docs.text:
Rows are sorted by due date (oldest first), then invoice ID. The last row is a TOTALS row adding up every money column.

Column Contents Invoice Invoice number Invoice Date YYYY-MM-DD Customer Company name Status Status value, as stored Terms Invoice terms Due Date YYYY-MM-DD Days Overdue Days past due as of today (negative = not due yet). Blank for Paid invoices Aging Bucket Not Due, 0-30, 31-60, 61-90, 91+, or Settled for Paid invoices Invoice Total Total including taxes Amount Paid Total minus balance Balance Amount still owed (0 for Paid invoices) Last Payment Same date as the Last payment column on screen Not Due · 0-30 · 31-60 · 61-90 · 91+ The balance, placed in the one column matching the invoice's bucket. The others show 0

Pivot-ready

Because each balance lands in exactly one bucket column, you can sum the bucket columns per customer to rebuild an aged receivables summary for exactly the invoices you filtered.

docs.title: File name
docs.text:
Files are named after your company, the layout, the status tab, the date range (when both dates are set) and today's date:

  • QuickBooks columns, no date range: <company>-invoices-<status>-on-DDMMYY.xlsx
  • AR aging detail, with a date range: <company>-invoice-aging-<status>-<YYYYMMDD>-to-<YYYYMMDD>-on-DDMMYY.csv

The status part is one of all-invoices, all-unpaid, new, invoiced, paid, partially-paid. The Excel worksheet is named after the status tab too (for example All unpaid).

Very large exports

An export builds the whole file at once, so it is capped at 20,000 invoices. If your filters match more than that, you go back to the list with the message "That export covers N invoices, which is more than the 20,000 this can build at once. Narrow it with the invoice date range, then export again." Pick a range such as This Year or Last 12 Months and export in batches.

docs.title: Audit Payments
docs.text:
Audit Payments (in the Tools panel, to the right of Export) is a read-only report. It opens a pop-up listing invoices that are marked Paid but whose payment lines do not add up to the invoice total.

What it checks:

  • Invoices with status Paid, invoice date January 1, 2024 or later, that have at least one payment line
  • The invoice total (orders + tax) is compared with the sum of its payment lines
  • Any difference greater than $0.02 is listed
  • It looks at all offices, not just the one you are working in
Column Shows Invoice # Invoice number. Click it to open a search for that invoice in a new tab Date Invoice date Status Status (always Paid) Invoice Total What the invoice should total Total Paid Sum of its payment lines Difference Invoice Total minus Total Paid. Positive = under-paid, negative = over-paid

If nothing is found, it reads "No discrepancies found. All paid invoices match their payment lines."

Nothing is changed for you

Audit Payments does not fix anything and has no bulk update. To correct an invoice, open it (cog menu > Record a payment or Edit) and adjust its payment lines. See Invoice Email & Payments.

docs.title: I searched for an invoice number and got nothing
docs.text:
Solution

Check two things:

  1. Search by the digits. If your invoice numbers have a prefix like A26 - 01234, search for 1234.
  2. Check the status tab. Search keeps the current tab, and the default is All Unpaid. Paid invoices only show on All or Paid.

Also make sure you are in the right office: the list only shows the current office's invoices.

docs.title: The footer total doesn't match my aged receivables
docs.text:
Solution

The footer only adds up the current page (50 invoices). For a full total, export with the AR aging detail layout (it ends with a TOTALS row) or use the Aged Receivables report. The report and this list are not expected to match exactly: the report starts from your invoicing start date and counts payments as of its date, while the list includes every invoice and treats status Paid as settled.

docs.title: A paid-up invoice still shows an aging badge
docs.text:
Solution

Aging is based on Status, not on the balance. An invoice stays aged until its status is Paid. Click the status text and change it to Paid.

docs.title: The status shows Failed!
docs.text:
Solution

The last email attempt failed. Hover over Failed! to read the error, fix the cause (for example a wrong recipient address: the To field is pre-filled from the customer's accountant email), and click the envelope to send again. See Invoice Email & Payments.

docs.title: My export has more (or fewer) rows than I expected
docs.text:
Solution

The export uses every active filter: status tab, search text, invoice date range and aging option. Read the caption under Export. It lists the count and filters before you click. Note that the export covers all pages, while the screen shows 50 at a time.

docs.title: An invoice from Audit Payments doesn't show when I click it
docs.text:
Solution

Audit Payments covers all offices, but the list only shows your current office. Switch to the invoice's office and click the link again. See Multi-Office.

docs.title: A dispatcher can't see the Invoices menu
docs.text:
Solution

This is expected. Dispatch users have no access to invoices. Give the person the Accountant or Manager role if they need it. See User Roles.

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
Tips

  • Start collections from AR Aging > 60+ days, then click a company name to see everything that customer owes.
  • Set a date range before exporting large histories. It keeps you under the 20,000-invoice cap and gives each file a clear period in its name.
  • Run Audit Payments before month-end close to catch Paid invoices with missing or mistyped payment lines.
  • Mark invoices Paid once fully paid so they leave All Unpaid and the aging filters.

docs.title: Brokers, Steamship Lines & Container Sizes
docs.text: Maintain the three small reference lists that feed dropdowns on your orders: Brokers, Steamship Lines and Container Sizes.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
These lists are simple: each entry has a name, an office and, for steamship lines and container sizes, a description and an Active checkbox.

  • Brokers (Manage Brokers): a list of broker names that you can pick as the Broker on a Dry Van order and as a payee in Order Expenses. Available to Admins and Managers.
  • Steamship Lines (Manage Steamship Lines): the shipping lines offered in the Steamship line field of container orders. Admins only, intermodal accounts only.
  • Container Sizes (Manage Container Sizes): the sizes offered in the Container size field of container orders. Admins only, intermodal accounts only.
  • Every entry belongs to an office. Each list shows the entries of the office you are currently working in.
  • Changes are recorded (when change history is turned on for your account; ask UTX support) and can be viewed with Actions → View History.
  • A broker can be deleted only while no order and no expense uses it. Steamship lines and container sizes are retired by unchecking Active.

Three different things are called \"broker\"

UTX Freight uses the word broker in three unrelated places. They are separate records and are not linked to each other:

What Where you manage it What it is used for Broker records (this page) User menu → Manage Brokers The Broker field on Dry Van orders, and the Broker group of payees in Order Expenses Customer companies flagged Broker Customers → edit a customer → Broker checkbox. See Managing Customers The Transport Company / Broker field on Dry Van orders, the blue Broker label and the Brokers filter on the Customers list Mobile users with the Broker role Mobile Users → Drivers, Brokers & Yard. See Mobile Users People who sign in from a phone. They have exactly the same rights as a Driver and appear in the driver lists

Adding a name on Manage Brokers does not create a customer or a mobile user, and checking Broker on a customer does not add it to Manage Brokers.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
1. Click your name at the top of the screen to open the user menu.
  2. Click Manage Brokers, Manage Steamship Lines or Manage Container Sizes.
  3. Click Add a new Broker (or Add a new Steamship Line, Add a new Container Size) at the top right.
  4. Enter the Name, check the Office, and click Save Changes.

The new entry is now available in the matching dropdown on your orders.

docs.title: Access & Permissions
docs.text:
Role Manage Brokers Manage Steamship Lines Manage Container Sizes Admin Full access Full access Full access Manager Full access No access No access Dispatch No access No access No access Accountant No access No access No access All other roles (Customer, Customer Service, Warehouse, Garage) and mobile users No access No access No access

How to get there:

  • Click your name at the top of the screen to open the user menu, then click Manage Brokers, Manage Steamship Lines or Manage Container Sizes.

These items sit in the user menu with the other Manage … items (Manage Cities, Manage Zones and so on). They are not inside the Settings page. A menu item only appears for users who have access to it.

Intermodal only

Manage Steamship Lines and Manage Container Sizes only appear when your account is set up for intermodal (container) work. This is switched on by UTX; ask UTX support if you need it. Manage Brokers appears for every account.

Multi-office

Each Manage … page shows the entries of the office you are currently working in. When you create or edit an entry, the Office dropdown lists the offices you belong to. See Multi-Office.

The dropdowns on the order itself are not limited the same way: the Steamship line and Container size fields of the order form, the Broker field of the dispatch form and the Broker group of Order Expenses list the entries of every office. Only the quick pickers on the Orders and Dispatch lists are limited to your current office. Giving entries distinct names per office avoids confusion.

docs.title: Manage Brokers
docs.text: The Brokers page (subtitle Management of Brokers) lists every broker of your current office, sorted by name, on a single page.

docs.title: Columns
docs.text: Column Description Name The broker name Orders The number of orders that have this broker in their Broker field Charges The number of expense lines (in Order Expenses) that have this broker as the payee (Expense report) The  Expense report button. See Expense report (Actions) The Actions menu: Edit, View History, Delete

docs.title: Creating a Broker
docs.text:
1. Open the user menu → Manage Brokers.
  2. Click Add a new Broker.
  3. Fill in the Broker Information form (see the table below).
  4. Click Save Changes. You return to the Brokers list.

Click Cancel to go back to the list without saving.

Field Required Description Name Yes The broker name (placeholder broker name) Office Yes The office the broker belongs to. Lists the offices you belong to; no blank option

Brokers have no Active checkbox and cannot be disabled.

docs.title: Editing a Broker
docs.text:
Actions → Edit opens the same form, titled Edit Broker. Change the Name or Office and click Save Changes.

Renaming a broker changes the name everywhere it is shown, including on existing orders and expenses, because they point to the broker record rather than storing a copy of the name.

docs.title: Expense report
docs.text:
The Expense report button opens the Expenses page (subtitle Tracking of expenses for brokers) with Expense payment status set to Unpaid Only. Choose the broker in Select a filter and click Search to review what you still owe that broker.

On the Expenses page you can refine the list with:

Filter Options Select a filter No Filter, or one payee. Payees are grouped by type: brokers (group Broker), mobile users and expense types Order status All statuses, or one order status Expense payment status Paid and Unpaid, Paid Only, Unpaid Only

Click Search to apply the filters. An expense counts as paid once it is attached to a check. See Order Charges & Expenses.

The Expenses page and its Select a filter list are not limited to your current office.

docs.title: Deleting a Broker
docs.text:
Actions → Delete asks Are you sure? and then removes the broker permanently.

The Delete item only appears when both the Orders and Charges columns are 0. A broker used on any order or any expense line cannot be deleted. There is no way to hide such a broker; rename it if you need to (for example, add (old) to the name).

Deleting cannot be undone

A deleted broker is gone from the list and from every dropdown. Only delete brokers that were created by mistake.

docs.title: Where Broker records are used
docs.text:
• Broker field on Dry Van orders: on the dispatch form, in the Delivery Information panel, next to Special Note. It is only shown for Dry Van orders. See Dispatch.
  • Order Expenses: the payee dropdown (the first field of each expense line) has a Broker group listing your brokers. Order Expenses is shown to users who can manage rates. See Order Charges & Expenses.
  • Expenses page: the Select a filter dropdown has a Broker group.

docs.title: Manage Steamship Lines
docs.text: The Steamship Lines page (subtitle Management of Steamship Lines) lists the steamship lines of your current office.

docs.title: Columns
docs.text: Column Description Name The steamship line name Description The optional description Orders Shows - on this page Active A green  when active, a red  when inactive (Actions) The Actions menu: Edit, View History

docs.title: Creating or Editing a Steamship Line
docs.text:
1. Open the user menu → Manage Steamship Lines.
  2. Click Add a new Steamship Line, or Actions → Edit on an existing line.
  3. Fill in the Steamship Line Information form.
  4. Click Save Changes (or Cancel to go back without saving).
Field Required Description Name Yes The name shown in the Steamship line dropdown on orders (placeholder Shipping Line) Office Yes The office the line belongs to. Lists the offices you belong to Description No Free text (placeholder Steamship Line description) Active No Checked by default. Hint: Only active shipping lines will be visible for new orders

docs.title: Where Steamship Lines are used
docs.text:
• The Steamship line field on Container Import, Container Export, Container Transfer and International Export orders. See Order Form.
  • On the Orders and Dispatch lists, users who can change the container status can click an order's steamship line to pick another one (window Select Steamship Line).

docs.title: Manage Container Sizes
docs.text: The Container Sizes page (subtitle Management of Container Sizes) lists the container sizes of your current office.

docs.title: Columns
docs.text: Column Description Name The container size name, as shown on orders (for example 40HC) Description The optional description Orders Shows - on this page Active A green when active, a red when inactive (Actions) The Actions menu: Edit, View History

docs.title: Creating or Editing a Container Size
docs.text:
1. Open the user menu → Manage Container Sizes.
  2. Click Add a new Container Size, or Actions → Edit on an existing size.
  3. Fill in the Container Size Information form.
  4. Click Save Changes (or Cancel to go back without saving).
Field Required Description Name Yes The name shown in the Container size dropdown and on the order lists (placeholder Container size) Office Yes The office the size belongs to. Lists the offices you belong to Description No Free text (placeholder Container size description) Active No Checked by default. Hint: Only active container sizes will be visible for new orders

docs.title: Where Container Sizes are used
docs.text:
• The Container size field on Container Import, Container Export, Container Transfer and International Export orders. See Order Form.
  • On the Orders and Dispatch lists, users who can change the container status can click an order's container size to pick another one (window Select Size).

Keep names consistent

Some automatic features fill these fields by matching the Name: orders created from scanned documents look up the container size by a standard size code (such as 20, 40DV, 40HC, 45HC), and container tracking fills an empty steamship line or container size by matching the carrier name or size reported for the container. When no entry matches, the field is left blank. Use standard names and avoid near-duplicates.

docs.title: Active vs. Delete (Steamship Lines & Container Sizes)
docs.text:
• Delete is not offered for steamship lines or container sizes.
  • To retire an entry, Edit it and uncheck Active.

Existing orders are not affected

Existing orders keep their steamship line or container size when you uncheck Active.

docs.title: View History
docs.text:
Every list on this page has Actions → View History. It opens a History window without leaving the page.

History is only recorded while change history is turned on for your account (ask UTX support). Changes made while it was off do not appear, and an entry with no recorded changes shows an empty table.

Column Description User The name of the person who made the change. Changes with no recorded user show System Changes One line per field that changed, with the field name (for example Name, Description, Active, Office) and its value When The date (for example Oct 10, 2026) with the time underneath (for example 2:15 pm)

How to read the Changes column:

  • The most recent change is at the top.
  • An edited value shows the old value in red, an arrow (->), and the new value in green.
  • When the entry was created, its values are shown in green only.
  • The Office is shown by office name. Active is shown as true or false.
  • Fields that were empty (or unchecked) both before and after are not shown.
  • Edits that changed nothing are not listed.

Click Close (or the ×) to close the window.

Same window everywhere

The same History window is used on other lists, such as zones, cities, terminals, charge types, expense types, taxes, equipment and document types.

docs.title: I can't see Manage Steamship Lines or Manage Container Sizes
docs.text:
Solution

Both are available to Admins only, and only when your account is set up for intermodal work (ask UTX support). Managers can open Manage Brokers but not these two lists. Ask an Admin. Also make sure you are looking in the user menu under your name, not on the Settings page.

docs.title: There is no Delete option for a broker
docs.text:
Solution

Delete only appears when the broker's Orders and Charges columns are both 0. Remove the broker from those orders and expense lines first, or keep the broker and rename it.

docs.title: How do I delete a steamship line or a container size?
docs.text:
Solution

Steamship lines and container sizes are not deleted. Edit the entry and uncheck Active. Past orders keep their value.

docs.title: I added a broker but I can't find it in the Transport Company / Broker field
docs.text:
Solution

The Transport Company / Broker field lists customer companies with the Broker checkbox checked, not the entries of Manage Brokers. Edit the customer and check Broker (see Managing Customers). The entries of Manage Brokers appear in the Broker field of the Dry Van dispatch form and in the Broker group of Order Expenses.

docs.title: I added a broker but they can't sign in on their phone
docs.text:
Solution

A broker record is just a name in a list; it has no login. To let a broker use the mobile app, create a mobile user with the Broker role under Mobile Users → Drivers, Brokers & Yard. See Mobile Users.

docs.title: The Expense report doesn't show paid expenses
docs.text:
Solution

The Expense report starts on Unpaid Only. To include expenses that have already been paid by check, choose the broker in Select a filter, set Expense payment status to Paid and Unpaid and click Search.

Best Practices

  • Set up steamship lines and container sizes once, when your account is configured, using the names your customers and terminals use.
  • Retire old entries by unchecking Active rather than renaming them to something else, so past orders keep the right value.
  • Use Manage Brokers for the third parties you pay on Dry Van moves, and the customer Broker checkbox for transport companies that carry the freight. Do not mix them up.
  • Before deleting a broker, check View History to confirm it really was created by mistake.

docs.title: Customers
docs.text: Create and manage the customer companies (and their contact people) that you place orders, invoices and statements for in UTX Freight.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Every order in UTX Freight is placed on behalf of a person who belongs to a customer company. Before you can create orders, you need at least one customer with one person.

  • Customers (companies) are the billing entities. Each one has an address, accountant emails for invoices and statements, a service type, a currency and statement format, and optional custom rates.
  • People belong to a customer. They are the contacts orders are placed for, they receive notifications, and they can log in. Each customer box on the list shows its people in a table. See People & Invitations for the details.
  • Your own company is listed too, as Your Company: . Your staff (admins, managers, dispatchers, accountants, drivers) are the people under it.
  • Custom rates override zone rates, terminal fees and warehouse charge prices for one customer.
  • Default tag pre-selects a tag on new orders for the customer.
  • Fuel surcharge exemption turns off fuel surcharges for the customer (Fuel Surcharge add-on).
  • Automatic statements can be scheduled per customer (when automatic statements are enabled on your account).

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
1. Go to Customers from the left menu.
  2. Click Add a new Customer (top right).
  3. Enter the Name (the only required field).
  4. Click Save Changes. You return to the Customers list, filtered to the new company.
  5. In the new company's box, click Add Person, fill in the person's details, and click Add this person.

The invitation is sent right away

When you click Add this person, UTX Freight immediately emails an invitation to the address you entered. Make sure the email address is correct before you save.

docs.title: Access & Permissions
docs.text:
Role Access Level Admin Full access: create, edit, delete, add and edit people, and Export Manager Full access: create, edit, delete, add and edit people. No Export button. In single-office accounts, a Manager can't edit your own company or its staff (see Editing your own company) Dispatch Full access (create, edit, add and edit people) only when your account has Dispatch customer management turned on (ask UTX support). Dispatch cannot delete customers or people, and has no Export. Otherwise, Dispatch has no access and the Customers menu is hidden Accountant No access. The Customers menu is not shown Customer, Driver, Warehouse, Garage No access
  • Only Admin and Manager can delete a customer or a person.
  • The Export button is shown to Admin users only.
  • Garage users manage their own customer list in the Garage module. See Garage Customers & Equipment.

How to get there:

  • From the left menu, click Customers

Multi-office accounts

In single-office accounts, users manage the customers of the offices they belong to. With Multi-Office, customers are shared: users can manage customers from any office, and the people of every office's customers appear in the order form. The Customers list itself shows the customers that belong to the office you are currently working in, and a new customer is created in your current office. The Offices column in the people table shows how many offices each person is assigned to.

docs.title: Filters
docs.text:
The filters sit in the box at the top left of the page:

Filter What It Shows (default) Your own company only. This is the filter selected each time you open Customers All Active Customers that are active (not disabled) Disabled Customers whose Active box is unchecked Brokers Customers with the Broker box checked Warehouse Customers whose Service includes Warehouse (Warehouse add-on only) Intermodal Customers whose Service includes Intermodal (shown with the Warehouse add-on)

After you create a customer, the list opens filtered to that company and its name appears as an extra filter link at the start of the box.

Deleted customers never appear under any filter.

docs.title: Search
docs.text:
Type in the Filter companies and users box to search. The search:

  • starts once you have typed 2 or more characters (clearing the box shows the full list again),
  • matches, case-insensitive and on partial text, the company name and the first name, last name and email of the company's people,
  • searches within the selected filter. With your own company selected (the default), the search covers all customers of the office you're working in that aren't deleted, both active and disabled. Your own company itself is not part of these search results.

The search does not match the Reference ID, address or phone numbers.

docs.title: What each customer box shows
docs.text:
The list shows 30 customers per page, active customers first, then sorted alphabetically by name. Each customer has its own box:

  • Header: your own company shows as Your Company: ; other customers show as - . A disabled customer's name is shown in red. Brokers have a blue Broker label.
  • Click the company name to open an info window with the customer's Address (Address 1, then city, state and postal code), Phone Number and Fax Number (each only when filled in) and Comments. Click Close to dismiss it. The hint under the search box says Click on the company name to view the company address and info.
  • Buttons (for users who can manage the customer): Edit Customer (always visible), Add Person, and Delete (only when deletion is allowed, see Deleting a Customer).
  • People table with the columns Name, Title, Email, Phone, Notifs, Alerts (only with a container tracking add-on), Active, Offices, and the Edit Person and Delete buttons. The first column shows a badge for staff (Owner, or the role name such as Admin, Manager or Dispatch) and an Invited badge for people who haven't accepted their invitation yet.

docs.title: Reference ID
docs.text: The Reference ID is built automatically from the first three letters of the company name (spaces and hyphens removed, in capitals) followed by the company's internal number, padded to at least three digits. For example, a company named "Acme Logistics" with number 7 shows as ACM007. Because it comes from the name, the Reference ID changes if you rename the company. You can't edit it directly.

docs.title: Creating a Customer
docs.text:
1. Navigate to Customers.
  2. Click Add a new Customer (top right).
  3. Fill in the Customer Information form. Only Name is required.
  4. Click Save Changes (or Cancel to go back to the list).

On success you see Customer was successfully created. If Name is empty, the form reloads and shows can't be blank under the field.

The form is a single page with these sections, from top to bottom: Customer Information, Rate to apply for new orders, Automatic Statement schedule for this customer (only when enabled), Custom rates for this customer, Fuel Surcharge (Fuel Surcharge add-on only), Broker / Transport Company, Additional comments and Customer visibility. The tables below follow that order.

docs.title: Customer Information: address and phone
docs.text: Field Description Name Company name (required). Leading and trailing spaces are removed when you save Web address Company website Address 1 / Address 2 Street address City City name State Province or state, picked from the dropdown ZIP/Postal Code Postal or ZIP code Country Canada (CA) or United States (US) Office # Office phone number Fax # Fax number

docs.title: Customer Information: accountant emails
docs.text: Field Description Accountant Email The default email of the customer's accountant, used when emailing invoices. It's also the "To" address for statements Accountant Email (CC) A CC address used when emailing invoices. Separate several addresses with commas

docs.title: Customer Information: service, tag and default user
docs.text: Field Description Service What this customer uses you for. Options: Intermodal; Warehouse and Intermodal & Warehouse (Warehouse add-on); Garage (Garage add-on). Only people of customers whose service includes Intermodal appear in the order form's Place the order on behalf of list. Customers with Warehouse are the ones available for warehouse orders Default tag Shown only when your account has order tags configured. See Default Tag Default user Shown only when editing an existing customer whose Service is exactly Intermodal (not Intermodal & Warehouse). Pick one of the customer's people who is active for orders. Used by automated document-to-order imports to decide which person the imported order is placed for

docs.title: Rate to apply for new orders
docs.text: Field Description Default Order Rate Read-only (greyed out). You can't change it on this form. It is copied into a new order's base rate when the order for this customer doesn't already have one Default Currency CAD or USD Default Statement Format PDF Format or Excel (.xlsx). The file format used when a statement is emailed to this customer. See Customer Statements

docs.title: Additional comments and Customer visibility
docs.text: Field Description Comments (section Additional comments) Free-text notes. They appear in the info window when you click the company name on the list Active (section Customer visibility) Hint: Order can only be placed for active customers. Uncheck to disable the customer (see Disabling a Customer)

docs.title: Editing a Customer
docs.text:
1. On the Customers list, find the company (use a filter or search).
  2. Click Edit Customer in the company's box.
  3. Update the fields as needed.
  4. Click Save Changes.

On success you return to the list with Customer was successfully updated.

The sections below are on the same form used for creating a customer.

docs.title: Default Tag
docs.text:
The Default tag field appears when your account has at least one order tag configured (it's not a separate add-on). Pick the tag that should be used for this customer's orders.

When an Admin, Manager or Dispatch user creates a new order and chooses one of this customer's people in Place the order on behalf of, the tag is pre-selected. You can still change it on the order. See Order Tagging.

docs.title: Automatic Statement Schedule
docs.text:
The Automatic Statement schedule for this customer section only appears when automatic statements are turned on for your account (ask UTX support). Choose a value in Send weekly statement on:

Option When the statement is sent Weekly on Sunday … Weekly on Saturday Every week on that day Bi-Weekly on the 2nd and 16th On the 2nd and the 16th of each month Monthly on the 1st On the 1st of each month Monthly on the 15th On the 15th of each month Not Scheduled Never sent automatically

The statement is emailed to the Accountant Email (with the Accountant Email (CC) addresses in CC), in the Default Statement Format, only if the customer is Active and has unpaid invoices. If there's nothing owing, no email goes out. In single-office accounts the delivery is then recorded as Statement Not Sent (0.0$). Without an Accountant Email, no automatic statement can be sent.

Choose a schedule for each new customer

On a new customer, or on any customer that has no schedule yet, Send weekly statement on starts at Weekly on Sunday, the first choice in the list. Choose Not Scheduled if the customer shouldn't receive automatic statements.

You can also change the schedule from the customer statements screen. For full details, see Automatic Statements.

docs.title: Custom Rates
docs.text:
The Custom rates for this customer section lets you set prices that apply only to this customer. Each row has:

  • Charge: a dropdown grouped into Zone, Terminal and Warehouse (warehouse charges). Only active items are listed.
  • Rate: the amount to use for this customer.

Click (+) Add another to add a row and (-) Remove to delete one, then click Save Changes.

Charge group What the custom rate overrides Zone The zone's rate. When an order's location falls in that zone, this customer's rate is suggested instead of the zone's standard rate. See Zones & Cities Terminal The terminal's Default Rate for the automatic Terminal Fee charge (the pickup terminal on imports, the return terminal on exports). The fee is only added while the order is not completed or invoiced, and only when the resulting rate is above zero. See Managing Terminals Warehouse The rate shown next to that warehouse charge in the charge drop-down on this customer's warehouse orders. See Warehouse Orders

docs.title: Fuel Surcharge Exemption
docs.text:
When the Fuel Surcharge add-on is enabled, the form has a Fuel Surcharge section:

  • Check Exempt from Fuel Surcharge. The hint reads: When checked, fuel surcharge will NOT be applied to this customer's orders. Use this for customers who have negotiated no fuel surcharge.

If you turn the exemption on and the customer has uninvoiced orders that are not Completed and already carry a fuel surcharge, a warning appears after saving:

has N open order(s) with fuel surcharges that need recalculation. Visit the Fuel Schedule to recalculate.

Go to Fuel Schedule and click Recalculate on the affected months to remove those charges. For full details, see Fuel Surcharge — Exempting a Customer.

docs.title: Broker / Transport Company
docs.text: Check Broker to flag the company as a broker. Hint: This company can be used as a broker and will show up in the brokers list. Broker companies get a Broker label on the Customers list and appear under the Brokers filter.

docs.title: Editing your own company
docs.text:
Your own company (Your Company: ) uses the same form. It isn't tied to an office and it can never be deleted.

Because it isn't tied to an office, in single-office accounts only Admin users see Edit Customer and Add Person on your own company, and the Edit Person and Delete buttons on your staff. Managers (and Dispatch users with customer access) see the box and its people but no buttons. With Multi-Office, Managers and Dispatch users with customer access can manage it too.

docs.title: Adding People
docs.text:
1. On the Customers list, find the company.
  2. Click Add Person.
  3. Fill in First Name, Last Name, Email and the other contact details.
  4. Click Add this person.

The invitation email goes out immediately. It contains a link where the person picks their own password and finishes setting up their account. You can start using the person on orders before they accept.

To change a person, click Edit Person on their row. If they haven't accepted their invitation yet, the Edit Person page shows when the last invitation was sent, a resend the email button, and the invitation link you can copy and send yourself. There's no resend button on the Customers list.

For roles, notifications, alerts, Active for orders and offices, see People & Invitations.

docs.title: Disabling a Customer
docs.text:
Disabled customers stay in the system with all their orders and invoices, but no new orders can be placed for them. To disable:

  1. Click Edit Customer.
  2. Uncheck Active in the Customer visibility section.
  3. Click Save Changes.

The company name turns red on the list and the customer moves to the Disabled filter. Disabled customers also stop receiving automatic statements. To re-enable, check Active again.

docs.title: Deleting a Customer
docs.text:
The Delete button only appears in a customer's box when all of these are true:

  • it's not your own company,
  • the customer has no invoices,
  • the customer has no people, including people who were deleted earlier.

Click Delete, then confirm Are you sure you want to delete this company? You see Customer was successfully deleted.

Only Admin and Manager can delete. A deleted customer is marked inactive and disappears from every filter and search, but its record is kept (it still appears in the export). There's no way to restore it from the Customers page.

Can't delete? Disable instead

A customer with invoices or people can't be deleted. Uncheck Active to hide it from new orders instead.

docs.title: Exporting Customers
docs.text:
Admin users see a green Export button on the right of the Customers page, next to the search box. It downloads a CSV file named <your company>-companies-<date>.csv.

Column Content Id Internal company number Name Company name Address one Address 1 City City State State/province Zip ZIP/postal code Country Country Active true or false

The export lists companies only: no people or contact details, and no emails or phone numbers. It includes every company: your own company, active, disabled and deleted customers. It ignores the filter and search on the page. See also Data Exports.

docs.title: Change History
docs.text: Changes to customer records are recorded in the system's change history. The Customers page has no Audit button to view it.

docs.title: Customer or person doesn't appear in the order form dropdown
docs.text:
Solution

The Place the order on behalf of list only shows people when all of these are true:

  • the customer is Active (check the Disabled filter) and not deleted,
  • the customer's Service includes Intermodal (a customer set to only Warehouse or Garage won't appear),
  • the person is not deleted and Active for orders is checked on their Edit Person page,
  • the customer has at least one person,
  • in single-office accounts, the person is assigned to the office you're currently working in (with Multi-Office, people from every office are listed).

docs.title: A person didn't receive the invitation email
docs.text:
Solution

Click Edit Person on their row. The page shows when the last invitation was sent. Click resend the email, or copy the invitation link shown there and send it to them yourself. Check that the email address is correct.

docs.title: There's no Delete button on a customer
docs.text:
Solution

The Delete button is hidden for your own company, for customers with invoices, and for customers that have (or had) people. Disable the customer instead. Also, only Admin and Manager can delete.

docs.title: I can't see the Customers menu
docs.text:
Solution

Accountants have no access to Customers. Dispatch users only see it when Dispatch customer management is turned on for your account. Ask UTX support.

docs.title: My search returns nothing
docs.text:
Solution

Type at least 2 characters. The search looks within the selected filter: if Brokers or Disabled is selected, only those customers are searched. Switch to All Active or to your own company filter to search more widely. Deleted customers are never found.

docs.title: I can't edit my own company
docs.text:
Solution

In single-office accounts, only Admin users can edit your own company and its staff. Ask an Admin. See Editing your own company.

docs.title: I can't change the Default Order Rate
docs.text:
Solution

Default Order Rate is read-only on the customer form. To give a customer different prices, use Custom rates for this customer (zones, terminals, warehouse charges).

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
Tips for managing customers

  • Fill in the Accountant Email right away. Invoices and statements use it.
  • Set the Service correctly. It decides whether the customer shows up for intermodal orders, warehouse orders, or both.
  • Use Custom rates for this customer for negotiated prices instead of editing each order by hand.
  • Disable customers you no longer work with rather than leaving them active. They stay in your history but drop out of the order form.
  • Double-check email addresses before clicking Add this person. The invitation goes out immediately.

docs.title: Terminals
docs.text: Create and manage the terminals (rail yards, port terminals and other pickup or return locations) that your orders pick containers up from and return them to.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Terminals are the physical locations where containers are picked up and returned. On an order, the Pick up Terminal and the Return Address terminal are both chosen from this list.

  • The Terminals page lists every terminal with its address, city, contact details, Default Rate and whether it is active.
  • Each terminal belongs to an office. Without the Multi-Office add-on, each office only sees its own terminals. With it, every office shares the same list.
  • The Default Rate is the terminal fee. On Container Import and Container Export orders it is added automatically as a Computed Terminal Fee charge, as long as a charge type is set as the Terminal Fee.
  • A customer can have its own rate for a terminal under Custom rates for this customer. That rate replaces the terminal's Default Rate for that customer.
  • Some terminal names are read by the app to drive order filters and container tracking (CN, CP, Termont, Viau, Racine, Cast). Choose and change names carefully.
  • Terminals cannot be deleted. Disable a terminal to remove it from new orders. Orders that already use it are not affected.
  • Every change is recorded and can be viewed with View History.

Intermodal only

Terminals are part of the intermodal (container) workflow. The Manage Terminals menu item only appears when your account runs in intermodal mode.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
1. Click your name in the top menu Manage Terminals.
  2. Click Add a new Terminal at the top right.
  3. Enter the Name and pick the Office.
  4. Optionally fill in the address, City (Must exist), contact details and Default Rate.
  5. Click Save Changes.

The terminal is immediately available in the terminal dropdowns on the order forms.

To set or change only the fee, click the amount (or not set) in the Default Rate column and type the new rate. See Editing the Default Rate in the list.

docs.title: Access & Permissions
docs.text:
Role Access Level Admin Full access: create, edit, edit the rate in the list, enable, disable, view history Manager Full access to the terminals of their own offices. With the Multi-Office add-on, full access to all terminals Dispatch No access by default. Full access (same as Manager) only if UTX has turned on dispatcher terminal management for your account Accountant No access All other roles (Customer, Driver and others) No access

There is no view-only access

A user either manages terminals or does not see the page at all. Dispatchers and Accountants without access do not see Manage Terminals in their menu.

Dispatchers: turning on terminal management

Dispatcher terminal management is an account-level option set by UTX. It is not a toggle in Settings, and it applies to all dispatchers on the account at once. To have it turned on, contact UTX support. Until then, ask an Admin or Manager to create or change terminals for you.

How to get there:

  • Click your name at the top of the screen to open the user menu, then click Manage Terminals.

Manage Terminals is in the user menu with the other Manage … items (Manage Cities, Manage Zones and so on). It is not inside the Settings page.

docs.title: The Terminals List
docs.text:
The page is titled Terminals (Management of Terminals). Two filter buttons at the top left switch the list:

  • All Active: active terminals (the default view).
  • Disabled: terminals that have been disabled.

Terminals are sorted by name, 25 per page, with page links at the bottom.

docs.title: Columns
docs.text: Column What it shows Terminal Name The terminal name in bold. Green when the terminal is active, red when it is disabled. The name is not a link. Address Street address Zip Postal code City The linked city, in green Country The linked city's country, in green Contact info Free-form contact details Email Terminal email Default Rate The terminal fee in bold green (for example $12.50), or a grey not set when the rate is $0.00 Active A green check mark for active, a red cross for disabled (Actions) The Actions dropdown for the row

docs.title: Row Actions
docs.text:
Click Actions (or the arrow next to it) at the end of a row:

Action What it does Edit Opens the Edit Terminal page with the full form View History Opens the History window for this terminal Disable Shown for active terminals. Disables the terminal Enable Shown for disabled terminals. Re-activates the terminal

There is no Delete action. Use Disable for terminals you no longer use.

docs.title: Creating a Terminal
docs.text:
1. Go to your name Manage Terminals.
  2. Click Add a new Terminal. The New Terminal page opens.
  3. Fill in the Terminal Information form (see the table below).
  4. Click Save Changes, or Cancel to go back to the list without saving.

docs.title: Terminal Information
docs.text:
Field Required Description Name Terminal name (placeholder Terminal name). Shown in order dropdowns, on the Orders and Dispatch pages and on reports. Some names drive filters and tracking, see Terminal Names, Filters and Tracking Office The office that owns the terminal. The dropdown lists the offices you belong to and has no blank option, so your first office is pre-selected Address Street address (placeholder Address) City (Must exist) The terminal's city, picked from a searchable list of the active cities of your current office. Shown in the City and Country columns of the list. Used for display only. If the city is missing, add it first under Manage Cities. See Zones and Cities Postal Code Postal or ZIP code (placeholder Postal Code) Contact Info Free-form contact details such as phone, hours or gate information (placeholder Contact Info) Email Terminal email address (placeholder Email) Default Rate The terminal fee. Hint: This rate will be applied as a charge to all orders using this terminal Starts at 0 (shown as not set in the list). See Terminal Fee for exactly when it is applied Active Under Terminal visibility. Hint: Only active terminals will be visible for new orders Checked by default for a new terminal

If Name is left blank, the form comes back with an error under the field and nothing is saved.

Keep names short and recognizable

The Name is what users see in every dropdown. Use a short, clear name such as Termont 68, and check Terminal Names, Filters and Tracking before you choose one.

docs.title: Editing a Terminal
docs.text:
1. Go to your name Manage Terminals.
  2. On the terminal's row, click Actions Edit.
  3. Change the fields on the Edit Terminal page and click Save Changes.

Changes to the name, address and contact details show everywhere the terminal is used, including orders already in progress, because orders point to the terminal record. Changes to the Default Rate work differently. See Terminal Fee.

Check before renaming a terminal

Renaming a terminal can change which orders appear under the CN, CP, Racine, Cast and Termont filters, which orders are tracked, and which source is used to look up the container status for orders that pick up there. Read Terminal Names, Filters and Tracking before you rename.

docs.title: Editing the Default Rate in the List
docs.text:
You can change a terminal's fee without opening the full form. This is the fastest way to price several terminals in a row, for example during the setup checklist.

  1. In the Default Rate column, click the amount, or not set if there is no rate yet.
  2. A small editor opens, titled Enter the default terminal fee.
  3. Type the rate and confirm.

The row refreshes with the new rate.

Accepted formats:

You type Saved as 12.50 $12.50 12,50 $12.50 (comma is read as a decimal point) $12.50 $12.50 (dollar sign is ignored) 12 $12.00 (spaces are ignored) 0 $0.00 (shown as not set)

Anything else (letters, a negative amount, an empty value, a thousands separator such as 1,250.00, more than one decimal point) is rejected with the message "<what you typed> is not an amount", and the rate is not changed. To remove a rate, enter 0.

Who can edit in the list

The rate is clickable only for users who can manage the terminal. It is the same permission as the rest of the page.

docs.title: Terminal Fee
docs.text: The Default Rate is turned into a charge on the order automatically. This is how it works.

docs.title: What is needed
docs.text:
• A charge type set as Use as default for: Terminal Fee. Set this on the charge type in Charge Types (see Charge Types and Taxes). If no charge type is set as the Terminal Fee, no terminal fee is ever added, whatever the terminal rates are.
  • A rate of $1.00 or more, either the terminal's Default Rate or the customer's custom rate for that terminal. Rates below $1.00 (including not set) do not add a charge.

docs.title: Which terminal is charged
docs.text: Order type Terminal used for the fee Container Import The pick up terminal (Full container pick up terminal) Container Export The return terminal (Full container return terminal) Any other type (Container Transfer, Dry Van Move and so on) No terminal fee

docs.title: Which rate is used
docs.text:
1. If the order's customer has a Custom rates for this customer row for that terminal, the custom rate is used.
  2. Otherwise, the terminal's Default Rate is used.

If the customer's custom rate for the terminal is under $1.00 (for example 0), no Terminal Fee is added to that customer's new orders for that terminal, even if the terminal has a Default Rate.

To set a customer-specific terminal rate, edit the customer, go to Custom rates for this customer, click (+) Add another, pick the terminal from the Terminal group of the Charge dropdown and enter the Rate. Only active terminals are listed (from every office). See Managing Customers.

docs.title: When the fee is calculated
docs.text:
The fee is calculated when the order is created, and again each time the order is saved (full form, Quick Edit, dispatch and the other order actions that save charges). Each time:

  • Any existing charge of the Terminal Fee charge type on the order is removed and replaced by one charge with the current rate and the note Computed Terminal Fee.
  • It only happens while the order is not invoiced and not completed. Completed and invoiced orders keep the charges they already have.
  • If the rate is under $1.00, nothing is added and an existing Terminal Fee charge is left as it is.
  • If several charge types are set as Terminal Fee, only the first one found is used.

With the Fuel Surcharge add-on, clicking Recalculate for a month on the Fuel Schedule also re-saves that month's open orders, so their Terminal Fee is recalculated too. See Fuel Surcharge.

Changing a rate does not reprice existing orders

When you change a terminal's Default Rate (or a customer's custom terminal rate), orders that already exist keep their old Terminal Fee. An open order picks up the new rate only the next time it is saved. Completed and invoiced orders never change.

Manual changes to the Terminal Fee are overwritten

If you edit the amount of the Terminal Fee charge by hand on an open order, it is replaced by the computed rate the next time the order is saved (as long as the computed rate is $1.00 or more). To charge a customer a different terminal fee permanently, use a custom rate on the customer instead.

docs.title: Enabling & Disabling Terminals
docs.text:
Terminals cannot be deleted. Instead, disable a terminal to take it out of the dropdowns used on orders and custom rates.

To disable a terminal:

  1. In the All Active list, click Actions Disable on the terminal's row.
  2. A notification confirms Terminal <name> - Disabled. The name turns red and the Active column shows a red cross. The row stays on screen until you reload the list, then it moves to Disabled.

To enable a terminal:

  1. Click the Disabled filter button.
  2. Click Actions Enable on the terminal's row.
  3. A notification confirms Terminal <name> - Enabled.

You can also check or uncheck Active on the Edit Terminal form.

Orders that already use a disabled terminal keep it and continue to show its name.

docs.title: History
docs.text:
Every change to a terminal is recorded.

  1. On the terminal's row, click Actions View History.
  2. The History window opens with one line per change, newest first:
Column What it shows User Who made the change (or System for automatic changes) Changes Each field that changed, with its old and new value (for example Default rate or Contact info). The office and city values are shown by name When The date and time of the change

Use it to see who changed a rate or renamed a terminal, and when.

docs.title: Terminal Names, Filters and Tracking
docs.text:
The app reads some terminal names to decide which orders appear under the terminal filters, which orders get container tracking, and where to look up the container status. Matching ignores upper and lower case, and looks at terminals of every office.

Group Terminals that belong to it CN A terminal named exactly CN CP A terminal named exactly CP Racine Any terminal whose name contains RACINE Cast Any terminal whose name contains CAST Termont Any terminal whose name contains TERMONT or VIAU

docs.title: Order filters
docs.text:
The TERMINAL filters on the Orders page (and the terminal filters on the Dispatch page) only appear when at least one terminal belongs to the group. They show orders by pick up terminal.

The Orders page shows all five filters. The Dispatch page shows CN, CP and Termont. See Orders and Dispatch.

docs.title: Container tracking
docs.text:
• Which orders are tracked. Automatic container tracking (CN, Termont / Port of Montreal and MGT for Racine and Cast, each a separate add-on) and the tracking icon in the order list apply to orders whose pick up terminal is in the CN, Termont, Racine or Cast group.
  • Which source the status window uses. When you open the container status of an order, the source is picked from the first word of the pick up terminal's name:
First word of the terminal name Tracking source RACINE or CAST MGT (Montreal Gateway Terminals) TERMONT or VIAU Termont CN CN

See Container Tracking.

Auto Orders

When an order is created automatically from a document, the pick up terminal is chosen from the text: CN or Canadian National goes to the first CN terminal, CP to the first CP terminal, Racine to the first Racine terminal and Termont to the first Termont terminal. See Auto Orders.

Rename with care

  • Renaming CN or CP to anything else (even CN Montreal), or removing Termont, Viau, Racine or Cast from a name, takes that terminal's orders out of the matching filter, and (for CN, Termont, Racine and Cast) out of container tracking.
  • Changing the first word of a Racine, Cast, Termont, Viau or CN terminal can stop the container status from being found for orders that pick up there.
  • Giving an unrelated terminal a name that contains CAST, RACINE, TERMONT or VIAU (or naming it exactly CN or CP) puts its orders under that filter (and into container tracking, where it applies).

If you are not sure, contact UTX support before renaming.

docs.title: Multi-Office Setups
docs.text:
The Office field and what you see in the list depend on whether your account has the Multi-Office add-on.

Without Multi-Office With Multi-Office Terminals list Only the terminals of your current office All terminals, from every office Terminal dropdowns on orders Active terminals of your current office All active terminals Who can manage a terminal Admins, and Managers (and enabled Dispatchers) of the terminal's office Admins, Managers and enabled Dispatchers, for every terminal Office field Decides which office sees and uses the terminal Records the owning office only. Every office sees and uses the terminal

The Office dropdown lists the offices you belong to. If you belong to more than one office, pick the right one before saving. Without Multi-Office, a terminal saved under the wrong office will not appear for the other office.

See Multi-Office.

docs.title: Setup Checklist
docs.text:
The setup checklist has a step called Set the default rate on your terminals, with an Open Terminals button that brings you to this page. The step is done when both are true:

  • A charge type is set as Use as default for: Terminal Fee.
  • At least one active terminal has a Default Rate above $0.00.

What the step suggests:

  1. Open Charge Types and mark one of them as the Terminal Fee.
  2. Open Terminals and set a default rate on the ones you actually pull from (the in-list rate editor is the fastest way).
  3. Disable the terminals you never use so they leave the dropdowns.

See Setup Checklist.

docs.title: I can't see a terminal on the order form
docs.text:
Solution

The terminal is probably disabled. Go to your name > Manage Terminals, click Disabled, and use Actions > Enable on it. Without the Multi-Office add-on, also check that the terminal belongs to the office you are working in.

docs.title: There is no Manage Terminals item in my menu
docs.text:
Solution

Check the following:

  • Your account must run in intermodal mode. The item is hidden otherwise.
  • Dispatchers only see it if UTX has turned on dispatcher terminal management for your account. Ask an Admin or Manager, or contact UTX support.
  • Accountants and other roles do not have access to terminals.
  • Look in the user menu under your name, not on the Settings page.

docs.title: The city I need isn't in the dropdown
docs.text:
Solution

The City (Must exist) dropdown only lists active cities of your current office. Add or enable the city under Manage Cities first, then come back to the terminal. See Zones and Cities. The city is for display only, so you can also leave it blank.

docs.title: The terminal has a rate but no Terminal Fee appears on the order
docs.text:
Solution

Check each of these:

  • A charge type is set as Use as default for: Terminal Fee.
  • The order is a Container Import (the fee uses the pick up terminal) or a Container Export (the fee uses the return terminal).
  • The rate is $1.00 or more. Check the customer's Custom rates for this customer too, because a custom rate for that terminal replaces the default rate.
  • The order is not completed or invoiced.
  • The order has been saved since the rate was set. Open it and save it to recalculate.

docs.title: I changed a terminal rate but my orders still show the old fee
docs.text:
Solution

A rate change does not reprice existing orders. Open orders get the new rate the next time they are saved. Completed and invoiced orders keep the fee they had.

docs.title: The rate editor says "… is not an amount"
docs.text:
Solution

Type a plain positive number such as 12.50, 12,50 or $12.50. Letters, negative numbers and empty values are rejected. To clear a rate, enter 0.

docs.title: How do I delete a terminal?
docs.text:
Solution

Terminals cannot be deleted. Use Actions > Disable. The terminal leaves the dropdowns and orders that already use it keep it.

docs.title: Orders disappeared from the CN, CP, Racine, Cast or Termont filter
docs.text:
Solution

These filters match on the terminal name (CN and CP must be the exact name). Check View History on the terminal to see whether it was renamed, and restore the name if needed. See Terminal Names, Filters and Tracking.

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
Best Practices

  • Set up the Terminal Fee charge type first, then price your terminals. Without it, terminal rates are never charged.
  • Use the in-list Default Rate editor to price several terminals quickly.
  • Use Custom rates for this customer for negotiated terminal fees instead of editing the charge on each order.
  • After changing a rate, re-save the open orders that should use the new fee.
  • Disable terminals you never use so they leave the dropdowns.
  • Do not rename CN, CP, Racine, Cast, Termont or Viau terminals without checking the impact on filters and tracking.

docs.title: Drivers, Brokers & Yard Workers (Mobile Users)
docs.text: Set up the people who use UTX Freight from a phone (drivers, brokers and yard workers) and give each of them an Access Code to sign in.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
A mobile user is someone who works in UTX Freight from a phone instead of the office screens. Mobile users are kept separate from office staff (who are added as people on your company, see People & Invitations). They don't have an email and password. They sign in with an Access Code or with a login link sent by dispatch.

  • Driver: is assigned to orders and completes them from the phone (signatures, delivered/returned). See Driver Workflow.
  • Broker: has the same mobile rights as a Driver and appears in the same driver lists.
  • Yard Worker: works the yard from the phone. Searches containers by number. Is not offered in the order driver lists. See Yard Management.
  • Each mobile user is either active or disabled. Only active users can sign in and be assigned.
  • Changes to mobile users are recorded in the audit history.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
1. In the left menu, open Mobile Users Drivers, Brokers & Yard.
  2. Click Add a new mobile user.
  3. Fill in Firstname and Lastname. Optionally add the Phone #.
  4. Pick the Role: Driver, Broker or Yard Worker.
