Column What it shows Shipper Delivery location name in capitals. Click it to drill down Invoices Number of different invoices those orders are on Completed Orders Number of invoiced orders delivered to that location All Income Sum of those orders' totals, before tax

docs.title: Drill-down: Invoices panel
docs.text:
Click a shipper name (or pick one in the Shipper filter). The Invoices panel lists each invoice with its orders for that location:

Column Order line Invoice line Invoice Invoice number (greyed) Invoice number Date Invoice date Order Order number Bill To Customer billed for the order Container# Container number Order Income Order total (before tax) All Income Whole invoice total with taxes Paid Income Amount paid on the whole invoice

Invoice lines cover the whole invoice

All Income and Paid Income on an invoice line are for the entire invoice, including orders delivered elsewhere. Only the order lines are limited to the selected location.

This report has no export button.

docs.title: Delivery by Zone
docs.text: A chart of how many orders were delivered in each zone, day by day. It counts orders only: it shows no revenue and has no table.

docs.title: Filters
docs.text:
Field Default Options Start date Monday of last week Compared with the order delivery date End date Sunday of this week Inclusive Chart type Bar Chart Bar Chart, Stacked Bar Chart, Line Chart

Click Update Report to redraw the chart.

docs.title: How orders are counted
docs.text:
• Each point is the number of orders with that delivery date, whatever their status (invoiced or not).
  • The zone comes from the city of the order's delivery location, using the zone assigned to that city in Zones & Cities.
  • No Zone is a series of its own: orders whose delivery location's city has no zone.
  • Orders whose delivery location has no city, and orders with no delivery location picked from Shippers / Receivers, are not counted in any series.
  • Days with no deliveries in a zone have no point for that zone.
  • Use the chart toolbar (top right of the chart) to download the chart as an image. There is no table or CSV export.

docs.title: Daily Income
docs.text: A bar chart with one bar per day: the total of order amounts for that day.

docs.title: Filters
docs.text:
Field Default Notes Start Date 7 days ago First day of the chart Days 7 Number of days to show, starting on Start Date

Click Filter to redraw the chart. Hover a bar to see Income for YYYY-MM-DD: followed by the amount and $.

docs.title: How it is calculated
docs.text:
• Orders are placed on the day of their delivery date.
  • Each day's value is the sum of those orders' totals (the order amount before tax).
  • All orders count, whatever their status, invoiced or not.
  • The page shows the chart only. There is no table and no export.

docs.title: Sales per Month
docs.text:
A table of invoiced sales per month for about the last 22 months (the current month and the 21 before it), newest first.

Column What it shows # Row number Month Month and year, for example Mar 2026 Invoices # Number of invoices with an invoice date in that month Sales Sum of those invoices' subtotals, before tax

There are no filters on this page.

Figures are precomputed

The monthly figures are calculated regularly in the background, and the page shows the most recent calculation, so a change you just made may take a little while to appear. The current month is a month-to-date figure. Use Income by Customer for a period when you need live figures.

docs.title: Order Sales / Profit
docs.text: Sales, expenses and profit for each order delivered in a date range. The page heading reads Order sales / profits.

docs.title: Filters
docs.text:
Field Default Notes Start Date 7 days ago First delivery date included Days 7 Number of days included. 0 is treated as 1

Click Filter to refresh. There is no customer or company filter, and all orders count whatever their status.

docs.title: Columns
docs.text:
Column What it shows # Row number Delivery Date Order delivery date (rows are sorted by it) Order # Order number Container # Container number P/O # Delivery P/O number Booking # Booking number Client The order's delivery location (Deliver To company), not the billed customer. For a transfer order it shows the customer's company name Sales Order total, before tax Expenses Sum of the expense lines in the order's Order Expenses section Profits Sales minus Expenses

Two rows close the table when there is at least one order: Totals (sum of each money column) and Average Per Order (each total divided by the number of orders).

Profit is an amount, not a margin

Profits is a dollar amount. The report does not show a percentage margin. Expenses come from the Order Expenses panel on each order; an order with no expenses shows its whole total as profit. See Order Rates, Charges & Expenses.

docs.title: Drivers Delivery Report
docs.text: The list of legs one driver moved, for orders delivered in a date range. The page heading reads Driver Delivery Report.

docs.title: Running the report
docs.text:
1. Go to Reports > Drivers Delivery Report.
  2. Pick the Driver. The list shows active drivers.
  3. Set Start Date (default: 7 days ago) and Days (default: 7; 0 is treated as 1).
  4. Click Report. The results appear below the filters without reloading the page.

The report covers one driver at a time. To compare drivers, run it once per driver.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
The header shows Driver Name: and Date: (a single date, or start to end for a range). Then one row per leg:

Column What it shows Leg Row number (#1, #2, ...) Date The order's delivery date Order # Order number Container # Container number Move From => To move locations of the leg; N/A when a location is missing
  • A leg is included when the selected driver is recorded as the driver who moved it.
  • The date range filters on the order's delivery date, not on when the leg was moved. Legs are sorted by that date.
  • The report shows no counts, totals or pay. Count the rows if you need a number of moves. Driver pay is recorded in Order Expenses and on Expenses & Checks.

See Order Legs & Move Locations for how legs are recorded.

docs.title: Customer Reports
docs.text:
The statements page: one row per customer with unpaid invoices, where you email, print or download a Statement of Account. Full details are in Customer Statements.

  • Which customers appear: only customers that have at least one invoice whose status is not Paid. Customers with everything paid are not listed. There is no date filter.
  • Customer filter: [ALL CUSTOMERS] by default, or pick one customer and click Update Report.
  • The list is paginated.

docs.title: Columns
docs.text:
Column What it shows Status Red when the customer has past due invoices, green otherwise Name Customer name, in red when the customer is inactive Orders Number of orders for the customer Invoices Number of invoices for the customer Income Total of all the customer's orders, all dates, before tax Past Due Unpaid balance (with taxes, minus payments) of invoices not marked Paid whose due date is before today Not Yet Due Unpaid balance of the other invoices not marked Paid (due today or later) Unpaid Invoices Number of past due invoices, as a red badge when above zero Sent date Date the last statement was emailed, or - Email Result of the last statement email (for example OK or Failed!) Delivery Day / Next Date Only when automatic statements are enabled on your account: the statement schedule (or Not Scheduled) and when the next one goes out. Click it to change the schedule (buttons) Email, Print, and the green Excel download

When automatic statements are enabled, the top of the page also shows how many customers are scheduled on each day (Sun to Sat, 1st, 15th, 2nd & 16th). See Automatic Statements.

docs.title: Aged Receivables (AR)
docs.text:
The Aged Receivables (AR) page shows unpaid balances per customer as of a date, aged by due date (Not Yet Overdue, 30 or Less, 31 to 60, 61 to 90, 91 or More, Total Unpaid). Pick the As of Date, click Update Report, and click Download Excel for the same figures as an .xlsx file.

For full details, see Aged Receivables.

docs.title: AR Export
docs.text:
AR Export generates and keeps monthly AR Excel files, so you can download a month's figures later. The page itself is headed Aged Receivables (AR) under Analytics, and the list of files is headed AR Reports. A note at the top explains that this is a business performance report covering the 12 months ending on the selected month.

  1. Go to Reports > AR Export.
  2. In Report Period, pick a quick selection (This Month, the default, Last Month, 2 Months Ago or 3 Months Ago, each shown with its month and year). To pick another month, choose Custom Month/Year and then select the Month and Year (from five years back to next year).
  3. Click Generate Report. The file is built straight away.
  4. In Generated Reports, click the green Excel button in the Download column once the Status is Ready.

The Generated Reports table shows Month/Year, Status (Ready, Generating or Failed), Total Income, Duration, Generated At, and the Download, Regenerate and Delete buttons. Total Income is the total of the invoices (with taxes) in the 12-month period. Only one report can exist per month and year: generating a month that already exists shows an error asking you to use Regenerate. Regenerate is available on Ready reports; a Failed report can only be deleted, then generated again.

The export is aggregated, not raw data

The Excel file has one row per customer of the office (every customer that is not deleted, including those with no invoices), not one row per invoice. Columns: Customer, Invoices, Completed Orders, All Income (with taxes), AR As Of YYYY-MM-DD (the unpaid total as of the last day of the selected month), 30 days, 60 days, 90 days and 90+ days, plus a TOTALS row. It covers invoices dated in the 12 months ending on the last day of the selected month.

Unlike Aged Receivables (AR), the AR Export ages unpaid amounts by invoice date (days from the invoice date to the end of the month), not by due date, and counts only payments dated on or before the end of the month. To see individual invoices, use Income by Customer or the Invoices list.

Regenerating replaces the file

Regenerate deletes the saved file for that month and builds a new one from current data. Use it after you correct invoices or record payments.

docs.title: Garage Reports
docs.text: If your account has the Garage add-on, garage reports are under Reports in the Garage sidebar, not in the freight Reports menu. See Garage Reports.

docs.title: I don't see the Reports menu
docs.text:
Solution

Only Admin users always see Reports. Manager users see it only when reports are enabled for managers on your account (contact UTX support). Dispatch and Accountant users never see it, and there is no per-report access.

docs.title: Report shows no data
docs.text:
Solution

Check which date the report uses:

  • Income by Customer, Income by Shipper, Sales per Month and AR Export only count invoices, by invoice date. Orders that are not invoiced yet do not appear.
  • Daily Income, Delivery by Zone, Order Sales / Profit and Drivers Delivery Report count orders by delivery date, invoiced or not.

Also check that you are in the right office: reports only show the current office.

docs.title: Two reports show different totals for the same period
docs.text:
Solution

This is expected. The reports use different dates and amounts:

Report Date used Amount Income by Customer Invoice date Invoice total with taxes Income by Shipper Invoice date Order totals before tax Sales per Month Invoice date Invoice subtotal before tax Daily Income Delivery date Order totals before tax Order Sales / Profit Delivery date Order totals before tax

An order delivered at the end of one month and invoiced in the next falls in different months depending on the report.

docs.title: Sales per Month doesn't match Income by Customer
docs.text:
Solution

Sales per Month is before tax and shows figures calculated regularly in the background, so a very recent change may not show yet. Income by Customer is live and includes taxes. Compare against Income by Customer for the same month to check live figures.

docs.title: The Income by Customer export has no invoice detail
docs.text:
Solution

Export Report only exports the summary (one line per customer plus TOTALS). For invoice and order detail, drill down on the page.

docs.title: Orders are missing from Delivery by Zone
docs.text:
Solution

Orders count only when their delivery location has a city. Orders whose city has no zone appear under No Zone. Give the city a zone in Zones & Cities.

docs.title: Numbers don't match my accounting software
docs.text:
Solution

Accounting software often uses payment or posting dates, while UTX Freight reports use invoice dates or delivery dates (see the table above). For month-end reconciliation, use Aged Receivables (AR) (as of a date, by due date) or the AR Export file. Note that the AR Export is aggregated per customer; it is not a raw invoice list.

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
Tips for reliable reports

  • Use Income by Customer or Sales per Month for invoiced revenue, and Daily Income or Order Sales / Profit for work delivered but not necessarily billed yet.
  • Record Order Expenses on every order so Order Sales / Profit shows real profit.
  • Assign a zone to every city your customers deliver to, so Delivery by Zone has as few No Zone orders as possible.
  • Generate an AR Export at each month end and keep it as your record of that month.

docs.title: Setup Checklist
docs.text: The setup checklist is a built-in page that checks your UTX Freight system and tells you, step by step, what still needs to be set up before you can raise a correct invoice.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
• The checklist lives at the top of the left menu, for Admin and Manager users only. Its menu label is Getting started, Setup check or Setup complete, depending on where your system is.
  • It has 6 stages and up to 20 steps, from pricing your zones to sending your first invoice.
  • Every step is checked automatically against the data in your system. You do not tick steps off by hand. The one exception is the two steps that offer a Looks right to me button.
  • While required steps are still open, exactly one step is marked Do this next: the first required step that is not done yet. Optional steps are never marked Do this next.
  • Some steps are Optional. You can skip them and still invoice, and they are not counted in the progress bar.
  • The checklist covers your whole system, not one office. Counts include every office.

For a walkthrough of creating your first customer, contact and order by hand, see Getting Started.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
1. In the left menu, click Getting started (or Setup check).
  2. The step marked Do this next is already open on the right.
  3. Read What we found and How to do it, then click the button at the bottom of the panel (for example Open Zones) to go and do the work.
  4. Come back to the checklist. The page re-checks everything each time it loads, so the step shows Done as soon as the work is saved.
  5. Repeat until the title reads Your setup is complete.

docs.title: Access & Permissions
docs.text:
Role Access Admin Sees the menu entry and can open the checklist. Can complete every step. Manager Sees the menu entry and can open the checklist. Some steps point to pages a Manager cannot open (see the warning below). Dispatch, Accountant, Customer Service, Customer, Warehouse, Garage, drivers and other users No menu entry. If they reach the checklist page some other way (for example from a saved link), they are sent to the home page with the message You do not have access to the setup checklist.

Navigation: left menu Getting started / Setup check / Setup complete (the first item in the menu).

Some steps lead Managers to pages they cannot open

Three steps send you to pages that only Admins can use:

  • Add your GST, QST and NIR numbers and Your email is configured use the Open Settings button.
  • Check what your website says uses the Open Manage Content button.

A Manager can see these steps but cannot open those pages. Ask an Admin to fill in the tax numbers. A Manager can still use Looks right to me on Check what your website says.

See User Roles for what each role can do.

docs.title: The Menu Entry
docs.text:
The checklist's entry in the left menu changes its label and icon as your setup progresses.

Label When it shows Icon Tooltip (on hover) Getting started No invoice exists yet, and required steps are still open N steps before your first invoice Setup check At least one invoice exists, and required steps are still open N things still to set up Setup complete Every required step is done (green) Everything on the setup checklist is done

N is the number of required steps still open. Optional steps are never counted.

The entry stays in the menu after setup is complete, so you can come back and read the checklist at any time.

The menu entry can take up to 5 minutes to update

To keep every page fast, the menu label and count are refreshed at most every 5 minutes. The checklist page itself always shows the current state. If you just finished a step and the menu still shows the old count, open the checklist page to see the true state. The menu catches up within 5 minutes.

Saving the Application Settings page (for example, adding the tax numbers) or clicking Looks right to me refreshes the menu entry, so it is up to date on the next page you open.

docs.title: Title and progress
docs.text:
The heading at the top of the page depends on where your system is:

Situation Title Text under the title No invoices yet Get your company to its first invoice The shortest path to your first invoice. Anything marked Optional can wait. Already invoicing, steps still open What is still not set up You are already invoicing, so nothing here is urgent - but each of these is either costing you money or waiting to. Anything marked Optional can wait. Every required step done Your setup is complete Everything on this list is done. It stays here if you ever want to read it again.

Below the title:

  • A progress bar with the text X of Y done. Y is the number of required steps (16, or 17 with the fuel surcharge add-on). Optional steps are left out of both numbers.
  • A summary line:
    • Before your first invoice: N steps between you and your first invoice
    • Once you are invoicing: N things still to set up
    • When complete: Everything is set up.
    • If any required step in Stage 1 (Set your prices) is still open, the line adds · N of them decide what you can charge.

docs.title: Step list (left) and panel (right)
docs.text:
The page is split in two:

  • Left: the step list. Steps are grouped under their stage heading, for example Stage 1 Set your prices. Each stage heading shows X of Y done, plus N optional if the stage has optional steps. A stage whose required steps are all done shows a ✓ before its count and collapses, unless the panel is showing one of its steps. Click a stage heading to open or close it.
  • Right: the panel. Shows the details of the selected step. When you open the page, the panel shows the Do this next step (or the first step, once everything is done).

Click any step in the list to show it in the panel. Once a step in the list has keyboard focus, you can also use the ↑ and ↓ arrow keys to move up and down the list (the hint ↑ ↓ to walk the list shows under the page). The arrow keys skip steps inside collapsed stages.

Each step in the list shows a mark, its name and a badge:

Mark Badge Meaning ✓ Done The step is done. ✓ Done · check The step is done but has a warning worth reading. The warning shows under the step name with a ⚠ sign. ▶ Do this next The first required step that is not done. Only one step has this badge at a time. ○ Optional An optional step that is not done. You can skip it. ○ (no badge) A required step that is not done, further down the list.

Steps that are not done also show a short finding under their name, for example No customers yet.

docs.title: What the panel shows
docs.text: Part What it contains Stage and state The stage number followed by Done, Do this next, Optional or Still to do. Step name The name of the step, for example Set the price of each zone. What we found What the checklist found in your system, for example 3 of 5 zones priced. A warning, if any, shows here too. Why A short paragraph explaining why the step matters. How to do it Numbered instructions. Button Takes you to the page where you do the work, for example Open Zones. Open Feedback opens the Feedback form in a pop-up instead of leaving the page. Looks right to me Only on Check your charge types and Check what your website says. See Looks right to me.

docs.title: Stages and Steps
docs.text: The steps appear in this order. The Done when column is the exact rule the checklist uses to mark a step done.

docs.title: Stage 1 — Set your prices
docs.text:
Step Button Done when Your cities are loaded Open Cities At least one active city exists. Cities are loaded when your system is built, so this is normally already done. Set the price of each zone Open Zones At least one active zone has a price above $0.00. Put the cities you deliver to in a zone Open Cities (with the Shipping filter) Every city you have delivered to has a zone. Also done if you have no deliveries yet. Set the default rate on your terminals Open Terminals A charge type is set as Use as default for: Terminal Fee, and at least one active terminal has a default rate above $0.00. Both are needed.

Zones at $0.00

Set the price of each zone is marked done as soon as one active zone has a price. If other active zones are still at $0.00, the step shows Done · check with the warning N active zones still have no price and will invoice at $0.00. An order delivered into one of those zones is invoiced for nothing, with no other warning. Price those zones, or disable the ones you do not use. See Zones and Cities.

Put the cities you deliver to in a zone only counts cities that a delivery address on one of your orders points to, not the full city list. The Shipping filter on the Cities page shows the same list. A city with no zone prices at $0.00.

For terminals, see Managing Terminals and Charge Types and Taxes.

docs.title: Stage 2 — Who you haul for
docs.text:
Step Optional Button Done when Add your first customer Open Customers At least one active customer company exists. Your own company does not count, and neither does the UTX Web Inc. support company. Add a contact at that customer Open Customers At least one active user with the Customer role exists. Add your shippers and receivers Optional Open Shipper / Receiver At least one active shipper/receiver exists, and every active shipper/receiver has a city set. Set special prices for a customer Optional Open Customers At least one customer has a negotiated price on a zone.

Adding a contact sends an invitation

Saving a new person emails them an invitation straight away. To set up a contact quietly, use an address like yourcompany+1@utxfreight.ca and change it later. See People and Invitations.

A shipper or receiver with no city set prices at $0.00, however well your zones are set. See Shippers and Receivers.

docs.title: Stage 3 — Your yard
docs.text:
Step Optional Button Done when Add one chassis Open Equipments At least one active piece of equipment (of any type) exists. Add one driver Open Mobile Users At least one active mobile user with the Driver or Broker role exists. Add your office staff Optional Open Customers At least one active user with the Dispatch, Accountant, Manager or Customer Service role exists.

See Equipment and Mobile Users. Office staff are added as people on your own company, at the top of the Customers list.

docs.title: Stage 4 — What appears on your invoice
docs.text:
Step Button Done when Add your GST, QST and NIR numbers Open Settings GST Number and QST Number (under Invoice Settings) and NIR Number (under POD Settings) on the Application Settings page are all filled in. Set this month's fuel surcharge Open Fuel Schedule A general (not customer-specific) monthly fuel surcharge rate exists for the current month. Only shown when your system has the fuel surcharge add-on. To have it turned on, ask UTX support. Check your charge types Open Charge Types At least one active charge type was changed more than one minute after it was created, or someone clicked Looks right to me. Check what your website says Open Manage Content Someone clicked Looks right to me. Editing the pages does not mark this step done on its own. Your email is configured Open Settings Always done. Email sending is set up when your system is built. The step is there so you can check where customer replies go.

These are your registration numbers, not tax rates

The GST, QST and NIR numbers are your own registration numbers, printed on every invoice and proof of delivery. The tax rates are already set. The What we found line names whichever numbers are still blank, for example QST and NIR numbers are still blank.

The fuel surcharge does not carry forward

The fuel step checks the current month only. At the start of each month the step goes back to not done until you add that month's rate. Without a rate, orders are built with no fuel charge. See Fuel Surcharge.

Check your charge types counts only active charge types, and leaves out any charge type set as Use as default for: Fuel Surcharge (the monthly fuel rates). Editing a fuel rate therefore does not complete this step.

docs.title: Stage 5 — Your first invoice
docs.text:
Step Button Done when Create your first order Open Orders At least one order exists. Dispatch it to your driver Open Dispatch At least one order has a driver (mobile user) assigned. Invoice it and email it to yourself Open Invoices At least one invoice exists.

When you create the order, watch the price appear as you choose the delivery address. If it shows $0.00, go back to Stage 1. See Orders, Dispatch and Creating Invoices.

Your first invoice changes the checklist's wording

As soon as one invoice exists, the menu label changes from Getting started to Setup check, and the page title changes to What is still not set up. The steps and rules stay the same.

docs.title: Stage 6 — Tell us how it went
docs.text:
Step Button Done when Send us a note when you are done Open Feedback At least one Feedback note exists in your system, sent by any user.

Open Feedback opens the same Feedback form as the Feedback button in the bar at the top of every page.

docs.title: Looks right to me
docs.text:
Two steps start with pre-filled content, so there is no blank value for the checklist to detect:

  • Check your charge types
  • Check what your website says

If you have reviewed them and they are fine as they are, click Looks right to me in the panel.

  1. Select the step in the list.
  2. Review the page behind the button (Open Charge Types or Open Manage Content).
  3. Back on the checklist, click Looks right to me.
  4. A confirmation asks: Mark "step name" as checked? You can still change anything on that page later.
  5. Click Yes, it looks right (or Cancel).

The step is marked Done, the next step becomes Do this next, and the step list, progress bar and summary update without reloading the page. The menu entry updates on the next page you open. The panel then shows Confirmed time ago, for example Confirmed 3 minutes ago. What we found reads N charges, confirmed as they are or N pages, confirmed as they are.

The button only shows while the step is not done. On Check your charge types, if you have already edited a charge type, the step is done and the button does not appear.

If the confirmation cannot be saved, this message appears next to the button: Could not save that. Nothing was changed - tell us if it keeps happening.

Confirmations apply to the whole system

A confirmation is saved once for your whole system, not per user or per office. There is no button to undo it.

docs.title: I finished a step but the menu still shows the old count
docs.text:
Solution

The menu entry can take up to 5 minutes to update. Open the checklist page: it is always up to date. The menu catches up within 5 minutes, or on the next page you open after saving the Application Settings page or clicking Looks right to me.

docs.title: I get "You do not have access to the setup checklist."
docs.text:
Solution

The checklist is for Admin and Manager users only. Ask an Admin to check the step for you, or to change your role. See User Roles.

docs.title: As a Manager, I cannot open Settings or Manage Content from the checklist
docs.text:
Solution

Settings and Manage Content are Admin-only pages. Ask an Admin to add the GST, QST and NIR numbers. For Check what your website says, you can click Looks right to me if the website text is correct, or ask an Admin to edit it.

docs.title: "Set the price of each zone" says Done · check
docs.text:
Solution

At least one zone is priced, but other active zones are still at $0.00 and will invoice for nothing. Open Zones, price the zones you deliver into, and disable the ones you do not use.

docs.title: The counts include another office's data
docs.text:
Solution

This is expected. The checklist asks whether the whole system is ready to invoice, so it counts every office, not just the one you are working in. See Multi-Office.

docs.title: "Set this month's fuel surcharge" was done last month and is open again
docs.text:
Solution

The step checks the current month only. Add this month's rate on the Fuel Schedule page. See Fuel Surcharge.

docs.title: I edited my website pages but "Check what your website says" is still open
docs.text:
Solution

This step is only marked done when someone clicks Looks right to me. Editing the pages does not complete it.

docs.title: The checklist entry is missing from my menu
docs.text:
Solution

The entry only shows for Admin and Manager users. If you are an Admin or Manager and the entry is missing, reload the page. If it is still missing, contact UTX support through Feedback.

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
Getting the most out of the checklist

  • Work from top to bottom. Do this next always points at the most important open step.
  • Do Stage 1 first. An order in an unpriced zone or a shipper with no city invoices at $0.00, and nothing else warns you.
  • Disable the zones, terminals and charge types you never use. They stop being counted and leave the dropdowns.
  • Email your first invoice to yourself, not to the customer, and check what arrives.
  • Check the checklist at the start of each month if you use the fuel surcharge add-on.

docs.title: Shippers & Receivers
docs.text: Keep a reusable address book of the pickup and delivery locations used on your orders, and link a location to a customer account for read-only portal visibility.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
A Shipper / Receiver is a pickup or delivery location: a company name, an address, a city and contact details. It is not the customer who pays for the order. Customers are managed separately in Managing Customers.

  • Address book for orders. On the order form, the Search for a shipper / receiver field looks up saved records and fills the address fields for you.
  • Built automatically. When you create an order on the order form with a pickup or delivery company name, UTX Freight creates a new Shipper / Receiver record or updates the matching one.
  • Linked to a city and zone. The City (Must exist) field links the record to a city from your city list. The Zone shown in the list comes from that city.
  • Consignee portal link. You can link a Shipper / Receiver to a customer account. That customer's users then get read-only visibility of orders delivered to this location.
  • Active or disabled. Only active shippers/receivers appear in orders.
  • Delete only when unused. You can delete a record only if no order uses it.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
1. Click Shipper / Receiver in the left menu.
  2. Click Add a new Shipper / Receiver at the top right.
  3. Enter the Company Name and choose the Office.
  4. Enter the Address, choose a city in City (Must exist) and enter the Postal Code.
  5. Optionally fill in Contact Info, Email and Comments.
  6. Click Save Changes.

You rarely need to add records by hand

Each new order created on the order form with a pickup or delivery company name adds that location to the list. Creating records by hand is mostly useful for setting up the City, Comments or Linked Customer Account before the first order.

docs.title: Access & Permissions
docs.text:
Role Access Level Admin Full access: create, edit, disable/enable, delete, view history and Export Manager Create, edit, disable/enable, delete and view history. No export Dispatch Create, edit, disable/enable, delete and view history. No export Customer Service Same as Dispatch Accountant No access to the Shipper / Receiver list Warehouse / Garage No access Customer No access to the list. Customer users linked through a consignee link can view the matching orders (see Consignee Links)

When your account has multi-office turned on (ask UTX support), Shipper / Receiver records are shared across offices: the list shows the records of every office and anyone with access can manage them. When multi-office is off, the list shows the shippers/receivers of the office you are working in, and Managers and Dispatch users can only manage records that belong to their own offices. See Multi-Office.

How to get there:

  • Click Shipper / Receiver in the left menu, or
  • Open the user menu at the top right and click Manage Clients.

Both links open the same page, titled Shipper / Receiver.

docs.title: Filters
docs.text:
The filter buttons sit at the top left of the page.

Filter Shows All Active Active shippers/receivers (the default) Disabled Disabled shippers/receivers Linked Shippers/receivers linked to a customer account for portal visibility, active or not

All filters sort the results alphabetically by company name and show 50 records per page.

docs.title: Search
docs.text:
Type in the Filter shippers / receivers by company name or city box. The list refreshes once you have typed at least 2 characters, and it resets when you clear the box. The search matches:

  • part of the Company Name, or
  • part of the name of the linked city (the City (Must exist) value).

The search looks in active records. To find a disabled record, click Disabled and browse the list. The search matches the linked city only, not the old free-text city of records shown in red (see below).

docs.title: Columns
docs.text: Column Description Company Name Shown in green when the record is active and in red when it is disabled Zone Zone of the linked city, shown as a badge. Shows N/A when the record has no city or the city has no zone Address Street address Zip Postal code City City name Country Country of the linked city (for example CA or US) Code Location code of the linked city Contact info Contact name or phone Email Email address Comments The first 25 characters of the comments Orders Number of orders that use this record as pickup company or delivery company Linked Account Name of the linked customer account with a badge, or — if there is none Active Whether the record is active (no heading) Actions button with a menu: Edit, View History, Disable / Enable and Delete

docs.title: Colour Guide
docs.text:
Colour Meaning Green City / Country / Code The record is linked to a city from your city list Red City / Country (Code empty) The record has no linked city and still uses the old free-text city and country Green Company Name Active Red Company Name Disabled

Fix records with a red City or Country

The notice at the top of the list says it: any City or Country in RED is not using the normalized UN Location and should be updated. Edit the Shipper / Receiver, choose a city in City (Must exist), and click Save Changes. Until you do, the record has no zone (N/A).

docs.title: Adding or Editing a Shipper / Receiver
docs.text:
• To add: click Add a new Shipper / Receiver at the top right of the list.
  • To edit: open the Actions menu on the row and click Edit.

The form opens on its own page (New Shipper / Receiver or Edit Shipper / Receiver). Click Save Changes to save, or Cancel to return to the list.

docs.title: Shipper / Receiver Information
docs.text: Field Description Company Name Required. Leading and trailing spaces are removed when you save Office Required. The office the record belongs to. The list contains the offices assigned to you Address Street address City (Must exist) Choose a city from the active cities of the current office (of all offices when multi-office is on). The city must already exist. Add it first in Zones & Cities if it is missing. The city sets the Zone and Code shown in the list Postal Code Postal or ZIP code Contact Info Contact name, phone or other details Email Email address Comments The comments show up when you create an order. When you pick this record with the order form search, the comments are copied into the address Comments field

docs.title: Portal Access — Consignee Link
docs.text:
Field Description Linked Customer Account Choose an active customer account, or — No linked account —

Linking a shipper/receiver to a Customer account gives that customer's users read-only visibility into all orders delivered to this location, even orders created for other customers (for example, other freight forwarders). See Consignee Links below.

docs.title: Shipper / Receiver visibility
docs.text: Field Description Active Only active shippers/receivers appear in orders

docs.title: System update note
docs.text: This section shows the old City and Country fields. They are read-only and cannot be edited. The note explains that city and country are deprecated and should be set with the City (Must exist) field instead, so that city names and the rates per city stay consistent.

docs.title: Consignee Links
docs.text:
A consignee link lets a customer see the deliveries made to their location, for example a warehouse that receives containers booked by several freight forwarders.

How it works:

  1. Edit the Shipper / Receiver that is the delivery location.
  2. In Portal Access — Consignee Link, choose the customer in Linked Customer Account.
  3. Click Save Changes.

From then on, users of that customer account can:

  • view (read only) every order whose delivery company is this Shipper / Receiver, including orders placed by other customers, and
  • open the documents attached to those orders.

They cannot edit these orders. Pricing is never shown to linked users.

Delivery only

The link applies to orders where this record is the delivery company. Orders where it is only the pickup company are not shared with the linked customer.

Find all linked locations

Use the Linked filter to list every Shipper / Receiver linked to a customer account. You can link several locations to the same customer.

If the customer account is deleted

Deleting a customer account removes the link from its shippers/receivers. The Shipper / Receiver records stay.

For what customers see in the portal, see Customer Portal.

docs.title: Automatic Creation from Orders
docs.text:
You don't need to add every location by hand. When an order is created on the order form (saved for the first time):

  • If the order has a delivery company name, UTX Freight looks for a matching Shipper / Receiver and links it to the order as the delivery company.
  • If the order has a pickup company name, it does the same for the pickup company.

What counts as a match:

Setup A record matches when Single office Same company name (exact), same office and same address Multi-office Same company name (not case sensitive) and same address, in any office

When a match is found, the record is updated with the values from the order. Only the fields that are filled in on the order are copied: address, city, postal code, contact, email (delivery only) and office. Blank order fields do not erase existing values. Comments, Active and Linked Customer Account are never changed by an order.

When no match is found, a new record is created with the company name, address, city, postal code, contact info and office from the order. Delivery locations also get the delivery email. Pickup locations have no email.

Small differences create duplicates

A different spelling of the address (for example 123 Main St vs 123 Main Street) creates a second record. To avoid duplicates, use the Search for a shipper / receiver field on the order form instead of typing the address by hand.

Editing an order does not update the list

Records are created or updated only when an order is created on the order form. Saving changes to an existing order does not create or update Shipper / Receiver records. Orders saved from the Auto Orders review window do not create records either: the delivery company is chosen from the existing list there.

docs.title: Using Shippers & Receivers on the Order Form
docs.text:
On a new order, the Pick Up Address and Delivery Address sections each have a Search for a shipper / receiver field: "Type the name of a previously used shipper / receiver in an order to automatically fill the following fields."

  1. Type at least 2 characters of the company name or the city.
  2. Pick a suggestion. Each suggestion shows the company name, address, city and province, and the contact info in brackets.
  3. The fields below fill in automatically:
Order field Pick Up Address Delivery Address Name Address City Zip Contact Email — Comments (from the record's comments)

If the record has no linked city, the City field is left empty. The record's comments replace whatever was already in Comments.

The search only suggests active shippers/receivers of the current office (of all offices when multi-office is on).

When you edit an existing order, the pickup and delivery company are chosen from a list of active shippers/receivers instead of the search field.

Adding a location while reviewing an Auto Order

In the Auto Orders review window, the New Client button under Delivery opens a short Shipper / Receiver Information form (Company Name, Office, Address, City (Must exist), Postal Code, Contact Info, Email). Click Create to add the record, then choose it as the delivery company.

See Order Form for the rest of the order fields.

docs.title: Disabling and Enabling
docs.text:
Disable a location you no longer use so it stops appearing in orders, without losing its history.

  1. Find the record in the list.
  2. Open the Actions menu and click Disable.

The row updates right away. Use the Disabled filter to find it again and click Enable to bring it back. You can also change the Active checkbox in the form.

Disabling a record does not change existing orders.

docs.title: Deleting a Shipper / Receiver
docs.text:
You can delete a record only if no order uses it, as pickup company or as delivery company. The Delete action appears in the Actions menu only when the Orders column shows 0.

  1. Open the Actions menu on the row.
  2. Click Delete.
  3. Confirm with Are you sure?

Deleting cannot be undone

For a location that has orders, use Disable instead. Disabled records keep their order history and can be enabled again.

docs.title: Viewing History
docs.text: Every change to a Shipper / Receiver is recorded. Open the Actions menu and click View History to see who changed which fields and when, including changes made automatically when orders were created.

docs.title: Exporting to CSV
docs.text:
Admin only. Click the green Export button at the top right of the list to download a CSV file.

The export:

  • contains only shippers/receivers used as the delivery company on orders created in the last 12 months,
  • does not apply the filter or search you have on screen,
  • includes records from all offices,
  • is sorted by company name.
CSV column Content Id Internal record ID Company name Company name Zone name Zone of the linked city, or N/A Address Street address Zip Postal code City name Linked city name, or the old free-text city if there is no linked city Country name Country of the linked city, or the old free-text country Contact info Contact info Active true or false

The file name includes the date, for example ...-shippers-receivers-2026-10-10.csv. For other exports, see Data Exports.

Records missing from the export?

Shippers/receivers used only as a pickup company, or not used on any order in the last 12 months, are not in the export, even if they are active.

docs.title: A shipper/receiver does not appear in the order form search
docs.text:
Solution

Check these in order:

  1. The record may be disabled. Use the Disabled filter and click Enable.
  2. You must type at least 2 characters of the company name or of the linked city name.
  3. When multi-office is off, the search shows records of the current office only. Switch to the right office, or check the Office field of the record.

docs.title: There is no Delete option for a record
docs.text:
Solution

Delete only appears when no order uses the record (the Orders column shows 0). Use Disable instead to hide it from new orders.

docs.title: The Zone column shows N/A
docs.text:
Solution

The record has no city in City (Must exist), or that city is not assigned to a zone. Edit the record and choose a city. If the city has no zone, assign one in Zones & Cities.

docs.title: The city I need is not in the City (Must exist) list
docs.text:
Solution

The list shows only active cities of the current office (of all offices when multi-office is on). Add or enable the city in Zones & Cities, then edit the Shipper / Receiver again.

docs.title: The same location appears twice
docs.text:
Solution

Orders with a slightly different company name or address create a new record. Disable the duplicate you don't want, or delete it if its Orders count is 0. Next time, pick the location with Search for a shipper / receiver on the order form.

docs.title: I can't see the Export button
docs.text:
Solution

Export is available to the Admin role only.

docs.title: A linked customer can't see an order
docs.text:
Solution

The customer only sees orders whose delivery company is the linked Shipper / Receiver. Check the order's delivery company. If the order was typed with a different name or address, it may be linked to another (duplicate) record. Link that record too, or correct the order.

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
Keep your address book clean

  • Always set City (Must exist) so every location has a zone. Fix the records shown in red.
  • Use Search for a shipper / receiver on new orders instead of retyping addresses, to avoid duplicates.
  • Put dock hours, appointment rules or gate instructions in Comments. They are copied into the order when you pick the location.
  • Disable locations you no longer use instead of deleting them.
  • Review the Linked filter from time to time to make sure each consignee link still points to the right customer.

docs.title: Bulk Tracking Updates (CN & Port Tracking)
docs.text: Compare the ETA, Last Free Day and weight of all your in-progress container orders against CN Rail or the Montreal port terminals, and update them in one click from the Dispatch board.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The CN Tracking and Port Tracking buttons on the Dispatch board open a bulk update window. Instead of checking containers one by one (see Container Tracking), you see every in-progress order for that source side by side with what the railway or terminal reports, and you copy the new values onto the orders with Update Selected.

At a glance:

  • CN Tracking -- asks CN live for the status of your containers each time you open it. Window title: Shipments Tracking for Canadian National.
  • Port Tracking -- reads the tracking data the app has already stored for Termont (Port of Montreal) and MGT (Racine/Cast). Window title: Shipments Tracking for Port of Montreal (this covers both Termont and MGT containers).
  • Side-by-side comparison -- for ETA, LFD and Weight, a check mark means the order already matches; an arrow (->) points to the new value from the source.
  • Update Selected -- overwrites ETA, LFD and weight on the checked orders. Port Tracking also fills in a blank seal number and steamship line.
  • No information table -- lists New orders for that source that the railway/terminal returned nothing for.
  • Current office only -- with multiple offices, only the orders of the office you are working in are listed.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
1. From the left menu, click Dispatch.
  2. Click CN Tracking or Port Tracking (the button shows Loading while the data is gathered).
  3. Review the table. Rows with a red value and an arrow (->) have something to update.
  4. Uncheck any order you do not want to change (all rows are checked by default).
  5. Click Update Selected.
  6. The window closes, an Updated message appears at the top of the screen, and the changed orders refresh on the board.

docs.title: Access & Permissions
docs.text:
The buttons live on the Dispatch board, so the same roles apply.

Role Access Admin Full access Manager Full access Dispatch Full access Customer Service Same as Dispatch Accountant, Customer, Driver, other roles No access -- they cannot open the Dispatch board

Which buttons you see depends on your company's add-ons:

Button Shown when Opens CN Tracking CN tracking add-on is enabled Shipments Tracking for Canadian National Port Tracking Port of Montreal (Termont) or MGT (Racine/Cast) tracking add-on is enabled Shipments Tracking for Port of Montreal

If an add-on is not enabled, its button's spot in the header is left empty.

How to get there:

  • Dispatch CN Tracking or Port Tracking (header buttons, to the right of the status buttons)

docs.title: Which Orders Are Included
docs.text:
Both windows start from your in-progress orders -- status New, App. Made or Dispatched -- created on or after the Order Archive Cutoff Date in Settings, then keep only those whose pickup terminal belongs to the source:

Window Orders included Where the data comes from CN Tracking Pickup terminal is a CN terminal A live request to CN for those container numbers, made when you open the window Port Tracking Pickup terminal is a Termont, Racine or Cast terminal Tracking data already stored in the app from the automatic Termont and MGT checks (see Container Tracking)

With multiple offices, the list is then limited to the office you are currently working in.

Each order then goes into one of two tables:

  • Main table -- the source returned data for the order's container.
  • No information table -- the source returned nothing for it (see No Information Table).

CN: up to 200 containers per request

Each time you open CN Tracking, CN is asked about up to 200 containers.

Port Tracking is as fresh as the last automatic check

Port Tracking does not contact the terminals when you open it. It shows what the app stored during its last automatic check, so a container that just changed at the terminal may not be reflected yet.

docs.title: The Main Table
docs.text: The heading shows a green badge with the number of orders found, followed by the source name (Canadian National or Port of Montreal).

docs.title: Columns
docs.text: Column What it shows (checkbox) Whether the order is included in Update Selected. All rows are checked when the window opens. The checkbox in the header checks or unchecks every row. Order The order status icon (hover for New Order, Appointment Made or Order Dispatched) and the order reference number Container Container number ETA The order's ETA date compared with the source's ETA LFD The order's Last Free Day compared with the source's Last Free Day Weight The order's weight compared with the source's weight Terminal Port Tracking only. The terminal section the container is at Customs Port Tracking only. The customs description from the terminal Status CN: the CN event name (hover for its full description). Port: a status badge (see below)

docs.title: How values are compared
docs.text:
The ETA, LFD and Weight cells show the order's current value first:

What you see Meaning Changed by Update Selected? Green value + The order already matches the source No Red value -> green value The order differs from the source. The green value is the new one Yes Red N/A -> green value The order has no value; the source has one Yes -- the field is filled in Value -> red N/A The source has no value No -- the order keeps its value Red N/A -> red N/A Neither side has a value No Not Available (orange, Weight column) The source reported a weight of 0 No -- the order weight is left alone

How each field is compared:

  • ETA and LFD are compared by calendar day only (time of day is ignored).
  • Weight is compared as exact text: the source value is written as the number followed by its unit, e.g. 24000 KG. If the order says 24000 kgs or 24,000 KG, it counts as different and will be overwritten with the source's format.
    • CN: the net weight and the unit CN reports.
    • Port: the gross weight reported by the terminal, always with the unit KG.
  • CN ETA: the CN ETA is only used when CN gives it for the Montreal (Taschereau) yard. An ETA for any other location is ignored, and the ETA column shows N/A on the right side.

docs.title: Port status and customs badges
docs.text:
Badge Meaning Ready (green) The terminal reports the container is available for pickup In Terminal (blue) The container is in the terminal but not yet available for pickup Departed (grey) The container has left the terminal Any other text, or Unknown (grey) The terminal's own visit state, or nothing reported

The Customs column shows the terminal's customs text in green when it contains "release", in orange otherwise, and a grey N/A when the terminal reported nothing.

docs.title: Sort order
docs.text: Window Sort order CN Tracking By CN event, in CN's event code order: De-ramped first, then Arrival Transit Location, Bad Order, Motor Carrier Arrival, Arrival at Destination, and so on through Ramped, Released, etc. Port Tracking Ready first, then In Terminal, then Departed, then everything else

docs.title: Step-by-step: Update orders from tracking data
docs.text:
1. Open CN Tracking or Port Tracking from the Dispatch board.
  2. Look for red values with an arrow (->) -- those are the fields that will change.
  3. Uncheck any row you want to leave untouched. Unchecked rows are not sent at all.
  4. Click Update Selected (it shows Updating while saving).
  5. The window closes and a message appears at the top of the screen. Orders that were changed refresh on the board.

docs.title: What gets changed
docs.text:
For every checked row, only fields that differ are sent:

Order field CN Tracking Port Tracking ETA date Overwritten with the source ETA when it differs Overwritten with the source ETA when it differs Last Free Day (LFD) Overwritten when it differs Overwritten when it differs Weight Overwritten when it differs (not when the source says 0) Overwritten when it differs (not when the source says 0) Seal number Not changed Filled in only if the order's seal number is blank and the terminal has one Steamship line Not changed Filled in only if the order's steamship line is blank and the terminal has one

Rows where nothing differs are skipped, even if checked.

Seal number and steamship line

The Port Tracking table has no seal or steamship line column. If the order has those fields blank and the terminal knows them, Update Selected fills them in. Existing values are never overwritten.

Update Selected overwrites what you typed

ETA, LFD and weight are replaced by the source value for every checked row that differs -- including dates or weights you entered by hand on purpose. Uncheck those rows before clicking Update Selected. There is no undo.

docs.title: Messages
docs.text:
Message When Updated -- Orders were updated! (green) The save went through. This also appears when no row had anything to change Update Failed -- Errors were encountered while updating orders. Please verify the result on 'Track and Trace' page (red) An order could not be saved

Check the result

Orders are saved one at a time. To confirm what was saved, reopen the window: rows that still show an arrow were not updated.

docs.title: No Information Table
docs.text:
Below the main table, a second heading shows a red badge and Canadian National - No information currently available (or Port of Montreal - No information currently available).

It lists orders for that source that the railway or terminal returned no data for -- for example, the container has not reached the rail network or terminal yet, or the container number is mistyped.

Column What it shows Status Order status icon Order Order reference number -- a link that opens the Orders list searched for that order, in a new tab Container Container number Delivery Date The order's delivery date Message No information returned from Canadian National (or Port of Montreal) Last Status The last CN event name stored by the app for this container (for example Ramped), if any. Usually blank for port containers Received At The time of that stored CN event, if any. Blank for port containers

Only New orders are listed

The table lists only orders with status New. App. Made and Dispatched orders are not listed, as the note at the top of the table says. Orders whose container number is blank or N/A are also left out.

Orders in this table cannot be updated -- there is nothing to copy. Check the container number on the order, or wait for the source to report the container.

docs.title: Alerts Panel (Port Tracking only)
docs.text:
When there are unread Termont or MGT alerts, the Port Tracking window opens with an orange panel at the top headed with the number of alerts shown (for example 1 Alert or 3 Alerts). It shows up to the 10 most recent unread port alerts: an icon for the alert type, the container number, the alert message and how long ago it was raised.

Icon Alert type Ready for pickup Customs released Last Free Day approaching Departed

Opening Port Tracking marks these alerts as read -- for everyone

As soon as the panel is displayed, the alerts shown in it are marked read for the whole company, not just for you. They disappear from the unread count on the Alerts button and from the unread alerts for every other user.

The alerts themselves are not deleted -- you can still find them on the Container Alerts page, whose list covers the last 90 days.

CN alerts are never shown in this panel, and the CN Tracking window has no alerts panel.

docs.title: I don't see the CN Tracking or Port Tracking button
docs.text:
Solution

Each button only appears when the matching tracking add-on is enabled for your company (CN for CN Tracking; Termont or MGT for Port Tracking). You also need access to the Dispatch board (Admin, Manager, Dispatch or Customer Service). Ask UTX support if the add-on should be turned on.

docs.title: An order is missing from both tables
docs.text:
Solution

Check that:

  • The order status is New, App. Made or Dispatched (Completed orders are never included).
  • The order's pickup terminal is a CN terminal (CN Tracking) or a Termont, Racine or Cast terminal (Port Tracking).
  • With multiple offices, you are working in the order's office.
  • The order was created on or after the Order Archive Cutoff Date in Settings.

An App. Made or Dispatched order with no tracking data is not listed in the no information table.

docs.title: The weight keeps showing as different
docs.text:
Solution

Weight is compared as exact text, including the unit. 24000 KG and 24000 kgs are treated as different. Click Update Selected once to store the source's format; after that the row shows a check mark.

docs.title: Port Tracking shows old information
docs.text:
Solution

Port Tracking uses data stored by the automatic terminal checks, not a live lookup. Wait for the next check. The container's own tracking popup on the order row reads the same stored data, and its Updated ... ago line shows when that container was last refreshed (see Container Tracking).

docs.title: My port alerts disappeared from the Alerts badge
docs.text:
Solution

Someone (possibly you) opened Port Tracking, which marks the alerts shown in its panel as read for everyone. Review them on the Container Alerts page.

docs.title: I got "Update Failed"
docs.text:
Solution

Some orders may have saved and others not. Reopen the window: any row still showing a red value and an arrow was not updated. Open that order and save the field by hand to see what needs fixing.

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
Best Practices

  • Scan before you click. Uncheck rows where you entered an ETA, LFD or weight by hand that you want to keep.
  • Use CN Tracking at the start of the day to pick up CN ETA and LFD changes in one pass instead of order by order.
  • Read the Port alerts panel when it appears -- once displayed, those alerts are marked read for the whole team.
  • Work the no information table. A New order that stays there for days often has a mistyped container number.

docs.title: User Roles & Permissions
docs.text: Every UTX Freight user has exactly one role. The role decides which menus you see, which pages you can open and what you can change on them.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
• There are two kinds of users:
    • Web users sign in with an email and password. Their roles are Admin, Manager, Dispatch, Customer Service, Accountant, Customer, Warehouse and Garage. They are people under a company on the Customers page.
    • Mobile users sign in on a phone with an Access Code or a login link. Their roles are Driver, Broker and Yard Worker. They are set up under Mobile Users, not on the Customers page. See Mobile Users.
  • Admin can do everything. Manager is close, but it is not the same as Admin, even on an account with a single office. See What a Manager cannot do.
  • Customer Service has exactly the same permissions as Dispatch. The only visible difference is one column on the Orders list.
  • A Customer becomes a consignee when their company is linked to one or more shipper/receiver records. They then also see, read-only, deliveries addressed to those records.
  • Some permissions depend on edition options that UTX sets for your account (for example, whether Managers can see Reports). You can't change these in the app. See Edition options.
  • Dispatchers have one per-user option, Can manage rates?, which is on by default.
  • Orders, invoices and checks always belong to an office. Most users only work with the offices they are assigned to. See Offices and permissions.
  • If you open a page your role can't use, nothing is changed and you are sent back. See When access is denied.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
To give a staff member a role (Admin only):

  1. Go to Customers and select your own company (the default filter).
  2. In the Your Company: box, click Add Person and invite the person. Every new person starts with the Customer role.
  3. Click Edit Person on the new row.
  4. Pick the Role and check the Offices the person works in.
  5. Click Save Changes.
  6. For a Dispatch or Customer Service user, open Edit Person again and check or uncheck Can manage rates?, then Save Changes.

For drivers, brokers and yard workers, use Mobile Users Drivers, Brokers & Yard instead. See Mobile Users.

docs.title: Access & Permissions
docs.text:
Who can change roles and user settings:

Role What they can do with users Admin Only role that can set or change a Role, Company, Offices and Can manage rates?. Adds, edits and deletes any person Manager Adds (invites) and edits customer people of the offices they belong to. Can delete people. Cannot change anyone's Role, Company or Offices Dispatch / Customer Service Adds and edits customer people only when your account has dispatch customer management turned on (an edition option set by UTX, off by default). Cannot delete people or change roles Accountant, Customer Edit their own details only, with Edit Profile Warehouse, Garage No access to people, including their own profile. An Admin updates their details Admin, Manager, Dispatch, Customer Service Add, edit, enable and disable mobile users (drivers, brokers, yard workers) and pick their role

If someone who is not an Admin sends a role, company or office change anyway, UTX Freight ignores it.

How to get there:

  • Customers > company box > Edit Person (staff and customer people)
  • Your name in the top bar > Edit Profile (your own details, for users who are not Admin or Manager)
  • Mobile Users > Drivers, Brokers & Yard (mobile users)

See People & Invitations for the full person form.

docs.title: The Roles at a Glance
docs.text: Role Kind In one sentence Admin Web Full access to everything, including Settings, website content, offices and exports Manager Web Runs the offices they belong to: orders, dispatch, invoices, customers, rates and most lists. No Settings, content, offices or exports Dispatch Web Day-to-day operations: orders, dispatch board, drivers, equipment, shippers/receivers. Rates and some lists depend on options Customer Service Web Same permissions as Dispatch Accountant Web Invoices, checks, taxes, charge and expense types, and (by default) full order management, in their offices Customer Web Sees their company's orders. Creates and edits new orders only when the edition allows it Customer (consignee) Web A Customer whose company is linked to shipper/receiver records. Also sees deliveries addressed to them, read-only Warehouse Web The Warehouse module only (Warehouse add-on) Garage Web The Garage module only (Garage add-on) Driver Mobile Sees and completes only the orders assigned to them Broker Mobile Same mobile rights as a Driver Yard Worker Mobile Container search and the yard buttons on a phone

docs.title: Admin
docs.text:
• Can open every page and do every action in the app.
  • Only Admins open Settings, Manage Content and Manage Offices, manage Alert Email Subscriptions, mark container alerts read, and use the CSV Export buttons.
  • Only Admins assign roles, offices and Can manage rates?.
  • On Manage Content and Manage Offices, Admins edit what exists. New website pages and new offices are added by UTX.
  • An Admin still works in one office at a time. The Orders, Invoices and Checks lists show the office you are currently in. See Multi-Office.

docs.title: Manager
docs.text:
A Manager has full access to orders, the dispatch board, invoices, customers and most lists for the offices they belong to.

What a Manager can do, in their offices:

  • Create, edit, dispatch, complete, reset, duplicate, delete and transfer orders, view order history, and edit rates, charges, expenses and legs on orders.
  • Use the Dispatch board, including Email POD and driver login links.
  • Manage Invoices, Customers (including deleting customers and people), Shipper / Receiver, Mobile Users and Equipments.
  • Manage Charge Types, Expense Types, Manage Taxes, Manage Brokers, Manage Cities, Manage Zones, Manage Terminals, Manage Container Statuses, Manage Document Types, Manage Equipment Types and Manage Move Locations.
  • Use Auto Orders (add-on) and the setup checklist (Getting started).
  • Open the Garage when the Garage add-on is on.
  • Receive the New Order email (as CC) for orders of their office, and the Invoicing Reminder (Monday, Wednesday and Friday).

docs.title: What a Manager cannot do
docs.text:
These are Admin-only, whatever the number of offices:

Not available to Managers Notes Settings See Application Settings Manage Content (website content) Not in the Manager's menu. See Website Content Manage Offices Not in the Manager's menu Manage Steamship Lines, Manage Container Sizes Not in the Manager's menu. See Lookup Lists Export buttons (Orders, Customers, Shipper / Receiver, Equipments) Hidden. See Data Exports Alert Email Subscriptions and marking container alerts read or unread Managers can view the alerts page but not change read status. See Container Alerts Changing a person's Role, Company or Offices, or Can manage rates? Only Admins see those fields Expenses page (left menu) Admin only. Managers still add expenses on orders Warehouse module Only Admin and Warehouse users. See Warehouse Overview

Two more Manager permissions depend on edition options:

  • Reports (including Aged Receivables (AR) and AR Export): only when manager access to Reports is turned on for your account (on by default).
  • Checks: only when manager access to Checks is turned on for your account (on by default).

docs.title: Dispatch and  Customer Service
docs.text:
Dispatch and Customer Service have the same permissions. Use whichever name fits the person's job.

What they can do, in their offices:

  • Create, edit, dispatch, complete, reset, duplicate, delete and transfer orders, and place orders on behalf of any customer.
  • Use the Dispatch board, Email POD and driver login links.
  • Manage Shipper / Receiver, Mobile Users (drivers, brokers, yard workers), Equipments, Manage Equipment Types and Manage Move Locations.
  • View (not change) Manage Container Statuses.
  • Use Auto Orders (add-on).

What depends on Can manage rates? (per user, on by default):

With Can manage rates? on With it off Rate, charge and expense sections on orders Hidden Order Legs on the full Edit Order form Hidden (the Order Legs section of Quick Edit is still shown) Charge Types, Expense Types, Manage Cities (and Fuel Schedule with the add-on) Not available View History (order audit) Not available

What depends on edition options:

  • Customers (and adding/editing customer people): only when dispatch customer management is turned on for your account (off by default). Even then, Dispatch can't delete customers or people.
  • Manage Terminals: only when dispatch terminal management is turned on for your account (off by default).

Never available to Dispatch or Customer Service: Invoices, Checks, Expenses page, Manage Taxes, Manage Zones, Manage Brokers, Manage Document Types, Manage Steamship Lines, Manage Container Sizes, Reports, Settings, the setup checklist, Garage and Warehouse.

The one difference: the Invoiced / Rate column

On the Orders list, Customer Service users see the Invoiced / Rate column (the order total), but without the button that opens the order's invoice. Dispatch users don't see that column at all. Everything else is identical.

docs.title: Accountant
docs.text:
Accountants work only with the offices they belong to.

  • Invoices: full access.
  • Checks: only when accountant access to Checks is turned on for your account (on by default).
  • Charge Types, Expense Types and Manage Taxes: full access. Fuel Schedule with the Fuel Surcharge add-on.
  • Orders, with accountant order management on (the default): full order management. Create, edit, change status, reset, go back one step, duplicate, delete, transfer between offices, open the scanned and signed POD files and View History.
  • Orders, with accountant order management off: view orders, plus edit and Complete orders that are Dispatched. They can't open the scanned or signed POD files.

Accountants do not have:

  • The rate, charge and expense sections of the order form (for Admin, Manager and Dispatch with Can manage rates?), the Order Legs section, or the Administrative information and Appointment Information sections of Edit Order (Admin, Manager, Dispatch). See Order Rates, Charges & Expenses.
  • Place the order on behalf of. An order an Accountant creates is placed under their own name.
  • Dispatch board, Email POD, the View POD link in the order menu, Customers, Shipper / Receiver, Equipments, Mobile Users, Expenses page, Reports (including AR), Settings or the setup checklist.

Accountants and aged receivables

Accountants can't open Reports, but they can use the AR Aging filter and AR aging detail export on the Invoices page. See Aged Receivables.

docs.title: Customer
docs.text:
A Customer is a person under one of your customer companies. They see the customer portal. See Customer Portal.

  • Sees all orders placed by anyone in their company, in the office(s) they belong to. Not only their own.
  • Opens View Details and the scanned or signed POD documents of those orders.
  • Creates orders only when your account has customer order entry turned on (an edition option set by UTX, off by default). Even then, they can only edit an order while its status is New. Once you make an appointment or dispatch it, the order becomes read-only for them.
  • Can't change order status, duplicate, transfer, view history, or see rates, totals, invoices or drivers.
  • Uses the shipper/receiver search while filling the order form, but has no Shipper / Receiver page.
  • Edits their own details with Edit Profile.

Customer people and offices

A customer person gets the office you are working in when you invite them. Edit Person doesn't show the Offices field for people of customer companies, so invite customer people from the office whose orders they should see. A customer only sees orders of the offices they belong to.

docs.title: Consignee behaviour
docs.text: A Customer is treated as a consignee when their company is linked to one or more shipper/receiver records. On top of their company's orders, they see, read-only, every order whose delivery is addressed to a linked record, even when the order was placed by another customer. The Orders page shows a Consignee view: banner and pricing is not shown. Linking is done on the shipper/receiver, with the Linked Customer Account field. See Shippers & Receivers and Customer Portal.

docs.title: Warehouse
docs.text:
• Only offered in the Role list when the Warehouse add-on is on.
  • Full access to the Warehouse module: Orders, Product, Location, Charges, Unit of Measure and Building. Also Charge Types (and Fuel Schedule with the add-on).
  • No freight Orders, Dispatch, Invoices, Customers or other freight pages.
  • Can't open their own Edit Profile.

See Warehouse Overview.

docs.title: Garage
docs.text:
• Only offered in the Role list when the Garage add-on is on, and only has permissions while the add-on is on.
  • Full access to every Garage page (Work Orders, Invoices and payments, Equipment, Parts, Templates, Customers, Taxes, Settings and Reports) for the offices they belong to.
  • No freight pages and no Edit Profile.

See Garage Overview.

docs.title: Driver and  Broker
docs.text:
Drivers and Brokers are mobile users, not web users. They don't have an email and password and are not people on the Customers page.

  • They sign in on a phone with their Access Code (5 to 16 characters, set on the mobile user), or with a login link copied by dispatch (Driver Login Links add-on). See Mobile Users and Driver Login Links.
  • They see only the orders assigned to them (as delivery or return driver) that are Dispatched. Orders marked Returned to terminal drop off their list.
  • On those orders they can open the details, collect the delivery and pickup signatures (POD) and mark the container returned. They can't change which driver is assigned.
  • A Broker has exactly the same mobile rights as a Driver.
  • Only active mobile users can sign in with an Access Code.

See Driver Workflow.

docs.title: Yard Worker
docs.text:
• A mobile user with the Yard Worker role, signed in with an Access Code.
  • Only has the container search and the yard buttons (Ground Container, Full at yard, Empty at yard). No order list and no POD signatures.
  • Not offered in the order driver lists.

See Yard Management.

docs.title: Web users
docs.text:
• Every new person, invited by anyone, is created with the Customer role.
  • Only an Admin can change it, from Customers > Edit Person. The Role and Offices fields only appear for people under your own company, and never for the account Owner.
  • The Role list contains Admin, Customer, Accountant, Dispatch, Manager and Customer Service, plus Warehouse with the Warehouse add-on and Garage with the Garage add-on.
  • To turn a customer contact into a staff member, an Admin first changes the person's Company to your own company and saves, then opens Edit Person again to set the Role and Offices.
  • Can manage rates? appears only after the role has been saved as Dispatch or Customer Service. Its note reads Specifies if this Dispatch can manage rates and charges across the app.

See Assigning Staff Roles and Offices.

docs.title: Mobile users
docs.text: Admin, Manager, Dispatch and Customer Service users pick Driver, Broker or Yard Worker in the Role field of the mobile user form. A mobile user belongs to one office. See Mobile Users.

docs.title: Edition Options (Set by UTX)
docs.text:
These options are set by UTX in your account's configuration. They apply to all users of that role at once. They are not in Settings and can't be changed from the app. Contact UTX support to change one.

Option Default What it changes Accountant order management On On: Accountants have full order management in their offices. Off: view only, plus edit and Complete on Dispatched orders Accountant access to Checks On Accountants see Checks and manage the checks of their offices Manager access to Checks On Managers see Checks and manage the checks of their offices Manager access to Reports On Managers see the Reports menu (all reports, including AR) Dispatch customer management Off Dispatch and Customer Service see Customers and can add and edit customers and customer people (not delete) Dispatch terminal management Off Dispatch and Customer Service see Manage Terminals with full access Customer order entry Off Customers can Create a new order and edit orders still New

The defaults above are the standard values. Your account may have been set up differently.

Add-ons also change what roles see: Garage, Warehouse, Fuel Surcharge (Fuel Schedule), Driver Login Links, Container Tracking (container alerts), Auto Orders and multi-office. See Add-ons & Options.

The only per-user option is Can manage rates? for Dispatch and Customer Service users. It is on by default and only an Admin can change it.

docs.title: Offices and Permissions
docs.text:
• Orders, invoices and checks are always office-scoped. Managers, Dispatch, Customer Service and Accountants only see and change those of the offices they belong to. The lists show the office you are currently working in.
  • Customers see orders of the office(s) they belong to.
  • Shared lists (customers, shippers/receivers, cities, zones, terminals, brokers, document types, mobile users, equipment, equipment types, charge types, expense types, move locations):
    • Without multi-office: a user can manage the records of the offices they belong to.
    • With multi-office: these records are shared, and users who can manage them can manage records of every office.
  • Permission to manage Taxes and container statuses is not limited by office.
  • Garage records stay office-scoped for Managers and Garage users. Warehouse orders are not office-scoped.
  • Transfer to Office (multi-office only) moves an order to another office you belong to. An invoiced order can't be transferred.
  • With multi-office, users who belong to more than one office switch office from the top bar. Admins only switch between the offices they are assigned to.

See Multi-Office.
