docs.text:
How to read the tables:

  • Yes: always allowed. No (or —): not allowed. The menu item or button is hidden unless the cell says otherwise.
  • R: Dispatch / Customer Service with Can manage rates? on (the default).
  • Edition options are named in full. Add-ons are noted in the first column.
  • "Own offices" means the offices the user belongs to.
  • Drivers, Brokers and Yard Workers have no access to any of these web pages. See Mobile users below.

Expenses vs Expense Types

Expense Types (user menu) is the list of expense categories you pick from on an order, such as fuel or tolls. The Expenses page (left menu, Admin only) lists the actual expense lines recorded on orders across all offices. Expense lines are added on orders by users who can manage rates. See Expenses & Checks and Charge Types & Taxes.

What \"manage rates\" covers

Rates are managed in several places. Charge Types holds the order charge (rate) types. Zone rates are edited in Manage Zones, terminal rates in Manage Terminals, and city zones in Manage Cities, each with its own rules below.

See Notifications & Emails and Email Notifications.

docs.title: Deleting Users
docs.text:
• Only Admin and Manager can delete a person, from Customers > Delete on the person's row. Anyone else gets Access Denied.
  • Deleting is permanent from the app. It turns off the person's notifications and changes their stored email, so they can't sign in any more. Their orders keep their history. See Deleting a Person.
  • Active for orders off does not block sign-in. To remove someone's access, delete the person.
  • Mobile users are not deleted this way. Disable them under Mobile Users so they can't sign in. See Mobile Users.

docs.title: When Access Is Denied
docs.text:
• Menu items and buttons you can't use are hidden.
  • If you open a page your role doesn't allow (for example from a bookmark or a typed address), UTX Freight cancels the action and sends you back to your starting page with an alert. Nothing is saved.
  • Some pages redirect instead: opening Dispatch without access sends you to Orders, and opening the setup checklist shows You do not have access to the setup checklist.
  • Pages of an add-on that is off redirect you, whatever your role (for example Container tracking is not enabled.).

docs.title: We have one office. Isn't a Manager the same as an Admin?
docs.text:
Solution

No. Even with one office, Managers can't open Settings, Manage Content, Manage Offices, Manage Steamship Lines or Manage Container Sizes, can't use the Export buttons, can't manage alert subscriptions or mark alerts read, and can't change roles. Reports and Checks depend on edition options. Give the Admin role to whoever needs those.

docs.title: My new dispatcher only sees customer screens
docs.text:
Solution

Every new person starts as Customer. An Admin must open Edit Person, set the Role to Dispatch (or Customer Service) and check the Offices, then save. The person must be under your own company for the Role field to appear.

docs.title: A dispatcher can't see rates, charge types or View History
docs.text:
Solution

Can manage rates? is off on their profile. An Admin opens Customers > Edit Person for that dispatcher, checks Can manage rates? and saves.

docs.title: A dispatcher can't see Customers or Manage Terminals
docs.text:
Solution

These are edition options set by UTX (dispatch customer management and dispatch terminal management), off by default. They apply to all Dispatch and Customer Service users at once. Manage Terminals also only exists on intermodal (container) accounts. Contact UTX support to turn them on.

docs.title: A Manager doesn't see Reports or Checks
docs.text:
Solution

Manager access to Reports or Checks is turned off for your account. These are edition options set by UTX. Contact UTX support.

docs.title: An accountant can only view orders
docs.text:
Solution

Accountant order management is turned off for your account. With it off, Accountants can only view orders, and edit and complete Dispatched orders. Contact UTX support to turn it on.

docs.title: An accountant can't change the rate on an order
docs.text:
Solution

That is expected. The rate, charge and expense sections of the order form are for Admin, Manager and Dispatch with Can manage rates?. Ask one of them to change the order's rate.

docs.title: A customer can't create orders
docs.text:
Solution

Customer order entry is turned off for your account (the default). Contact UTX support if your customers should create orders. When it is on, customers can only edit an order while it is New.

docs.title: A customer sees orders they didn't place
docs.text:
Solution

Customers see every order placed by anyone in their company. If their company is linked to shipper/receiver records, they also see deliveries addressed to those records (consignee view), read-only.

docs.title: Where do I set a driver's password?
docs.text:
Solution

Drivers, Brokers and Yard Workers don't have passwords. Give them their Access Code, or copy them a login link. See Mobile Users.

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
Roles

  • Keep the number of Admins small. Use Manager for office leads and Dispatch or Customer Service for operations staff.
  • Turn off Can manage rates? for dispatchers who shouldn't see or change pricing.
  • Give customer contacts a single office.
  • Set up drivers, brokers and yard workers as Mobile Users, never as people with an email and password.
  • Delete people who leave. Unchecking Active for orders doesn't stop them from signing in.

docs.title: Warehouse Orders
docs.text: Record the goods you store for a customer, the warehouse charges that apply, and the storage period, then let UTX Freight calculate the amount to bill.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
• Warehouse > Orders opens the Warehouse Orders page. It shows three counters (Open Orders, Completed, Total), filter buttons, an Orders / Products view switch and a search box. The list shows 20 orders per page.
  • A warehouse order has a customer person (Place the order on behalf of), a Storage Date, an optional Container Number, a list of warehouse charges and a list of products (product, quantity, unit of measure, location).
  • A warehouse order has two statuses: New (shown under Open) and Completed. You complete an order by entering its Closing Date. There is no way to reopen a completed order.
  • The Invoiced Rate column calculates what the order is worth: Fixed charges are added once; each Monthly charge is billed per product row as months in storage × square feet of the unit of measure × quantity × rate.
  • Each order has a Documents window where you attach files.
  • Warehouse orders are separate from freight orders. They do not appear on the Orders or Dispatch pages, and no invoice is created from them automatically. The Invoiced Rate is a calculated figure you use for billing.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
1. Click Warehouse in the left menu, then Orders.
  2. Click Create new Warehouse Order.
  3. In Place the order on behalf of, pick the customer's person.
  4. Pick the Storage Date and, if there is one, type the Container Number.
  5. Under Order Charges for Invoice Breakdown, click (+) Add another for each charge, pick it from the list and check the rate.
  6. Under Order Products, click (+) Add another for each product and fill in the product, Quantity, unit of measure and location.
  7. Click Create Order. The order appears under Open.
  8. When the goods leave the warehouse, click Complete on the order row, pick the Closing Date and click Submit. The order moves to Completed and its Invoiced Rate stops growing month by month.

docs.title: Access & Permissions
docs.text:
Warehouse Orders are part of the Warehouse add-on. When the add-on is not turned on for your company, the Warehouse menu does not appear and opening the Warehouse Orders page redirects you away from it. See Add-ons and Options.

Role Warehouse Orders (view, create, edit, complete, documents) Admin Yes Warehouse Yes. Warehouse users land on the Warehouse Orders page when they sign in. Manager, Dispatch, Accountant, Customer, Driver, Garage and other roles No

Where to find it:

  • Left menu Warehouse > Orders

The other items of the Warehouse menu (Product, Location, Charges, Unit of Measure, Building) hold the lists the order form uses. See Warehouse Setup and Warehouse Overview.

Offices

Warehouse orders are not tied to an office. The list and counters show every warehouse order in your account, whatever office you are working in. See User Roles for what each role can do elsewhere.

docs.title: Counters
docs.text:
At the top right of the page:

Counter Counts Open Orders Orders with status New Completed Orders with status Completed Total All warehouse orders

The counters always show the totals. They do not follow the filter or the search.

The Create new Warehouse Order button sits next to the counters.

docs.title: Filters
docs.text:
The filter buttons sit above the list. The selected one is green.

Filter Shows All Every warehouse order Open Orders with status New. This is the default when you open the page. Completed Orders with status Completed

Switching filters keeps your current search and view.

docs.title: Orders and Products views
docs.text:
Next to the filters, the Orders / Products switch changes what each row represents. Orders is the default.

Orders view — one row per warehouse order, 20 per page:

Column What it shows Status / Order# A grey WH label (warehouse order), the status label and the order number. New shows a red star (hover text "New Order"); Completed shows a grey check mark (hover text "Order Completed"). Bill To The customer company of the person the order was placed for Storage Date The date the goods went into storage Closing Date The date entered when completing the order. Hidden under the Open filter. Container The Container Number Product Count Number of product rows on the order Invoiced Rate The calculated amount, in dollars. Hidden under the Open filter. See How the Invoiced Rate is calculated. (actions) Complete on open orders, Edit on completed orders, plus a drop-down arrow. See Row actions. DOC A red file icon when the order has documents. Click it to open the Documents window.

Products view — one row per product line, across all orders that match the filter, 25 per page:

Column What it shows Status / Order# The order's WH label, status label and order number Bill To The order's customer company Storage The order's Storage Date Container The order's Container Number Product Name The warehouse product Sku The product's SKU Quantity The quantity on the line UoM The unit of measure on the line Location The warehouse location on the line

The Products view has no action buttons. To change a line, switch back to Orders and edit the order.

In both views, click a column header with a link to sort by it. Product Count, Invoiced Rate and DOC cannot be sorted.

docs.title: Search
docs.text:
The search box (placeholder "Order #, product name, location and more") is at the right of the filters. Type one term and click the search button. The term is matched anywhere in the text (case-insensitive) against:

  • the Order #
  • the Container Number
  • the product name and SKU of any product line
  • the location name of any product line
  • the customer company name

While a search is active, a green Search: tag with your term appears next to the view switch. The search stays applied when you change filters. Clicking Orders or Products clears it.

docs.title: Row actions
docs.text: Order status Main button Drop-down arrow New (open) Complete Edit, Documents Completed Edit Documents

docs.title: Creating and Editing a Warehouse Order
docs.text:
Click Create new Warehouse Order, or Edit on an order row. The Warehouse Order window opens.

When you edit an order, the top of the window shows the customer company's name and address, and the person's name and email.

docs.title: Customer
docs.text:
The Customer section has one field, Place the order on behalf of (hint: "You can create an order on behalf of any customer."). Each entry shows the person's name in capitals followed by the company in brackets, for example JANE SMITH [ Acme Imports ]. The list is sorted by company name, then person name.

The list includes a person only when:

  • the person belongs to the office you are currently working in,
  • the person is active and not deleted,
  • the person's company is active and not deleted, and
  • the company's Service includes Warehouse (Warehouse or Intermodal & Warehouse).

See Managing Customers and People and Invitations.

The person is required. The order's Bill To is that person's company.

docs.title: Storage Date and Container Number
docs.text:
The Customer section, these two fields and the charges all sit in the Order Income & Billing panel of the window.

Field Required Notes Storage Date Yes The date the goods went into storage. The first month of billing is the month of this date. Container Number No Free text. Shown in the Container column and searchable.

docs.title: Charges
docs.text:
The Order Charges for Invoice Breakdown section (heading Additional Charges) holds the charges billed on the order. It starts empty.

  1. Click (+) Add another to add a charge row.
  2. Pick the charge in the drop-down. A new row starts on the first charge in the list (the list has no blank entry). Each entry reads the charge name followed by its rate and a dollar sign in brackets, for example Storage (0.5$).
  3. The rate box next to it fills in with the rate from the drop-down. Change it if needed. The rate is required and must be a number.
  4. Click (-) Remove to delete a row.

The drop-down lists your Income charge types whose Service is Warehouse. Whether a charge is Fixed or Monthly comes from its Value Type on the charge type, and decides how it counts in the Invoiced Rate. See Charge Types and Taxes.

Negotiated rates: when the customer's company has a custom rate for a warehouse charge (Custom rates for this customer, Warehouse group, on the customer), the drop-down shows that rate instead of the default rate. See Managing Customers.

  • On a new order, the drop-down first shows default rates. As soon as you pick a person in Place the order on behalf of, the charge lists reload with that customer's rates.
  • When editing an order, the drop-down shows the order customer's rates.

Changing the customer updates the rates

When you change Place the order on behalf of, every charge row keeps its selected charge and its rate box is filled with the rate for the new customer. If you had typed a rate by hand, enter it again before you save.

docs.title: Products
docs.text:
The Order Products section lists what is stored. It starts empty.

  1. Click (+) Add another to add a product row.

  2. Fill in the row:

    Field Required Notes Product Always set A warehouse product. The drop-down has no blank entry and starts on the first product. See Warehouse Setup. Quantity Yes Number of units stored. Used in the monthly charge calculation. Unit of measure Always set No blank entry; starts on the first unit. Its Length (inch) and Width (inch) give the square footage for monthly charges. Location Always set No blank entry; starts on the first location. Where the product is stored.

  3. Click (-) Remove to delete a row.

Click Create Order (new order) or Update Order (existing order) to save, or Close to discard your changes.

docs.title: Completing an Order
docs.text:
1. On an open order row, click Complete.
  2. The Complete Order window opens with a Select closing date section.
  3. The Closing Date is filled in with today's date. Change it if the goods left on another day. It is required.
  4. Click Submit.

The order's status changes to Completed. It leaves the Open filter and the Open Orders counter, and appears under Completed with its Closing Date and final Invoiced Rate.

Completing cannot be undone

There is no Reopen action, and the order form has no status field. A completed order stays completed. You can still click Edit to change its customer, dates, container, charges and products, but the Closing Date can only be set from the Complete Order window.

Pick a Closing Date on or after the Storage Date, since the month count and the Invoiced Rate are based on these two dates.

docs.title: Documents
docs.text:
Click the drop-down arrow on an order row and choose Documents, or click the red file icon in the DOC column. The Documents window opens with an Order Documents section.

  • Each saved document shows a file icon and name (click to open), a download icon and the file size, plus a drop-down with its document type, which you can change.
  • Click (+) Add document to add a row, choose the file under Document and pick its type in - Select Type -. The type list shows your active document types. A document saved without a type is saved as Other.
  • Click (-) Delete on a row to remove that document.
  • Click Submit to save your additions and deletions, or Close to discard them.

Documents can be added to both open and completed orders. See Order Documents and POD for how document types are used on freight orders.

docs.title: How the Invoiced Rate is calculated
docs.text:
The Invoiced Rate column (shown under All and Completed) is calculated from the order's charges and product rows:

  1. Months in storage = calendar months from the Storage Date month to the closing month, counting both. The closing month is the Closing Date, or today's date for an order that is not completed. A storage date of January 30 and a closing date of February 1 count as 2 months. Storage and closing in the same month count as 1.
  2. Fixed charges — each charge whose charge type Value Type is Fixed is added once, at the rate on the order.

  3. Monthly charges — for each product row, and for each charge whose Value Type is Monthly:

    months in storage × square feet × quantity × rate

    where square feet = (Length (inch) ÷ 12) × (Width (inch) ÷ 12) of the product row's unit of measure.

  4. The Invoiced Rate is the sum of all of the above.

Example: an order has a Fixed "Handling" charge at 50, a Monthly "Storage" charge at 0.25, and one product row of quantity 10 on a 48 × 40 inch unit of measure. Storage Date March 15, Closing Date May 2 (3 months). Square feet = 4 × 3.33 = 13.33. Invoiced Rate = 50 + (3 × 13.33 × 10 × 0.25) = 50 + 100 = $150.

Units without dimensions are not billed monthly

If the product row's unit of measure has no Length (inch) or no Width (inch), that row is skipped for monthly charges. Fixed charges still count. Set both dimensions on every unit of measure you use for storage. See Warehouse Setup.

Display format

The amount is shown in dollars with a $ sign. The calculation does not include taxes.

docs.title: The customer is not in "Place the order on behalf of"
docs.text:
Solution

Check that the customer company's Service is Warehouse or Intermodal & Warehouse, that the company and the person are both active, and that the person belongs to the office you are working in. Customers set to Intermodal only do not appear. See Managing Customers.

docs.title: I can't see the Closing Date or Invoiced Rate columns
docs.text:
Solution

Those columns are hidden under the default Open filter. Click All or Completed.

docs.title: The Invoiced Rate is $0.0 or too low
docs.text:
Solution

  • Check that the order has charges. Without charges the rate is 0.
  • Monthly charges need product rows. With no product rows, only Fixed charges count.
  • The unit of measure on each product row needs both Length (inch) and Width (inch). Rows without them are skipped for monthly charges.
  • Check the Value Type of each charge type (Fixed or Monthly) under Warehouse > Charges.
  • For an order that is still open, view it under All to see its current amount.

docs.title: The charge rate is not the customer's negotiated rate
docs.text:
Solution

The drop-down shows the custom rate from the customer's Custom rates for this customer (Warehouse group). If none is set, it shows the charge type's default rate. The rate box is filled when you pick a charge or change the person; a rate typed by hand is kept until you change the person. Check the rate box before saving.

docs.title: I completed an order by mistake
docs.text:
Solution

There is no reopen. You can click Edit to fix the order's other details, but it stays Completed with the closing date you entered. No screen lets you change the Closing Date afterwards.

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
Tips

  • Set Length (inch) and Width (inch) on every unit of measure before using it on orders, or monthly charges will not count.
  • Set the Value Type of each warehouse charge type correctly: Fixed for one-time fees (handling, receiving), Monthly for storage priced per square foot.
  • Put negotiated prices in the customer's Custom rates for this customer instead of typing them on each order.
  • Pick the customer first, then add charges, so the rates fill in with the customer's prices.
  • Double-check the Closing Date before clicking Submit: it should be on or after the Storage Date. Completing cannot be undone.
  • Attach receiving slips and photos in Documents so the order history stays with the order.

docs.title: Warehouse Module Overview
docs.text: The Warehouse add-on lets you bill customers for storing their goods: you record what a customer stores, where, and on what kind of space, and UTX Freight works out the storage charge from the floor space used and the number of months the goods stay in the warehouse.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
• Warehouse is an add-on. It only appears when it is turned on for your installation. See Add-ons & Options.
  • It adds a Warehouse group to the main (left) menu with six items: Orders, Product, Location, Charges, Unit of Measure and Building.
  • The core record is the Warehouse Order: a storage order placed on behalf of a customer, with a Storage Date, an optional Container Number, one or more product lines (product, quantity, unit of measure, location) and the charges to bill.
  • Storage is billed by space and time. Each unit of measure has a Length (inch) and Width (inch), which give a floor area in square feet. Monthly charges are multiplied by that area, the quantity stored and the number of months; Fixed charges are added once. See How storage is billed.
  • A warehouse order stays open (it is listed under the Open filter and its status icon reads "New Order") while the goods are in storage. When they leave, you click Complete and enter a Closing Date, which stops the month count.
  • Only Admin and Warehouse users can use it. A Warehouse user lands on Warehouse Orders after signing in and does not see the freight Orders page.
  • Only customers whose Service is Warehouse or Intermodal & Warehouse can have warehouse orders.

Warehouse orders are separate from freight orders

Warehouse orders have their own list, numbering and statuses. They do not appear in the freight Orders list, on Dispatch, or in the driver app, and they are not turned into freight invoices from the Invoices page.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
1. Create at least one Building: Warehouse Building.
  2. Create the Locations inside that building: Warehouse Location.
  3. Create your Units of Measure with their Length (inch) and Width (inch): Warehouse Unit of Measure.
  4. Create the Products you store (name and SKU, optional default location and unit of measure): Warehouse Product.
  5. Create your warehouse Charges with Charge Type = Income and Service = Warehouse: Warehouse Charges.
  6. Make sure the customer's Service is Warehouse or Intermodal & Warehouse and that it has at least one active person: Customers.
  7. Go to Warehouse Orders and click Create new Warehouse Order.

Details for each setup step are in Warehouse Setup. Creating, completing and searching orders is covered in Warehouse Orders.

docs.title: Access & Permissions
docs.text:
Role Warehouse access Admin Full access to every Warehouse page, plus all freight pages Warehouse Full access to warehouse Orders, Product, Location, Charges, Unit of Measure and Building. On the Charges page they can manage every charge, not only Warehouse ones. No access to freight Orders, Dispatch, Invoices or Customers Manager, Dispatch, Customer Service, Accountant, Customer, Garage, drivers and yard workers No access. The Warehouse menu group is hidden
  • The add-on must be turned on. If it is off, the Warehouse menu group is hidden for everyone, and opening a Warehouse page sends you back to the main application.
  • The Warehouse role is only offered in the role list when the Warehouse add-on is on. See User Roles and People & Invitations.
  • Inside the Warehouse module there are no finer permissions: a Warehouse user can create, edit and complete orders, and create, edit, enable and disable buildings, locations, units of measure, products and charges.

Managers do not see the Warehouse menu

Unlike the Garage add-on, the Warehouse module is not available to the Manager role. Only Admin and Warehouse users see the Warehouse menu group.

Where to find it:

  • Main menu Warehouse — click it to expand the group, then pick an item.

docs.title: Offices
docs.text:
• Warehouse orders are not office-scoped. Admin and Warehouse users see every warehouse order in the Warehouse Orders list, whatever office they are working in.
  • Setup records belong to an office. Buildings, locations, units of measure, products and charges each have an Office field, and their setup lists show the records of the office you are currently working in.
  • The warehouse order form is not filtered by office. The product, unit of measure and location lists on an order line show products, units of measure and locations from all offices. The charge list shows Income charges with the Warehouse service, also from all offices.
  • The customer list in the order form (Place the order on behalf of) shows the people of the current office.

See Multi-Office for how offices work.

docs.title: Landing Page
docs.text:
Who signs in Where they land Warehouse user, add-on on Warehouse Orders (the Open filter) Warehouse user, add-on off The home page of the application. There is nothing else for this role to open Admin The freight Orders page, as usual. Open the Warehouse menu group to get to warehouse orders

The Warehouse Orders page header shows three counters, Open Orders, Completed and Total, and the Create new Warehouse Order button. Below it are the filters All, Open, Completed and Not Invoiced, and a toggle between the Orders view (one row per order) and the Products view (one row per product line).

What a Warehouse user sees in the menu

A Warehouse user's main menu contains the Warehouse group. The freight Orders item is hidden for this role, as are Dispatch, Invoices, Customers and the other freight items. If the Fuel Surcharge add-on is also on, the Fuel Schedule item is visible to Warehouse users too, because they can manage charges.

docs.title: The Warehouse Menu
docs.text:
The Warehouse group lists its items in this order:

Menu item What it opens Details Orders Warehouse Orders: the list of storage orders, with Create new Warehouse Order Warehouse Orders Product The products you store, each with a Name, Sku, an optional default Location and default Unit of Measure, and an optional Image Warehouse Setup Location Storage locations, each belonging to a Building Warehouse Setup Charges The Charges list opened on its Warehouse filter: charge types whose Service is Warehouse Warehouse Setup, Charge Types & Taxes Unit of Measure Units of measure with their Length (inch) and Width (inch), which drive the space calculation Warehouse Setup Building Warehouse buildings, with Address, City (Must exist), Postal Code, Country, Contact Info and Email Warehouse Setup

docs.title: Setup Order
docs.text:
Some records must exist before others can be created. Set things up in this order:

Step What Why it comes here 1 Building A location must belong to a building. The building's City (Must exist) is picked from your active cities, so add the city first if needed (see Zones & Cities) 2 Location Each location needs a Building. Only active buildings are offered 3 Unit of Measure Gives the floor area used for monthly billing. Fill in both Length (inch) and Width (inch) 4 Product A product's optional default Location and Unit of Measure are picked from the active ones you created in steps 2 and 3. Name and Sku are required. The defaults are shown in the product list; they are not filled in automatically on warehouse order lines 5 Charges Create charges with Charge Type = Income and Service = Warehouse. Use Value Type = Monthly for storage billed per square foot per month, and Fixed for one-time fees (handling, in/out, etc.) 6 Customer with the Warehouse service Only customers whose Service is Warehouse or Intermodal & Warehouse can be picked on a warehouse order (see below)

Only Income charges with the Warehouse service appear on orders

The charge list on a warehouse order shows only charges whose Charge Type is Income and whose Service is Warehouse. A charge set to Expense, or to the Intermodal service, will not be offered.

docs.title: Customers and the Warehouse service
docs.text:
Customers are set up in the freight Customers page by a user who can manage customers, such as an Admin or Manager (Warehouse users cannot open Customers). See Managing Customers.

  1. Navigate to Customers and open or create the customer.
  2. Set Service to Warehouse or Intermodal & Warehouse.
  3. Make sure the customer is active and has at least one active person. A warehouse order is placed on behalf of a person, and the order form lists each person as their name in capitals followed by the customer name in brackets.
  4. Optional: under Custom rates for this customer, pick a charge from the Warehouse group and enter the customer's own rate. When you pick one of this customer's people on a warehouse order, the charge list shows that rate next to the charge name and pre-fills it in the rate box.
  5. Click Save.

With the add-on on, the Customers list also has Warehouse and Intermodal filters, so you can see which customers have each service.

docs.title: Company Service Types
docs.text:
Every customer has a Service that says what you do for them. The choices depend on which add-ons are on:

Service Shown when Effect Intermodal Always The customer's people can be picked on freight orders. They cannot be picked on warehouse orders Warehouse Warehouse add-on on The customer's people can be picked on warehouse orders. They do not appear in the freight order form's Place the order on behalf of list Intermodal & Warehouse Warehouse add-on on The customer can be used on both freight orders and warehouse orders Garage Garage add-on on Used by the Garage add-on. See Garage Module Overview

Charges also carry a Service (for example Intermodal or Warehouse). The Warehouse service is only offered on the charge form when the Warehouse add-on is on.

docs.title: How Storage Is Billed
docs.text:
The amount shown in the Invoiced Rate column of the Warehouse Orders list is calculated as follows:

  1. Fixed charges on the order are added once, at the rate entered on the order.
  2. For each product line, the floor area is worked out from its unit of measure: (Length (inch) ÷ 12) × (Width (inch) ÷ 12) = square feet.
  3. For each Monthly charge on the order: square feet × Quantity × charge rate × number of months, added for every product line.
  4. The number of months counts calendar months from the Storage Date to the Closing Date, including both the first and the last month. While the order is still open, today's date is used instead of a closing date.

Example

A unit of measure of 48 × 40 inches is 4 ft × 3.33 ft = 13.33 sq ft. Ten of them stored from March 20 to May 5 count as 3 months (March, April, May). With a Monthly charge of $0.50: 13.33 × 10 × 0.50 × 3 = $200.00. A Fixed charge of $75 on the same order brings the total to $275.00.

Units of measure without dimensions are not billed monthly

If a unit of measure is missing its Length (inch) or Width (inch), product lines using it add nothing to Monthly charges. Fixed charges are not affected, because they are added once per order.

The Invoiced Rate column (and the Closing Date column) is shown on every filter except Open. On the All filter, open orders are calculated up to today. UTX Freight does not create invoices from warehouse orders.

See Warehouse Orders for the full order workflow.

docs.title: I don't see the Warehouse menu
docs.text:
Solution

Check two things: the Warehouse add-on must be turned on for your installation (see Add-ons & Options), and your role must be Admin or Warehouse. Managers, dispatchers and other roles do not see the Warehouse group.

docs.title: A customer is missing from "Place the order on behalf of"
docs.text:
Solution

The list only shows active people of active customers whose Service is Warehouse or Intermodal & Warehouse, in the office you are currently working in. Open the customer in Customers, check its Service, and make sure it has at least one active person.

docs.title: A charge is missing from the order's charge list
docs.text:
Solution

Open Warehouse Charges and check that the charge's Charge Type is Income and its Service is Warehouse. Charges with the Intermodal service or the Expense type are not offered on warehouse orders.

docs.title: A Warehouse user can't open Orders
docs.text:
Solution

That is by design. The Warehouse role has no access to freight orders. Warehouse users work from Warehouse Orders. If the person also needs freight orders, give them an Admin account instead. See User Roles.

docs.title: I can't pick a building when creating a location
docs.text:
Solution

The Building list only shows active buildings of the office you are working in. Create the building first (or enable it), then come back to Location.

docs.title: The order total is lower than expected
docs.text:
Solution

Check the unit of measure on each product line: without both Length (inch) and Width (inch) it adds nothing to Monthly charges. Also check that the storage charge is set to Value Type = Monthly; a Fixed charge is only counted once.

Best Practices

  • Follow the setup order: Building Location Unit of Measure Product Charges customer Service.
  • Always enter both dimensions on a unit of measure; they are what monthly storage is billed on.
  • Keep storage fees as Monthly charges and one-time fees (handling, receiving, shipping out) as Fixed charges.
  • Use Custom rates for this customer on the customer to give a customer its own warehouse prices instead of editing the rate on each order.
  • Complete orders as soon as the goods leave, so the month count stops at the right Closing Date.

docs.title: Warehouse Buildings, Locations, Products, Units & Charges
Warehouse Buildings, Locations, Products, Units & Charges
docs.text: Set up the master data the Warehouse add-on needs before you create warehouse orders: Buildings, Locations, Products, Units of Measure and warehouse Charges.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
These five lists are the building blocks of a warehouse order. You set them up once, then pick from them on every order line and charge row.

  • Buildings are your warehouse sites, with an address, a city, a contact and an email.
  • Locations are the storage spots inside a building (an aisle, a bay, a room). Every location belongs to one building.
  • Units of Measure describe the footprint of what you store (for example a pallet). Their Length (inch) and Width (inch) give the floor area in square feet that Monthly charges are billed on.
  • Products are the goods you store, with a Name, a Sku, an optional default location and unit of measure, and an optional image.
  • Charges are the warehouse fees: charge types with Service = Warehouse. Monthly charges are billed per square foot per month; Fixed charges are added once.
  • Buildings, locations, units of measure and products share the same list behaviour: All Active / Disabled filters, an Actions menu with Edit, Disable and Enable, and a short notification when you disable or enable an entry. See Shared list behaviour.
  • None of these records can be deleted from the screen. Disable them instead.

For how these records are used on orders and how storage is billed, see Warehouse Module Overview and Warehouse Orders.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
Set things up in this order, because each step uses the one before it:

  1. Warehouse Building → Add a new Warehouse Building. Enter the Name and click Save Changes.
  2. Warehouse Location → Add a new Warehouse Location. Enter the Name, pick the Building and click Save Changes.
  3. Warehouse Unit of Measure → Add a new Unit Of Measure. Enter the Name, Length (inch) and Width (inch) and click Save Changes.
  4. Warehouse Product → Add a new Warehouse Product. Enter the Name and Sku, optionally pick a Location and Unit of Measure, and click Save Changes.
  5. Warehouse Charges → Add a new Order Charge. Set Charge Type = Income, Service = Warehouse, choose Value Type Monthly (storage) or Fixed (one-time fee), enter the Default Rate and click Save.

You can now create a warehouse order. See Warehouse Orders.

docs.title: Access & Permissions
docs.text:
Role Building, Location, Unit of Measure, Product Charges Admin Full access Full access Warehouse Full access Full access Manager No access Full access to the Charge Types page, but no Warehouse menu Accountant No access Full access to the Charge Types page, but no Warehouse menu Dispatch No access Only when Can manage rates? is checked on the user's form, and no Warehouse menu All other roles No access No access
  • The Warehouse add-on must be turned on. When it is off, the Warehouse menu group is hidden and opening a Building, Location, Unit of Measure or Product page redirects you away (Admins land on the freight Orders list, Warehouse users on the home page). The Charges page (Charge Types) stays available, but without the Warehouse and Intermodal filter buttons. See Add-ons & Options.
  • The Warehouse menu group is only shown to Admin and Warehouse users.
  • There are no finer permissions inside these pages: anyone who can open a list can add, edit, disable and enable its entries.

How to get there:

  • Main menu Warehouse — click it to expand the group, then click Product, Location, Charges, Unit of Measure or Building.
  • Warehouse > Charges opens the Charge Types page (title Order Charges) already on its Warehouse filter. The same page is also in the user menu as Charge Types. See Charge Types & Taxes.

Multi-office

Every building, location, unit of measure, product and charge has an Office. Each list shows the entries of the office you are currently working in. When the Multi-Office add-on is on, these records are shared: every office sees all of them, and the dropdowns on the setup forms (for example Building on a location, Location and Unit of Measure on a product) list the entries of every office. The Office dropdown on each form lists the offices you belong to. See Multi-Office.

docs.title: Shared List Behaviour
docs.text: The Building, Location, Unit of Measure and Product pages all work the same way.

docs.title: Page header
docs.text:
Page Menu item Page title Subtitle Add button Buildings Building Warehouse Buildings Management of Warehouse Buildings Add a new Warehouse Building Locations Location Warehouse Locations Management of Warehouse Locations Add a new Warehouse Location Units of Measure Unit of Measure Unit Of Measures Management of Unit Of Measures Add a new Unit Of Measure Products Product Warehouse Products Management of Warehouse Products Add a new Warehouse Product Charges Charges Order Charges Management of Order Charges Add a new Order Charge

The add button sits at the top right of the page. Clicking it opens the form on its own page, titled New … (for example New Warehouse Building). Actions → Edit opens the same form titled Edit … (for example Edit Warehouse Building).

docs.title: Filters
docs.text:
Button Shows All Active Entries whose Active box is checked. The page opens on this filter. Disabled Entries whose Active box is unchecked.

The selected filter button is highlighted in green. Lists show 50 entries per page, with page links below the table.

docs.title: Name colour and Active column
docs.text:
• The Name is shown in green for an active entry and in red for a disabled one.
  • The Active column shows a green for active and a red for disabled.

docs.title: Actions menu
docs.text:
Each row ends with an Actions button () and a dropdown arrow. The menu contains:

Action What it does Edit Opens the form to change the entry. Disable Shown on active entries. Unchecks Active right away, without leaving the page. Enable Shown on disabled entries. Checks Active again, without leaving the page.

After Disable or Enable, the row updates in place (the name changes colour and the Active icon flips) and a message appears at the top of the screen for about two seconds:

Action Message (title Update) Colour Disable a building Warehouse building Name - Disabled Red Enable a building Warehouse building Name - Enabled Green Disable / Enable a location Warehouse location Name - Disabled / - Enabled Red / Green Disable / Enable a unit of measure Unit of measure Name - Disabled / - Enabled Red / Green Disable / Enable a product Warehouse product Name - Disabled / - Enabled Red / Green

The row stays in the list you are looking at until you reload the page or switch filter. You can also disable or enable an entry by unchecking or checking Active in its form.

docs.title: Saving and cancelling
docs.text:
• Every form ends with Save Changes (blue) and Cancel (red, on the right).
  • Save Changes saves and returns you to the list, on its All Active filter. While saving, the button reads Please wait....
  • If a required field is missing, the form stays open and shows the error next to the field.
  • Cancel returns to the list without saving.

docs.title: Buildings
docs.text: Menu: Warehouse Building

docs.title: Columns
docs.text: Column Description Name The building name, green if active, red if disabled Address The street address Zip The postal code City The city picked in City (Must exist) Country Canada or United States Contact Info Free text, for example a contact name and phone number Email The building's email address Active Green check (active) or red cross (disabled) (Actions) Edit, Disable / Enable

docs.title: Creating a Building
docs.text:
1. Click Add a new Warehouse Building.
  2. Fill in the Warehouse Building Information form (see the table below).
  3. Click Save Changes.
Field Required Description Name Yes The building name (placeholder warehouse building name) Office Yes The office the building belongs to. Lists the offices you belong to; no blank option Address No The street address City (Must exist) No Picked from the active cities of your current office. The city must already exist; add it first in Manage Cities if needed. See Zones & Cities Postal Code No Shown in the Zip column Country No Canada or United States. No blank option, so Canada is selected by default Contact Info No Free text Email No The building's email address Active — In the Warehouse building visibility section. Checked by default for a new building

Why disable a building

Only active buildings of your current office are offered in the Building dropdown when you create or edit a location. Disabling a building does not change the locations that already belong to it.

docs.title: Locations
docs.text: Menu: Warehouse Location

docs.title: Columns
docs.text: Column Description Name The location name, green if active, red if disabled Building The building the location belongs to Active Green check (active) or red cross (disabled) (Actions) Edit, Disable / Enable

docs.title: Creating a Location
docs.text:
1. Make sure the building exists and is active (see Buildings).
  2. Click Add a new Warehouse Location.
  3. Fill in the Warehouse Location Information form (see the table below).
  4. Click Save Changes.
Field Required Description Name Yes The location name (placeholder warehouse location name), for example an aisle or bay code Office Yes The office the location belongs to. Lists the offices you belong to; no blank option Building Yes Picked from the active buildings of your current office. No blank option Active — In the Warehouse location visibility section. Checked by default for a new location

Where locations are used

  • A product's default Location is picked from the active locations of your current office.
  • Each line of a warehouse order has its own Location. See Warehouse Orders.

docs.title: Units of Measure
docs.text:
Menu: Warehouse Unit of Measure

A unit of measure is the footprint of one stored item, such as a standard pallet. Its length and width are what Monthly warehouse charges are billed on.

docs.title: Columns
docs.text: Column Description Name The unit name, green if active, red if disabled Length The length in inches Width The width in inches Active Green check (active) or red cross (disabled) (Actions) Edit, Disable / Enable

docs.title: Creating a Unit of Measure
docs.text:
1. Click Add a new Unit Of Measure.
  2. Fill in the Unit of Measure Information form (see the table below).
  3. Click Save Changes.
Field Required Description Name Yes The unit name (placeholder Unit of measure name), for example Pallet 48x40 Office Yes The office the unit belongs to. Lists the offices you belong to; no blank option Length (inch) No, but needed for billing Length of one item, in inches. Decimals are allowed Width (inch) No, but needed for billing Width of one item, in inches. Decimals are allowed Active — In the Unit of measure visibility section. Checked by default for a new unit

docs.title: How length and width drive billing
docs.text:
For each line of a warehouse order, the app converts the line's unit of measure to square feet:

sq ft = (Length (inch) ÷ 12) × (Width (inch) ÷ 12)

Each Monthly charge on the order then adds:

sq ft × Quantity × charge rate × number of months

The number of months counts calendar months from the order's Storage Date to its Closing Date (or today, while the order is open), including both the first and the last month. Fixed charges are added once and do not use the unit of measure. See How Storage Is Billed for a worked example.

Length (inch) Width (inch) sq ft per item 48 40 4 × 3.33 = 13.33 48 48 4 × 4 = 16 120 96 10 × 8 = 80

Enter both dimensions, in inches

  • If Length (inch) or Width (inch) is empty, order lines that use this unit are skipped by Monthly charges: only Fixed charges count for them.
  • The values are read as inches. Entering feet (for example 4 instead of 48) bills 1/144 of the expected area.
  • Editing a unit's dimensions changes the total shown for every warehouse order that uses it, including existing ones, because the Warehouse Orders list recalculates the total from the current values each time it is displayed.

docs.title: Products
docs.text: Menu: Warehouse Product

docs.title: Columns
docs.text: Column Description Name The product name, green if active, red if disabled Sku The product SKU Location The product's default location Unit of Measure The product's default unit of measure Image An  icon. Click it to open the product image in a new tab Active Green check (active) or red cross (disabled) (Actions) Edit, Disable / Enable

docs.title: Creating a Product
docs.text:
1. Click Add a new Warehouse Product.
  2. Fill in the Warehouse Product Information form (see the table below).
  3. Click Save Changes.
Field Required Description Name Yes The product name (placeholder warehouse product name) Sku Yes The product SKU (placeholder warehouse product sku) Location No Default location. Picked from the active locations of your current office; can be left blank Unit of Measure No Default unit of measure. Picked from the active units of measure of your current office; can be left blank Image No Upload a picture of the product, for example a JPG or PNG Office Always set The office the product belongs to. Lists the offices you belong to; no blank option, so one is always selected Active — In the Warehouse product visibility section. Checked by default for a new product

Default location and unit of measure

The product's Location and Unit of Measure are reference values shown in the Products list. On a warehouse order, you pick the Unit of Measure and Location on each order line.

Search warehouse orders by product

The search box on Warehouse Orders matches product Name and Sku, so a clear, unique SKU makes orders easy to find. See Warehouse Orders.

docs.title: Warehouse Charges
docs.text:
Menu: Warehouse Charges

Warehouse charges are ordinary charge types (page title Order Charges) whose Service is Warehouse. The menu item opens the Charge Types page on its Warehouse filter. The full page is documented in Charge Types & Taxes; this section covers what matters for the warehouse.

docs.title: Filters
docs.text:
Button Shows All Active Active charge types of every service Disabled Disabled charge types of every service Warehouse Charge types whose Service is Warehouse, active and disabled, Income and Expense. This is where Warehouse > Charges opens Intermodal Charge types whose Service is Intermodal, active and disabled

The Warehouse and Intermodal buttons are only shown when the Warehouse add-on is on. Charge types are sorted by name, 50 per page. When the Fuel Surcharge add-on is on, charge types whose Use For is Fuel Surcharge are hidden from this list (they are managed on the Fuel Schedule) and a Back to Fuel Schedule button is shown.

docs.title: Columns
docs.text:
Column Description ID The charge type's number (icon) A warehouse icon for Warehouse charges, a ship icon for Intermodal ones Name Green if active, red if disabled Service Warehouse or Intermodal Type Income or Expense Default Rate The rate, shown as a dollar amount Rate Type Fixed or Monthly Use For Terminal Fee (or Fuel Surcharge) when set, otherwise not set Effective Period The Applicable on month when set, otherwise not set Active Green check (active) or red cross (disabled) (Actions) Edit, View History

No Disable / Enable action on charges

Unlike the other warehouse lists, the Charges Actions menu has no Disable or Enable item. To disable a charge, open Edit, uncheck Active and click Save.

docs.title: Creating a Warehouse Charge
docs.text:
1. Navigate to Warehouse Charges.
  2. Click Add a new Order Charge.
  3. Fill in the Order Charge Information form:
Field Set it to Description Name Required The charge name shown on the warehouse order (placeholder Category Name), for example Storage per sq ft or Handling in/out Charge Type Income Income (selected by default) or Expense. Only Income charges are offered on warehouse orders Default Rate Required, a number For Monthly: the price per square foot per month. For Fixed: the flat amount Value Type Fixed or Monthly Fixed is selected by default. See Fixed vs Monthly below Service Warehouse Warehouse is only offered when the add-on is on. Only Warehouse charges are offered on warehouse orders Office Required The office the charge belongs to. Lists the offices you belong to; no blank option Use as default for Leave blank Used for the freight Terminal Fee (and Fuel Surcharge when the Fuel Surcharge add-on is on). Not used by warehouse orders Applicable on (Month) Leave blank Only shown when the Fuel Surcharge add-on is on. Not used by warehouse orders Active Checked Uncheck to move the charge to the Disabled filter
  1. Click Save. You return to the Charge Types list on All Active (not on the Warehouse filter).

docs.title: Fixed vs Monthly
docs.text:
Value Type How it is billed on a warehouse order Typical use Fixed Added once to the order total, at the rate on the order Receiving, handling, shipping out, labelling Monthly For every product line: sq ft × Quantity × rate × number of months Storage space

The square footage comes from the line's unit of measure (see How length and width drive billing).

docs.title: Customer custom rates
docs.text:
A customer can have its own price for a warehouse charge, which replaces the Default Rate on that customer's orders.

  1. Navigate to Customers and open the customer. Customers is available to Admins and Managers, and to Dispatch users when this has been turned on for your account (ask UTX support). Warehouse users cannot open Customers.
  2. In Custom rates for this customer, click (+) Add another.
  3. In the Charge dropdown, pick the charge in the Warehouse group. The group lists the active charges with the Warehouse service (Income and Expense).
  4. Enter the customer's Rate and click Save Changes.

On a warehouse order for a person of that customer, the charge dropdown shows the custom rate, for example Storage per sq ft (0.45$), and picking the charge pre-fills the Rate box with it. Changing the person in Place the order on behalf of reloads the charge rates for the new customer and resets the Rate box of every charge row already on the form to that customer's rate (or the Default Rate), so re-check any rate you typed by hand. The rate stays editable on each order. See Managing Customers and Warehouse Orders.

docs.title: I don't see the Warehouse menu or the setup pages
docs.text:
Solution

The Warehouse add-on must be on and your role must be Admin or Warehouse. If the add-on is off, opening a Building, Location, Unit of Measure or Product page redirects you away from it. See Add-ons & Options and User Roles.

docs.title: The Building dropdown is empty when I create a location
docs.text:
Solution

The dropdown only lists active buildings of the office you are working in. Create the building first, or open Building → Disabled and use Actions → Enable.

docs.title: My city is missing from "City (Must exist)"
docs.text:
Solution

The list shows the active cities of your current office. Add or enable the city in Manage Cities first. See Zones & Cities.

docs.title: A location or unit of measure is missing from the product form
docs.text:
Solution

The product form only offers active locations and units of measure of your current office. Check the Disabled filter on Location or Unit of Measure and enable the entry.

docs.title: Storage is not billed for some product lines
docs.text:
Solution

Open Unit of Measure and check that the unit used on those lines has both Length (inch) and Width (inch). Without both, Monthly charges skip the line. Also check that the storage charge's Value Type is Monthly.

docs.title: The storage amount is far too high or too low
docs.text:
Solution

Check that the unit's Length (inch) and Width (inch) are in inches, and that the Monthly charge's rate is a price per square foot per month. For example, a 48 × 40 pallet is 13.33 sq ft.

docs.title: A charge is missing from the warehouse order
docs.text:
Solution

Only charges with Charge Type = Income and Service = Warehouse are offered. Open Warehouse > Charges (the Warehouse filter shows Income and Expense) and check the Type and Service columns.

docs.title: The customer's custom rate is not used
docs.text:
Solution

Check that the custom rate on the customer points to the right charge in the Warehouse group, and that the order is placed on behalf of a person of that customer. If you changed the person after adding charges, check that the Rate box was refreshed.

docs.title: How do I delete a building, location, unit, product or charge?
docs.text:
Solution

You can't from the screen. Use Actions → Disable (or uncheck Active on a charge). Disabled entries move to the Disabled filter and stay linked to existing orders.

Best Practices

  • Follow the setup order: Building → Location → Unit of Measure → Product → Charges.
  • Always enter both Length (inch) and Width (inch) on a unit of measure, in inches.
  • Use Monthly charges for storage (rate per sq ft per month) and Fixed charges for one-time fees.
  • Give each product a unique Sku so warehouse orders are easy to search.
  • Use Custom rates for this customer for negotiated prices instead of editing the rate on every order.
  • Disable entries you no longer use.

docs.title: Website Content (Manage Content)
docs.text: Edit the text of your company's public website (the Home, Equipment, Tracking and Contact pages) from inside UTX Freight.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Every UTX Freight system comes with a small public website at the root address of your system. It is what visitors see before they sign in. The page layout, logo and main image are fixed. The text comes from content pages that an Admin edits on Manage Content.

  • The public site reads six content pages, each identified by its Name: about, company, contact, equipment, tracking and login. A new system also has a seventh page, home_equipment, which is not shown anywhere on the public site. See The Pages List.
  • You can edit and view these pages. There is no button to create or delete a page.
  • Content is written in Textile, a simple text markup. It is converted to formatted text (headings, bold, lists, links) on the public site and in the preview.
  • Each public page shows two content pages: one in the large main column and one in the narrow side column. See Which page appears where.
  • Changes appear on the public site as soon as you save.
  • Manage Content is for Admins only.

Placeholder text

The public pages ship with placeholder text. Your logo, tax rates and company record are set when your system is built, but the website text is the part only you can write. The Setup Checklist reminds you of this in the Check what your website says step.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
1. Click your name at the top of the screen to open the user menu, then click Manage Content.
  2. Find the page you want to change in the Name column (for example contact).
  3. Open its Actions menu and click Edit.
  4. Change the text in the Content box, using Textile formatting.
  5. Click Save Changes.

The message Page was successfully updated. appears and the new text is live on the public site.

docs.title: Access & Permissions
docs.text:
Role Access Admin Can view and edit every content page. Cannot create pages, and there is no button to delete one. Manager No access Dispatch No access Accountant No access Customer, Driver, Warehouse, Garage and other users No access

How to get there:

  • Click your name at the top of the screen to open the user menu, then click Manage Content. It sits near the bottom of the menu, just above Manage Offices.
  • From the Setup Checklist, the Check what your website says step has an Open Manage Content button.

The Manage Content item only appears in the menu for Admin users. Any other signed-in user who opens the page address directly is sent back to the dashboard with a not-authorized message.

Not per office

The content pages are shared by your whole system. They are not tied to an office, so switching offices does not change what you see on Manage Content or on the public site.

docs.title: The Pages List
docs.text:
Manage Content opens the Pages list (subtitle Management of Pages). All content pages are shown on one screen.

Column Description Name The page's fixed name, such as about or contact. This name is what links the page to the public site. It cannot be changed. Content Preview The full page content, already formatted from Textile, so you can see how it will read. (Actions) The Actions menu with Edit and Show.

There is no Add button on this list. Admins cannot create new content pages, and the public site only reads the six names listed in Which page appears where.

The home_equipment page

A new system is set up with a seventh content page, home_equipment, holding a copy of the starting equipment list. No public page reads it, so editing it changes nothing on your website. To change the equipment text visitors see, edit the equipment page.

docs.title: Editing a Page
docs.text:
1. On the Pages list, open the Actions menu of the page and click Edit.
  2. The Edit Page screen opens. Inside the Content box it shows Page Name: name. The name cannot be changed.
  3. Change the text in the Content box. Use Textile formatting for headings, bold text, lists and links.
  4. Click Save Changes.

You return to the Pages list with the message Page was successfully updated. The Content Preview column shows the new text.

To leave without saving, click Cancel.

Content cannot be empty

The Content field is required. If you clear it and click Save Changes, the page is not saved and the field shows an error. To hide a section, replace the text with something short instead of leaving it blank.

Do not repeat the section heading

Each block on the public site already has a heading (for example CONTACT US or COMPANY). Start your content with the text itself rather than repeating that heading.

docs.title: Viewing a Page
docs.text:
On the Pages list, open the Actions menu and click Show. The page shows Page Name: name with the subtitle Website page content, and the content formatted as it will appear on the website.

From here, click Edit to change the page, or Back to return to the list.

docs.title: Which Page Appears Where
docs.text:
The public website has four pages, reached from the top menu: HOME, EQUIPMENT, TRACKING and CONTACT. Each one shows a fixed main image, a large main column and a narrow side column. The heading of each column is fixed; the text below it comes from a content page.

Public page Main column heading Content page used Side column heading Content page used HOME (the root address of your system) ABOUT about OFFICES company EQUIPMENT EQUIPMENT equipment LOGIN login TRACKING TRACKING SYSTEM tracking LOGIN login CONTACT CONTACT US contact COMPANY company

Key points:

  • The company page is shown on two public pages: as OFFICES on HOME and as COMPANY on CONTACT. Put your address, phone and fax there.
  • The login page is shown on two public pages: EQUIPMENT and TRACKING. It has no sign-in form; a new system starts it with a short sentence and a My Account link. The actual sign-in is the LOGIN link at the top of the public site (it reads MY ACCOUNT when you are already signed in).
  • Editing one content page changes every public page that uses it.

docs.title: Mobile version
docs.text:
Visitors on a phone see a simpler mobile site with Home, Equipment and Contact in the menu (there is no Tracking item). The sign-in link at the top reads Login, or Account when you are already signed in.

Mobile page Content pages shown Home about only Equipment equipment only Contact contact and company

On the mobile Home and Equipment pages there is no side column, so company (as OFFICES) and login are not shown there. Because the Tracking page is not in the mobile menu, the tracking and login text is normally not seen on a phone.

docs.title: When changes appear
docs.text: As soon as you save a content page, your change shows on the public site the next time the page is loaded. You do not need to clear anything or wait.

docs.title: Textile Formatting
docs.text:
Content is written in Textile. Plain text works as-is; the markup below adds formatting. The Content Preview column and the Show screen display the formatted result, so you can check your work after saving.

You type Result A blank line between two blocks of text Two separate paragraphs *Open Monday to Friday* Open Monday to Friday (bold) _by appointment_ by appointment (italic) h3. Our yard at the start of a line, followed by a blank line A heading reading "Our yard" * Dry van on separate lines A bulleted list # Call dispatch on separate lines A numbered list "Email us":mailto:info@example.com A link reading "Email us" that opens an email "Our services":https://www.example.com A link reading "Our services"

Example for the company page:

*Your Company Inc.*
123 Example Street
City, Province A1A 1A1

Phone: 555-555-0100
Fax: 555-555-0101

HTML in your content

Textile also lets plain HTML through. The contact page of a new system starts with an HTML line at the top and a matching </div> line at the bottom. You can keep those lines or remove them; write your text between them if you keep them.

Keep it short

The side column (company and login) is narrow. A few lines of address and phone details read better there than long paragraphs.

docs.title: The "Check what your website says" Setup Step
docs.text:
The Setup Checklist has a step called Check what your website says, in the stage about what appears on your invoice. It points you to Manage Content with the Open Manage Content button and suggests:

  1. Open Manage Content.
  2. Read the Company page (company). That is your address, phone and fax.
  3. Read the Contact and About pages (contact, about) and put your own words in.
  4. Tell UTX if you want the logo or anything else on the invoice changed.

What we found counts every page on the Pages list (including home_equipment), for example 7 public pages, none confirmed yet.

This step is not completed by editing the pages. When the text is right, go back to the checklist and click Looks right to me on this step. It then reads, for example, 7 pages, confirmed as they are. See Looks right to me.

Managers and this step

A Manager can see this step and click Looks right to me, but cannot open Manage Content. Ask an Admin to make any changes.

docs.title: How do I add a new page to my website?
docs.text:
Solution

You cannot. The public website has a fixed set of four pages (HOME, EQUIPMENT, TRACKING, CONTACT) fed by six fixed content pages, and Admins cannot create new content pages. To add information, put it in an existing page, for example a new heading and paragraph on the about page.

docs.title: How do I remove a page?
docs.text:
Solution

There is no button to delete a content page, and the public site needs all six it reads. To make a section say less, edit it down to a short line of text.

docs.title: I do not see Manage Content in my menu
docs.text:
Solution

Manage Content is shown only to Admin users. Ask an Admin to make the change, or to give you the Admin role. See User Roles.

docs.title: I changed my address but it only changed in one place
docs.text:
Solution

Check which content page you edited. Your address normally belongs on the company page, which appears on both HOME (as OFFICES) and CONTACT (as COMPANY). If you also typed it into about or contact, update those too.

docs.title: My text shows stray asterisks, underscores or quotes
docs.text:
Solution

Textile treats *, _, # and "text":link as formatting. Check that each * or _ has a matching closing one, that list lines start with * or # (with a space), and that links use the "text":address form with no space before the colon. Open Show to check the result.

docs.title: Can I change the logo or the main image?
docs.text:
Solution

No, not from Manage Content. The logo and the main image on the public site are part of your system's setup. Contact UTX support if you want them changed.

docs.title: I edited my pages but the setup step is still open
docs.text:
Solution

Editing does not complete Check what your website says. Go to the Setup Checklist and click Looks right to me on that step.

Best Practices

  • Replace the placeholder text in about, company and contact before you send customers to your website.
  • Keep your address, phone and fax in one place, the company page, so they stay consistent on HOME and CONTACT.
  • Use the login page to tell customers how to get an account or who to call for tracking access.
  • After saving, open the public site (and check it on a phone) to see the result in context.

docs.title: Yard Worker Mobile Screen
docs.text: Search a container by number on your phone, then ground it (take it off its chassis) or mark it Full at yard or Empty at yard.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Yard Workers use UTX Freight in their phone's web browser. There is no app to install. After signing in, a Yard Worker sees one screen: a container search.

  • Search a container — type all or part of a container number in the Container # box and tap Search.
  • See the order — each match shows the container number and order type, then CUSTOMER, POD #, NOTE (when there is one), CONTAINER STATUS and CHASSIS NUMBER.
  • Ground Container — removes the chassis from the order. Only shown when a chassis is assigned.
  • Full at yard / Empty at yard — sets the order's container status.
  • REFRESH — reloads the order's status and chassis without changing anything.
  • Nothing else — Yard Workers cannot open the order list, sign PODs or change the order status.

Changes go straight to the order

The buttons save to the order immediately. The office sees the new container status and chassis on the order.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
1. On your phone, open UTX Freight, tap Mobile Login, type your Access Code and tap Sign in.
  2. Type the container number (or part of it) in the Container # box and tap Search.
  3. Tap the container in Search Results to open it.
  4. Tap Ground Container, Full at yard or Empty at yard. The card updates on the spot.

docs.title: Access & Permissions
docs.text:
Role Access Yard Worker (mobile user) Container search and the yard buttons (Ground Container, Full at yard, Empty at yard, REFRESH). Nothing else. Driver / Broker No access. They land on their own list of orders. See Driver Mobile App. Admin, Manager, Dispatch, other office roles No container search screen. After sign-in they land on Orders (Warehouse users land on the warehouse orders). They change the container status and equipment from the order itself. See Orders and Order Form.

Who sets up Yard Workers: an Admin, Manager, Dispatch or Customer Service user adds the person under Mobile Users Drivers, Brokers & Yard, picks the Role Yard Worker, and gives them an Access Code. See Mobile Users.

How to get there: sign in on the phone. A Yard Worker always lands on the container search screen.

Yard Workers are mobile users, not office accounts

The Yard Worker role only exists under Mobile Users (with Driver and Broker). It is not in the Role list when you add a person with an email and password. The yard buttons are only allowed for a Yard Worker signed in with an Access Code.

Phone layout only

The container search is part of the mobile layout, which UTX Freight uses automatically on a phone browser. On a desktop browser the page shows Dashboard - Transportation orders coming soon instead. Use a phone.

docs.title: Signing In
docs.text:
1. Open UTX Freight in the phone's browser. Under the email and password form, the page shows Are you a driver or yard worker ?
  2. Tap Mobile Login.
  3. Type your code in the Access Code field and tap Sign in.

You go straight to the container search. The phone remembers you, so you don't have to type the code every time. See Mobile Users for the sign-in rules.

docs.title: Searching for a Container
docs.text:
1. Type the container number in the Container # box. You can type only part of it (for example the last digits). Upper or lower case does not matter.
  2. Tap Search.

The results appear under Search Results. If nothing matches, the screen shows No Results Found. The screen also shows No Results Found before your first search.

Which orders are searched:

Included Not included Orders with status New, App. Made or Dispatched Completed orders Every order whose container number contains what you typed Orders created before the Order Archive Cutoff Date in Settings (see Application Settings)

Several matches

A short search (for example 3 digits) can match several orders. Each one is listed as its own card. Check the container number and order type in the card title before you tap a button.

docs.title: What Each Result Shows
docs.text:
Tap a result to open it. The card title shows the container number followed by the order type code in brackets, for example [CI].

Type code Order type CI Container Import CX Container Export TF Transfer DV Dry Van IX International Export WH Warehouse

Inside the card:

Field What it shows CUSTOMER The delivery company on the order. For a Transfer order, it shows the name of the customer company that owns the order. POD # The order's Reference number. NOTE The order's Special Note, in red. Only shown when the order has one. See Order Form. CONTAINER STATUS The order's current container status, for example Full at yard. Empty when no status is set. CHASSIS NUMBER The Equipment assigned to the order. When the equipment is Borrowed, the borrowed chassis number is shown instead. Shows -- no chassis -- in red when no equipment is assigned.

Below the fields are the yard buttons.

docs.title: Yard Buttons
docs.text:
Each button saves right away. There is no confirmation and no Save button. The card updates on the spot without reloading the page.

Button Shown when What it does Ground Container The order has a chassis (equipment) assigned Removes the equipment from the order. CHASSIS NUMBER changes to -- no chassis -- and the button disappears. Full at yard The container status is not already Full at yard Sets the order's container status to Full at yard. CONTAINER STATUS turns green and the button disappears. Empty at yard The container status is not already Empty at yard Sets the order's container status to Empty at yard. CONTAINER STATUS turns green and the button disappears. REFRESH Always Reloads CONTAINER STATUS and CHASSIS NUMBER from the order, so you see changes made by the office. Changes nothing.

docs.title: Grounding a container
docs.text:
1. Search for the container and open its card.
  2. Check that CHASSIS NUMBER shows the chassis you are taking it off.
  3. Tap Ground Container.

The chassis is taken off the order, so the office sees the order without Equipment. Grounding does not change the container status. If the container is now sitting in the yard, also tap Full at yard or Empty at yard.

Grounding cannot be undone from the phone

There is no button to put a chassis back on the order. The office must pick the Equipment again on the order. See Order Form.

docs.title: Setting Full at yard or Empty at yard
docs.text:
1. Search for the container and open its card.
  2. Tap Full at yard if the container is loaded, or Empty at yard if it is empty.

Only the container status changes. The order status (New, App. Made, Dispatched) stays the same. Switching from one to the other is allowed: after you tap Full at yard, the Empty at yard button is still there, and the other way around.

On the office side, these statuses feed the Full at Yard and Empty at Yard counters on the Orders page (intermodal accounts). See Orders.

docs.title: The search shows No Results Found but the container exists
docs.text:
Solution

The search only finds orders that are New, App. Made or Dispatched. It does not find Completed orders or orders created before the Order Archive Cutoff Date. Check the order's status with the office. Also check the number: try typing only the last few digits.

docs.title: The Ground Container button is missing
docs.text:
Solution

Ground Container only shows when the order has a chassis. If CHASSIS NUMBER shows -- no chassis --, there is nothing to remove. Tap REFRESH if the office has just assigned a chassis.

docs.title: The Full at yard (or Empty at yard) button is missing
docs.text:
Solution

The button is hidden when the container status already has that value. Look at CONTAINER STATUS.

docs.title: I can't see the list of orders or sign a POD
docs.text:
Solution

That is expected. Yard Workers only have the container search and the yard buttons. POD signatures are collected by Drivers and Brokers in the Driver Mobile App. If this person also drives, they need a separate mobile user with the Driver role.

docs.title: I only see "Dashboard - Transportation orders coming soon"
docs.text:
Solution

You opened UTX Freight on a desktop browser. The container search only appears in the phone layout. Sign in from a phone.

docs.title: The buttons don't do anything
docs.text:
Solution

Make sure you signed in with an Access Code as a Yard Worker set up under Mobile Users. Only a Yard Worker signed in this way is allowed to use the yard buttons. Also check that the phone has a data connection, then tap REFRESH.

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
Tips for yard work

  • Search with enough digits to get one match. With several matches, check the container number and type code before tapping.
  • Tap REFRESH before you act if the card has been open for a while, so you see the office's latest changes.
  • After Ground Container, set Full at yard or Empty at yard so the office knows the container is in the yard and in what state.
  • Give each Yard Worker their own Access Code. See Mobile Users.

docs.title: Zones, Cities & Zone Rates
docs.text: Group your delivery cities into zones, give each zone a rate, and let UTX Freight fill the Base rate of an order automatically from the delivery city.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Zones and cities work together to price your orders:

  • Cities are the locations (UN locations) that your Shippers / Receivers are linked to. UTX loads the city list for you when your account is set up, so most of the cities you need already exist.
  • Zones are groups of cities. Each zone has one rate — the standard price for delivering to any city in that zone.
  • Each city can belong to one zone. A city does not have its own rate: the Rate shown for a city always comes from its zone.
  • A customer can have a custom rate for a zone. That rate replaces the zone rate on that customer's orders.
  • When you choose the delivery location on an order, the Base rate is filled from the customer's custom zone rate, or otherwise from the zone rate of the delivery city.
  • Zones and cities are never deleted. You can disable a zone, and you can mark a city as not Active.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
1. Click your name at the top of the screen to open the user menu, click Manage Zones, then click Add a new Zone.
  2. Enter the Name and the Rate for cities in this zone, then click Save Changes.
  3. Open the user menu again, click Manage Cities, then click Shipping to see the cities you actually deliver to.
  4. Click the Zone value (or N/A) of each city and pick its zone.

From now on, when the rate lookup runs for an order delivered to a Shipper / Receiver in one of those cities, the order's Base rate is filled with the zone rate (see How the Order Base Rate Is Set).

docs.title: Access & Permissions
docs.text:
Role Manage Zones Manage Cities Admin Full access Full access Manager Full access Full access Dispatch No access Full access only if Can manage rates? is checked on the dispatcher's profile Accountant No access No access Customer / Driver / Warehouse / Garage No access No access

Dispatchers and Manage Cities

Can manage rates? is a checkbox on the dispatcher's person profile ("Specifies if this Dispatch can manage rates and charges across the app"). An Admin or Manager can turn it on. See People & Invitations and User Roles. Dispatchers never see Manage Zones, even with this permission.

How to get there:

  • Click your name at the top of the screen to open the user menu, then click Manage Zones.
  • Click your name at the top of the screen to open the user menu, then click Manage Cities.

Both items sit in the user menu with the other Manage … items. They are not inside the Settings page. A menu item only appears for users who have access. See Navigation & Account.

Multi-office
